author: jgstern
body:
`File f = new File(p); f.createNewFile();` emitted
`java:external:0-0:f.createNewFile:unresolved` — the dst named the VARIABLE.
The type was never missing: `var_types` already infers it from four sources and
the analyzer already threads it out as `meta["receiver_type_hint"]`, but that
hint's only consumers are the Tier-2 `inherited_calls` / `receiver_type_dispatch`
linkers, which resolve PROJECT-INTERNAL symbols. Nothing carried it to the
external surface, so every catalogue consumer saw a bare method on an unknown
receiver.

That is fatal rather than lossy. `io_boundary.gate_named_entry` opens with an
unconditional `if call_construct == "method": return None`, so with no module
hint a method call matches NOTHING — not a method-kind entry, not even a
function-kind one. A nine-language measurement (one instrument, production's own
`_match_propagation_entry`, per-language positive controls) found not one
language legitimately matching a method-kind sink: java, scala, swift,
python-two-step, rust and objc all EMIT and all die at that gate. 67 of java's
69 catalogued sinks are method-kind. Emitting the edge was never the missing
piece.

The typed-local branch now writes the imported fully-qualified type into the
module slot, gated on that type being in `imports` so the slot only ever carries
a path the file declares. An unqualifiable type is left alone rather than
written in bare — a simple name there asserts a module that does not exist.

IT OPENED A PHANTOM-BARRIER CHANNEL ON THE WAY IN, and the guard is the
interesting half. Naming the type also SHORTENS the callee from `w.doFinal` to
`doFinal`, and `_register_sanitizer_callers` matches sanitizers on the SHORT
NAME while never consulting the module hint — so the shortening alone made
`com.example.Widget.doFinal` bind the catalogued `javax.crypto.Cipher.doFinal`.
Measured, not feared: the barrier really did register. A phantom barrier earns
`sanitized`, and a sanitized flow is DROPPED from the claim's violation set
(#214), so the recall win would have been paid for in silently deleted findings.
`make_unresolved_edge` grows a `call_construct` kwarg (additive, default None,
no existing caller affected) and this branch declares "method", which both taint
gates already honour. It costs nothing on the sink side: `_lookup_named_entry`
returns from its module-filter branch before `gate_named_entry` ever sees it.

Direction, measured on both signs. Sinks: java's two-step form moves from
no-match to match. Sanitizers: zero barriers register either way — not for the
wrong receiver type (the phantom, which is the point) and not for the correct
one either, because the sanitizer path has no module filtering to distinguish
them. Deliberate, and it follows `_register_sanitizer_callers`'s own ruling: a
missed barrier costs precision, an invented one costs a real finding.

Scope, stated rather than implied. This moves the TYPED-LOCAL form only.
`new File(p).createNewFile()` still emits `external` and does not match — a
receiver-shape gap, not a typing one. A fully-qualified declaration
(`java.io.File f = new java.io.File(p)`) also still misses, because the inferred
type is then `java.io.File` while `imports` is keyed by simple name. Both are
untouched and neither is claimed.

Tests: 21985 passed, mypy strict ratchet clean, all six packages 100% in
isolation. The core-package tests for `make_unresolved_edge` exist because the
helper lives in core while its java caller lives in mainstream, and CI measures
coverage per package.

Signed-off-by: jgstern-agent <josh-agent@iterabloom.com>

author: nicolasbriere1
body:
## Description

`sendgrid_teammate` cannot create or update a non-admin SSO teammate whose only intended access is `subuser_access`. SendGrid enforces two rules the provider didn't account for:

- `POST /sso/teammates` rejects an empty `scopes` list on create, even for a teammate whose scopes are meant to stay empty.
- Any request to `PATCH /sso/teammates/{username}` that carries both non-empty root `scopes` and `subuser_access` is rejected with `"cannot specify scopes for a restricted subuser access teammate"` - and this holds for both the create-time follow-up call and any later update, regardless of whether the account already had `subuser_access` before.

Before this fix, `scopes = []` failed outright on create; a non-empty placeholder scope let create succeed but then broke the follow-up `subuser_access` call and every subsequent apply.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Code refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Test improvements
- [ ] Chore (dependency updates, tooling, etc.)

## Related Issues

Fixes #113

## Changes Made

- `resourceSendgridTeammateCreate`: use a placeholder scope (`user.profile.read`) only when `scopes` is empty and `subuser_access` will be applied, to satisfy the create-time validation. The follow-up `subuser_access` call omits `scopes` entirely.
- `resourceSendgridTeammateUpdate`: omit `scopes` whenever `subuser_access` is managed, regardless of what `scopes` is configured to.
- `scopes` schema attribute is now `Optional: true, Computed: true`, mirroring `subuser_access`: once a teammate has `subuser_access`, its root scopes are frozen server-side and can never be reset to empty through this attribute (the SDK's `omitempty` means an empty/nil `scopes` is dropped from the request, not sent as a clearing value).
- `CustomizeDiff` now calls `d.Clear("scopes")` whenever `subuser_access` has entries. `Optional+Computed` alone only suppresses the diff when `scopes` is *omitted* from config; an explicit `scopes = []` (the shape used in the original bug report) still produced a diff that `Update()` can never actually apply. This closes that gap unconditionally.

## Testing

### Unit Tests

- [x] I have added unit tests for my changes
- [x] All unit tests pass locally (`go test ./...`)

New tests:
- `TestTeammateCreate_SubuserOnly` - create sends a placeholder scope, the subuser_access follow-up never resends `scopes`.
- `TestTeammateUpdate_SubuserAccess` - update never resends a stray `scopes` value once `subuser_access` is managed.
- `TestTeammateScopesClearedWithSubuserAccess` - an explicit `scopes = []` against a teammate with `subuser_access` produces no diff. Verified this test fails without the `CustomizeDiff` change (reproduces the exact stuck diff) and passes with it.
- `TestTeammateResourceSchema` extended to assert `scopes` is now `Optional+Computed`.
- `TestTeammateSubuserAccessComputedNoDiff` updated with a realistic prior `scopes` value now that the attribute is Computed.

### Acceptance Tests

- [ ] I have added/updated acceptance tests (`make testacc`)
- [ ] All acceptance tests pass with a real SendGrid account
- [ ] Tests include Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations (if applicable)

### Manual Testing

Reproduced both original failures against a real SendGrid account before this fix, then verified the fixed behavior manually against the same account (create, subuser_access apply, and repeated no-op applies) before opening this PR. No acceptance tests added since they'd require a real SendGrid API key in CI; the unit tests above cover the request-shape and diff-convergence behavior this fix changes.

```
go vet ./...   # clean
go test ./...  # ok, all packages
gofmt -l .     # no output for the two files touched by this PR
```

## Documentation

- [ ] I have updated the documentation in `docs/`
- [ ] I have added examples to `examples/resources/`
- [ ] I have updated the CHANGELOG.md
- [x] I have added/updated code comments where necessary
- [x] All exported functions have godoc comments

The `scopes` schema `Description` was updated to note it's frozen once `subuser_access` is set.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's [coding standards](CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards)
- [x] I have run `make fmt` to format the code
- [ ] I have run `make lint` and fixed all issues
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings or errors
- [x] I have checked for any breaking changes
- [x] My commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format

## Breaking Changes

**Is this a breaking change?** No

`scopes` becoming `Computed` only changes behavior for teammates that also have `subuser_access` configured - existing plain root-scoped teammates are unaffected.

## Additional Context

Two commits:
1. `fix(teammate): never combine scopes and subuser_access in the same request` - fixes both hard failures from #113.
2. `fix(teammate): clear scopes diff via CustomizeDiff when subuser_access is managed` - closes a residual "permanent diff" gap found in review: `Optional+Computed` alone doesn't cover an explicitly-configured `scopes = []`.

## Reviewer Notes

The `CustomizeDiff` change in the second commit is the part most worth a close look - `d.Clear("scopes")` unconditionally drops any scopes diff once `subuser_access` has entries, on the reasoning that `Update()` can never apply it anyway. Happy to discuss alternatives if there's a preferred pattern for this in the codebase.

author: aahoughton
body:
Fixes #656. Stacked on #681 (which stacks on #680); merge those first.

Implements the issue's proposal: the members `oaverify compile-spec`
writes into the consumer's generated module move to a new
`@oaverify/core/codegen-runtime` subpath (the issue's working name,
kept), documented as semver-covered because generated output in
strangers' repos depends on it. `validator/internals` keeps the
convenience members, and its "nothing here is covered by semver"
warning becomes true. Per the issue's lean, no deprecated re-exports:
emitted output is the only known consumer, it is bundled (so existing
files keep working), and it is regenerated by the same CLI that moved.

One deviation from the issue's grouping, stated: membership follows
what emitted output actually imports (the twelve names on emit-spec's
import line), not the issue's list. That pulls `deserialize`,
`matchParsedMediaType`, `matchResponseKey`, `resolveOperationRef`, and
`contentTypeErrorMessage` to the covered side, and leaves
`readBodyFromFetch` (which no emitted output references; it is the
inner half of the fetch wrappers) on internals. The membership rule is
written into the module header so the next addition has a principle.

Also per the issue: pack-smoke gains the installed-consumer assertion —
pack, install with esbuild, `compile-spec` a fixture, execute the
emitted module and assert a valid/invalid pair. That is the only place
the new exports-map subpath resolves against a packed tarball rather
than workspace aliases. I ran the same flow locally against freshly
packed tarballs and it passes.

Wiring: root exports map + tsup entry + src shim, workspace alias for
`@oaverify/core/codegen-runtime` (compile-spec tests execute emitted
modules through it), internal package exports, docs/modules.md section.
All four gates pass; the compile-spec suite (which bundles emitted
modules) covers the membership in both directions.

author: adamflagg
body:
## Summary

- **#2039** — `guardUnitYear` now covers `lodging_units` itself, following both `area` (into `lodging_areas`) and `parent_unit` (a self-relation) instead of only the four placement/availability tables that point *at* units.
- **#2035** — a new test drives `guardUnitYear` through `OnRecordUpdate`, not only `OnRecordCreate`.
- **#1870** — `pocketbase/CLAUDE.md`'s "WAL checkpoint required" line is now scoped to the sync layer, matching the decision already applied to `.coderabbit.yaml` in #1903.

## #2039 details

`guardUnitYear` watched four tables (`lodging_availability`, `lodging_assignments`, `lodging_assignments_draft`, `lodging_slot_merges`) for a row whose own `year` disagreed with the unit it named — but never `lodging_units` itself. A 2027 room could name a 2026 `area` or a 2026 `parent_unit` with no error anywhere: Manage would drop it into "No area", and the roster's `area` expand would silently resolve the wrong season's name and `sort_order`.

The refs table moved from `map[string][]string` to a slice of `{field, target}` structs (`yearScopedRefs`), because Go map iteration order is randomized and `lodging_units` is the first entry carrying **two** relations — a row cross-year on both would otherwise name a different field on every test/prod run.

`lodging_units` is the odd one out twice over: it's both a referencing and a referenced table (`parent_unit` is a self-relation), and `area` resolves into `lodging_areas` rather than into itself. A self-skip (`if id == rec.Id { continue }`) handles the self-relation case — without it, editing a **legacy** self-parented row's year (data written before `guardUnitParentCycle` existed; its diff gate lets an already-self-parented row's *other* edits through untouched) would be refused, naming the row as the offending relation.

**Correction to the issue body:** #2039 cites migration `1500000140` as the one that year-scoped the registry. At HEAD (`9b99c220`), `1500000140` is `lodging_slot_merges_scenario_optional.js` — the year-scoping migration is **`1500000141_lodging_registry_year.js`**, which gives both `lodging_units` and `lodging_areas` their own `year` and re-indexes both on `(code, year)`. `hooks.go`/`hooks_test.go` already cited 141 correctly.

### Mutation-check 1 — update binding (closes #2035)

Deleted `hooks.go`'s `OnRecordUpdate` binding block for the year-scoped tables and re-ran the full `TestGuardUnitYear*` set (re-run against the final tree; corrects an earlier version of this section that pasted only a 5-test partial run):

```
$ go test ./lodging/ -run TestGuardUnitYear -count=1 -v
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearRow
--- FAIL: TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearRowOnUpdate
    hooks_test.go:1263: re-pointed a 2027 row at a 2026 unit; want a refusal
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearChecksEveryMemberOfTheMultiRelation
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearAllowsAMatchingRow
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearSkipsAnAbsentCollection
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearArea
--- FAIL: TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearParentUnit
    hooks_test.go:1407: re-parented a 2027 room under a 2026 building; want a refusal
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearAllowsAUnitWhoseParentAndAreaShareItsYear
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearIgnoresAnEmptyParentUnit
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearSkipsAUnitsSelfReference
FAIL
```

Two tests fail, not one: `TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearParentUnit` also exercises the update path (it re-saves an already-created child unit via `app.Save`, same as the row-level update test), so it reds too when the `OnRecordUpdate` binding is gone. The other eight stay green. Restored the block, re-ran, all green.

### Mutation-check 2 — self-skip (part of #2039)

Deleted the `if id == rec.Id { continue }` line and re-ran:

```
$ go test ./lodging/ -run TestGuardUnitYear -count=1 -v
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearRow
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearRowOnUpdate
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearChecksEveryMemberOfTheMultiRelation
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearAllowsAMatchingRow
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearSkipsAnAbsentCollection
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearArea
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearParentUnit
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearAllowsAUnitWhoseParentAndAreaShareItsYear
--- PASS: TestGuardUnitYearIgnoresAnEmptyParentUnit
--- FAIL: TestGuardUnitYearSkipsAUnitsSelfReference
    hooks_test.go:1504: a row must not be refused for disagreeing with itself: Lodging_units row is for year 2027 but its parent_unit relation names "test-unit-a" from year 2026.
FAIL
```

Only `TestGuardUnitYearSkipsAUnitsSelfReference` failed; every other test, including the two positive controls, stayed green. Restored the line, re-ran, all green.

### Also fixed: a stale comment

`TestGuardUnitYearSkipsAnAbsentCollection`'s doc comment claimed `lodging_slot_merges` "has not merged yet" — false as of `1500000139`/`1500000140`, both at HEAD. The test still validly pins the skip path (the *fixture* just doesn't create that collection), so only the comment changed, not the test body or assertion.

### Follow-up not done here

The fixture gap above means `lodging_slot_merges`'s own guard coverage is untested (`setupCollections` never creates that collection). Closing it means adding the collection to the fixture — a separate, larger change, out of scope here.

**Review follow-up: the guard's scope is one-directional, and residual, not a regression.** `guardUnitYear` only checks the row being written against its own outgoing relations (the entries in `yearScopedRefs`). Two gaps follow from that: editing an existing `lodging_areas` row's own `year` in place hits no binding at all (`lodging_areas` is a valid target above but not itself a key in the map), leaving every `lodging_units` row already pointing at it silently cross-season; and editing a `lodging_units` row's own `year` is checked against that row's area/parent_unit, but does not re-check the rows that point AT it (`lodging_availability`, `lodging_assignments`, `lodging_assignments_draft`, `lodging_slot_merges`). Closing either means cascading to every dependent row on a parent's write, not validating only the row under write — out of scope for this PR. Documented in the `yearScopedRefs` doc comment (`hooks.go`); tracking issue to follow.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` — clean
- `go test ./lodging/ -count=1` — all green (including the 9 `TestGuardUnitYear*` cases and the new roll-forward regression guard)
- `go test ./...` — 100% packages passing (`lodging` 110.6s, `sync` 283.9s, rest fast)
- `golangci-lint run ./lodging/...` — `No issues found`, `exit=0` (not in pre-push, run explicitly)
- `./scripts/dev/verify-lodging-schema.sh` — real `pocketbase serve` boot against a throwaway DB, all 103 JS migrations applied cleanly with the new hook wiring (`TestApp` in the Go suite skips `Start()`, so this is the check that actually proves the binary boots)
- Full pre-push suite (ruff, markdownlint, shellcheck, pb-js-lint, go-build, api-types-freshness, mypy, pytest, tsc): all green, `6007 passed, 41 skipped` (all pre-existing/expected skips per `tests/CLAUDE.md`)
- Pushed and confirmed landed: `git fetch -q && git rev-list --count origin/feature/lodging-unit-year-guard..HEAD` → `0`

**Unrelated pre-existing issue noticed, not caused by this branch:** `./scripts/dev/verify-lodging-seed.sh` fails with "no lodging_units rows — the boot loader did not run" both with and without this PR's changes (confirmed by stashing this diff and re-running against the committed baseline). Not a regression from this work; flagging for awareness.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearRowOnUpdate` (closes #2035)
- [x] `TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearArea`
- [x] `TestGuardUnitYearRejectsACrossYearParentUnit`
- [x] `TestGuardUnitYearAllowsAUnitWhoseParentAndAreaShareItsYear` (positive control)
- [x] `TestGuardUnitYearIgnoresAnEmptyParentUnit`
- [x] `TestGuardUnitYearSkipsAUnitsSelfReference`
- [x] `TestApplyRollForwardSurvive

author: tim-nish
body:
Stacked on #124 — review/merge that first (which stacks on #123, which stacks on #122).

## Summary

Closes #107.

`terrain.mjs subdivide` implements SPEC.md §8: a large group subdivides into LLM-classified SubGroups each carrying its own composed claim, **built and runnable but not offered by default**, writing its record to the machine-local run workspace as the dogfood specimen §8.1's offering gate needs.

**Merging this does not discharge the offering gate — it makes it due.** Co-tags remain the default for a run naming no substrate; no default path so much as mentions subdivision (verified: `grep -c subdivi` over `survey`, `view` and `cotags` output = 0).

### The flagged open question — resolved by the served surface, not by a pick

#107's Review Focus flagged whether "which model performs the LLM classification" is itself a deferred slot, given the judge-migration tripwire. **It is not, and the surface says so directly rather than leaving it open.** `topics/knowledge-architecture.md:84@f918c515` ADOPTS the judge pin for per-invocation judged surfaces and names **terrain screens, claims and groupings** among them, with the mechanism spelled out — *a fourth component (model id + effort tier) on the existing pin discipline* — because where drift is undetectable, "*recomputed fresh* silently becomes *recomputed by a different judge* with nothing in the record distinguishing that from ordinary nondeterminism". `:85` is its complement: the pin makes a judge change **observable**, the tripwire makes it **consequential**, and "either alone leaves the loop open".

So the ratified shape makes the model a **per-invocation pinned fact**, not a design decision to embed. **This code names no model.** `--judge-model` and `--judge-effort` are required arguments and the record carries them, so the tripwire's input finally has a writer. The consult receipt is on the spec commit (`request_id 3013a256`, outcome `discriminating`).

## Acceptance Criteria Mapping

| AC | Implementation | Test |
|---|---|---|
| GroupClaim first, then SubGroups with their claims, then Lessons | `cmdSubdivide` render order | live specimen output |
| No member hidden; those fitting none in an explicit named SubGroup; cover after composition | unplaced members land in `(fits no composed SubGroup)`; invented members refused; `SUBDIVISION_COVER_INCOMPLETE` | `Cover: 10 of 10`; the dropped member reappeared in the explicit SubGroup |
| Leaf condition CONJUNCTIVE | `sg.leaf = honest && tighter`, with distinct reasons per failing conjunct | one subgroup reported "split further", another "the split bought nothing" |
| Degenerate-claim disclosure | judge verdict **or** the claim naming a member's slug | fired on "Trials and joins" |
| Undiscriminating-claim disclosure, disjunctive with the first | judge verdict **or** claim identical to parent's; evaluated independently | fired on "Batch grading" — a *different* subgroup, which is the disjunctiveness |
| Three instruments, three quantities, none a member-count threshold | `relative_share_of_placements`, `screen_budget_lines`, `legible_at_a_glance` — reported, gating nothing | printed per subgroup; no branch reads them |
| Co-tags default; subdivision not offered | no default path names it; `offered_by_default` pinned false | `grep -c subdivi` = 0 on every default path |
| Capturable as a dogfood specimen | `*.terrain-subdivision.json` written to the run workspace | specimen written; record inspected below |
| Ranks, trims, hides nothing | no proposal record; trim guard untouched | stated in output; `MAX_STRAND_OPTIONS` unchanged |
| Counts name families + Lessons denominator | reuses `strandFigure`/`denominator` | every SubGroup line |

## Review Focus

- **`--judge-model` / `--judge-effort` are required and the record pins them.** This is the story's most consequential choice and it is the served surface's, not mine. A run that cannot name its judge cannot produce a specimen.
- **No numeric constant in split or stop logic** — §8's declared reopen trigger is exactly that. Both leaf conjuncts are the judge's verdicts, never re-derived from a proxy; the screen budget arrives per run; the only literal in the file is `LINES_PER_SUBGROUP_HEADER = 2`, which is rendering arithmetic for the screen-budget instrument and gates nothing. Worth checking that reading.
- **The two disclosures each have a judge-independent signal.** A claim naming a member's slug is enumerating; a claim textually identical to its parent's is undiscriminating by construction. Neither is a count, and both hold when the judge's self-report is wrong — which matters, since a judge grading its own claim is the weaker half.
- **§8's member-count prohibition stays uncarried, deliberately.** This PR does not convert it into a check; §8 declares state three with a reopen trigger and the review lane as its reader, and naming that weakness is the point. Nothing here should be read as having closed it.
- **The parked offering gate is untouched.** It is outside this story's acceptance criteria on purpose — "the owner has verdicted subdivision's output" cannot be satisfied by an implementing PR. This PR produces a specimen so the gate can *become due*.

## Changed Areas

- `specs/spec-terrain/survey-schema.json` — the `subdivision` record shape, judge pin required
- `terrain/terrain.mjs` — `cmdSubdivide`, the `subdivide` subcommand and its usage

## Test Plan

Registered check suite (all 10): `FAILED: none`. Earlier commands regression-checked (`cotags`, `view`, `validate`) — unchanged.

Dogfood specimen, `agents × testing` (10 members), judged by `claude-opus-5[1m]` at effort `default`:

```
agents × testing (17 — 10 lessons + 7 journeys); 10 of 144 Lessons
  in common: these lessons are about verifying that a system does what it appears to do

  Guards that are present and structurally dead (4 — 2 lessons + 2 journeys); 2 of 144 Lessons
    in common: a safeguard can be merged, correctly placed and completely unable to fire, ...
    leaf: the claim composes honestly AND is tighter than its parent's
    instruments (three quantities, none a threshold, none gating): relative share of placements 20.0%; screen budget 4 lines needed of 40; legible at a glance: true

  Trials and joins (2 — 2 lessons + 0 journeys); 2 of 144 Lessons
    in common: these cover absence-verification-counts-exercised-trials and derived-view-dogfood-needs-its-join-key
    NOT a leaf: the claim does not compose honestly — split further
    DISCLOSURE — degenerate-claim: the claim trails into enumeration (it names a member's slug)

  Batch grading (2 — 1 lesson + 1 journey); 1 of 144 Lessons
    in common: these lessons are about verifying that a system does what it appears to do
    NOT a leaf: the claim composes honestly but is not tighter than its parent's — the split bought nothing
    DISCLOSURE — undiscriminating-claim: honest, but true of every member at the size served ...

  (fits no composed SubGroup) (2 — 1 lesson + 1 journey); 1 of 144 Lessons
      lesson:coverage-exploration-not-reward-search

Cover: 10 of 10 parent members placed in at least one SubGroup — counted AFTER composition, over placements. No member is hidden.
Judge pin: claude-opus-5[1m] (effort default) — the fourth component on the pin discipline, so a change of serving judge is OBSERVABLE and fires the judge-migration tripwire.
NOT OFFERED BY DEFAULT. ... Producing this specimen ARRIVES at §8.1's offering gate rather than discharging it ... The hub-side gate remains undischarged.
```

The record:

```
judge: {'model_id': 'claude-opus-5[1m]', 'effort_tier': 'default'}
offered_by_default: False
cover: {'placed': 10, 'of': 10, 'counted_over': 'placements'}
subgroups (name, leaf, #disclosures):

author: houdini91
body:
## What this proves

The repo's flagship claim — **byte-integrity catches a same-GUID module swap that membership/signatures miss** — was previously only demonstrated by a hand-authored fixture (`oss-lane/fixtures/byte-integrity-modified.json`) plus unit tests. Nothing took a *real* module, swapped its bytes under the *same* GUID, ran the *real* producer, and showed MODIFIED → gate DENY.

This PR closes that gap with a committed, reproducible end-to-end demo.

## How to run

```
make attack-demo
```

Self-contained: committed fixtures + `opa` + `python3`. Runs locally and in CI.

It:
1. Takes a **real edk2 PE32** (`tests/fixtures/pe/pcdpeim.declared.efi`), registers it in a 1-module SBOM as a DXE driver, and wraps it in a real FFS.
2. Ships a copy with **one byte flipped in the PE body under the SAME FILE_GUID/name** — a same-GUID swap.
3. Runs the **real** `producers/reconcile/byte-integrity.py` over both:
   - clean → `verified=1 modified=0` (exit 0)
   - trojaned → `⛔ MODIFIED DemoNetworkDxe: declared 3b830c78… != observed e5fc5b4b…` (exit 1)
4. Folds each real verdict into the **real** OPA deploy gate (`oss-lane/gate.sh`, via the real assembler):
   - clean → `✅ ALLOW`
   - trojaned → `⛔ DENY` on `component-byte-integrity`

## Before / after (the crux)

In **both** runs `reconcile-membership` PASSES — the GUID is present, so membership can't see the swap. Only `component-byte-integrity` flips ✅→⛔, and that flip is what turns the gate from ALLOW to DENY:

```
⛔ DENY — tampered-gate-input.json  (VSA: FAILED)
   • byte-integrity: 1 module(s) MODIFIED — shipped bytes differ from the SBOM's declared hash (possible same-GUID swap)
RESULT: same-GUID byte swap — reconcile-membership PASSED, component-byte-integrity DENIED. ✔ caught.
```

## Real vs. user-supplied

- **Real & self-contained:** a real PE32, real byte-tampering, the real producer, the real OPA gate — over a **minimal 1-module demo image** built from committed fixtures, so it runs anywhere with no edk2 tree. The only substitution vs. production is the extraction *source*: the producer reads the pre-carved FFS via a new `--ffs-dir` flag instead of an `--image` + FMMT carve. An already-carved FFS is exactly what `FMMT -e` emits, so the downstream PE32-carve + SHA-256 verdict is byte-for-byte identical.
- **User-supplied (optional full run):** `make attack-demo FW_IMAGE=/path/OVMF.fd EDK2=/path/edk2` additionally exercises the producer's real `--image` + FMMT carve over your full multi-module OVMF build (against `inputs/sbom.cdx.json`, the 122-module reference SBOM).

## CI / tests

- New `tests/test_attack_demo.py` runs the whole harness end-to-end and asserts clean→ALLOW / trojaned→DENY. Wired into `make test` and `.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml`.
- `make test` stays green.

## Files

- `producers/reconcile/byte-integrity.py` — add `--ffs-dir` extraction source (image/edk2 now optional; mutually-exclusive with ffs-dir).
- `scripts/attack-demo.sh`, `scripts/attack_demo_build.py` — the harness.
- `tests/test_attack_demo.py` — CI end-to-end proof.
- `Makefile` — `attack-demo` target + test wiring.
- `docs/DEMO.md` — §5 "Attack demo: same-GUID trojan caught" with the actual captured output.

body:
> 두 건 다 **실측으로 재확인**한 뒤 고쳤다.

## ① amber 배너가 막다른 CTA 였다

`/project/new` 의 배너는 화면에서 **가장 눈에 띄는 것**(유일한 난색)인데 *"저장하려면 먼저 폴더를 열어야 합니다"* 라고만 말했고, **이 화면 어디에도 폴더를 여는 컨트롤이 없었다** — 전수 **0개**.

헌장의 강등 문법은 «왜 안 되는지 **+ 어디로 가면 되는지**» 다(`.claude/rules/surfaces.md`). 문서함이 같은 문제를 이미 그렇게 풀었다 — *"누르면 그것을 가능하게 하는 곳(내 폴더 열기)으로 간다."* 그 선례를 그대로 따라 배너에 **「내 폴더 열기」**(→ `/`)와 한 줄 힌트를 붙였다.

## ② 보조 패널의 「0%」가 페이지 제목과 동률이었다

둘 다 **30px**(`text-hero`). 미리보기 패널의 수치가 그 화면 제목과 같은 급이면 «무엇이 먼저인가»가 사라진다. `text-display`(23)로 한 단 내렸다 — 실측 **30 → 23**, 제목은 30 그대로.

## 게이트 — `tests/e2e/screen-hierarchy.spec.ts` 신설

**둘 다 코드에 아무 값도 안 남기는 결함이다.** 「0%」는 램프 안의 **정당한 칸**을 쓰고 있었고 배너는 문구가 멀쩡했다 — 값을 보는 lint 도, 소스를 훑는 계약도 볼 수 없다. **그려진 화면에서만 보인다.**

그리고 「제목보다 큰 것이 없다」는 **두 원소의 관계**이고 그 둘은 서로 다른 파일에 산다(제목은 페이지, 통계는 폼 위젯). 한 파일의 구문 트리를 보는 검사로는 원리적으로 표현할 수 없다.

| 검사 | 무엇을 잠그나 |
|---|---|
| ① | h1 보다 크거나 같은 글자 **0개** (공회전 방지 — h1 을 못 찾거나 훑은 원소가 20 미만이면 먼저 빨개진다) |
| ② | 배너에 갈 곳이 있고 **눌러서 실제로 열린다** (「눌러도 아무 데도 안 가는 버튼 0개」 규율) |

**프로브 2종 실측**: 「0%」를 `text-hero` 로 되돌리면 ①이 `[{"text":"0%","px":30}]` 로 빨강 · 배너에서 갈 곳을 떼면 ②가 빨강.

- `pnpm lint` — **0 errors / 91 warnings** (변경 전과 동일)

body:
Follow-up to #1669, which that PR named as owed once #1658 landed.

Annex A of N4 still reports pack signature verification as self-certifying (A.4) and the canonical serialization as partial (A.3). #1669 closed both. #1658 introduced the annex and landed first, so `main` carries an annex describing a vulnerability that was fixed hours later — and that annex is the document a reader consults to decide whether the implementation can be trusted.

Informative annex only. No normative text touched.

## Changes

- **A.4** reads as closed and says what replaced it: `:pack/signed-by` resolved as a key identifier against a configured trust-root store that ships empty, so a deployment that configures nothing trusts nothing. Records the two adjacent defects closed with it (RFC 8032 raw key decoding, non-reproducible canonical bytes).

  It also names what is **still open**, which #1669 did not close:
  - §8.2 steps 4 and 5 — signature timestamp against a key validity window, and publisher permitted for the pack (§5.1.8).
  - The gate that would call any of it. §5.1.8's `require-signature-verification` and `enforce-publisher-allowlist` are declared with `:rule/detection {:type :custom}` and no `:custom-fn`, so `verify-signature` has no caller outside its component. The verifier is correct; it is not yet reachable.

- **A.3** describes what `policy-pack/canonical-edn` and `canonical-order` now do, replacing the "partial on determinism" note.

- **Annex preamble** — a closed row says so and names the change rather than being deleted. The annex is the record of what the gap was, not only of what remains. Date to 2026-08-06.

- **Version history** — one entry for this annex-only revision.

author: burpeesdaily
body:
Closes task 3.1. A single-file command-line tool that drives the whole public API end to end, so the library has something to *use*, not just an API to read about.

## Commands

| | |
|---|---|
| `import <dir>` | `import_dir` with content-hash dedup; `--no-recursive`, `--allow-duplicates`, `--device` |
| `list` | `query` + `count`, filtered by `--since/--until/--type/--label/--device`, with `--limit/--offset` |
| `show <id>` | every field of one record |
| `tag <id>` | `--add`/`--remove` labels, `--describe`, via `update_enrichment` |
| `embed` | compute embeddings for images; `--force` to recompute |
| `similar <id>` | `search_similar`, self excluded, `--limit`/`--threshold` |
| `export <id> <dest>` | `retrieve`, accepting a file or a directory |
| `delete <id>` | record + backing file |
| `stats` | counts, bytes, embedding coverage, date span, top labels |
| `reconcile` | orphaned files and dangling rows |

Ids can be given as the 8-character prefix shown in listings; ambiguous and unknown prefixes fail with a clear message.

A library is two things on disk — `<library>/media/` and `<library>/catalog.db` — which is the two-folder portability claim made concrete.

## On the embedding

`embed` computes a 64-dimension **color-layout signature**: a 4x4 grid of mean RGB (48 values) plus a 16-bin luma histogram, L2-normalized so cosine similarity is meaningful.

It matches on **color and composition, not meaning**. The README and the docstring both say so directly rather than calling it semantic search. It is here so the similarity path is exercised for real instead of staying theoretical while `LocalEnricher` is still a stub. Swapping in CLIP means replacing one function and bumping `EMBEDDING_MODEL`; storage and search do not change.

Verified it actually ranks correctly — reds retrieve reds, blues retrieve blues — not merely that it returns rows.

## Dependencies

Everything except `embed` runs on the stdlib-only core. `embed` needs a decoder, so it requires `[exif]`, and fails with an actionable message when Pillow is missing:

```
error: embed requires an image decoder.
       python -m pip install "spectator-db[exif]"
```

Confirmed by running the full CLI with `PIL` forced to fail: import, list, tag, and search all work; only `embed` stops.

## Tests

`tests/test_example_photos.py` — 32 tests driving the CLI against a real library on disk, so the example cannot silently rot as the API moves. The 5 embedding tests skip where Pillow is absent, which is what CI does.

Suite: **120 passed, 5 skipped**. black, flake8, mypy, and pydocstyle all clean.

## Note

Branched off `main`, so it does not carry the version bump in #12. If #12 merges first this may want a trivial rebase — both touch the top of `CHANGELOG.md`.

author: taipanbox
body:
Invariant 31, and the gate for it. Per the standing rule, an approved decision is not
finished until it is both.

## Why this is invariant 29's debt and not a new idea

Putting `std::process::id()` into a fixture path was right. It also changed the price
of never deleting one:

| | path is a constant | path carries the pid |
|---|---|---|
| never wiped | 1 stale directory, reused forever | 1 **new** directory on **every** run |

That is why five of these sat here unnoticed for so long, and why they all became
visible in the same day: the fix turned a leak that did not grow into one that does.

`@measured` 6 August 2026, five runs of each affected suite, counting `$TMPDIR`
afterwards:

| Suite | directories left |
|---|---|
| `signed` | 55, **holding 55 EC private keys** |
| OTLP JSON oracle | 5, holding 80 files |
| `two_verifiers` | 5 |
| `inflate` | 5 |

The keys are what make this a rule rather than tidiness. They are throwaway test keys
and nothing in them is secret. A fixture that leaves key material lying about teaches
that leaving key material lying about is normal, and that habit does not stay in the
fixtures.

## What the gate does

`scripts/scratch-cleanup.sh` counts each `temp_dir()` binding against the
`remove_dir_all` calls naming it, through `self.` as well so a `Drop` counts.

**Counting rather than looking is the part that matters.** The projection oracle had
two fixtures and one wipe. Any check asking merely "does this file remove anything"
would have called it clean, and it was one of the five that leaked.

Run against the tree as it stood before #17 and #20, it reports all five:

```
crates/trailryx-ingest/tests/inflate.rs:327: `dir` is built from temp_dir() 1 time(s) and removed 0
crates/trailryx-otlp/tests/jsonenc_is_otlp_json.rs:234: `dir` ... 1 time(s) and removed 0
crates/trailryx-projection/tests/oracle.rs:44: `dir` ... 2 time(s) and removed 1
crates/trailryx-store/tests/signed.rs:51: `scratch` ... 1 time(s) and removed 0
crates/trailryx-store/tests/two_verifiers.rs:137: `dir` ... 1 time(s) and removed 0
```

That is the run which says it can fail at all, per invariant 19. On the current tree
it reports 12 scratch paths, all removed.

## Its blind spots are measured, not assumed

Both are written into the script's header and into the invariant:

- **A pre-clean satisfies the count exactly as a real wipe does.** Verified rather
  than guessed: I deleted `anchored.rs`'s `Drop` impl and the gate still passed,
  because its pre-clean `remove_dir_all` already satisfied the count.
- **A wipe below an early return is one it cannot see past.** `inflate` needed its
  call moved *above* two returns, and this check would have been happy either way.

Both are the removal being in the wrong *place*. What the gate holds is the removal
never being *written*, which is what happened all five times.

## What stays a judgement

Where the wipe goes, and the invariant says so rather than pretending the gate
decides it:

- `inflate` needed its wipe **above** its two early returns.
- The OTLP oracle needed its wipe **below** its assertion, because that assertion
  names the file it failed against, and a message pointing at a deleted path is worse
  than no path at all. A `Drop` guard is the wrong tool there for exactly that
  reason, and the right one on `Openssl`, which owns its directory and has nothing
  worth leaving behind.

## Twentieth check

The hook, CI and the README's count move together, which `scripts/gate-count.sh`
requires and confirms:

```
the gate's own count    ok  20 checks in the hook, 20 in CI, README says twenty
```

All 20 pass locally.

author: alexdarch
body:
## ⚠️ CI will be red — that is the point of this PR

This adds **8 corpus tests that fail today**. No grammar or scanner change is
included. Each expected tree is the tree a *correct* parse should produce, so
the suite goes from 0 to 8 failures. It's a bug report expressed as executable
tests, not something to merge as-is — happy to reshape it into whatever form is
useful (issues, draft-until-fixed, or paired with fixes in follow-ups).

`src/parser.c` and `src/grammar.json` are untouched, and I verified that
regenerating from the committed `grammar.js` reproduces both byte-for-byte, so
the "parser matches grammar" check is unaffected.

## The eight cases

### `expressions.txt`

**`in`/`out` on a typed lambda parameter** — `(in int value) => value`

The parameter reading is shadowed by `argument`'s
`optional(choice('ref','out','in'))`, so the input reduces to
`argument → declaration_expression` and then errors on `)`. `--debug` shows no
GLR split (`version_count` stays 1). Only `in`/`out` are affected: `ref int x`
escapes because it also reads as `ref_type` (which is why the existing *Lambda
expression with ref modifier* test records `type: (ref_type …)` and no
`(modifier)` node), and `this`/`scoped`/`readonly` aren't argument prefixes.
Deleting `'in'` from `argument` in a scratch copy makes the input parse as
`(parameter (modifier) type: (predefined_type) name: (identifier))`.

**Assignment through a cast pointer** — `*((uint*) ptr) = 1`, `*(ulong*) ptr = 2`

`_pointer_indirection_expression` restricts `*`'s operand to an
`lvalue_expression`, but a cast — parenthesized or bare — is a non-lvalue, so
neither form parses. In C# `*` applies to any pointer-typed expression and
yields an lvalue. This looks like fallout from the `&`/`*` split in #430.

**Assignment to a ref-returning call** — `Slot() = value`

`assignment_expression`'s `left` is `lvalue_expression`, which has no
`invocation_expression`, so a `ref`-returning method can't be assigned through.

### `contextual-keywords.txt`

**`required` as an ordinary identifier**

`required` is in `modifier` but missing from `_reserved_identifier` (unlike
`file`, `scoped`, `var`, …). As a parameter name it's fine — keyword extraction
falls back to `_identifier_token` where the keyword isn't valid — but in
statement position `local_declaration_statement`'s `repeat($.modifier)` makes
the keyword valid, so `required = true;` commits to a local declaration and dies
at `=`. `required` isn't a legal local-variable modifier in C# at all. The
`[$._reserved_identifier, $.modifier]` conflict already exists, so adding
`'required'` to `_reserved_identifier` looks like the minimal fix.

### `literals.txt`

**Nested braces in an interpolated string** — `$"{{{string.Join(", ", value)}}}"`

Scanner bug. `brace_advanced` is a single function-scope variable shared by the
`INTERPOLATION_OPEN_BRACE` and `INTERPOLATION_STRING_CONTENT` branches. On
`{{{`, OPEN_BRACE consumes the first `{`, leaves `brace_advanced == 1`, then
bails because the next char is `{`. STRING_CONTENT inherits the stale `1` while
`open_brace_count == 0`, so its `brace_advanced == open_brace_count` stop can
never fire at the third brace — and it's only reset once a non-`{` is seen, by
which point all three braces are consumed. Content then runs to the first `"` it
meets, which is the one inside `", "`. Result: `string_content` = `{{{string.Join(`,
the interpolation never opens, and `", "` becomes a separate `string_literal`.
`$"{{x}}"` works because two braces never need the third-brace stop.

**Empty interpolated string** — `$""`

The scanner consumes both quotes probing for a raw string and, finding only two,
deliberately pushes nothing onto `interpolation_stack` ("If there's only two
quotes, that's just an empty string") — but still returns
`INTERPOLATION_REGULAR_START` with `mark_end` after the `$`. The grammar then
requires `interpolation_start_quote`, whose handler needs a non-empty stack and
returns false. Result: `(ERROR (interpolation_start)) (string_literal)`.

### `preprocessor.txt`

**`#if` around a base list**

No `preproc_if` variant is valid in base-list position — `preprocIf` is
instantiated for declarations, top-level items, expressions, enum members and
attribute lists only, and `_class_declaration_initializer` accepts just
`type_parameter_list | parameter_list | base_list`. A
`preprocIf('_in_base_list', $ => $.base_list, 0, false)` variant allowed in the
class/struct/interface/record initializers would cover it. **The expected tree
here is a guess at house style** (`preproc_if` as an unnamed child of
`class_declaration`, following the `preproc_if_in_attribute_list` precedent) —
no corpus test exercises that variant, so please redirect it if you'd shape the
node differently.

**`#if`-controlled braces inside a method body**

`preproc_if_in_top_level` content is `choice($._top_level_item_no_statement,
$.statement)`, and a lone `{` or `}` is neither. **This one is not fully
fixable**: the `{` sits in one `#if…#endif` region and its `}` in another, so a
node pairing them would have to overlap the two `preproc_if` nodes. The
expectation records the best a tree can represent — no ERROR, with the
conditional scope simply unmodelled — reachable only by letting `preproc_if`
content accept a bare brace. Include it or drop it as you prefer; it's a
limitation record more than a bug.

## Notes for anyone picking these up

- The `*`/lvalue and ref-return fixes both widen exactly the machinery #430
  narrowed to make `(a) && (b > 0)` parse correctly, so re-run the
  *Logical AND vs cast disambiguation* test and the `examples/**` sweep after
  either.
- This grammar has an external scanner, so use `tree-sitter test -r`. Without
  the forced rebuild a stale compiled artifact can invent failures — it cost me
  a wrong diagnosis while writing this up.

## Summary

- Removed the app's dark theme entirely (`ThemeProvider`/`useTheme`, the theme-toggle button, dead `AppLayout.tsx`, and all `dark:` Tailwind classes) per explicit request to keep the UI light-only.
- Root cause of "dashboard shows nothing": Tailwind v4 defaults the `dark:` variant to the OS `prefers-color-scheme` media query unless `@custom-variant dark` is explicitly configured — this project never configured it, so the app's own JS `.dark` class toggle had no effect on Tailwind utilities. `.card`'s `dark:bg-gray-800` could activate purely from OS dark mode while `KpiCard`'s hardcoded `text-gray-800` had no dark variant, making the dashboard numbers invisible (dark text on dark background).
- While live-testing the dashboard fix, found and fixed a second, unrelated bug: a hard page refresh (or opening the PWA on a direct deep link) permanently bounced authenticated users back to `/login` despite a valid saved token. Auth state was restored from `localStorage` inside a `useEffect` that runs *after* `ProtectedRoute`'s first render, so it already committed to `<Navigate to="/login">` before the session was restored — and the login page never re-checks `isAuthenticated` afterward to send the user back. Fixed by loading the saved session synchronously at auth-store creation time instead of via a post-render `hydrate()` effect.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc -b` — no errors
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 19/19 tests pass
- [x] Live-tested locally (backend + Postgres via `backend/docker-compose.yml`, frontend via `vite dev`, Playwright): logged in as admin, opened `/dashboard` — KPI cards and per-district table now render correctly.
- [x] Live-tested with `prefers-color-scheme: dark` emulated + hard page reload on `/dashboard` — page stays light, data stays visible, and (post auth-store fix) the user is no longer bounced back to `/login`.

author: aatchison
body:
Closes #110

Stacked on feat/r9-109-add-a-devonly-packagejson.

## What changed
- **CI workflow** running `npm ci && npm test` on `push` / `pull_request` to `main`, on `ubuntu-latest`, Node 20 with `cache: npm`. Steps: `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`, `npm ci`, `npm test`.
- **Least privilege:** explicit `permissions: contents: read` — default read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, no secrets, no deploy, no write scopes.
- **README `Development / CI` note:** the site stays zero-build, the `package.json`/`node_modules` tests are dev-only, and the workflow must be enabled by a maintainer with `workflow` scope (this commit only *proposes* the file).

## Scope caveat (why not `.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
The automation token that opened this PR lacks GitHub's `workflow` scope, and GitHub **rejects any push that adds a file under `.github/workflows/`** without it (verified: the initial push was `remote rejected`). The issue anticipated exactly this ("committed for a human to enable rather than pushed live"). So the ready-to-run file ships at **`.github/workflows-proposed/ci.yml`** — identical content, only the path differs. A maintainer with `workflow` scope enables it:

```bash
git mv .github/workflows-proposed/ci.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "ci: enable workflow" && git push
```

## Verification
- `npm test` passes locally: 6/6 (SAMPLES manifest + 5 sample parses through the app's real `buildGroupFromOcctResult` path).
- Workflow parsed as valid YAML (`yaml.safe_load`); confirmed triggers `push`/`pull_request`, `permissions.contents: read`, `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, and the four expected steps.
- No regression to viewer features — this change touches only CI config + README.

author: sinelaw
body:
Reviewed the flaky e2e tests listed below against `CONTRIBUTING.md` and fixed what didn't follow it. Every failure traces to one of three shared mechanisms rather than to the features under test.

## The three mechanisms

**1. `harness.sleep()` waits zero real time.** It is `advance_time()` — logical time only, as its own doc comment warns. Every `for _ in 0..N { …; harness.sleep(50ms) }` "let it settle" block waited nothing at all, so what followed sampled an arbitrary mid-async frame. Worst case is `test_git_gutter_refreshes_after_external_git_checkout`, where the sleep existed *specifically* to separate the reset's mtime from the opened file's, and so left the hazard it was written to prevent fully live.

**2. `drain_async_work` had a hidden ~200 ms timeout** (`tests/common/harness.rs`), sitting behind every `send_key`/`type_text`, giving up with only a `tracing::warn!` that CI never renders. On a loaded runner a slower plugin action left the drain early and silently, and the next assertion read a stale screen — a timeout inside a test (Testing §3) whose failure mode carries no diagnostic.

**3. Quick Open re-filters on input change only** (`app/prompt_lifecycle.rs::update_quick_open_suggestions`), never on a render or a tick. "Type the name, press Enter" therefore fires on whatever row was selected when the last keystroke landed; and for a plugin-registered command that hasn't finished `registerCommand`, the row cannot appear at all — a later wait for it then blocks until nextest kills the test at 180 s with no failed assertion. This is the remaining explanation for the `code_tour_dock` timeouts on both ubuntu and windows: that module already waited for the filtered row, which fixes the wrong-row half but not the late-registration half, since nothing re-runs the filter.

## Changes

- **Harness**: wait out in-flight plugin actions against a budget no real action can miss, and report giving up on stderr — the one channel nextest surfaces for a failed or killed test. Still bounded, so a plugin callback that never returns can't deadlock every later keypress; bridge quiescence keeps its own short bound because PTY output and timer-driven polls are legitimately continuous. New `run_palette_command` / `wait_for_palette_command` wait for a command to be listed as a *result* rather than as the echoed query, retyping to re-run the filter so a late registration is picked up.
- **`GitTestRepo`**: new `touch_until_mtime_after` bumps a file until its observed mtime actually moves past a floor — semantic waiting on the real condition instead of sleeping past a filesystem's granularity.
- **Tests**: replaced fake-time settle loops and fixed-count `tick_and_render` pumps with waits on the invariant each test is actually about; routed palette invocations through the new helper; waited for LSP readiness before triggering a `didSave`-driven publish (Code §3); promoted two checks that asserted nothing (Code §16) into real gates; stopped deriving an expected value out of model state (Testing §2); and moved the remote-FS fixture out of the real `$HOME` into the tempdir that was already being created but never used (Testing §4).

## Per-test

| Test | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `locale::test_locale_switch_via_command_palette` | palette race; assertions sampled off one frame | `run_palette_command`; waits |
| `locale::test_multiple_locales_can_be_loaded` | — | unchanged; see caveat below |
| `plugins::plugin::test_diagnostics_api_with_fake_lsp` | fake 1 s LSP warm-up, save raced init → no publish → 180 s hang; hook check asserted nothing | waits for plugin load, then server ready, then the rendered `E:1` |
| `remote_fs_test::test_remote_file_explorer_anchored_at_working_dir` | fixture in the real `$HOME`; wait matched `"root"`/`"runner"` anywhere on screen | tempdir; wait anchored to explorer tree rows |
| `terminal::test_terminal_tab_title_follows_foreground_process` | `for _ in 0..2000` spin with no sleep, then `expect`; expected value read from the model | `wait_until` on the tab bar vs `detect_shell()` |
| `code_tour_dock::{test_next_key_advances_step, test_step_range_is_highlighted_in_the_editor}` | already well-written; missing plugin-registration precondition | `run_palette_command` |
| `plugins::gutter::test_git_gutter_updates_after_save` | fake-time settle, then a baseline sampled off an arbitrary frame; `count > initial` could be unsatisfiable → hang | `wait_for_async_quiescence`, assert the settled baseline is zero, then wait for the added line's green indicator |
| `plugins::gutter::test_git_gutter_refreshes_after_external_git_checkout` | `harness.sleep(2100ms)` for mtime separation waited no real time | `touch_until_mtime_after` |
| `plugins::live_diff::test_live_diff_virtual_line_anchored_to_correct_modified_line` | palette race enabling live-diff | `run_palette_command` |
| `plugins::review_diff_ux_bugs::test_issue2117_discard_hunk_with_no_trailing_newline` | read the file back microseconds after `d`, before git had applied the patch | waits for the restored content or a rendered patch error |

## Three regressions the first CI run caught, since fixed

Worth recording, because two of them are the same mistake this PR is about — asserting on something unverified.

- **The gutter settle loop was load-bearing**, though not for the reason its comment gave: the plugin establishes its HEAD baseline asynchronously on open, and editing before that lands leaves it without one, after which the save produces no indicators at all. Removing it wholesale hung the test on every platform. Restored as `wait_for_async_quiescence` — which is what the loop's `process_async_and_render` calls were approximating. (Bisect: master's version of the test passes against this branch's harness; this branch's version hung.)
- **The status bar elides elements that don't fit the terminal width.** At the diagnostics test's 100 columns, `Diagnostics received: 1 total, URI count: 1` renders as `Diagnostics ...`, so waiting for the full string could never resolve. Now waits for `E:1`, the layout-stable rendering of the same fact.
- **Canonicalizing `GitTestRepo`'s path broke Windows.** `fs::canonicalize` returns an extended-length `\\?\D:\...` path there, which git does not accept, and `plugins::package_manager` uses a repo path as a git remote. Dropped entirely rather than made conditional: it targeted a macOS `live_diff` failure I never reproduced, and the bisect showed it fixed nothing here.

## Caveats

- `test_multiple_locales_can_be_loaded` is the one case I could not pin down. Its search-option labels render synchronously in `view/`, so the immediate assert is mostly safe, and the process-global locale race documented in `harness.rs` cannot fire under nextest (process per test) — it is real for local `cargo test` only. Its remaining exposure is that it builds nine harnesses in one test. Left as is rather than changed on a guess.
- The global-locale `TODO(flakiness)` in `harness.rs` is untouched for the same reason: it is a `cargo test` problem, not a CI one.
- Other tests in `gutter.rs` still use `harness.sleep` in the same way. Out of scope here; they are the same defect and worth a follow-up.
- Verified locally, serially (to emulate nextest's process-per-test, since several of these mutate process cwd): gutter 22, live_diff 14, plugin 12, package_manager 9, review_diff 3, locale 15, code_tour_dock 33, remote_fs 4, and the terminal title test — all pass. `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` clean, with a warning count identical to master.

author: dlgpdmsly2
body:
`meta.json` records how big a frozen change is (`additions` / `deletions` / `scope`) and which paths it touched (`changed_files`). Neither says **how spread out** it is, and that is not recoverable later: a path list can count files but carries no hunk counts, so `single_hunk` cannot be reconstructed by any reader afterwards. A 400-line change in one file and a 400-line change across nine modules are different review problems at identical `scope`.

The rule already exists and is already the pipeline's own — `localizationFromDiff` in `classify.mjs`: pure, exported, no model, no network, no I/O. It is imported, not reimplemented, following the `scopeSize` precedent one line above it, and it is applied to the **frozen** diff for the same reason `additions` is — the merged PR's file list spans whatever the post-review fix loop touched.

It lands before the pilot corpus is frozen because a corpus item is write-once **and** because the omission would be invisible. `corpusItemDrift` compares a fixed field list, so a field outside it cannot drift: adding this later and re-extracting would print `= unchanged`, re-index `manifestItem(stored.meta)` — spreading the absence into the manifest as a key `JSON.stringify` drops — and never rewrite.

So the field joins `corpusItemDrift`, and the reason generalises: **the diff bytes prove the input is stable and say nothing about the derivation.** Edit `localizationFromDiff` (it lives in `classify.mjs`, maintained for the labelling pipeline) and a re-extraction yields a different value from identical bytes — the diff matches, the hash matches, only the meaning moved. The same entry makes an item frozen *before* the field existed drift rather than re-index silently. The rule, stated in the code and the README: a derived field joins the drift list in the commit that adds it. `additions`/`deletions`/`scope` are the same class and are not there yet — named as a gap, not left to read as a distinction.

`manifestItem` carries it beside `scope`, since "small single-hunk items against small cross-module ones" is one query answerable off the manifest. The `+` log line prints it, which is what `--dry-run` shows.

## The spread rule was miscounting deletions (second commit, after review)

`localizationFromDiff` read only `+++ b/<path>` lines. A deletion's `+++` line says `/dev/null` and a pure rename has no `+++` line at all, so neither named its file. A deletion-only diff therefore answered `unknown` — and, worse, one modified file plus one deletion in another module answered **`single_file`**, because the deleted file's `@@` was counted while the file was not. Two modules recorded as one file, on a write-once item.

It now reads the `diff --git a/… b/<path>` header too, which is where `changedFilesFromDiff` has always taken a deletion's path from. Adding it unconditionally is safe — for an ordinary modification it names the same path the `+++` line does, and `files` is a `Set`, which is also why renames were never double-counted (checked; asserted in both test files). Editing `classify.mjs` was a non-goal of the first commit on the grounds that the labelling pipeline owns the helper; the helper was miscounting for both consumers, so that is reversed and recorded in the task doc.

Over the **same** 20 PRs as the measurement below, the distribution is unchanged at 18/2 — this corrects no item in that sample, and matters for populations that delete files.

## Verification

`cd scripts/agent && node --test '**/*.test.mjs'` from the committed tree, no `node_modules` anywhere: **1297 tests, 1291 pass, 0 fail, 6 skipped**, against **1294 / 1288 / 0 / 6** on this branch before the deletion fix. `npx eslint scripts` (`eslint@9.24.0`): exit 0. Both deletion tests mutation-tested: removing the header fallback fails 3 tests with `actual: 'unknown', expected: 'cross_module'` and `actual: 'single_file', expected: 'cross_module'`.

A test per return value, all five, driven through `buildItemMeta` rather than the helper (which `classify.test.mjs` already covers). Three mutations, each failing: drop the field → 8 failures; hard-code `"single_hunk"` → 3; derive from `view.files` → 7, `actual: 'cross_module', expected: 'single_hunk'`.

`--dry-run` against real PRs, nothing written:

```text
  + pr-664 (4 files, +418/-1 L, cross_module, issue_spec=false, @pr-open 61101a1b, fork-point)
  + pr-683 (3 files, +133/-2 M, cross_module, issue_spec=false, @pr-open d0c7290f, fork-point)
```

## What is left open, and one number worth knowing

A diff whose paths git C-quoted (`+++ "b/na\303\257ve.ts"`) is the one remaining cause of `unknown`, and the one case where `changed_files` can be populated while this field is not: the C-unquoter is private to `extract-corpus.mjs`, and copying it into `classify.mjs` would fork the very path parser whose divergence caused the deletion bug above. Pinned by a test and stated in the `localization_scope` README row.

And the axis is nearly constant on this repository. Over the 20 most recent merged PRs at `--review-point pr-open`: **18 `cross_module`, 2 `multi_file`, 0 `single_hunk`, 0 `single_file`, 0 `unknown`** (n=20). House convention puts a task doc under `docs/` in every PR, so almost every change crosses a module boundary by construction. The field is worth freezing — it is free and the item is write-once — but it will not separate this population until the rule discounts documentation-only paths.

author: drswith
body:
## Summary

`release-workflow` says a prerelease is cut by declaring `Release-As: <version>` with a prerelease suffix. **It is not.** Merging #517 with `Release-As: 1.8.7-beta.1` on the commit produced a Release PR for stable **1.8.7**.

release-please emits prerelease versions only when its config declares them — the retired `release-please-config.beta.json` carried `versioning: prerelease`, `prerelease: true`, `prerelease-type: beta`, which is why the old branch could produce `-beta` at all. `release-please-config.json` carries none, so the suffix is normalized away.

### Why the requirement passed review

`release:dry-run` was run and reported green. It exercises the build and staging chain, and it *did* confirm the publish side derives the `beta` dist-tag from a prerelease version. It never touches release-please's version computation — the half that had to work. One half was verified, the other assumed, and the assumption went into a contract.

### Why the channel goes rather than getting a third mechanism

| | count |
| --- | ---: |
| published versions | 102 |
| prereleases | 12 |
| prereleases before 1.0 | 11 |
| **prereleases in the entire 1.x line** | **1** |

That one is `1.8.2-beta` — published 2026-08-04, abandoned immediately, and the origin of the `@beta`-older-than-`@latest` inversion this workstream has spent three iterations chasing. Nothing demonstrates a need for the feature.

So: no replacement mechanism. `main` is the only release line and publishes to `latest`.

### What is deliberately kept

The version-to-dist-tag derivation in `release-seal-contract.ts` stays, restated as a **fail-safe** rather than a feature: if a prerelease-suffixed version ever reaches publication it goes to `beta`, never `latest`. It is written into the spec so a future reader does not delete it as unreachable code.

## Linked Artifacts

- OpenSpec: `retire-prerelease-channel`

## Validation

- [x] `bun run memory:check`
- [x] `bun run lint`
- [x] `bun run format:check`
- [x] `bun run typecheck`
- [x] `bun run test` (165 files, 2001 passed, 2 skipped)
- [x] `bun run openspec:validate` (19 passed)

## Release Intent

- Release: not applicable - release contract and documentation only; no code changes

## Release Summary

- Not applicable - this source PR does not produce a release entry.
- For a release-worthy source PR, replace this with a non-empty release-please commit override written for users.
- For a one-shot release, also declare the same `Release-As: <version>` footer that the merged commit carries.

## Docs Updated

- [x] `docs/releases.md` — the `Prereleases` section is gone
- [x] `docs/sessions/2026-08-05-project-structure-audit.md` — its open P0 recorded the model that was just disproved; closed with what actually happened
- [x] `openspec/changes/retire-prerelease-channel/` — proposal, tasks, delta

## Scope Check

- [x] I did not add a new ad hoc root-level Markdown file.
- [x] I updated the relevant issue, ADR, spec, runbook, or captured the missing doc work as follow-up.
- [x] I did not silently expand project scope without recording it explicitly.

## Closure Check

- [x] Working tree was clean after commit.
- [x] Branch was pushed and this PR is the active delivery artifact.
- [x] OpenSpec change is not needed, still active until this merge, active across milestone merges by design, queued for agent-driven archive closure after completion, or already archived.
- [x] Release is not applicable, delegated to release automation, or verified.

## Notes

`openspec/specs/` is deliberately untouched. The removal lives in the delta and applies during archive closure — applying it here as well is what made an earlier archive abort on a header that was already gone.

**Maintainer action this PR cannot perform**: the npm `beta` dist-tag still points at `1.8.2-beta`, and `latest` is now `1.8.7`, so the gap is currently at its widest. Removing the tag is registry state and needs publish credentials:

```
npm dist-tag rm quantex-cli beta
```

This is the third design in this area, and the first one validated against release-please's real behaviour rather than reasoned about. The correction is a subtraction, not another mechanism.

author: ako
body:
Follow-up work since PR #4 merged. 13 commits, rebased onto current `main`.

## App changes

**Mendix 11.13.0** (`mx convert --in-place`, run with the target version's toolset). Unlike `update-widgets` and `module-import`, `convert` preserves the MPR v2 layout — 409 `mprcontents` units before and after, 0 errors. Verified on a throwaway copy first: it built, booted on the 11.13.0 runtime, and played a full workload with zero server-side errors, then re-confirmed against the live app.

`scripts/setup-tools.sh` now reads the Mendix version from the project (`_MetaData._ProductVersion` in the `.mpr`, which is SQLite) instead of pinning it. The hardcoded constant would have gone stale the moment this conversion landed, leaving the hook pre-caching a version nothing uses.

**Layout fix — the page no longer resizes when you select a square.** Reported with screenshots: the page was 842px wide with an empty square selected and 1103px with a dealt one, and the number pad stretched from 264px to 525px with it. `.sd-app` resolves its width from content (it's a flex item under Atlas's placeholder, so its 1180px `max-width` never binds), which left `.sd-rail { flex: 1 }` sized by whichever child had the widest max-content — normally the pad, but the lock note is one 489px sentence. The rail now has a definite width so long copy wraps. Measured after: 842px page and 264px rail in all three states, no horizontal overflow at 1440/1000/700, stacked layout unchanged.

**`ACT_MarkPeers` takes the square list as a parameter** instead of re-retrieving it. Measured on a real game, before → after (p50): `ACT_MarkPeers` 8.55ms/3 queries → 3.62ms/2, `ACT_Refresh` 15.41 → 11.29, a move (`ACT_ApplyValue`) 27.28 → 22.53. `ACT_SelectCell` flat as predicted, `ACT_LogMove` untouched as a control.

**Pages re-authored** with mxcli's widget-augmentation fixes, which emit required widget properties that were previously missing (`AllowUpload` on 33 widgets) and drop a stray container. Verified equivalent, not merely smaller: all 34 conditional-visibility settings preserved, all 68 text items byte-identical.

`theme-cache/` is no longer tracked — it's mxbuild output, verified regenerable by deleting it outright and rebuilding.

## Findings 32–38

The main deliverable. Several were filed against mxcli builds and have since been fixed and re-verified here:

| | |
|---|---|
| **32** | Upgrading a widget package on MPR v2 costs you the v2 layout |
| **33** | `Client: Script error.` on every interaction — 1:1 with `ACT_MarkPeers` across four games and two mxcli builds; server clean, cause unreachable from a container |
| **34** | The container suspends when the session idles, taking the app with it |
| **35** | What tracing is good for — including a correction of an earlier claim of mine |
| **36** | `get_log_settings` throws instead of answering |
| **37** | No way to update an installed marketplace module (widget-type items are fine; modules are not) |
| **38** | `mxcli widget sync` reaches further but corrupted the project — **fixed in `3d253189`, verified here** |

Finding 38's fix was verified against the same fixture: 2160 distinct GUIDs across 2223 objects with 9 duplicated becomes 2223 distinct with none, and `mx update-widgets` afterwards saves cleanly instead of leaving the project unloadable.

Finding 35 corrects something I got wrong earlier in this project: I reported the 81-cell list as "retrieved twice per interaction, 1.79s, the app's largest cost". Those spans' parent is `POST /*` — they're the client's board refetch, never inside the microflow. Grouping spans by name reads like a profile and isn't one.

author: meltface-80
body:
Six albums a day by artists NOT in the library: five "adjacent", drawn from the corner of music the library already lives in, and one deliberate "stretch" from a genre it barely touches. Ported from the MusicD Remote Roon extension v1.7.43 and adapted where LMS forces a different shape.

The idea that makes it work: similarity quality INVERTS with seed popularity. Seeding from a library's biggest names returns Nirvana and Coldplay; seeding from its obscure end returns real finds. So seeds are the library's least famous well-played artists, "famous" is decided by the world listen chart, and if that chart can't be fetched the whole build aborts rather than invert.

New modules
- lib/smartpickalgo.js  the choosing, as pure functions (like radioDecision)
- lib/discovery.js      three keyless public reads — ListenBrainz similar
                        artists + world chart, MusicBrainz tag roster
- lib/smartpicks.js     the JSON store (picks, seen, blocks, attempts)
- lib/smartcache.js     TTL cache; a MISS is cached, because "nothing findable"
                        is the expensive answer

Forced by LMS, and different from the Roon build
- A pick cannot carry an addable handle: the LMS Qobuz plugin exposes no album ids, only menu nodes that expire with the session. Add re-resolves by search at the moment it is tapped, and the live favItemId is stripped before caching.
- Every qobuz dispatch is needs-client=1, so a build needs a connected player. With none it is skipped WITHOUT marking the day attempted, so it retries rather than writing the day off.
- Auto-add defaults OFF (ON in the Roon build). There it makes Roon import overnight; here favouriting is favourite-only, so it would write five albums a day into the owner's Qobuz account unasked and they still would not play until a scan.

Fixes found by the end-to-end run
- The Qobuz menu row's artist carries a trailing year ("Labradford (1997)"), so the identity check never matched and every resolve silently returned nothing.
- A screen taking over the album grid inherited the previous screen's content until its own fetch landed; enterFullWall now takes the grid empty.

Pre-existing defect this forced into the open
- Three independent MusicBrainz rate gates, and within each one the timestamp compare let concurrent callers read the same `last` and fire together (measured: four callers, all at 1103ms — a 4x breach of the one-per-second policy). lib/musicbrainz.js is now the one gate, serialising on a promise chain. Smart Picks is the heaviest consumer, which is what forced the fix.

Also: enterFullWall() factored out of the Not-played and Library walls.

Verified: npm test green (77 new unit assertions across four modules), and a 44-check end-to-end run against a fake LMS with a Qobuz plugin plus stub ListenBrainz and MusicBrainz servers, so the whole build executes for real.

author: debalghosh
body:
#### Merge Checklist  <!-- REQUIRED -->

- [x] The changes in the PR have been built and tested
- [x] Documentation has been updated to reflect the changes (or no doc update needed)
- [x] Ready to merge

#### Description <!-- REQUIRED -->

ubuntu24 builds fail in pre-processing, while downloading image packages:

```
ERROR debutils/download.go:988  kernel version mismatch: requires kernel version "6.17",
                                but available versions are: [6.8.0-31.31 7.0.0-28.28~24.04.1]
```

Four default configs under `config/osv/ubuntu/ubuntu24/imageconfigs/defaultconfigs/`
pin `kernel.version: "6.17"` alongside the **rolling** metapackage
`linux-image-generic-hwe-24.04`, and Ubuntu noble no longer ships 6.17 — the HWE
series has rolled past it. `archive.ubuntu.com` currently offers, for that
metapackage:

| Pocket | Version |
|---|---|
| `noble` (GA) | `6.8.0-31.31` |
| `noble-updates` | `7.0.0-28.28~24.04.1` |

which is the error message verbatim.

##### Templates that look clean still fail

A template inherits the default's `kernel` block whenever it does not set
`kernel.version` itself, so the stale pin reaches templates that were already fixed:

| Reproducer | Where the 6.17 comes from |
|---|---|
| `ubuntu24-x86_64-minimal-initrd.yml` | declares **no** `kernel` block → `default-initrd-x86_64.yml` |
| `ubuntu24-x86_64-dkms-demo.yml` | declares a `kernel` block with **no** `version` → `default-raw-x86_64.yml` |
| `default-initrd-x86_64.yml` | built directly |

##### Which CI workflows this repairs

Resolving every ubuntu24 template that a build workflow exercises shows **five**
inheriting the stale pin — so the blast radius is wider than the reported
reproducers:

| Workflow | Template | `kernel.version` before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build-ubuntu24-immutable` | `ubuntu24-x86_64-edge-raw.yml` | `6.17` | `''` |
| `build-ubuntu24-raw` | `ubuntu24-x86_64-minimal-raw.yml` | `6.17` | `''` |
| `build-ubuntu24-arm-raw` | `ubuntu24-aarch64-minimal-raw.yml` | `6.17` | `''` |
| *(not CI-built)* | `ubuntu24-x86_64-minimal-initrd.yml` | `6.17` | `''` |
| *(not CI-built)* | `ubuntu24-x86_64-dkms-demo.yml` | `6.17` | `''` |
| *(not CI-built)* | `robotics-demo-ubuntu24-x86_64.yml` | `6.17` | `''` |

**This means the long-standing `build-ubuntu24-immutable` failure on `main` is this
bug**, reached through `edge-raw` → `default-raw-x86_64.yml` — not an unrelated
breakage as it has been assumed to be. This PR should turn that job green, which is
useful independent confirmation of the fix.

Not affected: `build-ubuntu24-iso` and `build-ubuntu24-unattended-iso` already
resolve to no pin, and `build-ubuntu24-dlstreamer` pins a *concrete* kernel package
(`linux-image-6.12-intel`), which is legitimate and untouched.

##### Relation to #765

**#765 removed exactly this antipattern from the 12 affected user templates but never
touched the OS defaults.** That is the whole of this bug, and the reason the failure
returned for a fourth time after #494 (6.14→6.17), #669 (6.17→7.0) and #761
(6.17→6.8). #765's own description lists `ubuntu24-x86_64-dkms-demo.yml` as fixed —
it was, at the template layer only.

`image-templates/robotics-demo-ubuntu24-x86_64.yml` was also missed by #765 and
carries the same `6.17` + rolling-metapackage pairing, so it is fixed here too.

#### The fix

Drop the `version:` line; keep the metapackage. `KernelVersion == ""` makes
`matchesKernelVersion` short-circuit (`internal/ospackage/debutils/resolver.go:1392-1395`)
and skips the mismatch guard (`internal/ospackage/debutils/download.go:1019`), so
`apt` resolves whatever the metapackage currently points to. No pin, nothing to go
stale.

**Deliberately no replacement version.** Substituting a new number is what produced
the previous three iterations of this fix. Templates that pin a *concrete* kernel
package (`linux-image-6.11.0-17-generic`, `linux-image-6.12-intel`,
`linux-image-6.18-intel`) genuinely mean it and are unaffected.

5 files, 5 deleted lines, plus one release note.

#### Still carrying the same pattern, left out of scope

Both resolve against today's archive, so neither is failing — but both are one roll
from the identical break, and are worth a follow-up:

- The three ubuntu26 defaults (`default-raw-x86_64.yml`, `default-raw-aarch64.yml`,
  `default-initrd-x86_64.yml`) pin `7.0` with rolling `linux-image-generic`.
- `image-templates/ubuntu24-x86_64-fde-raw.yml` pins `6.8.0-31.31` with the rolling
  HWE metapackage.

#### Any Newly Introduced Dependencies

None.

#### How Has This Been Tested? <!-- REQUIRED -->

Built, not just resolved:

```
sudo -E ./image-composer-tool build image-templates/ubuntu24-x86_64-minimal-initrd.yml
  -> minimal-os-image-ubuntu-24.04.img, 1m58s
  -> grep -c "kernel version mismatch" == 0
```

All six affected templates now resolve with an empty `kernel.version` and their
metapackage lists unchanged.

`go build ./cmd/... ./internal/...` clean, and `validate` over every template passes
except the pre-existing `ubuntu24-x86_64-fde-raw.yml`, whose `fde.passphraseFile`
points at a nonexistent `/home/user/test-fde.txt` (unrelated to this change).

> This fix was previously folded into the template-reorg PR #796 (and before that
> stood alone as #802). It is re-isolated here because it is an urgent
> build-blocking fix that should not wait on a larger refactor. The duplicate commit
> has been removed from #796.
