body:
## Executive summary

This change binds scheduler-trace evidence to the exact firmware executable, running image,
registered NFF, candidate file, and stable transport endpoint. It also removes a redundant 16 KiB
trace merge buffer so the restored default image passes health and complete self-test checks.

## Review status

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Exact reviewed head | `2d136ac4cc9aec40e60cf6c0fe2fdcd6fb278f0f` |
| Required Software CI | All 8 checks passed in [run 31934882896](https://github.com/pcesar22/domes/actions/runs/31934882896) |
| Independent judge | Approved all 10 acceptance criteria; no rework required |
| Registered-NFF trace | 74 events; zero drops/discontinuities; complete causal chain |
| Measured command overhead | 155 us disabled / 238 us enabled for 32 records |
| Default restoration | Exact-head default image restored; two boots passed health and self-test 10/10 with tracing disabled and empty |
| Merge authority | Human only; the controller did not approve or merge |

## What changed

- Adds device-reported firmware version, executable hash, running-image hash, and hardware identity
  to retained trace sessions.
- Verifies that a supplied firmware candidate exactly matches the running device before binding it
  as evidence.
- Records the stable transport endpoint without publishing raw device identifiers.
- Replaces the redundant merge scratch with a bounded, order-preserving in-place merge.
- Reconciles the execution plan and program ledger with the exact reviewed candidate and evidence.

## Retained evidence

- Raw trace SHA-256: `1a959146680b820c936a56c8882c6838ca549e6894c18eff172c0abbcbedcaee`
- Session SHA-256: `fa31c3c4ac8dbec471bd5efaa159d9c3bbbdfa282f95c68683c90d4d300b07c3`
- Normalized SHA-256: `f2f6e83e59b4fa50329fb80bc1466e540c262e448a08838e2e9350984252957f`

The controller-attested trace is bound to the exact reviewed head and registered hardware. Detailed
schema-validated worker and judge handoffs are retained on issue #101; raw role transcripts are

## Claim boundary

Approval establishes exact-head software CI, deterministic QEMU trace behavior, registered-NFF
trace capture, device/image identity binding, measured command-visible overhead, and two-boot

author: elithrar
body:
## Summary

- replace the OpenCode GitHub Actions harness with Pi in non-interactive JSON mode
- organize Bonk around explicit Prepare → Run Pi → Finalize ownership
- give Pi authoritative run metadata through the system-prompt channel and only the triggering request as the user message
- make Pi emit one structured answer, review, or change result through a single Bonk-owned `submit_result` extension
- keep GitHub comments, reviews, commits, pushes, and pull request creation in trusted Finalize code
- update prompts, workflow templates, Worker setup compatibility, tests, AGENTS guidance, and README documentation

## Prepare → Pi → Finalize

- **Prepare** validates the actor and event, resolves the authoritative target, serializes trusted execution metadata, tracks runnable non-fork requests before token exchange, independently obtains a short-lived App token, checks out the exact PR head/default branch, removes checkout credentials, and snapshots repository-local Git control state
- **Run Pi** removes GitHub, OIDC, runner-command, SSH, and Git-control variables before the supervisor starts; the supervisor filters again, loads repository instructions, `.pi/skills`, `.agents/skills/**/SKILL.md`, and the selected `agent:` prompt, then emits only a structured result
- **Finalize** validates the structured result, worktree, and prepared Git control state first; it then independently obtains a fresh App token, revalidates the boundary, batches inline findings, publishes an idempotent top-level response, and owns commit/push/PR lifecycle

The composite action still shares one GitHub Actions runner. These controls minimize credential exposure and constrain trusted side effects; they are not a general-purpose process or filesystem sandbox.

## Prompt and extension discipline

- pass versioned, JSON-serialized execution metadata through Pi's system-prompt channel
- pass only the triggering comment/task through the user-message channel
- append repository-selected agent guidance before Bonk's final authoritative contract
- keep exactly one explicit extension, `github/extensions/bonk-result.ts`, with one `submit_result` tool
- keep that extension independent of GitHub clients, OIDC, publication code, prompt frameworks, and a repository dependency on Pi
- disable repository-controlled extensions, prompt templates, and themes
- remove the direct cross-repository credential wrapper

## Security and failure behavior

- never persist an App installation token in a step output, Git remote, or across the Pi stage
- exchange separate short-lived tokens in trusted Prepare and Finalize stages
- remove all repository-local HTTP authorization headers, credential helpers, and push URLs before Pi
- use an explicit validated repository URL for authenticated pushes
- reject any Pi mutation to repository-local Git control state before issuing publication credentials
- force forks and `NO_PUSH` runs to read-only contents permission
- reject review-only worktree changes, unexpected answer/review changes, and Pi changes to the prepared HEAD/branch
- disable Git hooks and keep Finalize credentials out of Git subprocess environments
- track non-fork runs before App-token exchange so infrastructure failures retain reaction and in-thread failure feedback
- preserve Worker polling and `workflow_run.completed` as failure-feedback safety nets
- avoid retrying ambiguous GitHub POST mutations

## Compatibility

- preserve every v1 Action input
- retain `opencode_version` and `opencode_dev` as accepted, ignored inputs
- preserve OpenCode Zen model identifiers and `OPENCODE_API_KEY`
- preserve `.agents/skills/**/SKILL.md` and `.pi/skills` loading
- preserve `agent:` resolution from `.pi/agents`, `.agents/agents`, legacy `.opencode/agents`, and bundled agents
- recognize the OIDC-verified calling workflow path, including `bonk.yml`, `bonk.yaml`, and custom workflow filenames
- keep fork review behavior fail-closed and review workflows explicitly `token_permissions: NO_PUSH`
- intentionally stop loading OpenCode configuration, plugins, and provider definitions for Bonk v2

## Review contract carried forward from #217

- keep workflow prompts narrow and free of direct PR title/body interpolation
- distinguish authoritative execution context from untrusted task/evidence text
- publish all actionable inline findings in one empty-body `COMMENT` review
- keep the top-level result nonduplicative and update it by run marker on reruns

## Validation

- `bun run lint`
- Worker and Action TypeScript checks
- full test suite — 5 files, 208 tests
- focused Action, prompt, and compatibility suites
- YAML parsing for the composite action and repository workflows
- Pi 0.83.0 version and explicit multi-system-prompt/extension-load smoke test
- `bun run build`
- `wrangler types --check`
- generated Worker configuration dry-run deploy
- final diff, credential-flow, fork/no-push, failure-feedback, compatibility, and extension-containment review

author: larspohlmann
body:
Closes #292

## The bug

An entry whose title or summary carries a long string with no whitespace in it
— a compound noun, a base64 id, a bare URL — was not wrapped. The CSS initial
value `overflow-wrap: normal` forbids breaking inside a word, so the token
stayed one line box: on a narrow column it painted out of its card and off the
right edge of the window, on a wide one it was clipped through the middle of
the word. The same held in the open article.

Measured on the running stack with the app's own API stubbed, before the fix:

| surface | viewport | before |
|---|---|---|
| list row | 375×812 | title escaped by 341 px, snippet clipped by 688 px |
| list row | 1280×900 | title clipped by 266 px, snippet clipped by 688 px |
| magazine | 375×812 | title escaped by 341 px, dek escaped by 661 px |
| magazine | 1280×900 | dek escaped by 174 px |
| article | 375×812 | headline clipped by 552 px, body by 1032 px, a bare link escaped by 1016 px |
| article | 1280×900 | link escaped by 671 px |

## The fix

`overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `body`, inherited everywhere
(`frontend/src/styles/_base.scss`). One rule fixes the list rows, every
magazine block, the open article, its contents list and the add-feed dialog
alike.

Not a third per-component copy: `add-feed-dialog` and `entry-compact` had each
already patched themselves and every other surface had not. Both local copies
are deleted here.

`anywhere` rather than `break-word` because only `anywhere` also lowers the
element's min-content width, so the same token cannot force a flex or grid
ancestor wide either. A surface that must hold one line already opts out with
`white-space: nowrap`, where `overflow-wrap` is inert — which is why the kicker
line and the sidebar rows keep truncating exactly as before.

`docs/design-language.md` records the rule under Type, with the instruction not
to repeat it in a component.

## Verification

New `frontend/e2e/unbreakable-word.spec.ts` — one guard for one rule, six
cases: the list and the magazine layout and the open article, each at 375 px
and 1280 px. The article fixture carries the shapes a feed body really arrives
in: an unbreakable heading, a base64 token in the copy, a bare URL, a code
block and a 12-column table.

It measures both halves of the symptom — a box wider than its column, and a box
whose content is wider than the box (the clipped-mid-word case a bounding-box
check misses). Deliberate exceptions are excluded and named: `white-space:
nowrap`, and the article's code and table scrollers, which hold their overflow
inside the column instead of pushing the page.

- All six cases fail with the rule removed, pass with it in place.
- Full Playwright suite: 58 passed — including `magazine-kicker-one-line` and
  `sidebar-tag-truncation`, the two specs that pin what must keep truncating.

## Description
This PR fixes real bugs found in the codebase:

- Fixed default sort: `.sort()` coerces elements to strings, so `[10, 9, 2]` sorts as `[10, 2, 9]`; numeric comparator sorts correctly.

author: danhnm1203
body:
Closes the last open item in #39.

## Why

Three templates now share one engine. That was the point of 0.3.0 — a fix to
the decode window lands once instead of three times. It also means a mistake in
`lib/` breaks all three at once, and the way it breaks is by silently emitting
nothing. The build exits 0. The page loads. It just does not work.

That already happened. The engine built its worker URL through an indirection
rather than the literal `new Worker(new URL(...))`; Vite traced nothing and
Astro shipped a page that could never decode off the main thread. Every test
passed. Next passed, because Turbopack traces it independently. A human opening
a browser is what caught it.

## What the gate does

Per template: scaffold it, run the real frame pipeline over a synthesised clip,
build it, then read the output for four files whose absence is silent.

| Artifact | What its absence looks like |
|---|---|
| decoder worker | decode moves to the main thread; a 404 worker hangs the page forever |
| engine stylesheet | every beat renders unstyled over the footage; the measured scrim does nothing |
| reduced-motion rules | a visitor who asked not to be moved loses the whole page |
| frame images | the engine renders a black canvas forever |

The worker is matched on `HTTP `, a string in its fetch error and nowhere else
in `lib/` or `templates/`. It survives minification — `createImageBitmap` and
`postMessage` do not identify a worker chunk, because the engine names both
itself. There's a test for that confusion specifically.

Reduced motion is its own artifact rather than a detail of the stylesheet,
because it is a separate promise: that block is not a degraded animation, it is
the entire page for someone who asked for it.

## Verification

I put the worker indirection back and ran it. Astro's output went from 9 files
to 8 and the gate failed with `the astro build emitted no decoder worker`. All
three templates pass on the current tree.

`mount.test.js` already guards that exact source shape, so this is defence in
depth, not a duplicate — the source test catches that one regression, the gate
catches a missing worker whatever caused it, including a bundler changing its
own behaviour on upgrade.

## Placement

`ci/`, not `tests/`: it installs from the network and runs a bundler. The
offline suite runs in about a second and that is a constraint, not a preference.
`ci/` is outside `files` in package.json, with a test asserting it.

It also runs on release, gating the publish. `npm test` is not a publish gate
for a scaffolder — what ships is the project that comes out of it, and the last
two release-worthy bugs were both invisible to the suite and obvious the moment
a generated project was built.

368 tests green.

## Summary

- add `template/` as the canonical directly copyable, profile-aware Agent Skill template artifact
- preserve `template-scaffold`, all eight concrete profile tags, `instruction-only` exclusivity, and union-of-required-contracts composition
- add an exact `distribution-manifest.json` covering copied inventory, source mirrors, distribution-owned files, forbidden maintainer paths, and byte/mode preservation
- add positive and negative distribution validation for missing, undeclared, transformed, symlinked, and byte-drifted content
- distribute self-contained concrete-Skill validators and a minimal GitHub Actions workflow under `template/.github/`
- make the branch-root `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` describe the template-product source repository rather than an installable Skill
- validate `template/` as the canonical Skill root in structure, extended-profile, and portable-consumption workflows

## Base state

This pull request is based directly on `skill` commit `e2b7c512cbbb5e3de3050ecaf7c86206afb05fca`, the merge commit of PR #104.

GitHub Pages deployment remains suspended on `site` at merge commit `3cc8d4f830918781f8a225d2c555021abc20e85d`. This pull request does not restore Pages authority or change the `site` source lock.

## Copy contract

The supported copy operation is:

```sh
mkdir -p /path/to/new-skill
cp -a template/. /path/to/new-skill/
```

The destination becomes the Skill root and contains `SKILL.md` directly. Copying is byte-preserving and performs no placeholder substitution, profile selection, path renaming, runtime selection, or license selection.

## Artifact boundary

The complete branch remains the template-product source artifact. `template/` is the user-facing distribution. Canonical fixtures, negative fixtures, publication integration, source audits, review guidance, and template-maintainer workflows remain outside the distribution.

Concrete-Skill validators are included inside `template/.github/scripts/` because they operate independently from the copied Skill root. The distribution also includes a bounded CI workflow that runs the complete repository validator.

## Transitional scope

This pull request establishes a usable and validated distribution before removing the old root-level scaffold inputs. Existing root contract, resource, and validator files remain transitional byte-authoritative mirrors declared by `distribution-manifest.json`. Later Skill pull requests will migrate adoption and installation tests to copy `template/.` directly, separate source-maintainer tooling, and then remove obsolete root mirrors.

Public document IDs and current publication source paths are unchanged in this pull request. Site integration is deferred until the final reviewed Skill merge commit.

## Validation

At the current head:

- structure validation passes, including source/distribution classification, exact manifest validation, negative distribution tests, independent `template/` validation, template baseline checks, publication validation, and secret scanning
- the distribution contains 43 tracked files with 39 byte-preserving source mirrors
- all extended profile-contract and executable fixture jobs pass, including packaged CLI, MCP, CLI+MCP, browser, headless service, and systemd service evidence
- portable consumption passes on Ubuntu and macOS; Windows has passed canonical template validation, reduced layouts, adoption, completion hygiene, installation modes, vendoring, and non-mutating consumption and is completing the final space/Unicode path check

This pull request also triggers the build-only Skill-to-site documentation compatibility workflow. It has no Pages deployment job or Pages/OIDC write authority.

author: cyberantonz
body:
Part of #2198 (ADR-0003): the in-process integration rig moves off fakeidp onto a container-imported generated realm. fakeidp itself stays until the compose default flips — this is the prerequisite for that deletion, scoped so it does not touch any file #2253 rewrites.

## What changed

**The rig's IdP is now a real Keycloak.** `run-e2e.sh` boots one Keycloak 26.4 container (the image compose already pins) with `--import-realm`, importing the generated compose realm (`gen-realm.py`, dev user anchored at the suite's `E2E_USER`) plus a new e2e overlay, `tests/kc-realm-overlay.py`: dedicated per-suite test users, a 15 s access-token lifespan so the background refresher cycles in seconds, the client's back-channel logout registration (pointing at the authenticator on the docker host), and a user-less second realm as the host-keyed map's second issuer (user-less because Keycloak user ids are globally unique across realms).

**fakeidp's `/_control/*` hooks become real-IdP seams** (`tests/common/kc.rs`):
- login: the realm's actual login form, driven by the shared helper;
- back-channel logout: admin-API user logout — Keycloak fires a signed `logout_token` per session; the test polls both devices to 401 instead of trusting a synchronous `rp_status`;
- definitive `invalid_grant`: admin user disable — kills via the refresher path without the back-channel side-channel an admin logout would also fire;
- transient outage: `docker pause`/`unpause` — requests hang until the OIDC client's own 10 s timeout and fail as transport errors.

**`e2e_override` runs parallel again** (the re-fixture #2198's note asks for): each of the five tests owns a disjoint {impersonator + targets} user set, so one test's revoke-all can never reach a sibling's view-as session. No `--test-threads=1`.

**Person resolution keys on email** (`idp.external_id_claim=email`): the realm's `sub` is a Keycloak uuid, and the identity stub resolves logins and `__override` targets to the same person from the email alone — its fakeidp sub→email table is gone.

**Rig ports are env-overridable** (defaults unchanged, so CI is untouched): the historical defaults collide with a running compose stack (8083/8085/8093), and the overrides let the suite run beside one.

The workflow trigger drops the fakeidp path and gains the realm generator's (`deploy/compose/keycloak/**`, `deploy/seed/profiles.py`).

## Sequencing vs #2253

Zero file overlap. When #2253 lands, the only touch-point here is the one `gen-realm.py` invocation in `run-e2e.sh` (it becomes the seed package's installed entry point) plus the two workflow trigger paths above.

## Verification

- `run-e2e.sh` end to end on this branch: 10 suites, 18 tests, PASS — including the override suite 5/5 under default parallel execution, back-channel logout killing both devices via container→host delivery, and the refresher surviving a 12 s paused-container outage then dying on the disabled user's `invalid_grant`.
- Endpoint coverage gate on the produced ledger: 13/14 operations exercised, 0 missing (same BLOCKED profile as before).
- `cargo check` / `clippy` / `fmt` clean; suite also verified green with all ports overridden.

author: smaug123
body:
`Path.GetFullPath` had no test coverage. It splits cleanly in two, so this adds one test for each half rather than a single test that only reaches the first:

- **`PathGetFullPathRooted.cs`** — rooted input skips the current-directory lookup and exercises `PathInternal.RemoveRelativeSegments`, collapsing `..` and `.` segments. Passes today.
- **`PathGetFullPathRelative.cs`** — relative input must first resolve the process's current directory, which on Unix is `Interop.Sys.GetCwd()`. `SystemNative_GetCwd` has no handler registered in `Native/NativeDispatch.fs` at all, so it stops at `NativeCall.failUnimplemented`. Parked.

The relative test asserts only what holds whatever the current directory is — that the result is rooted and ends with the requested path — so it does not bake in the host's cwd.

Landing the parked half is deliberately left alone: the current directory is exactly the sort of host-visible value `EmulatedKernel` exists to hold as data, so the fix is a kernel-state field plus a handler rather than a host `Directory.GetCurrentDirectory()` read, and that belongs in its own change.

Found while investigating a reported `Path.GetFullPath -> String.Split -> SegmentedArrayBuilder` failure; orthogonal to that investigation, hence its own branch.

Full test suite green. Reviewed by `codex review --base origin/main`, which reported no findings and independently confirmed the rooted case passes under PawPrint while the parked case passes its real-runtime oracle.

 backend/modules/plugins/camera/__init__.py      | 25 +++++++++++++++
 backend/modules/plugins/camera/config_schema.py | 41 +++++++++++++++++++++++++
 3 files changed, 96 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

## Analyse de conséquences

- **Impacts directs** :
  - `backend/modules/apps.py` enregistre `CameraModule()` — inchangé, mais le module tombe désormais dans la branche « preconditions unmet » de `modules/registry.py:54` et n'entre plus dans `_active`.
  - `backend/modules/collectors.py` (`tools()`, `capabilities()`, `context()`) et `backend/modules/scheduler.py` itèrent sur `registry.running()` / `active()` : le module en étant absent, ses deux outils ne sont plus déclarés, son contexte n'est plus injecté et son tick de 10 s ne tourne plus. C'est l'objet du correctif.
  - `backend/pipeline/context.py:213` (`ai.conversation_tool_modules` vide = « tous les modules démarrés ») voit mécaniquement deux outils de moins.
  - `backend/communication/channels/camera.py` : `_push_frame` refactorisé autour d'un helper `_camera_module()` ; `connect()` refuse la connexion quand le module est éteint (nouveau code de fermeture **4003**, non utilisé ailleurs).
  - `backend/GestionSysteme` : nouvelle section de configuration `module_camera` (order=72, entre `module_email` 71 et `module_rss` 73). Elle porte le préfixe `module_`, donc `core_sections()` l'exclut de la page Configuration cœur et elle s'affiche dans l'espace du module — comportement identique à email/rss/forge. L'espace reste listé par `shell.module_spaces()` (basé sur les modules *enregistrés*, pas *actifs*).
- **Effets de bord** :
  - **Changement de comportement par défaut assumé** : sur une installation existante où un appareil poussait déjà des frames, la caméra devient muette tant que `camera.enabled` n'est pas coché puis le module activé. C'est exactement ce que demande l'issue (opt-in) ; la connexion refusée le dit explicitement au device.
  - **Contrat WebSocket `ws/camera` étendu** : un client peut maintenant recevoir `{"type":"error","message":"Module caméra désactivé…"}` suivi d'une fermeture 4003 dès `connect()`. Aucun client n'est livré dans `frontend/`, donc aucun consommateur interne à adapter ; un producteur externe doit gérer ce cas (ou simplement reconnecter).
  - **Accès ORM pendant `AppConfig.ready()`** : `is_available()` lit `camera.enabled` via `config_service`, ce qui déclenche une `RuntimeWarning` Django « Accessing the database during app initialization is discouraged » au démarrage et dans le résumé pytest. C'est le point à arbitrer par le reviewer. Aucune exception possible (`configs/service.py::_fetch_value_row` avale largement l'échec et retombe sur le défaut du schéma) ; sur une base non migrée le module est simplement indisponible, ce qui est le comportement voulu.
  - `is_available()` est aussi appelé par `get_status()` et `registry.list_all()` (page Modules du tableau de bord) : lectures en cache après la première, coût nul.
  - Aucun abonnement au bus d'événements modifié — le module n'était attaché qu'au démarrage, et il ne démarre plus. Aucun ordre de bloc de prompt touché ; le bloc `[camera] …` de `--- CONTEXTE MODULES ---` disparaît simplement quand le module est éteint.
- **Base de données** : **aucune migration**. `camera.enabled` vit dans `ConfigValue` via le registre de configuration existant (aucun modèle, aucun champ, aucun queryset modifié). Le module ne déclare pas de `get_models()`, donc pas d'installation/suppression de table.
- **Tests** : aucun test existant ne référence le module `camera` (`backend/tests/test_router.py:72` et `test_pipeline_integration.py:221` n'utilisent que `source="camera"` sur une `Perception`, sans rapport). Points à surveiller côté reviewer : (a) un test qui compterait les sections de configuration ou les items du registre (16 sections / 70 items aujourd'hui) ; (b) `test_config_env_bridge.py` exige qu'aucun `ConfigItem` ne déclare d'`env_fallback` et que tout réglage opérationnel ait un défaut — les deux sont respectés (`default=False`, pas d'`env_fallback`) ; (c) `test_gestion_systeme.py` vérifie les espaces de modules, non impacté puisque l'espace reste listé. Exécuté : `test_module_interface.py` → 13 passed.
- **Verdict** : deux points à valider par le reviewer — (1) la `RuntimeWarning` Django au démarrage, conséquence directe de la lecture de configuration à l'enregistrement prescrite par l'issue (aucune conséquence fonctionnelle, documentée dans la docstring d'`is_available()`) ; (2) le refus explicite de la connexion `ws/camera` avec le code 4003, ajout hors du strict périmètre de l'issue mais qui évite que l'opt-in ne devienne un silence non diagnosticable côté appareil.

## Checklist pour le reviewer

- [ ] Les corrections sont pertinentes et justifiées
- [ ] Pas de régression fonctionnelle introduite
- [ ] Aucun fichier sensible n'a été modifié
- [ ] Les tests passent correctement

body:
Closes #20

## 摘要

按 ADR-004（`docs/adr/0004-conversation-store-split.md`）将混在 `ACPClient` 中的每会话对话状态与对话动作（resume / send / cancel）提取到新的 `ConversationStore`。重构完成后 `ACPClient` 仅保留连接生命周期、凭据与会话列表，并把对话工作委托给 store。用户与 view 层看不到任何行为变化。

本分支同时包含 #6 的会话视图实现（流式渲染 + 输入 + 中断）与两份 ADR 文档（0003 / 0004），供 #6 的 code-review 后续一并审查。

## 主要改动

- **新增 `ConversationStore`**（internal）：唯一持有 `conversations` 字典，承载 resume / send / cancel 动作、会话更新摄入与 sign-out 清空；通过注入的 `isConnected` 闭包执行连接守卫（连接生命周期仍归 `ACPClient`）
- **`ACPClient` 收敛**：公开 API 签名零变化（view 层零改动，ADR-001 继续成立）；`ConversationStore` internal 化使「视图不可达 store」在编译期强制
- **行为保持关键点**：store 的 `objectWillChange` 转发到 `ACPClient`，保证视图经 `@EnvironmentObject` 仍能观察到对话状态变化（流式更新 / 乐观气泡 / 发送中状态）
- **命名**遵循 CONTEXT.md 词汇表（`ConversationStore`），未使用与 `SessionConversation` 混淆的名字

## 提交列表

- `3455322` feat(ios): 会话视图 - 流式渲染 + 输入 + 中断（#6）
- `64abe7c` docs(adr): Add conversation store and decode-variant ADRs
- `eae5acb` Extract ConversationStore from ACPClient (behavior-preserving) (#20)

## 测试

- 92 个 Swift 测试全绿（含新增 `ConversationStoreTests` 10 例 + 变更转发回归测试 1 例）
- `xcodebuild` iOS Simulator 构建通过

author: debpalash
body:
The 2026-08-05 nightly preview build **refused to publish its own healthy build**, and has been failing since. All four matrix legs were green:

```
Refusing to publish a preview manifest: the macOS updater bundle(s)
['OmniVoice.Studio_aarch64.app.tar.gz'] were last uploaded before this run's
versioned artifacts (2026-08-05T08:08:24+00:00), so they are from an EARLIER build.
```

## Why it was wrong

The version-less darwin tarballs carry nothing in their names tying them to a build, so #1362 tied them to the **sibling versioned artifacts' upload times**, with 2 minutes of slack. But matrix legs finishing minutes apart is *normal* — the fast Apple-Silicon leg routinely beats a slow Windows leg by more than any slack worth allowing. The check reads that as "stale" and refuses. Preview-channel users quietly stop getting builds; the failure looks like a build problem when nothing was built wrong.

## The fix

Bind the tarballs to the **run**: anything uploaded after the run was created belongs to it, since only one preview run touches the rolling release at a time. That margin is hours, not minutes, so leg skew can't trip it — while the case the check exists for (macOS legs never uploaded, last night's tarball still sitting there) is still refused.

`release.yml` passes the run's `created_at`, **not** `run_started_at` — the latter resets on every re-run, so re-running just this job would judge the bundles its own earlier attempt uploaded as stale and reproduce the same false refusal. The old leg-to-leg comparison stays as the fallback when no run timestamp is supplied (direct/manual invocation).

## Tests

New `TestBindingByRunStart` covers the exact 2026-08-05 shape (mac legs 3 min early → accepted), the genuinely stale case (→ still refused), boundary clock skew, the no-timestamp fallback, and an unreadable timestamp being refused rather than silently ignored. Plus a workflow-level test that `release.yml` passes the timestamp **and** reads `created_at` rather than `run_started_at`. 28 passed.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Preview manifest validation now binds macOS updater tarballs to the workflow run’s earliest job start time and serializes preview runs per ref without cancellation. This prevents queued runs from accepting artifacts from a preceding run while allowing normal matrix-leg completion skew and rejecting stale or unreadable artifacts. Review run metadata lookup and manifest wiring because failures could reject valid builds or accept stale tarballs.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: konicatc-techcoding
body:
## What changed and why

daily 檔已在本機累積並排入 `pending_uploads`，但 App 沒有 Google 身分。本 PR 補上帳號連結整條路：Core 新增 `Auth/` 層（PKCE S256、授權 URL／callback 解析、token 端點請求組裝與回應解析、`GoogleAuthSession` actor 負責 token 供應與 refresh 決策），HTTP 傳輸與 token 保存以 protocol 注入所以 CI 可測整個流程；App 端提供 `ASWebAuthenticationSession` 包裝、Keychain 保存與 URLSession 傳輸，probe 畫面新增 Drive 區塊。client ID 經 gitignored 的本機 xcconfig 疊在進版控的空預設值上，未設定時 App 照常編譯執行並顯示提示。

Closes HEA-17

## Scope ledger

- AC-1 — `RootView` 新增 Google Drive 區塊：未連結顯示「連結 Google Drive」；點擊走 `WebAuthenticator`（`ASWebAuthenticationSession`）→ Google OAuth（authorization code + PKCE S256，scope `drive.file openid email`）→ 完成顯示「已連結：email」
- AC-2 — `KeychainGoogleTokenStore`：access／refresh／過期時間／email 整組 JSON 存 generic password（`kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock`）；不落 UserDefaults 或檔案；重啟後 `refreshDriveState` 從 Keychain 讀回已連結狀態
- AC-3 — `GoogleAuthSession.validAccessToken()`：未過期（60 秒邊際）直接給；過期以 refresh token 換新並回寫；`invalid_grant` 映射為 `GoogleAuthError.reauthorizationRequired` 並清保存，供上傳流程辨識「需重新連結」。請求組裝與解析全在 Core（`GoogleOAuthEndpoints`），傳輸注入，20 個 CI 測試覆蓋
- AC-4 — `disconnect()`：盡力呼叫 revoke（失敗不阻擋，含離線測試）、清 Keychain、UI 回未連結；可重新連結
- AC-5 — `Config/GoogleOAuth.xcconfig`（進版控、空預設）`#include?` gitignored 的 `GoogleOAuth.local.xcconfig`；範本 `GoogleOAuth.local.xcconfig.example` 含步驟說明；client ID 經 Info.plist `GoogleOAuthClientID` 注入；callback scheme 由 client ID 推導（`reversedClientID`）；未設定時 Drive 區塊顯示明確提示、`beginAuthorization` 拋 `notConfigured`、App 不崩潰
- AC-6 — 取消：`ASWebAuthenticationSession` 的 `canceledLogin` 與 callback 的 `access_denied` 都映射為中性「已取消連結」提示；保存是流程最後一步，測試證明拒絕授權後 store 為空
- NG-1 — 無任何 Drive 檔案 API 或 `pending_uploads` 消化程式碼
- NG-2 — 零第三方依賴：只用系統框架（CryptoKit、AuthenticationServices、Security）
- NG-3 — 單帳號：Keychain 單一 entry，`save` 即覆寫
- NG-4 — 同步流程、彙整、daily 檔零改動
- Other behavior changes: None

## Manual test steps

1. Google Cloud Console 建 OAuth client（iOS 類型、bundle ID `com.konicatc.healthsync`），依 `Config/GoogleOAuth.local.xcconfig.example` 建立本機設定、`xcodegen generate`、實機安裝
2. 按「連結 Google Drive」→ Google 登入 → 畫面顯示已連結與 email
3. 殺掉 App 重開 → 仍是已連結
4. 「解除連結」→ 回未連結；再連結成功
5. 授權視窗按取消 → 回未連結、顯示中性「已取消連結」、無錯誤

body:
This security hardening fix addresses a symbolic link path traversal bypass in vault path validation. Although path.resolve is used to ensure the path starts with the user's home directory, it does not resolve symbolic links. Thus, a symlink within the home directory pointing outside could still be followed by Node.js filesystem APIs. We resolve symlinks using fs.realpathSync when validating vault paths to prevent this vulnerability. A test suite was added to verify the protection works.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
## What this is

rf2-v8561 reported three CLJS namespaces failing per-ns isolation in the fast-PR spine — `views-current-component`, `story open-in-editor-ownership`, `story presence-real-clock`.

**They do not leak, and there was nothing to fix in them.** What the gate could not say is *why* it was red, so this PR makes it say so.

## Does it reproduce? No — and here is what actually happened

A clean worktree off `origin/main`, fresh `npm ci`, fresh `node-test` compile, then the bead's own repro (`cd implementation && node scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs`), twice:

```
per-ns isolation: all 17 namespace(s) pass standalone (196 tests, 731 assertions in total)   exit 0
```

The three named namespaces run **3 tests / 4 assertions**, **5 / 13** and **6 / 31** standalone. All non-zero, all plausible, both runs identical.

The mechanism is visible in the roster: the three reported namespaces are its **last three entries, consecutively**. That is not three independent fixture defects, it is a contiguous tail — the signature of something collapsing partway through a sweep that spawns one node process per namespace over ~4.5 minutes.

`compile-node-test.cjs` **unlinks `out/node-test.js` before every compile**, deliberately, so a failed compile leaves nothing stale (rf2-6t03c). A compile starting mid-sweep therefore pulls the bundle out from under every run still to come. Injecting exactly that — unlinking the bundle 225s into a 276s sweep — reproduces the reported signature namespace for namespace:

```
  isolating re-frame.subs-override-seam-cljs-test ... ok (8 tests, 18 assertions)
  isolating re-frame.views-current-component-cljs-test ... ENVIRONMENT
  isolating re-frame.story.open-in-editor-ownership-cljs-test ... ENVIRONMENT
  isolating re-frame.story.play.presence-real-clock-cljs-test ... ENVIRONMENT
```

Both recorded sightings were worktrees with other builds running. This matches them.

## The fix

Three causes reach a non-zero standalone exit; the gate reported all three as the first.

| | meaning | remedy |
|---|---|---|
| `ISOLATION` | tests ran and failed | the fixture remedy — what the gate is for |
| `ROSTER` | selector matched nothing (renamed/deleted ns) | update the curated list |
| `ENVIRONMENT` | the bundle moved underneath the sweep | let builds settle, rerun |

They are separated by one structural fact: `--test=<ns>` is a **runtime** selector over a bundle linking **every** test namespace, so every run loads the whole graph whichever namespace it selects. A module-load crash cannot single a namespace out — it hits all of them. So a red carrying cljs.test's `Ran N tests containing M assertions.` got far enough to be a verdict about that namespace, and a red without one never did.

A sweep whose bundle moved is now **indeterminate**, not red: its greens are worth no more than its reds, so it exits 2 and asks for a quiet rerun rather than naming namespaces it cannot vouch for.

Also closed, since the summary was already being parsed: a green must now carry a **non-zero test count**, so a run that certifies nothing cannot be counted as coverage. Per-namespace counts are printed, which is how a thinned selector becomes visible at all.

The `ROSTER` case is not speculative — `9dd9633d0b` and `d3969eb67b` are both commits fixing a stale roster entry that the gate had reported as a fixture defect.

## A/B under an identical injected fault

| | old gate | new gate |
|---|---|---|
| verdict | `16 namespace(s) FAILED when run in isolation` | `INDETERMINATE — 17 of 17 run(s) never became a verdict` |
| remedy printed | add `make-reset-runtime-fixture` | let the concurrent build finish, then rerun |
| exit | 1 | 2 |

Every one of the old gate's 16 accusations was `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

## Quality gates

Run in the worker worktree, foreground, to completion.

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs --self-test` | **exit 0** — 18 assertions pass |
| `node scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs` (clean, run 1) | **exit 0** — 17/17, 196 tests, 731 assertions |
| `node scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs` (clean, run 2, timed 276s) | **exit 0** — identical counts |
| old gate under injected unlink fault | exit 1, 16 false accusations *(positive control)* |
| new gate under injected unlink fault @6s | **exit 2** INDETERMINATE, 17/17 *(positive control)* |
| new gate under injected unlink fault @225s | **exit 2** INDETERMINATE, exactly the 3 reported namespaces *(positive control)* |
| `npm run test:script-policy` | **exit 0** |
| `npm run test:script-helpers` | **exit 0** |
| `python scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` | **exit 0** — 77 required jobs, map clean |
| `python scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py` | **exit 0** — 40 gate commands, 0 unbeaded holes |

The self-test is pinned to output shapes transcribed from real runs of this bundle, not invented strings — including the discrimination itself: the same non-zero exit classifies differently with and without a summary.

## Scope

One file, `implementation/scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs`. The curated roster is unchanged, no test namespace is touched, and no fixture was added — because none was needed.

author: mandakan
body:
Fixes #664.

## What was wrong

`Job` had no shooter identifier, and stage numbers repeat across every shooter in a match. Two distinct failures shared that root cause:

1. **Backend (the "impossible to start" half):** the submit-time dedupe `find_active(kind="shot_detect", stage_number=n)` matched shooter A's in-flight job when shooter B posted the same stage, so B's POST returned a snapshot of **A's job** and B's detection never started. This, not the `max_concurrent=2` cap, was the blocker - B's submit was never reached.
2. **SPA (the display half):** `Audit.tsx` / `PrereqGate.tsx` predicates over `listJobs()` matched on `kind + stage_number`, so A's running jobs painted B's stages as busy.

## The fix

- `Job` (wire model, `compute_jobs` row, SPA mirror) gains `shooter_slug`.
- Every shooter-scoped submit (`detect_beep`, `trim`, `shot_detect`, `export`, `match_export`, the auto-chain paths) sets it; slug-less jobs (`model_download`, `generate_proxy`, `compare-grid`, lab jobs) stay `NULL`.
- Both backends' `find_active` and every SPA `listJobs()` predicate match the slug strictly, mirroring `stage_number` semantics: a slug-less lookup only matches slug-less jobs.
- Alembic migration `f6acac06499c`: nullable `ADD COLUMN`, no RLS DDL, no backfill (rows are boot-swept).

## Verification

- New tests at all three layers (registry, Postgres backend, endpoint) were run against the pre-change code and fail there; the endpoint test fails on the exact symptom (`shooter B adopted shooter A's job`, identical job ids) and passes with the fix.
- Full pytest suite green except 4 pre-existing ffmpeg-environment failures that fail identically on clean `main` (`test_compare_grid_overlay_integration`, `test_runtime_ffmpeg_capabilities`, `test_compare_mp4_grid_overlay`).
- ruff + black clean; SPA `tsc -b`, vitest (66 passed), and scoped eslint clean of new issues.
- **Not run:** `pytest -m docker` (live-Postgres migration smoke). The host disk is 100% full and the colima VM is throwing I/O errors even on prune - see PR discussion. The migration is a bare nullable `ADD COLUMN` in the established pattern (`20aa31aeca11`).

author: pcarrier
body:
Rebased onto `main` now that #230 has landed — a single commit on top of it, using the size hints that PR stores. Crate suite re-run after the rebase.

This is the follow-up #230 said it was leaving alone, now with the pixels to justify it.

A pane narrower than its client's declared minimum showed a **cropped** window: the right-hand side of Chromium's toolbar, and whatever the page put near its right edge, simply were not there.

## Cause

`native_composite_size` is the render target, and it followed the pane alone. A client that declared `set_min_size` draws at that minimum no matter what we configure — Chromium's is 500 logical pixels wide, and it restates it after every configure — so a 300-wide pane got a 500-wide surface rendered into a 300-wide target at a 1:1 offset. Everything past 300 fell outside. Not a squeeze, a cut.

## Fix

Apply the client's own range on the way out of `native_composite_size`, which is the single place both the render target and the native size reported to the server come from. Compositing at the size the client really drew hands the viewer an oversized frame, and the browser already scales one of those down into its pane — that is the everyday multi-viewer case.

Deliberately only there. `surface_sizes` keeps the pane's own size, so the advertised output mode and the server's resize bookkeeping are untouched; the clamp lands where the pixels are decided and nowhere else.

## Testing

New protocol test squeezes a pane below a client's declared minimum and reads back the size the compositor settles on. Fails before the fix:

```
composited at the pane's width, which crops everything the client drew past it
  left: (300, 700)
 right: (500, 700)
```

End to end, real Chromium squeezed from 1920 to a 300-wide pane, reading the composited frames straight off the event stream. The page had a lime bar on its left edge and a red one on its right:

| | composite | what the frame contains |
|---|---|---|
| **before** | 300×700 | lime bar only. Toolbar cut mid-URL (`data:text/h`), no tab close button, no omnibox icons, **no red bar** |
| **after** | 500×700 | both bars, whole tab strip, whole omnibox — and the viewer scales it down to fit |

Crate suite (52 tests), clippy and fmt clean.

body: > **Empilée sur #70** — la base est `feat/ancestry-shortcut`, pas `main`, parce que la popin s'appuie sur `pairing.ts`. Une fois #70 fusionnée, GitHub rebasera la base sur `main` tout seul ; si le squash l'en empêche, je rebase et j'ouvre une PR neuve. Trois écrans, la même origine : depuis #59, deux montures de même couleur ne se valent plus. Rien dans l'outil ne le montrait, et rien dans le **jeu** ne permettait de les distinguer. ## 1. Les noms Le jeu laisse renommer une monture — 20 caractères, « Anonyme » par défaut — et c'est le seul champ qui se lise depuis la liste de l'écurie sans ouvrir une fiche. C'était la moitié manquante de #59 : savoir qu'une gen 2 à ascendance Amande gen 3 vise la gen 4 ne sert à rien si, devant quarante montures toutes nommées « Anonyme », rien ne dit laquelle c'est. Convention retenue, celle que tu as choisie : **`G3 AMA-DOR`** — la génération la plus haute de la généalogie, puis les codes des deux parents. | Cas | Nom | Longueur | | --- | --- | --- | | Née d'Amande (gen 3) × Doré (gen 1) | `G3 AMA-DOR` | 10 | | Née d'Ambre (gen 9) × Doré | `G9 AMB-DOR` | 10 | | Née d'Aigue-marine-Turquoise × Aigue-marine-Émeraude | `G10 AIGEME-AIGTUR` | 17 | | Achetée ou capturée | `Anonyme` | — | Dix caractères au plus sur vingt : la moitié reste libre pour ta note. **Découper un nom de couleur n'allait pas de soi.** Les composées prennent un tiret — « Doré-Amande » — mais « Aigue-marine » en prend un aussi, et c'est une seule couleur. C'est la **casse** qui les sépare : un composant commence par une majuscule, une continuation par une minuscule. Vérifié sur les 226 couleurs des trois familles — « marine » est la seule continuation qui existe, et aucune couleur ne porte plus de deux composants. Rien n'est jamais tronqué. **Un défaut attrapé dans le navigateur :** le même accouplement donnait `G4 AMA-DOR` ou `G4 DOR-AMA` selon que l'Amande était le mâle ou la femelle. Deux montures identiques sous deux noms, et le tri de l'écurie — toute la raison d'être de ce nom — cessait de les rapprocher. Les codes se rangent maintenant par ordre alphabétique. **Les montures déjà saisies** gardent un nom vide : on ne peut pas deviner ce qui est écrit dans le jeu. L'écurie affiche le nom **suggéré** à côté, en orange, cliquable — tu renommes en jeu, tu cliques, c'est noté. Le retard se rattrape au rythme où tu y passes. ## 2. Les fournées, par lots Une ligne par couple pour dix accouplements. Or un enclos ne se charge pas par couples : on y dépose vingt montures, et le jeu apparie. Ce qu'il faut lire, c'est ce qu'on **sort de l'écurie** : ``` ♀ Orchidee Anonyme × 4 ♀ Ebene Anonyme × 3 ♂ Amande G3 EBEPOU-INDORC × 1 aaaaaa ♂ Dore Anonyme × 1 ``` Les lots se distinguent par couleur, sexe **et nom**. Confondre « ♂ Doré Anonyme » et « ♂ Doré G9 AMB-DOR » ferait charger celle qui ne porte pas le raccourci. ## 3. La saisie, depuis la fenêtre d'accouplement Une liste déroulante à 120 couleurs par couple : dix accouplements, dix ouvertures, dix recherches à la lettre, dix clics sur le sexe. Or un accouplement ne peut pas rendre 120 couleurs — il en rend **quatre ou cinq**, et on les connaît d'avance. Le jeu les affiche lui-même avant l'accouplement ; il n'y avait qu'à les reproduire. `matingOutcomes` reconstitue cette fenêtre, et la reconstitue **exactement** : sur le relevé #59, 48,30 % sur Doré-Amande puis 21,81 / 21,81 / 8,08, somme à 1,000000. Rien de neuf n'est calculé — la masse de réussite vient de `targetGenerationRate`, le reste de `lineageDistribution` partagé moitié-moitié, ce que `lineageValue` faisait déjà pour chiffrer. Deux clics par naissance, sur une liste courte, à côté de la probabilité. Et **le nom à donner sur chaque issue, avant le clic** : il dépend de ce qui est né, donc il ne peut pas être dicté avant. Les deux orientations d'un même croisement sont un seul bloc — 2 blocs au lieu de 4 sur la fournée testée. **Une approximation, signalée dans le module :** quand plusieurs couleurs occupent la génération visée, le jeu ne les partage pas à parts égales (40,02 + 5,34 + 5,34 relevé, et non trois fois 16,68). Le partage retenu suit les poids de la recombinaison, qui reproduisent le rang mais pas forcément la valeur. Le **total** de la ligne « Génération cible » est exact. Sans conséquence pour saisir : on clique sur la couleur obtenue, pas sur sa probabilité. ## Migration `20260806190000_breeding_mount_names.sql` **ajoute une colonne `name` nullable** et un commentaire. Rien n'est réécrit, rien ne bouge, les lignes existantes restent valides avec un nom vide. ## Vérifié `npx tsc --noEmit` et `npx eslint src` verts (3 warnings `` préexistants). Dans le navigateur, sur une écurie mockée : | Écran | Constaté | | --- | --- | | Fournées | 8 lots pour 9 accouplements, noms et effectifs corrects | | Popin | 2 blocs, probabilités du relevé, noms sur chaque issue | | Clic sur une issue | compteur `2/7`, récapitulatif « à renommer » alimenté | | Écurie | `G3 AMA-DOR` sur la nommée, `Anonyme → G3 AMA-DOR` sur l'autre | Aucune erreur console. Ce test est ce qui a attrapé le `DOR-AMA` / `AMA-DOR` et les blocs en double. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
Follow-up to #4 and #5. This is the change that actually makes `/` serve live figures to crawlers.

## Problem
`/api/landing` works and returns live database figures (`104,621 / 14 / 493 / 183`), but `/` still returns the frozen static document with `104,217` and no stat block.

## Cause
**Vercel resolves static files before applying `rewrites`.** `dist/index.html` existed, so `/` was always answered from that file and the `"/" -> /api/landing` rewrite could never run. Neither #4 nor #5 could have fixed this on their own.

## Fix
Rename the Vite output to `app.html` at the end of the build, so `/` has no static match and the rewrite applies. The landing function reads `/app.html` as its shell, and its last-resort redirect targets the same path.

## Verification
`npm run build` -> `dist/app.html` present, `dist/index.html` absent. Handler returns `200`, no redirect, `crawler-stats` block in raw HTML, `assets/index-sPd0A44E.js` hash preserved.

Unchanged: ingestion worker, `0 */6 * * *` cron, API contract, displayed data, methodology, licensing, `vite.config.js`.

author: cuttlefisch
body:
Closes the first half of #2. Refs #10, #12.

The library targets 25.10.5 but embedded only a 25.04 schema, so nothing could answer *"does this method exist on this appliance"* for the target platform.

## The schema is interim, and says so in code

It was converted from a vendored `core.get_methods` dump taken at **25.10.1** — not the 25.10.5 target — and captured from the legacy `/websocket` DDP endpoint rather than `/api/current`. Embedding it unblocks everything downstream that does not need hardware.

Rather than bury that in a comment inside a 4.8 MB JSON file, it is a `Provenance` record with `Verified bool`. Two tests enforce it:

- every embedded schema must have a provenance entry, and an unverified one must carry an explanatory note;
- `TestProvenance_25_10_IsStillInterim` **fails deliberately** when `Verified` flips to true, so the re-fetch, the ADR-004 evidence section and the tracking issue get closed out together instead of drifting apart.

The source dump's `_metadata` block is **not** copied — it carries an `api_endpoint` naming a third party's appliance address, which has no business in a public repo. Only the methods object is retained, in the same flat compact form as `api/25.04/methods.json`.

## Resolution direction is the load-bearing detail

`ResolveVersion` returns the highest embedded schema **not exceeding** the appliance:

| appliance | resolves to | why |
|---|---|---|
| 25.10.5 | `25.10` | never down to 25.04, or a method *removed* in 25.10 reads as available |
| 25.05–25.09 | `25.04` | highest not exceeding |
| 26.x, 27.x | `25.10` | clamps to newest — under-reports new methods rather than over-reporting removed ones |
| 24.10 | error | no answer beats a wrong one |

`api` stays a leaf package with no internal dependencies; the version is parsed locally rather than importing the root package's `ParseVersion`.

## FEATURES.md

`api.LatestVersion()` is the matrix denominator, so this moves for every service: 771 → 768 total, and `SnapshotService` now reports `pool.snapshot` instead of `zfs.snapshot` — the rename correctly reflected per version. Implemented count unchanged at **74**, so no service lost a method to the 25.10 removals. Committed separately as its own mechanical commit.

## Test plan
`mise run ci`, which forces `GOTOOLCHAIN` to go.mod's pin:

```
check-versions   ✓
build / vet      ✓
golangci-lint    ✓ 0 issues
staticcheck      ✓ 0 issues
FEATURES.md      ✓ up to date
go test -race    ✓ all pass
coverage         86.4% (threshold 86.0, baseline 86.3)
govulncheck      ✓ 0 vulnerabilities
```

- [x] `ResolveVersion` table-tested across exact, between, future and too-old appliances
- [x] `MethodsForVersion(25,10)` finds `sharing.smb.share_precheck` (25.10-only) and `MethodsForVersion(25,4)` does not — proving the right schema answered rather than a fallback
- [x] featurematrix output verified deterministic across 4 runs (same checksum)

author: henningwold
body:
Bakgrunn: grunnet bridge network mode på ECS Anywhere/EXTERNAL launch type fungerer det ikke å slå på Datadog i eksisterence modul. Har brukt KI assistanse til å implementere en fiks for dette.

Mulig man ønsker å kutte ned litt på Claude sine inline kommentarer - lar det bli opp til reviewers. Merk at endringen _vil_ gi diff også på vanlige Fargate deployments - dette fordi loggene til log-router flyttes til CloudWatch (veldig vanskelig å debugge den komponenten om den feiler når loggene gikk til seg selv 😓). Limer inn forklaringen på endringene nederst her:

# Fix Datadog on `launch_type = "EXTERNAL"` (ECS Anywhere)

Enabling `enable_datadog = true` on a service with `launch_type = "EXTERNAL"` produced a task
that could never start. `EXTERNAL` forces `network_mode = "bridge"`, and two assumptions in the
Datadog path only hold for `awsvpc`. A third problem turned out to be on the container instances
rather than in this module — see **Prerequisite** below.

Fargate/awsvpc consumers are unaffected apart from one deliberate change, noted at the bottom.

## 1. The log router was logging through itself

`aws_ecs_task_definition.task_datadog` applied `logDriver = "awsfirelens"` to *every* container,
including `log-router` itself.

In `awsvpc` the ECS agent hardcodes the fluentd address to `127.0.0.1`, so this is a silent
no-op. In `bridge` the agent has to resolve the router's own bridge IP, which doesn't exist yet
at create time — and it deliberately refuses to make the router wait for itself
(`addFirelensContainerDependency()`). The router is `essential`, so the task died with:

    DockerClientConfigError: unable to get BridgeIP for task in bridge mode

**Fix:** `log-router` now gets an explicit `awslogs` log configuration. Its own diagnostics no
longer depend on FluentBit being healthy.

## 2. In bridge mode nothing could reach the Agent

Each container has its own netns, so `localhost:8126` in the app container is the app container.
Scoped to `EXTERNAL` only:

- `ECS_FARGATE = "true"` is no longer set — it put the Agent in Fargate mode on a real Docker host.
- Added `DD_APM_NON_LOCAL_TRAFFIC` / `DD_DOGSTATSD_NON_LOCAL_TRAFFIC`; the Agent binds loopback only.
- Added the Agent's ECS-on-EC2 host mounts (`docker.sock`, `/host/proc`, `/host/sys/fs/cgroup`) and matching task volumes.
- App container gets `DD_AGENT_HOST = "datadog-agent"` and `links = ["datadog-agent"]`.

`links` rather than host port mappings: several tasks share an ECS Anywhere instance and would
collide on a fixed host 8126/8125. ECS converts each link into an implicit `dependsOn`/`START`,
so the Agent is up before the app. A caller-supplied `links` list is extended, not replaced.

## Prerequisite: ECS agent >= v1.93.0 on the instances

With the above fixed, container creation still failed on our current fleet:

    CannotCreateContainerError: unknown log opt 'fluentd-async-connect' for fluentd log driver

ECS agents before v1.93.0 write `fluentd-async-connect` unconditionally; Docker deprecated it in
20.10.0 and **removed it in 28.0.0**. v1.93.0 picks the option based on the Docker server version
(aws/amazon-ecs-agent#4558). The instance we tested on ran **agent 1.86.3 with Docker 29.5.2** —
an incompatible pairing. This is not fixable from Terraform, and
`ECS_ENABLE_FIRELENS_ASYNC=false` does not help either: the old agent still writes the key, just
with value `"false"`, and the daemon rejects the key itself.

The ECS Anywhere instances are being upgraded, so this PR keeps FireLens unconditional whenever
Datadog is enabled. The requirement is recorded as a comment above the `log-router` definition so
the next person to register an instance knows about it, along with the command to check a running
instance:

    aws ecs describe-container-instances --cluster <cluster> --container-instances <arn> \
      --query 'containerInstances[].versionInfo'

**Merge order matters:** deploying an `EXTERNAL` + Datadog service before its instances are on
agent >= v1.93.0 will still fail with the error above.

## Also

`network_mode` was a duplicated ternary in both task definition resources; it is now
`local.network_mode`.

## Testing

`terraform fmt` and `terraform validate` clean. Since `validate` only type-checks, the rendered
`container_definitions` JSON was diffed for both launch types:

- **EXTERNAL** — 4 containers; `awsfirelens` everywhere except `log-router` on `awslogs`; app
  container has `links` + `DD_AGENT_HOST` and keeps its `dependsOn: init:SUCCESS`; Agent has the
  3 host mounts and both non-local-traffic flags and no `ECS_FARGATE`.
- **FARGATE** — unchanged from `main` except the `log-router` log driver; `ECS_FARGATE` still set,
  no bridge wiring, no host mounts.

Also verified that a caller-supplied `extra_options.links` list is merged rather than replaced.

## Behaviour change for existing consumers

`log-router`'s own logs move from Datadog to CloudWatch for **all** Datadog-enabled services,
including Fargate (item 1 is not gated on network mode, since the router logging through itself
is wrong everywhere). This shows up as a task definition diff on the next apply. Everything else
in this PR is behind `launch_type == "EXTERNAL"`.

author: upupming
body:
Adds `references/external-bundle.md` to the `vanilla-lynx` skill. External bundles are the general mechanism for splitting *any* package out of a Lynx app — a utility library, an SDK wrapper, a component library, a rarely-used feature, a runtime shared across cards — so the reference covers the workflow rather than any particular package.

Two halves:

- **Producer**: build the package into a standalone `.lynx.bundle` / `.web.bundle` with `defineExternalBundleRslibConfig`, including the section naming contract (section name = rslib entry key, with `__main-thread` / `:CSS` derived from it) and how `output.externals` moves a dependency out of the bundle onto `lynx[Symbol.for('__LYNX_EXTERNAL_GLOBAL__')]`.
- **Consumer**: load it at runtime by hand with `lynx.fetchBundle` + `lynx.loadScript`, instead of letting `pluginExternalBundle` generate the loading code.

The reference is grounded in behavior verified against lynx-stack rather than docs alone:

- section names emitted by `ExternalBundleWebpackPlugin` (`utils`, `utils__main-thread`, `utils:CSS`), read back from `DEBUG=rspeedy` `tasm.json`
- entry `layer` only takes `'react:background'` / `'react:main-thread'`; `'background'` is silently ignored and still emits both sections, and an explicit main-thread layer does not add the `__main-thread` suffix
- a hand-written two-stage load — mount a dependency bundle's exports, then load a bundle compiled against it — running on the real web runtime via a temporary `web-core-e2e` case
- skipping the mount fails with a `TypeError` thrown from inside the bundle at evaluation time, which is why the ordering rule is called out explicitly rather than left implicit

Also documents the native/web divergence (`ResponseHandler` with `wait()` vs a real `Promise`, `error_msg` vs `errorMsg`, who applies the bundle's CSS), and says when to prefer `pluginExternalBundle` instead — bundles exporting main-thread components need their main-thread section evaluated before first render, which the plugin does from chunk runtime init.

SKILL.md gets the routing row, a core rule, and description triggers. Eval definitions extended with one task eval and five trigger queries; `pnpm eval:skill:check` reports `vanilla-lynx ... score=100.0`.

author: lboue
body:
# What does this implement/fix?

Adds OpenThread support to `platform: zephyr, variant: efr32mg24` (Silicon Labs xG24 Explorer Kit / xG24-EK2703A), fully validated including a real Thread network join. Follow-up to #63/#67, addresses #68.

**Requires `framework: source: {type: git, ref: main}`** -- the ieee802154 driver for this SoC (`drivers/ieee802154/ieee802154_silabs_efr32.c`) landed on Zephyr's `main` branch on 2026-02-12 (commit `bd89985e6`, "drivers: ieee802154: Add support of 802.15.4 for EFR xG24"), and postdates `v4.4.1` -- Zephyr hasn't cut a release containing it yet. Once it does, `efr32mg24`'s default/min version can be bumped and this requirement goes away; until then this is opt-in via the `framework:` override, same mechanism already used by e.g. the `nrf54lm20a` example in zephyr-examples.

## Changes

- **`efr32mg24.py`**: `"openthread"` added to `transports`, with a comment documenting the `ref: main` requirement. Also carries the `blobs=("hal_silabs", ...)` fetch (Zephyr's `hal_silabs` blob check verifies the HAL's entire manifest once BT *or* 802.15.4 is enabled -- `IEEE802154_SILABS_EFR32` directly `depends on ZEPHYR_HAL_SILABS_MODULE_BLOBS`, so this is needed for OpenThread too, not just BLE).
- **`core.cpp`**: `get_mac_address_raw()`'s `hwinfo_get_device_id()` path extended to `USE_ZEPHYR_VARIANT_FAMILY_SILABS` -- was only wired up for ESP32-family/Nordic, an undefined-reference link error waiting to happen for any other zephyr family that actually exercises it (here, via the network stack under OpenThread).
- **`api/__init__.py`**: `cv.SplitDefault(CONF_MAX_CONNECTIONS, ...)` / `CONF_MAX_SEND_QUEUE` had no `zephyr_efr32mg24` entry -- `to_code()` raised `KeyError` instead of falling back to a default. Added values matching nrf52/nrf54l15's reasoning (~256KB RAM, BSD sockets, Thread).
- **`esphome/ota/__init__.py`**: same gap for `CONF_SWAP_METHOD` -- the generic `zephyr="scratch"` fallback isn't valid here (no scratch partition in this board's flash layout), so added an explicit `zephyr_efr32mg24="move"` entry matching nrf52/nrf54l15/nrf54lm20a.
- **`api_connection.cpp`**: `ESPHOME_MANUFACTURER`'s `#if` chain had no branch for `USE_ZEPHYR_VARIANT_FAMILY_SILABS` -- another undefined-reference link error once `GetDeviceInfoResponse` actually got built (nothing had exercised it on this variant before this PR).

None of the last three are OpenThread-specific -- all three are generic gaps for this variant, surfaced simply by being the first time `api:` got configured on `platform: zephyr, variant: efr32mg24` at all.

## Validation

Compiled and flashed on real hardware via J-Link, joining a real Thread network end-to-end (not a placeholder dataset):

```
[I][openthread:036]: Thread role changed to detached
...
[I][openthread:036]: Thread role changed to child
[I][openthread:106]: SRP client has started
[I][openthread:039]: Thread network data updated
[C][api:269]: Server: ... Max connections: 4
```

The device attached, received real network data and a global (OMR) IPv6 prefix from the network's border router -- not just a locally-derived mesh-local address, confirming genuine two-way radio communication over the ieee802154 driver -- and its SRP client successfully registered its service with the network's SRP server. A `switch`/`binary_sensor` pair (LED0 + the board's physical BTN0 button) was also verified working end-to-end through Home Assistant over the API connection.

Example config pushed to [zephyr-examples#6](https://github.com/esphomeplatformzephyr/zephyr-examples/pull/6) (`efr32mg24/xg24_ek2703a_openthread.yaml`).

## Types of changes

- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] New developer-facing feature (adds functionality for component developers; no end-user configuration change)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) -- [policy](https://developers.esphome.io/contributing/code/#what-constitutes-a-c-breaking-change)
- [ ] Developer breaking change (an API change that could break external components) -- [policy](https://developers.esphome.io/contributing/code/#what-is-considered-public-c-api)
- [ ] Undocumented C++ API change (removal or change of undocumented public methods that lambda users may depend on) -- [policy](https://developers.esphome.io/contributing/code/#c-user-expectations)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

**Related issue or feature (if applicable):**

- fixes https://github.com/esphomeplatformzephyr/esphome/issues/68

  name: xg24-ek2703a-openthread-example

zephyr:

```

author: janwidmer
body:
### Summary

In wp-admin, when adding a Block with a lazyblock gallery control, the control exectues a call to `/wp-json/wp/v2/media/xxx?context=edit&_locale=user` via function `getEntityRecord` for every image added to the gallery.

As this call is async, it bootstraps a new DB Connection every time, the call arrives in the backend. This leads to too many open DB Connection on certain hostings.

### Fix

Use the function `getEntityRecords` which requests the data for up to 100 media files. Repeat this for more than 100 files.

### Reproduction

1. Create a block with a gallery control in it
2. Add this block on a page
3. Add 100 images
4. notice the calls failing with Error 500 (only if your hosting provider has a concurrent DB Connection limit)

Closes https://github.com/nk-crew/lazy-blocks/issues/376

author: vikasprogrammer
body:
## What

`agent_propose_update` already let any agent propose an edit to any *other* agent's listing/CLAUDE.md — that half was never self-only. What was missing: every proposal landed identically whether the proposer had 200 clean runs or was on its first. Both ends of that were wrong. A brand-new agent could fill an owner's queue with prompt rewrites for teammates; a long-proven one couldn't fix an obvious stale instruction without a human round-trip.

The **proposer's maturity score** (`src/state/agent-stats.ts` — autonomy × (1 − denialRate) × volumeConfidence) now routes the call against workspace-configurable tiers (`AgentProposalTrust`, **Settings → Runtime → Cross-agent edits**, `GET`/`PUT /api/settings/agent-proposal-trust`):

| proposer maturity | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `< minMaturity` (0.40) | **refused** — no write, and no card either. The error tells the agent what earns the right and to raise it with a human instead. Audited `agent.update.proposal.blocked`. |
| middle band | unchanged **propose-don't-apply**: owner-addressed card, applied only by an owner who can run the target. The card now also carries the proposer's maturity, so the reviewer weighs the author's record, not the prose alone. |
| `≥ autoApplyAt` (0.80) | **applied immediately, no human in the loop**; admin-addressed notice after the fact naming the revision to revert. Audited `agent.update.applied`. |

## The top tier, stated plainly

It removes the human from the loop for a privilege-bearing act. What makes that a defensible trade:

- **Hard to reach by construction** — maturity multiplies in `volumeConfidence = runs/(runs+8)`, so 0.80 is unreachable below ~32 runs and additionally needs near-perfect autonomy and a clean denial record.
- **Revertable, not just auditable** — it commits a normal revision (author `agent:<proposer>`), so it shows up in the same Revision history panel as every other edit.
- **Switchable** — `autoApply:false` disables the tier entirely, restoring exactly the previous owner-gated behaviour while keeping the new floor.

## One write path

All three lanes now share `applyAgentEdit` in the new `src/state/agent-edit.ts`, extracted verbatim from the owner-approve route (same sanitizers, same `agent.json`/`CLAUDE.md` write, same `os.registerAgent`, same `AgentRevisions.commit`). An auto-applied edit is validated and snapshotted exactly like a human-approved one; only authorship differs.

## Verification

An isolated-home harness (`AGENT_OS_HOME` scratch dir — never the live `./data`) drives `proposeAgentUpdate` at each band and asserts against disk + DB, not just return values:

- refused tier: nothing written, no card, blocked event audited
- middle tier: card posted with maturity, `agent.json` and CLAUDE.md untouched, identical-delta dedupe still holds
- top tier: description + CLAUDE.md written, revision committed and authored `agent:proposer`, admin notice posted
- `autoApply:false` at the same maturity falls back to a card
- settings sanitiser clamps to 0..1 and never leaves the floor above the bar

**27/27 pass**, alongside `npm run typecheck`, `cd web && npm run build`, and `npm run test:governance` (20/20).

author: wamakologeorge-dev
body:
## Objective

Restore a reliable public Amosclaud account system and make GitHub an optional connected developer workspace rather than the only login method.

## Public account access

- `/login` serves one professional account portal.
- Visitors can create an account with name, email, and password.
- Signup is verified through a short-lived email code.
- Existing users can sign in with password or request a one-time email code from any device.
- Password recovery remains available.
- The production gateway no longer shadows these routes or returns HTTP 410.

## GitHub sibling workflow

- GitHub identity is optional and requests identity scopes only.
- Existing email/password accounts keep their password when GitHub is linked.
- Repository authorization remains a separate, explicit connection step.
- Amosclaud stores the GitHub authorization encrypted, lists accessible repositories, imports or clones selected projects, pulls updates, commits verified workspace changes, pushes branches, and creates GitHub issues.
- GitHub App webhooks continue to receive repository, pull-request, issue, check, workflow, and installation events.

## Railway reliability

- Account email delivery accepts the documented `MAIL_SMTP_*`, legacy `SMTP_*`, and HTTPS Resend variables consistently.
- `www.amosclaud.com` remains the canonical host with host-only cookies.
- Production storage uses `AUTH_DB_PATH=/data/auth.db` and `REPOSITORY_STORAGE_PATH=/data/repositories`.
- A Railway Volume must be mounted at `/data`; Client IDs and secrets do not preserve accounts, sessions, encrypted GitHub connections, or repositories across redeployments.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` must remain stable or users must reconnect GitHub.

## Security

- Email delivery failure never creates an unverified administrator account.
- Ordinary GitHub users do not receive administrator access.
- The separate owner-recovery flow remains restricted to the configured immutable GitHub identity.
- Sensitive repair candidates still require human approval; ordinary verified repairs continue automatically.

## Developer-platform direction

The new `docs/DEVELOPER_PLATFORM_GLUE.md` defines Amosclaud as an open developer utility connecting accounts, source control, autonomous engineering tools, CI/CD, cloud workspaces, deployment, and monitoring.

## Validation

This PR must pass formatting, the full Python test matrix, account creation and recovery contracts, GitHub linking tests, repository workflow tests, and deployment checks before merge.

author: kate-shine
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `scripts/release-packages.ps1` and `scripts/ci/semver-report.ps1` fail during the
`cargo semver-checks` baseline build:

```
LINK : fatal error LNK1104: cannot open file '...\deps\<crate>-<hash>.exe'
```

`cargo-semver-checks` nests its baseline registry checkout under the workspace target
directory, so intermediate artifact paths grow well past 260 characters. The MSVC `link.exe`
is **not long-path aware** — it fails regardless of the `LongPathsEnabled` registry setting
or a long-path-aware manifest on the calling process.

## Fix

Link the baseline build with `rust-lld`, which prepends the `\\?\` prefix internally and
handles those depths.

Measured on a dev machine with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` at 239 characters:

| Linker | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `link.exe` (default) | `LNK1104: cannot open file ...\debug\deps\<crate>.exe` |
| `rust-lld` | linked successfully |

### How the override is applied

`Invoke-SemverChecksCli` sets `CARGO_TARGET_<HOST_TRIPLE>_LINKER` (e.g.
`CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_PC_WINDOWS_MSVC_LINKER`) to `rust-lld.exe` for the duration of the call,
restoring or removing the variable in a `finally`.

That variable is just the environment spelling of `[target.<triple>] linker = "..."` in
`.cargo/config.toml` — the same knob, applied only where the problem is rather than to every
build in the repo. CI runs in short paths and does not have this problem, so switching its
linker would be blast radius for no gain.

An environment variable is used rather than a CLI flag because it is the only channel that
reaches the build that actually overflows `MAX_PATH`. `cargo-semver-checks` (0.47.0) exposes
no flag to forward cargo configuration, and as an *external* subcommand it receives
`--config` itself rather than letting cargo interpret it — while the failing build is the one
the tool spawns internally.

Two things keep the implementation small:

- **The bare name is enough.** `rustc` puts its own linker directory on `PATH` when it
  invokes the linker, so `rust-lld` resolves without locating the sysroot. No flavor flag is
  needed either — `rustc` infers the `link` flavor from the `rust-lld` stem.
- **Only the linker is overridden.** Deliberately *not* via `RUSTFLAGS`, which *replaces*
  `target.<triple>.rustflags` from `.cargo/config.toml` and would silently drop the
  repository's `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3`. Verified with a verbose build that the linker
  override and the repo's `target-cpu` flag coexist.

Non-Windows platforms are unchanged; their default linkers already handle long paths.

## Known limitation

This fixes the **link step only**. `cl.exe` / `lib.exe` invoked by `cc`-based build scripts
remain MAX_PATH-bound. In practice the semver-checks baseline builds have not hit that, but
it is a narrower guarantee than relocating the whole target directory would give.

## Also in this PR

`scripts/ci/semver-report.ps1` now routes its `cargo semver-checks` invocation through the
shared `Invoke-SemverChecksCli` instead of calling cargo directly. Besides picking up the
linker override, this fixes a latent bug where `$LASTEXITCODE` was read after an intervening
command and could be stale.

## Tests

- `scripts/tests/Pester/unit/releasing/SemverChecksLinker.Tests.ps1`: env-var naming for the
  host triple, that `rust-lld` is actually in the environment *while* cargo runs, and
  save/restore including the case where cargo throws.
- `PureFunctions.Tests.ps1`: updated the `LNK1104` hint assertion.
- Full Pester suite green (431 passed, 0 failed, 1 platform skip).

author: seonghobae
body:
## Replacement scope

This PR supersedes stale duplicate early-return proposals #161, #168, and #173 on current `develop`. It preserves the terminal-output neutralization merged in #229, repairs the terminal suite's ffprobe isolation exposed by the new exact-head CI, and adds executable cache-hit and cache-miss contracts before changing production behavior.

## Buyer-visible behavior

- A caller-selected output path that resolves to a non-empty regular file returns success before `yt-dlp` discovery, installation, or network activity.
- The existing artifact remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The cache-hit reason is displayed through `terminal_print_value`; untrusted path bytes never enter `%b` or shell source.
- Missing outputs and zero-byte regular files remain cache misses and preserve the original `yt-dlp -- URL` boundary.

## Test-first evidence

- Exact test-only head `b67911afc42f8a37e0018c072f863c5442078eab` passed ShellCheck and failed the executable CLI contract because `yt-dlp` was invoked for a non-empty cached artifact. The failure log captured the full argument vector.
- Exact implementation head `795bbbd921d22a3b18b8415ede987d17fc588a89` proved the new cache-hit and zero-byte branches but exposed an existing test-isolation defect: the terminal suite could not reach its missing-file assertion when `ffprobe` was absent on the clean runner.
- Exact verification head `8b8c4144555ad02308b9059c663c64faffa3797b` provided explicit `FFMPEG` and `FFPROBE` stubs and passed exact-head checkout, ShellCheck, the complete executable CLI and terminal-neutralization suites, clean-worktree verification, Security Scan, and Semgrep.
- Exact current head `202f8dd480d0f17085b7ed0a686786b38b1711ac` addresses the current-head review finding by adding an APA 7 retrieval date and `n.d.` date treatment for the mutable yt-dlp README reference. No production or executable test behavior changed; all required checks and reviews must rerun on this head.

## Production and contract changes

- `.github/workflows/cli-ux.yml`: immutable checkout pin, literal PR-head verification, read-only permissions, warning-or-higher ShellCheck, complete executable contracts, clean worktree.
- `download-reference.sh`: narrow `-f && -s` short circuit before dependency/network work, with the shared terminal renderer.
- `test_cli_ux.sh`: cache-hit, artifact-preservation, zero-byte miss, original-URL, and no-`yt-dlp` execution assertions.
- `test_terminal_output.sh`: deterministic ffprobe preflight isolation on clean runners.
- `docs/doctoring/download-cache-hit.md`: behavior, limitations, rollback, APA 7 references to GNU Bash and official yt-dlp documentation.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased buyer-visible behavior.

## Explicit limitations

The output path is the caller-owned cache key. This shortcut does not prove URL provenance or media integrity. A caller requiring a refresh must remove the old artifact or choose a different output path; a force-refresh interface would be a separate tested change.

## Merge gate

Do not merge until exact current head `202f8dd480d0f17085b7ed0a686786b38b1711ac` has completed every required security and repository check, no unresolved review thread remains, and independent non-author current-head approval is present. Queued, pending, skipped-required, cancelled, absent, stale-head, failed, or author-only evidence is not success.

Follow-up to the review comment on #488. Moves the known cursor fields onto the table classes and passes them to `decode_cursor`.
