body:
## Summary

Double-clicking a **Begin** or **End** time — either the number itself, or the label beside it — fills that field in with the reconstruction time currently being viewed.

## Why

Creating a feature at the time you are looking at means reading the reconstruction time off the main window and typing it back in by hand. That is the common case when building a model forward through time, and it is easy to mistype.

## Where it appears

The gesture is added to `EditTimePeriodWidget` rather than to `CreateFeatureDialog`. That widget is shared, so one change covers **both** the Create Feature dialog and the feature-properties editor, instead of only the dialog where it was first wanted.

## Behaviour

- An event filter catches `QEvent::MouseButtonDblClick` on four widgets: each time spinbox's **line edit**, and each **Begin/End label**. The label is accepted as well as the number because it is a fair-sized, easy target sitting next to a small one.
- The filter goes on the line edit rather than on the spinbox as a whole so that **the step arrows still step**. Clicking an arrow repeatedly is a normal way to nudge a spinbox; filtering the whole widget would have turned a quick double-nudge into a jump to the current time, discarding whatever had just been dialled in. The arrows are not part of the line edit, so they behave exactly as before.
- The reconstruction time is read via `GPlatesPresentation::current_time()`, so no additional state needs plumbing into the widget.
- Setting the time clears that field's **Distant Past** and **Distant Future** checkboxes first. Those states have no numeric value, so leaving one checked while filling in the spinbox would display a time the feature does not actually use — it would look set without being set. The spinbox is then re-enabled through `enable_or_disable_spinbox()`, the same helper the checkboxes use, rather than by duplicating that logic.
- `set_dirty()` is called explicitly rather than relying on the spinbox's `valueChanged()` signal, which only fires when the number actually changes and would miss the case where only the checkboxes were cleared.
- `commit_me()` is emitted, matching what the checkbox handlers already do.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `EditTimePeriodWidget.h` | `eventFilter()` override, two line-edit members, two private slots |
| `EditTimePeriodWidget.cc` | filter installation and implementation, slot implementations |

No `.ui` change: the gesture reuses widgets that were already on the form.

## Validation

- **Compiled and linked** in this configuration: MSVC 2022 / Ninja / Qt 6, Release, incremental build to completion. `EditTimePeriodWidget.cc`, `CreateFeatureDialog.cc`, `EditFeaturePropertiesWidget.cc`, `EditWidgetChooser.cc`, `EditWidgetGroupBox.cc` and the Qt MOC/UIC output all rebuilt; `gplates.exe` produced.
- **Double-click confirmed interactively** — setting Begin and End from the displayed reconstruction time works in the running program.
- That testing was done on a tree carrying the fork's current feature set. This branch is the same change on `gplates`; the patch applies cleanly but **this exact branch has not been separately compiled**.
- The step-arrow behaviour is **compiled but not yet re-confirmed by hand** since the filter moved to the line edit.

## Open question

**Discoverability.** Nothing on screen advertises the double-click. An earlier revision of this branch carried a small ◆ button beside each field; it was dropped as clutter in an already crowded row. A tooltip on the Begin/End labels is probably the cheaper way to surface it, if it needs surfacing at all.

author: arst
body:
## Problem

Audit findings #4 (HIGH) and the encumbrance off-by-one:

1. **Capacity invariant breaks permanently.** `IsFull => GetFreeSlots() == 0`, but a bulky item costs 2 slots and `AddItem` only checked `IsFull`. Adding a bulky item with 1 free slot — or losing Strength so `MaxCapacity` drops below current occupancy (`Character.ModifyAbility`) — drives free slots negative. From then on `IsFull` is false forever and every subsequent `AddItem`/`BuyItem` succeeds without limit.

2. **Encumbrance off-by-one.** `IsEncumbered` used `<=`, penalizing a character carrying exactly Strength+8 slots with +2 DR on every Strength/Agility test — contradicting the rule comment in the same file and Mork Borg's carry rule. The boundary tests had encoded the bug (`occupied == Str+8 → encumbered`); they now assert exact-at-limit is free.

## Fix

- `IsFull` is `<= 0`; `AddItem` requires the item's whole slot cost (2 if bulky) to fit
- `IsEncumbered` is strictly-above-allowance
- `BuyItem` drops its redundant `IsFull` pre-check — `AddItem` is the single gate, and silver is deducted only after the add succeeds

## Tests

- New: bulky add at 1 free slot throws; overstuffed-from-persistence inventory stays full and rejects adds
- Updated: encumbrance boundary cases assert exactly Strength+8 is carried free
- WretchedWhispers.Tests: 544/544 pass

## Summary

- Allow slide encoders with multiple declared outputs to select any registered variant while preserving the fixed-output behavior of existing single-output slide encoders.
- Resolve slide preprocessing geometry and variable-input capability from the tile dependency, but supported/default spacing from the slide encoder itself.
- Add public registry and configuration regression tests, including undeclared and explicitly empty output variants.

This separates image-geometry ownership from slide-spacing ownership so a future PRISM2 preset can use Virchow2's 224 px geometry while narrowing preprocessing to 0.5 µm/px.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Work test-first from the public registry and configuration seams.
- [x] A slide encoder may select any output variant declared in its registry metadata, and undeclared variants fail with the available variants named.
- [x] Existing single-output slide encoders remain fixed to their sole declared output and retain their current default behavior.
- [x] Slide preprocessing inherits tile size and variable-input capability from the declared tile encoder.
- [x] A slide encoder's own supported/default spacing takes precedence over the broader spacing capabilities of its tile encoder.
- [x] Existing tile-, slide-, and patient-level preset behavior remains unchanged outside the new declared slide-output capability.
- [x] Focused registry/configuration tests, the full non-GPU test suite, and relevant static checks pass.

author: ikayoun86-byte
body:
## Le fait, signalé par la session 7

Elle l'a écrit sur l'issue #20 ce matin, sur un instrument qui est le mien :

> *Le vérificateur dit maintenant : « `AGT-01` : aucun des 50 derniers commits ne cite de compétence consultée ». Il en comptait **6 sur 50** ce matin. Rien ne s'est dégradé : mes propres commits ont poussé les six hors de la fenêtre.*

Elle a raison, et je peux le chiffrer. Mesuré en élargissant la fenêtre, sur le dépôt du moment :

```
 50 commits  →   0 citation
100          →   9
200          →  32
400          →  48
```

**Le zéro de la fenêtre étroite n'était pas un zéro.** Il suffisait de la doubler.

---

## Ce que le vérificateur en tirait

```
◦ AGT-01 : aucun des 50 derniers commits ne cite de compétence consultée —
  la première règle d'AGENTS.md, et la table du chapitre 23, sont sans effet mesurable.
```

C'est une conclusion que la mesure ne porte pas. Et elle a un biais : **elle tombe d'abord sur les sessions les moins bavardes**, dont les citations sont les premières chassées par le débit des autres. Une session qui livre beaucoup rend muette la mesure de toutes les autres, sans que personne ait changé de conduite.

C'est le motif que ce dépôt traque depuis une semaine, dans l'instrument écrit pour le traquer : **un zéro qui se lit comme un vrai zéro.** Troisième fois ce matin, et la troisième était déjà dans un de mes outils.

---

## Ce que ce lot change, et ce qu'il ne change pas

**Il ne corrige pas la fenêtre.** La bonne largeur dépend d'un rythme de commits que personne ne maîtrise, et la choisir au jugé remplacerait un chiffre trompeur par un autre.

**Il refuse d'en tirer une conclusion qu'elle ne porte pas.** Le relevé regarde quatre fois plus loin *avant* de conclure au zéro, et distingue deux phrases :

```
◦ AGT-01 : aucun des 50 derniers commits ne cite de compétence — mais 30 sur les
  200 derniers le font. LA FENÊTRE EST TROP ÉTROITE POUR CONCLURE : une session au
  fort débit chasse les citations des autres, sans que personne ait changé de conduite.
```

et, si l'élargissement ne trouve rien non plus :

```
◦ AGT-01 : aucun des 50 derniers commits ne cite de compétence consultée, ni aucun
  des 200 derniers — la première règle d'AGENTS.md … sans effet mesurable.
```

**La seconde reste disponible, et c'est elle qui vaut verdict.** Le lot ne supprime pas l'alerte : il lui rend le droit d'être crue.

---

## Épreuves

Le compte est extrait dans **`compterCitations`**, pure, éprouvée sur des messages construits pour elle. L'ancienne version ne pouvait se vérifier que contre le dépôt vivant, dont le verdict change à chaque commit — une épreuve qui ne prouve rien de durable.

Trois épreuves, dont celle-ci, qui n'est pas une formalité :

> **Un « Compétences consultées : aucune » déclaré honnêtement compte comme une citation.**

La session qui a regardé et le dit **applique** `AGT-01`. Ne pas la compter ferait tomber le relevé sur les plus scrupuleuses — le même biais que celui qu'on corrige, retourné.

> **1787 / 1787 en local, `make verifier` sans écart — CI non exécutée, panne d'infrastructure `OBS-59`.**

---

## Ce que ce lot ne fait pas

author: mzxchandra
body:
## What

Adds a multi-provider **Embeddings** block (OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere, Mistral) and extracts the embedding engine into a shared core that both the block and knowledge-base indexing consume.

The knowledge-base path already had a real multi-provider engine — BYOK→env→rotating-key resolution, token-aware batching, retry, L2 normalization. The block had a bare `fetch` with none of it. Nothing bridged the two, so the block couldn't reach Gemini and the KB engine couldn't be reached from a workflow. This extracts the shared core first, then builds breadth on top, rather than adding a third parallel implementation.

## Shape

- **`lib/embeddings/`** — catalog (single source of truth for 7 models), client, key resolution, batching, L2 normalization, and adapters for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere, Mistral
- **`lib/knowledge/embeddings.ts`** — now a thin wrapper; exported signatures unchanged, and the 1536-dimension pgvector invariant does not move
- **`tools/embeddings/`** — one tool per provider from a shared factory, behind a single `/api/tools/embeddings` route and contract
- **New `embeddings` block type.** The `openai` block is left functionally untouched and only leaves the discovery surfaces via `hideFromToolbar` + `sunset.replacedBy`, so placed instances keep working with no migration. `openai_embeddings` is now an alias of `embeddings_openai`, so legacy instances pick up batching, retry, and metering with no visible change.

## Verification

**Live provider matrix, 16/16** against real APIs across all four providers. Each case asserts vector count, input ordering (two identical inputs must return cosine ≈ 1.0 while an unrelated one stays far below), emitted *and* reported dimensionality, L2 norm, and non-zero token usage. Gemini's Matryoshka reduction is normalized at both 1536 and 768.

Three bugs were found by that matrix and by manual testing, each fixed with a regression test:

- **Every unreduced request to `text-embedding-ada-002` and `mistral-embed` failed** with a provider 400. `resolveDimensions` returns the native size when no reduction is requested, and that concrete value reached the adapter, so the field was always sent. Models supporting Matryoshka accept their own native size, which hid it for 4 of 6 models; the two with no `supportedDimensions` reject the parameter outright.
- A stale `dimensions` or `taskType` survived a model switch. The per-model dropdowns share one subblock id and nothing clears a stored value when `dependsOn` fields change, so a choice made for one model was forwarded for another.
- An unsupported `dimensions` returned 502 instead of 400 — a client input error reported as an upstream failure.

Also: 3657 tests passing, typecheck clean across 23 tasks, `check:api-validation` passing.

## Reviewer attention

**Model-input provenance (#6247).** That commit added secret projection to the two files this branch rewrote. A textual merge would have compiled, passed CI, and silently dropped the control — the projection entry gate is fail-open (`if (!registry || modelInput?.mode !== 'project') return params`). Carried through as:

- the tool factory declares `request.modelInput`, covering all four provider tools and the legacy alias
- `embed()` takes a `projectInputs` projector that the KB wrapper supplies, preserving `projectKnowledgeModelInputs` and its use of projected values for token estimation

`projectInputs` is **required and explicitly nullable** rather than optional, so a new caller can't omit it silently — that's the same fail-open shape as the bug above. The route passes `null` because `prepareToolRequest` already projected at the HTTP hop. Projection runs once outside the retry loop. This makes `EmbedOptions` a source-breaking change for any future `embed()` caller, deliberately.

@vikhyathvikku — the projector threading is a design call inside your feature's territory, made by someone shipping an unrelated block. Worth your eyes.

## Not in this PR

A platform fix for copilot `edit-workflow` validation, which resolves same-id conditional subblock variants instead of silently using the last-declared one. The embeddings block surfaced it, but it affects ~20 blocks (`video_generator.duration` has 12 variants) and it narrows what programmatic edits accept, so it ships separately. Until then, a programmatic edit to an embeddings block validates `model`/`dimensions` against the last-declared provider variant. The block is unaffected in the editor and at runtime.

## Testing done

KB index + search regression confirmed. Still worth a look post-merge: discovery surfaces (legacy block absent from toolbar/search/mentions, new one present) and run-log cost attribution on a hosted-key vs BYOK run.

body:
## Problem

Quartz's `CreatedModifiedDate` plugin uses `new Date(d)` in `coerceDate()`, which only supports ISO 8601 format. Chinese date formats like `2025年8月13日 14:30` produce `Invalid Date`.

## Solution

Added `parseChineseDate()` function that handles:

| Format | Example |
|--------|---------|
| Chinese + time | `2025年8月13日 14:30` |
| Chinese + h:m:s | `2025年08月13日 14:30:00` |
| Chinese date only | `2025年8月13日` |

The parser:
- Validates date components (rejects invalid dates like Feb 30)
- Uses local timezone (consistent with ISO date-only handling)
- Falls back to `new Date(d)` for all other formats (backward compatible)

## Changes

- `src/transformer.ts`: Added `chineseDateRegex` and `parseChineseDate()`, modified `coerceDate()` to try Chinese format before falling back to native `Date` constructor.

author: abhijeetnarvekar
body:
## Summary

- Adopts the shared `document_ref` format for this integration ([INT-692](https://markup-ai.atlassian.net/browse/INT-692)). The backend keys `document_registry` on `document_ref`, and the Markup session id derives its document component from `SHA-256(document_ref)` — so every surface must spell the same document the same way. Until now this extension sent a bare `document.uri.toString()`.
- Bumps `@markupai/sidebar-adapter` to **^1.4.0** and composes the reference with `buildDocumentReference` instead of sending the raw value, so validation and idempotency are consistent with every other integration.
- **Prefix choice: `vscode` (new).** None of the existing prefixes (`gdocs`, `word`, `heretto`, `madcapflare`, `ixiasoft`, `url`) fits an editor-local file, and the ticket explicitly allows introducing a platform prefix without an adapter release. There is no cross-surface counterpart to correlate against — a workspace file isn't reachable from the Chrome extension — so, as with `figma`, the prefix is adopted for consistency: grouping a user's work on a document works regardless; only cross-product correlation is out of scope.
- **Id choice: `document.uri.toString()`** — the same value the extension already keys its check sessions on. It is stable across close/reopen of the same file (a `file:` URI has no volatile query parameters), satisfying the ticket's stability rule.
- The reference is byte-identical for a whole-document check and a selection check: both flow through the single `getContent` path in `sidebarBridge.ts`, and a new test pins that invariant. Example value now sent: `vscode:file:///Users/me/docs/guide.md`.

## Migration note — coordinate before releasing

This changes the value sent as `document_ref`, which creates new rows in `document_registry` and breaks per-document continuity with this integration's historical data (a one-time re-key). Per the ticket:

- Agree the cutover with data engineering before release, so reporting expects the discontinuity.
- Ship in a **single release** — no partial rollout; a mixed population produces two references for one document simultaneously.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run type-check`, `npm run lint:check`, `npm run format:check` — clean
- [x] `npm test` — 86 tests pass (7 files), including two new assertions: the exact `vscode:<uri>` value satisfies `isDocumentReference`, and `getSelectedContent` returns a reference byte-identical to `getContent`'s
- [x] `npm run compile` — all three esbuild bundles build
- [ ] Data engineering: confirm the new references land under this integration's `integration_id` after release


[INT-692]: https://markup-ai.atlassian.net/browse/INT-692?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
## The finding that had nothing behind it

gate-64 recognised the ADR-040 autoload prelude only as a **quoted literal inside the call parentheses**:

```php
\OC_App::registerAutoloading('openregister', $path);              // accepted
\OC_App::registerAutoloading(self::OPENREGISTER_APP_ID, $path);   // REJECTED
```

The second is the same call with the app id given a name, four lines below `private const OPENREGISTER_APP_ID = 'openregister';`. doriath writes it that way — and gate-64 reported it as an AppHost adoption with **no** prelude, with the prelude present, correct, and unit-tested.

Measured on doriath#163: `FAIL — 2 AppHost adoption(s) with no OpenRegister autoload prelude`.

A gate that fails the tidier spelling of the thing it is asking for is not reporting a defect. It teaches people to write the untidy spelling, and it spends the reader's attention on nothing.

## The fix, and why it does not go blind

Resolution is deliberately **shallow and literal**: a name counts only when the same source blob binds it to the exact string `'openregister'` — via `const`, `define()`, or a plain variable. Imports are not followed, and **a name that cannot be seen bound is not accepted**.

That last property is the whole design. "Accept any argument" would clear doriath and blind the gate in the same stroke, so two of the four new tests exist to fail in exactly that direction.

| test | direction |
|---|---|
| `test_named_constant_bound_to_openregister_is_GREEN` | doriath's shape passes |
| `test_variable_and_define_spellings_are_accepted` | the other two bindings |
| `test_constant_bound_to_another_app_still_FAILS` | `registerAutoloading()` for a **different** app is not a prelude |
| `test_unknown_constant_still_FAILS` | an unresolvable name is not taken on trust |

### Mutants — disjoint sets, both directions

| mutant | tests turned red |
|---|---|
| accept any argument name | the 2 discriminators |
| resolve nothing (regression to the bug) | the 2 acceptance tests |

## Measured against the real trees

This is what settles it — the gate must lose the false positive **and keep both true positives**.

| repo | gate-64 @ `main` | with this fix | |
|---|---|---|---|
| doriath | `rc=1` FAIL | `rc=0` PASS | false positive cleared |
| scholiq | `rc=1` FAIL | `rc=1` FAIL | real defect, still caught |
| openbuild | `rc=1` FAIL | `rc=1` FAIL | real defect, still caught |

scholiq and openbuild genuinely have no prelude, and openbuild is the acute one: its `class_exists(Bootstrap::class)` guard answers **false** on a perfectly healthy instance, because `openbuild` sorts before `openregister` and `Coordinator::registerApps()` registers autoloading one app at a time. So `Bootstrap::register()` has apparently never run there, and its generic controllers, install repair steps and deep-link listener are silently absent. Those are fixed in their own repos, not here.

⚠️ Note on my own method: my first before/after table was **wrong in the safe-looking direction** — I copied the "baseline" helper *after* patching it, so both columns ran the fixed matcher and doriath appeared to pass on `main`. The table above is re-measured against `git show origin/main:` and the md5sums were checked. A baseline captured after the edit is not a baseline.

18 gate-64 tests pass.

author: helmihyo
body:
Adds French, German, Swedish, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Norwegian Bokmål and Danish, bringing SH-RPi level with HALPI2 and HALMET. Nine languages, 117 pages.

## The glossaries are HALPI2's, and that was measured

All three products are Hat Labs boards, so either sibling glossary was a candidate. Counting decided it: HALMET's additions — analog input, digital input, constant current, pull-up, galvanic isolation — occur **zero** times in the SH-RPi documentation, while HALPI2's power vocabulary occurs throughout (supercapacitor 23, daemon 26, watchdog 13, blackout 4).

Each glossary adds 61–86 rows for stacking boards on a Pi and for supercapacitor hold-up, and keeps every inherited typography rule. Nine navigation labels came back diverging from the siblings for no reason and were aligned to them.

`tutorials/openplotter-server/index.md` is untranslated, as in the Finnish branch: it warns it is out of date for v2 hardware and its body renders at 30% opacity. `translation_status.py` reports `missing=1` rather than hiding the gap.

## Verification

| | |
|:--|:--|
| Structure vs. the English source | 0 deviations across 117 pages |
| **15 safety figures × 10 languages** | all present |
| `mkdocs build --strict` | clean |
| `check_anchors.py` | all anchors resolve |
| `check_typography.py` | clean in all nine |
| `check_glossary.py` | clean in all nine |
| `translation_status.py` | `current=13` in all nine |
| **Passages read against English** | **4545** |

The safety figures were checked by name rather than by diffing every numeral: the input ranges, the three current limits, the 8.0/5.0 V thresholds, the 4 A fuse, the 33 V suppressor, the 70 s hold-up, the 10 s watchdog. A general numeric diff produced seven "differences" that were all artifacts — identifiers like `I2C` and `CAN0`, and one bug in the comparison itself.

## Review

Two semantic defects survived adversarial verification, both misinformation rather than hardware risk:

- **Dutch** called the power source `storingsgevoelig` — *susceptible to interference* — where the English says *noisy*, meaning it emits interference. The sentence had the SH-RPi protecting the Pi from a source that is itself a victim.
- **Norwegian** softened *Not functional in v2.0.0 hardware* to `ikke i bruk`, which describes a header left unpopulated rather than one that is defective. The errata page says the pins are shorted to ground and inoperable.

The measurement phase found more, and **the largest was in the Finnish** — an English heading left untranslated in the Italian, a percent sign without its space in Dutch, two German proper names carrying English spacing into a compound, and four Finnish rules the glossary states and the pages broke.

## The finding worth reading

The Finnish used `power supply` and `power source` the opposite way round from the glossary, plus a third word `teholähde`. **`check_glossary.py` was green throughout**, because both prescribed words appear on the Finnish side — only their English partners were swapped. That is exactly the blind spot the script's own docstring admits to, seen in the wild for the first time.

I argued from how the pages read, and from how HALPI2's Finnish reads, that the rows were inverted and the prose was right. **Matti ruled the other way**: the rows stand, the pages follow. Fourteen occurrences across four pages now do, `teholähde` is gone, and one exception is recorded rather than forced — *DC power source* stays `tasavirtalähde`, because `tasavirransyöttö` is not a Finnish word.

## One fix to the shared glossary checker

The word boundary added earlier — so Finnish `virtalähde` would not count as used merely because `vakiovirtalähde` appears — was reporting correct Danish prose as a violation, because a compounding language legitimately puts a short common noun at the end of a compound: `pakke` inside `salgspakke` is the same concept. The boundary now applies only to terms of eight characters or more.

Verified both ways: `virtalähde` is still not matched inside `vakiovirtalähteen`, `pakke` is now matched inside `salgspakken`, and all nine languages in halpi2 and all nine in halmet return unchanged verdicts.

## Known, and not addressed here

**hatlabs/halpi2 has the same Finnish inconsistency.** Its `getting-started.md` renders `- 12V or 24V power source` as `- 12 V:n tai 24 V:n virtalähde`, where its own glossary prescribes `virransyöttö`. Its checker is green for the same reason. That is a separate change in a separate repository and is not touched here.

Two English defects remain open in #25: the second stage converter called both *buck* and *boost*, and Linux instructions asking for Homebrew. The translations reproduce the English as written in both places.

## What this needs from a reader

**Nobody who reads these eight languages has read them.** Every mechanical check passes, and none of them can tell whether a sentence about supercapacitor thresholds says the right thing about supercapacitor thresholds. Corrections belong in `solutions/translation/<language>-glossary.md` as well as in the pages.

author: smaug123
body:
CoreLib's `MetadataImport.GetMethodSignature` dispatches on the token kind: MethodDef tokens go to `GetSigOfMethodDef` (already implemented), MemberRef tokens go to `GetMemberRefProps`, which was unimplemented.

## Implementation

The InternalCall's contract is "raw signature blob bytes for the supplied MemberRef token" — CoreCLR's FCall forwards to `IMDInternalImport::GetNameAndSigOfMemberRef` and discards the name.

PawPrint decodes MemberRef signatures eagerly into `MemberSignature` when an assembly is read, so the unparsed blob isn't retained. Two options for recovering it:

1. **Read it back from the metadata reader on demand.** This is what `GetSigOfMethodDef` already does for MethodDef blobs, so it keeps the two siblings symmetric and is trivially reversible.
2. **Store the raw blob on `MemberReference<'parent>` at parse time.** Preserves more information at the domain level, but grows a hot domain type and costs memory for every MemberRef row in every loaded assembly, to serve one InternalCall.

I took (1). If a future caller needs blobs often enough that the re-read matters, (2) is a mechanical change from here.

author: adriangohjw
body:
## Problem

_What problem are you trying to solve? What issue does this close?_

Hardens the dependency supply chain across pnpm, CI/CD, and Docker — closing gaps against typosquatting, malicious postinstall scripts, unpinned CI actions, and maintainer-credential compromise (e.g. the Aug 2025 s1ngularity attack, the chalk/debug incident).

## Solution

_How did you solve the problem?_

**pnpm (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`)**:

- Explicit `registries.default` (no silent registry redirection via global config/env)
- `minimumReleaseAge: 1440` (24h cooldown on new versions, direct + transitive) + `minimumReleaseAgeIgnoreMissingTime: false`
- `blockExoticSubdeps: true` (no git/tarball URLs for transitive deps)
- `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` + `trustPolicyIgnoreAfter: 525600` — fails install if a package's publishing-trust level drops vs. its own prior releases
- `overrides.uuid: ^11.1.1` — `aws-sdk`/`sequelize` both hard-pin a vulnerable `uuid@8.x` internally (GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq); verified both only use the stable named `v1`/`v4` exports
- Documented `trustPolicyExclude` for `ua-parser-js@0.7.41` after investigating: same maintainer/signing key as the provenance-enabled 2.x line, just published via the legacy 0.7.x line's non-CI path — not a repeat of the Oct 2021 takeover (which was `0.7.29`/`0.8.0`/`1.0.0`)

**CI (`.github/workflows/*.yml`)**:

- Every third-party GitHub Action pinned to a full commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment (Dependabot's `github-actions` updater reads this to keep pins fresh)
- Least-privilege `permissions: contents: read` added to every workflow
- `audit-signatures` job extended into a `supply-chain` job: `pnpm audit signatures` + `pnpm sbom --sbom-format cyclonedx` uploaded as a build artifact
- Replaced `datadog/test-visibility-github-action@v2` (was tracking a mutable **branch**, not a tag) with a pin to its latest actual release tag

**Docker**:

- Base images (`Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dev`, `Dockerfile.maildev-logging`, `docker-compose.yml` services) pinned by digest instead of a mutable tag
- The IBM Plex font `wget` in `Dockerfile`/`Dockerfile.dev` pinned to a commit (was `master`) with a hardcoded sha256 checksum, since IBM publishes none

**Unpinned ad-hoc execution**:

- `npx sequelize-cli` / `npx lint-staged` / `npx commitlint` / `npx @datadog/datadog-ci` replaced with pinned devDependencies invoked via `pnpm exec`, across `package.json` scripts, husky hooks, and CI

**Dependabot**:

- Added `github-actions` and `docker` ecosystems (monthly) so the new SHA/digest pins get refreshed automatically instead of going stale forever

**Misc**: added `"private": true` to `package.json`.

## Tests

_What tests should be run to confirm functionality?_

- `pnpm install` — passes the new supply-chain policy checks (`trustPolicy`, `minimumReleaseAge`)
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check` — all pass
- `pnpm run test` — 58 suites / 481 tests pass
- `pnpm audit signatures` — all 1779 packages verified
- CI: the new `supply-chain` job should run `pnpm audit signatures` and produce an `sbom` artifact

Not verified in this environment (sandboxed, no working Docker daemon): an actual `docker build`. Base image digests and the font checksum were independently verified against the registry/commit rather than via a real build — worth a real build check before merge.

## Before & After Screenshots

N/A — this PR touches config/CI/Docker/dependency-pinning only, no UI changes.

## Deploy Notes

_Notes regarding deployment of the contained body of work. These should note any new dependencies, new scripts, etc._

**New dev dependencies**:

- `sequelize-cli@6.6.5` : previously invoked via unpinned `npx`; now a pinned devDependency
- `@datadog/datadog-ci@5.22.0` : previously invoked via unpinned `npx` in CI; now a pinned devDependency

**Config changes**:

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` : new supply-chain policy settings (see Solution above) — first `pnpm install` after this merges will re-verify the whole lockfile against these policies
- `.github/dependabot.yml` : two new ecosystems (`github-actions`, `docker`)

author: ulfdahlstrand
body:
Closes #89. The design is yours; this is it built.

## The shape

```
persons              (id, club_id, created_at)          -- anchor, nothing else
person_personal_ids  (person_id PK, club_id, personal_id, created_at)
                     UNIQUE (club_id, personal_id)
person_external_ids  (id, person_id, club_id, source, external_id, created_at)
                     UNIQUE (club_id, source, external_id)
```

`person_id` **as the primary key** of `person_personal_ids` is what makes the personnummer one per person — by construction, not by a check that can be forgotten. `person_external_ids` is deliberately *not* unique on `(person_id, source)`: several rows per person is the point.

Both children carry `club_id` and reach `persons` through a composite foreign key, so a child row cannot drift into another tenant (ADR-003). `persons` gains `UNIQUE (id, club_id)` to make that possible — the same trick `members` already uses for its team.

**A person no longer needs a personnummer to exist.** That is what makes this worth doing: 13 of 49 members in your database have none, including all of P14, and they are exactly the people name matching keeps failing on.

## Source names

Two SportAdmin identifiers are not one namespace, and they do not join:

| source | what | from |
|---|---|---|
| `sportadmin` | internal member id (`showProfileCard(4214437)`) | the närvaro page |
| `sportadmin-medlemsnr` | the club's own membership number | `Medlems Nr` in the export |

## ADR-022's gate survives

`personal-id.ts` is still the only module that reads or writes a personnummer — `grep person_personal_ids` returns it and nothing else. Arguably the gate got stronger: a `selectAll()` on `persons` can no longer carry the number either.

`external-ids.ts` is deliberately **not** gated. An external id identifies nobody outside the system that issued it; it is a row number in someone else's database, not a fact about a human, and matching on it has to be cheap.

## What it fixes

The attendance import now matches on the id first and falls back to name — and **records the id when the name is what matched**. So the first import of a team teaches the club who everybody is, and every import after that is exact.

A test spells the surname wrong on the second run and it still finds the same member. That is the shape of the failure that produced 36 duplicate members.

## Migration verified against real data

Not just against an empty test database. A copy of the development database, with 36 real personnummer:

- **up** — 36 persons, 36 personal ids moved, 36 still unique, 36 members still linked, `persons` down to `id, club_id, created_at`
- **down** — 36 back on `persons`, still unique

Round trip, nothing lost. The copy was dropped afterwards.

## Also here

author: marcelkarras
body:
One rule, reaching every process: **an agent may state only what it has actually observed.** The plugin previously carried only scattered anti-fabrication language — wargame `RECON NEEDED`, verify-feature evidence planes, the Phase 6 witness cross-check — with no common origin.

## Source of truth

`docs/evidence-discipline.md` states six rules: no unobserved assertion; cite the observation; mark the unverifiable as unverified; settle assumptions before acting; never invent an identifier; never restate a result this session did not produce.

It lives under `docs/` on purpose. `manifestRuntimeEntries` in `hooks/lib/session-control-core-v1.js` folds `hooks`, `agents`, `skills`, `docs` and `templates` into the Session Control runtime digest — a top-level `rules/` directory would have left the declared source of truth the one normative surface an installed-plugin edit could change undetected.

## Three carriers, each covering a hole the others leave

| Carrier | Reaches | Hole it covers |
|---|---|---|
| `hooks/session-start-evidence-discipline.sh` | main thread on every `SessionStart` (incl. `resume`/`compact`), every subagent on `SubagentStart` | free-form work that never invokes a skill; context lost to a compaction |
| `agents/*.md` (6) | every spawned agent | a child whose hook context is advisory or absent |
| `skills/*/SKILL.md` (22) | every invoked workflow | a session started before the plugin was installed or updated |

The hook **reads the canonical block at run time** instead of duplicating it, so it cannot drift when the rule is reworded, and it refuses a symlinked rule file. It consults no config and honors no opt-out flag — `hooks.sessionBanner:false`, or disabling every other hook, does not silence it. It fails silent on an unknown event, a malformed payload, a missing `node`, or an unreadable block, so an always-on hook can never block a prompt or a spawn. The one deliberate non-silent branch is the shared plugin-root guard, hardened here with `CDPATH=` and `--`.

It is the only **advisory** hook without a config flag; the other three un-flagged hooks are enforcement hooks that must not be disableable.

## The block deliberately names no file

A `reviewer-readonly-v1` subagent resolves tool paths against the **project** root, not the plugin root, so a pointer inside the block could only ever resolve into the repository under review — letting a hostile repo reviewed through a team review plant that path and have its own text ingested as the authoritative rule. The two leased `evidence-worker-v1` agents would additionally burn a bounded turn on a read their lease denies. The block therefore declares itself complete and forbids any workspace file claiming to be the rule from overriding it.

## Enforcement

`tests/structure/test-evidence-discipline.sh` (24 checks) pins all three carriers and fails when a **newly added agent or skill omits the block** — the point is that the next surface cannot ship without the rule.

Anti-vacuity is pinned as hard as the feature itself: extraction hard-aborts rather than degrading to an empty pattern that would match any blank line across all 28 files; the carrier predicate is exercised against missing, paraphrased and unterminated fixtures; and the content assertions run against the hook's **emitted context**, not its source text, so replacing the directive with a placeholder cannot leave the suite green.

The tdd skill's pinned line cap moves 430 → 433 in the three tests that carry that constant, by the size of the mandatory block, so the previous headroom is preserved rather than consumed.

## Drive-by fix

`tests/structure/test-chain-recover.sh` was added without a classification in the runner's suite inventory. `tests/run-all.sh` validates that every structure test on disk is classified **before it runs anything**, so the whole runner aborted with `suite classification inventory is incomplete; refusing execution` and not a single suite executed — on `main` as well. Registering it is what made verifying this change possible at all.

## Verification

`bash tests/run-all.sh --ci` — **122 passed / 0 failed / 0 hung / 0 blocked**, exit 0, on the exact tree in this PR.

Review chain: five parallel aspects → judge second pass → consume-mode reviewer → self-review. Two fix rounds, converged at PASS with zero unresolved findings. The chain caught, among others: the digest-coverage gap that moved the file to `docs/`; a 29th independently-authored copy of the rule inside the hook; the hostile-repo pointer; and two false universal claims I had written into the README of the feature about not making unverified claims.

**Not covered:** no Promptfoo eval exists for this. The structure test proves *delivery* — text present, wired, injected, non-drifting. It does not prove *effect*, i.e. that an injected directive measurably changes model behavior. `evals/context-nudge-reaction/` is the precedent for such an eval; building one is follow-up work and costs API credits (local-only, never run in CI).

author: danielpolowork
body:
## Summary

Adds `egl-utils-js/text` — `truncate`, `wrapText`, and `fixedWidth` — the first item of
the spec-02 wave. Pure string shaping measured in UTF-16 code units, on its own
Node-safe entry so the root bundle is untouched.

## Motivation

ROADMAP 9.1, spec 02 §2 F26–F28. Applications keep re-implementing these three helpers,
and each copy re-discovers the same edge cases: a marker pushing the result past the very
budget it was supposed to respect, a re-truncated string collecting a second ellipsis, a
cut landing between the halves of a surrogate pair and rendering as mojibake, a column
helper that returns *approximately* the requested width and leaves the table ragged.

## Changes

- **New `/text` entry** with three pure functions:
  - `truncate(str, maxLength, {ellipsis, position})` — marker counts inside the budget,
    returns a fitting string unchanged (so it is idempotent), truncates the ellipsis
    itself when the budget cannot hold it, and supports keep-the-end truncation.
  - `wrapText(str, width, {breakLongWords})` — greedy wrap; whitespace runs collapse,
    existing line breaks survive as paragraph boundaries (re-wrapping at the same width
    is a no-op), long words overflow their own line unless breaking is requested.
  - `fixedWidth(str, width, {align, truncate, pad})` — **exactly** `width` code units for
    any input; left/right/center alignment, multi-character pad, either truncation side.
- **Subpath wiring** — the four coordinated edits: `package.json` `exports`,
  `tsup.config.js` `entry`, `typedoc.json` `entryPoints`, `.size-limit.json` (one
  whole-entry row + one scenario row per function).
- **Spec amendments in the same PR** (AGENTS.md §5 divergence rule): F26 now states the
  at-most budget with its surrogate exception, the ellipsis-truncation rule, and
  idempotence; F27 states whitespace collapsing, paragraph preservation, and the
  narrower-than-one-code-point overflow rule. NFR-08 now says a new entry's budget is set
  from its **landing measurement** plus headroom, and records `/text` at 837 B — the
  0.8 kB figure it replaces was written before any code existed and was never measured.
  Consolidating the three near-identical enum checks into one helper recovered 4 B, which
  is what confirmed the estimate was simply low rather than the implementation bloated.
- **ADR-0019** settles the two wave-wide questions this item forced (below).
- README usage subsection, CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`, changeset (`minor`), journal
  checkpoint, ROADMAP checkbox + spec-02 coverage glyphs.

## Design Patterns

None — three pure functions; no classical pattern applies and none was forced. The
wave's pattern adoptions (Interpreter, Strategy, Repository) arrive with the items that
genuinely exercise them.

The two contracts this item does fix are recorded in
[ADR-0019](docs/adr/0019-subpath-family-and-code-unit-text-semantics.md):

1. **Capability groups get their own Node-safe subpath entries, not root exports.** The
   root has ~0.9 kB of headroom under the frozen 6 kB NFR-01 ceiling; spending it on
   three optional groups would have forced a ceiling renegotiation to avoid a design
   decision. The four-edit wiring quadruple is now the checklist `/net`, `/table`, and
   `/logging` follow.
2. **Length means UTF-16 code units, and no helper ever emits a lone surrogate.** Code
   units because that is what `String.length` reports, so caller-side column math agrees
   with the library; code points and graphemes both silently disagree with it. A cut that
   would split a surrogate pair drops the pair — `fixedWidth` keeps its exact-width
   promise (padding absorbs the freed unit), so `truncate` is the one that guarantees *at
   most* `maxLength`. Graphemes and East-Asian display width are explicitly out of scope,
   with the reasoning recorded rather than left to be rediscovered.

## Verification

- [x] Builds cleanly on the full CI matrix (Linux (Node.js 18, 20, 22))
- [x] Unit tests pass; new/changed behavior covered (≥ 95% line) — 48 new tests
      (37 examples + 11 property laws); repo-wide 646 tests, **100% lines and 100%
      branches** on `text.js` and on every other module
- [x] `Prettier` clean; `ESLint (flat config) + tsc --noEmit with checkJs (JSDoc type-check)` clean on the diff
- [x] ESLint --max-warnings 0; vitest --detectOpenHandles (leak/handle) green (where applicable)
- [ ] Benchmark numbers attached (when perf-relevant) — not perf-relevant; spec 02 §3
      explicitly opts this wave out of NFR-04 parity claims
- [x] `python tools/consistency_lint.py` passes

Also green: `pnpm docs:api` (typedoc warning-free), `pnpm check:api-floor` (this entry
adds **no** platform globals — pure ECMAScript built-ins), `pnpm check:version`,
`publint --strict`, `attw --profile node16`, `agadoo`, zero-runtime-deps.

**Sizes.** Whole entry 837 B (budget 0.9 kB). Per-import: `truncate` 374 B, `wrapText`
476 B, `fixedWidth` 464 B — each far under the 1 kB clause, which also demonstrates the
entry shakes properly rather than shipping as one blob.

## Documentation Impact

- [x] README.md updated (if user-facing surface changed) — new *Text shaping* subsection
- [x] ROADMAP.md checkbox flipped — 9.1 done; spec-02 coverage rows now 🚧
- [x] ADR added/updated — ADR-0019 + index row
- [ ] docs/patterns/README.md updated — no pattern adopted, refined, or rejected here
- [x] Spec updated — F26/F27 tightened to the shipped behaviour, NFR-08 budget policy
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated (for user-visible changes) + changeset (`minor`)
- [x] PR metadata set — assignee (the owner), one type label, release milestone

## Lesson

Lesson: write per-entry size budgets as ceilings on a *landing measurement*, not as
pre-implementation predictions — an unmeasured estimate that turns out 5% low otherwise
invites shaving real code to defend a number nobody measured.

author: hamjina
body:
## 관련 이슈
closes #133

## 작업 내용

같은 사용자가 면접을 반복하면 이전 세션과 거의 같은 캐물지점·질문이 다시 생성됐습니다. 후보풀 추출과 여는 질문 생성이 해당 세션의 포트폴리오·JD 컨텍스트만 입력으로 받았기 때문입니다. 특히 여는 질문은 입력이 (axis, 직무, 연차, JD 키워드)뿐이라 반복 세션에서 거의 같은 문장이 나왔습니다.

이전 면접에서 **실제 출제된 질문 원문**을 프롬프트에 넘겨 같은 지점·같은 표현을 피하게 했습니다.

### 이력 조회 (`PriorQuestionReader`)
- 범위: 같은 **사용자 전체**(portfolioId 무관). 포트폴리오를 수정·재업로드하면 portfolioId가 바뀌는데, 이때가 바로 "같은 사람이 다시 면접 보는" 대표 케이스라 포트폴리오로 범위를 좁히면 중복 회피가 무력화됩니다.
- 대상: `COMPLETED` + `ABANDONED` 세션. 중단된 세션에서도 질문은 이미 사용자에게 노출·재생됐습니다.
- 데이터: `Question.content`만. 요약 질문(`turnLevel = 0`)은 고정 템플릿이라 제외했습니다.
- 상한: 최근 5개 세션, 질문 40개.

### 캐싱 (`PriorQuestionCache`)
여는 질문 생성은 라이브 턴마다 호출되므로, preload에서 한 번 조회해 Redis에 담아둡니다. 기존 `JdOpenerContextCache` 패턴을 그대로 따랐고 세션 종료 시 함께 정리합니다.

### 프롬프트 반영
`ProbeCandidateExtractor.extract`와 `QuestionTextGenerator.generateOpener`에 이력을 넘기고, 각 시스템 프롬프트에 회피 규칙을 한 줄씩 추가했습니다.

**이력은 시스템 프롬프트가 아니라 유저 메시지에 실었습니다.** 프롬프트 캐싱은 프리픽스 매칭이라 사용자별 이력을 시스템 프롬프트에 붙이면 지금 전 세션이 공유하는 정적 프리픽스가 세션 단위로 쪼개지고, 세션 첫 턴이 캐시 읽기(0.1배) 대신 쓰기(1.25배)가 됩니다. 턴 지연을 줄여온 #128과 정면으로 충돌합니다. 덧붙여 현재 모델 `claude-haiku-4-5`의 최소 캐시 가능 프리픽스는 4096 토큰인데, opener 시스템 프롬프트는 템플릿+axes.yaml(~3.5KB)로 미달이라 어차피 캐시가 잡히지 않습니다.

### 안전장치
이력 조회에 실패해도 preload 전체를 실패시키지 않고 빈 이력으로 진행합니다(기존 동작 유지).

## 범위 밖
- `LiveTurnAnalyzer`의 newProbes 생성 — 매 턴 프롬프트가 길어져 #128에서 줄인 턴 지연과 충돌
- 이전 세션 후보풀(`QuestionCandidate`) 참조 — `USED` 캐물지점은 실제 나간 질문과 1:1이라 정보가 겹치고, 후보풀을 쓰면 "노출된 것만 고르기"가 상태 필터에 의존하게 됩니다. 질문 원문은 존재 자체가 "출제됨"입니다.
- 중복 질문 하드 필터링 — 후보 고갈 위험이 있어 프롬프트 회피만 적용

## 테스트
- `./gradlew test` / `./gradlew integrationTest` 통과
- `PriorQuestionPersistenceAdapterIntegrationTest` — 상태 필터·현재 세션 제외·요약 질문 제외·세션 상한
- `PriorQuestionPromptSectionTest` — 이력 유무에 따른 유저 메시지 섹션 포함/생략
- `PriorQuestionDedupLlmE2eTest`(`llmE2eTest`) — 실제 Anthropic 호출로 확인. 이력을 넘기자 후보풀이 이미 물어본 분산락·응답 지연 지점에서 결제 재처리 배치(재시도 주기, 멱등키, 정산팀 협의) 쪽으로 이동했고, 여는 질문도 매 실행에서 각도가 바뀌었습니다.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **새 기능**
  * 최근 면접 질문 이력을 저장하고 다음 면접 생성 과정에서 활용합니다.
  * 이전 질문과 중복되지 않도록 새로운 질문 소재와 관점을 제안합니다.
  * 최근 완료·중단된 면접의 질문을 기반으로 개인화된 질문을 생성합니다.
  * 질문 이력은 일정 기간 보관되며, 면접 종료 또는 초기화 시 정리됩니다.

* **개선 사항**
  * 이전 질문 정보를 불러오지 못해도 면접 진행이 중단되지 않습니다.
  * 질문 이력 조회 시 현재 면접과 불필요한 질문은 제외됩니다.

## Summary
- configure an explicit 30-second SQLite busy timeout for Store connections
- add a real two-connection regression test that holds a write lock beyond the previous five-second default
- document the bounded contention policy

## Root cause
The Windows test runner exposed transient SQLite writer contention in concurrent_appends_get_distinct_seqs. One append returned SQLITE_BUSY before the contending writer released its lock.

## Verification
- confirmed the new test fails with SQLITE_BUSY before the production change
- cargo fmt --all

author: karthi012
body:
This PR adds support for the Cadence GEM Ethernet IP block as a reusable driver core.
  
  An Ethernet driver for this IP already exists in the tree, added by Immo Birnbaum, but its implementation is specific to the Xilinx SoC family.
  
  Since the underlying MAC is a licensed Cadence IP that other vendors also integrate, this PR splits the driver into two layers:
  
  - Core layer (drivers/ethernet/cdns_gem/eth_cdns_gem_core.c): the IP handling — descriptors, buffers, TX/RX paths, ISR and PHY link state  handling. This layer carries no SoC-specific knowledge.
  - SoC glue layer (eth_xlnx_cdns_gem.c): the Xilinx-specific integration — SLCR/CRL_APB TX clock divider programming and the clkc register region.
  
  With this split, any SoC integrating the Cadence GEM can reuse the driver by implementing only a small glue layer. The devicetree bindings are split along the same line (cdns,gem-common.yaml, included by xlnx,gem.yaml), with no changes to the xlnx,gem compatible, its properties or CONFIG_ETH_XLNX_GEM.

  The PR has been tested on digilent/zybo (DHCP and ping at 1 Gbit, no packet loss); the Zybo-specific enablement changes are included here as  well. That said, this PR still needs broader validation on the other boards using this driver, and review from the original author would be much appreciated.

  Note: the existing eth_xlnx_gem driver is intentionally not removed in this PR. Once the new structure has been tested and validated on all applicable boards, the old implementation can be removed in a follow-up.

author: sfoulad
body:
Enabling **Settings → System → Pre-release** did nothing to the Library update prompt.

"Check for Update" has always read that toggle — `OtaUpdater::checkForUpdate()` picks GitHub's full release list from it. But the Library path ignored it entirely and inferred the channel from whether the **running build** happened to have `-rc` in its version:

```cpp
if (strstr(CROSSPOINT_VERSION, "-rc") != nullptr) offer = newerOrNull(latest["rc"]);
```

So the two disagreed. A device on a **stable** build with Pre-release ticked was offered RC builds by Check for Update and **never** by Library — the toggle silently had no effect there. That's how this surfaced: the Library check looked broken while the manual one worked.

## Why it was written that way

The original reasoning (from the commit that added this) was that a device running a release had opted out of pre-releases *by doing so*, and a popup was not the place to change that. That holds only while there is no explicit opt-in — once the setting exists, **it is the opt-in**, and second-guessing it from the version string is what produced the inconsistency.

## Now

Channel comes from the setting. A device already on an `-rc` still gets rc offers whatever the toggle says — it is on that channel already, and the alternative strands it there with no route forward. The stable tag stays the fallback either way, which is what carries an RC device off a pre-release once the equal-numbered release lands.

The diagnostic line added in #94 now records the resolved channel too, since "rc names a newer build but this device is on stable" and "rc names nothing" both produce no popup and only the toggle separates them:

```
[FDT] firmware check: rc=v1.8.48-rc+… stable=v1.8.28 channel=pre -- none newer than 1.8.48-rc+…
```

## Test plan
- [x] `gh_release_rc` builds clean; `cppcheck` no defects; `clang-format` a no-op
- [ ] hardware, the case that was broken: on a **stable** build with Pre-release ticked, open Library — an RC newer than the running build should now be offered
- [ ] hardware: with Pre-release off on a stable build, Library must still never offer an RC
- [ ] hardware: the `firmware check:` line reports `channel=pre` / `channel=stable` matching the toggle

## 목적

`develop` 을 현재 `main` 과 동일한 상태로 되돌린다. `develop` 은 일회성 배포용이라 쌓인 커밋을 보존하지 않는다.

## 방법

`main` 에서 브랜치를 따 `git merge -s ours origin/develop` 했다. 머지 커밋은 **`main` 의 트리를 그대로 유지**하면서 `develop` 을 조상으로 포함하므로, 이 PR 을 머지하면 `develop` 이 fast-forward 되어 트리가 `main` 과 정확히 같아진다.

`git diff origin/main HEAD` 결과는 비어 있다.

force push 가 아니라 PR 로 처리하는 방식이라 `develop` 의 기존 이력 자체는 남는다. 트리만 `main` 과 같아진다.

## 영향

머지하면 `develop` 에 얹혀 있던 배포 커밋 `72d55d820d` (`fix(opencode): ensure_dev_server 가 기록된 커맨드에 고정되지 않는다`) 의 내용이 `develop` 에서 빠진다. 그 변경은 #208 로 `main` 에 들어가므로 유실되지 않는다.

배포 검증이 아직 안 끝났다면 이 PR 은 검증 후에 머지하면 된다.

author: itismyfield
body:
## Summary

- Five predicates that answer **"does this finished answer fit in one Discord message?"** compared `text.len()` — a Rust **byte** count — against `DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT`, which is Discord's **character** limit. Korean is 3 bytes per UTF-8 character, so every one of them flipped at ~**667 characters** instead of 2000. Commit 1 (`6cd2df545`) converted two of them onto a single shared, character-counting `needs_multiple_messages` helper; commit 2 (`e843e2036`) converted the remaining three and folded the two already-correct open-coded `char_count(...) <= DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT` budget checks onto the same helper, so the question now has exactly one definition (10 call sites, counted).
- **This is not a body-splitting defect.** `split_message` has counted characters since #4214 — its single-chunk test is `remaining_chars <= effective_limit` — so a 667..=1990-character Korean body yields exactly **one** chunk down either branch. What these predicates select is the **delivery path**: *edit the existing placeholder in place* vs *delete the placeholder and POST fresh messages*. Sending a single-message Korean answer down the second branch costs it its channel position, its reply anchor and its message id, and moves delivery-lease ownership to the chunk path. No content is lost or truncated by this defect.
- Residual, honestly out of scope and left for its own change: the remaining byte comparisons against the constant are **budget arithmetic** in panel/label composition (`single_message_panel.rs:122`, `:310`, `tmux_placeholder_suppression/mod.rs:72`, `:80`, `:88`). Those truncate **content** (a Korean panel body is cut at ~630 characters) — a different defect class, tracked as **#5177**.
- The change also corrects a false claim carried in the previous commit message and copied into the `needs_multiple_messages` doc comment ("that disagreement is not reachable in the send path" — it *is* reachable on the replace path), plus three stale byte-wording comments. No production predicate, branch or constant changed as a result of those corrections.

### The three predicates converted in commit 2

| Predicate | Live callers |
|---|---|
| `terminal_delivery_should_send_new_chunks` (`turn_bridge/terminal_delivery.rs:53`) | `turn_bridge/terminal_outcome_delivery.rs:402`; `turn_bridge/terminal_controller_cutover.rs:72`, `:98` |
| `watcher_should_send_ordered_new_chunks_for_terminal_fallback` (`tmux_watcher/session_bound_ack.rs:424`) | `tmux_watcher/terminal_direct_fallback.rs:122`, `:181`; `tmux_watcher/terminal_send.rs:85` |
| `done_result_requires_full_terminal_replay` (`turn_bridge/response_delivery.rs:88`) | `turn_bridge/stream_loop/content_arms.rs:362` |

A full `rg DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT` sweep found **no fourth** production comparison asking "does this answer fit one Discord message" in bytes.

### Known residual seam (unchanged, deliberate)

In the 1991..=2000-character band the predicate and the chunker genuinely disagree: `effective_limit = DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT - tag_overhead - 10`, and that 10-character code-fence reserve applies even to fence-free text. The predicate is deliberately **not** `split_message(text).len() > 1` — those texts really do fit one Discord message, and adopting the chunker as the predicate would push them down the multi-message path on every surface, including the three direct-POST callers that deliver them as one message today. The #3089 A0 characterization rejects that form for the same reason. On the replace path the disagreement costs one extra continuation message and a line break promoted to a message break — no truncation, no over-limit chunk, no rejected send.

## Test plan

Regression tests pin the Korean case at the **predicate** level in each newly converted module — never on a message/chunk count, which stays 1 whether or not the defect is present and so proves nothing. Each uses the oracle established in commit 1: a body that **is** over the limit in bytes (`assert!(body.len() > DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT)`) must still make the predicate return `false`. 900 Korean characters (2700 bytes) stay single-message; 2100 do not.

- [x] `cargo check --all-targets` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo doc --no-deps --lib` — 0 warnings
- [x] `scripts/ci-script-checks.sh` — pass
- [x] 6 module test suites — 269 passed, 0 failed
- [x] **Mutation M4 (predicate definition):** revert `needs_multiple_messages` in `formatting/delivery.rs:541` to `text.len() > DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT` (the original defect) → all **5** new tests **KILLED** by assertion, not by compile error:
  - `services::discord::session_relay_sink::tests::korean_answer_under_the_character_limit_stays_one_message`
  - `services::discord::standby_relay::tests::korean_answer_under_the_character_limit_stays_one_message`
  - `services::discord::tmux::tmux_watcher::session_bound_ack::tests::korean_answer_under_the_character_limit_stays_one_message`
  - `services::discord::turn_bridge::response_delivery::tests::korean_answer_under_the_character_limit_stays_one_message`
  - `services::discord::turn_bridge::terminal_delivery::tests::korean_answer_under_the_character_limit_stays_one_message`
- [x] **Mutations M1–M3 (call sites):** reverting each converted predicate individually is caught — `terminal_delivery.rs:53` by 4 tests, `session_bound_ack.rs:424` by 4, `response_delivery.rs:88` by 2. All assertion deaths.
- [x] `long_authoritative_done_after_rollover_replays_full_body` had a Korean fixture of 2891 bytes but only 1991 **characters** — it fit one Discord message and passed only because of the byte comparison. Its prefix grows from 220 to 240 repeats and a character-count precondition is asserted alongside the byte one. **No assertion was removed.**
- [x] `scripts/lib_test_inventory_manifest.txt` re-pinned for the five new tests: **+5 lines, −0**.

author: nikomoritz
body:
## What

Adds an opt-in `--thread-follow` / `BUZZ_ACP_THREAD_FOLLOW` flag to the ACP harness (mentions mode only). When enabled, the harness tracks the threads an agent participates in; replies in those threads then trigger turns **without a fresh @mention**. A human tags the agent once at the top of a thread and keeps talking.

## Why

Today every message to a managed agent needs an explicit @mention, even mid-conversation in a thread the agent itself is driving. That makes agent threads feel like filling out a form rather than talking to a teammate. (Motivated by real usage in our community — the question "warum muss ich dich in deinem eigenen Thread jedes Mal taggen?" came from our founder within the first day of use.)

## How

- **Subscription:** in mentions mode with the flag set, per-channel subscriptions drop the server-side `#p` filter; the mention gate is re-applied client-side. With the flag off (default), nothing changes — same REQ filters, same behavior.
- **Follow set:** new `thread_follow` module with a dependency-free bounded set (HashSet + VecDeque FIFO eviction, cap 1024). Roots are learned from (a) events that @mention the agent — after the respond-to author gate — and (b) self-authored replies, before the ignore-self drop.
- **Matching:** `filter::match_event` gains a `mention_exempt` parameter that waives `require_mention` when the event's NIP-10 thread root (marker `root` > `reply` > bare `e` tag) is in the follow set. Exempted events get prompt tag `thread-follow` so the prompt shows why the turn triggered.

## Safety / semantics

- The respond-to author gate is evaluated **before** the follow-set exemption and applies unchanged: in `owner-only` mode, only the owner's un-mentioned thread replies are admitted.
- `--thread-follow` warns and is ignored in `config` mode; it is a logged no-op in `all` mode.
- Follow set is in-memory: a restart forgets followed threads until the next mention (the mention catch-up pass repopulates active ones). Documented in the module docs; persistence felt like over-engineering for a first cut.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p buzz-acp` — 707 tests green (10 new: NIP-10 root extraction incl. marker precedence, follow-set insert/dedupe/eviction/clamp, p-tag check, mention-exempt match).
- `cargo clippy -p buzz-acp --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo check -p sprig -p buzz-cli -p buzz-relay` green.

## Follow-up (separate PR)

A Desktop per-agent toggle ("Follow threads") mapping to `BUZZ_ACP_THREAD_FOLLOW`, through the persona/managed-agents plumbing — kept out of this PR to keep the harness change reviewable on its own. Until then the flag is reachable via env for headless/self-hosted harnesses.

author: nunoamaral-hue
body:
## Summary

Fixes the GATE-10 runtime-certification failure. The backend readiness probe's default transport (`agent_health_probe._default_transport`) POSTed the signed NEGOTIATE to the **bare** `BETA_AGENT_BASE_URL`. The validation agent serves **exactly** `POST /provision` and answers any other path with `unknown_route` (404), so every probe was route-rejected and the agent could never reach `HEALTHY`. The provisioning transport (`beta_worker.make_http_transport`) always appended `/provision` correctly — only the probe transport had drifted.

## Fix

- New client-side helper `provision_url(base_url)` in **`mgmt_client.py`**. It lives on the client side (the agent is a server and never builds outbound URLs), so it stays **out of** the bundle-shared `mgmt_protocol.py` — **no agent/manifest/host impact**.
- Both backend transports now derive the URL from it. `make_http_transport`'s change is byte-identical to its prior inline `base_url.rstrip("/") + "/provision"`.
- `BETA_AGENT_BASE_URL` is **unchanged**.

## Tests (9 new)

`ProbeRouteContractTests` / `TransportRouteDriftGuardTests` / `ProbeCreatesNoValidationAttemptTests`:
- bare / trailing-slash / multi-slash base URL → `/provision` appended **exactly once**
- readiness probe completes a **signed NEGOTIATE via the real route → HEALTHY**
- PR#290 connect-timeout / read-timeout classifications **unchanged**
- probe issues **NEGOTIATE only** → no VALIDATE_LOGIN / MT5 / `BrokerAccountValidationAttempt` (DB-backed proof)
- **drift guard**: both transports build the identical URL (`== provision_url(base_url)`)

## Scope / safety

- Repository engineering only. **No migration.** Backend-only — no bundle/manifest/host change.
- Does **not** touch broker validation, MT5, `:8788`, or customer accounts.
- Route audit: no other caller posts to the bare agent root. Adversarial review (7 disproof lenses): **0 findings**.

## Verification

`make check` exit **0** — backend **2848 tests OK**, frontend lint **0 errors** (19 pre-existing warnings), build OK.

author: aravinds2511
body:
Fixes #2777

## Problem

`slither-read-storage` rejected any target that wasn't a `.sol` file or a
project directory. Feeding it a solc Standard JSON input file (as produced by
`solc --standard-json`, or hand-built, per the [Standard JSON input
format](https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/latest/using-the-compiler.html#input-description))
failed with:

```
slither.exceptions.SlitherError: Invalid compilation:
0424.json is not the expected format '.sol'
```

## Root cause

The error comes from crytic-compile's `Solc` platform, which only accepts
`.sol` files. crytic-compile already ships a `SolcStandardJson` platform
(`NAME = "Solc-json"`) that reads a Standard JSON input file directly, but
it's never auto-selected for `.json` targets — its `is_supported()` is
inherited unchanged from `Solc` (`target.endswith(".sol")`). The only way to
reach it today is the undocumented `--compile-force-framework solc-json` flag.

## Fix

`slither-read-storage`'s `main()` now checks whether the given target is a
`.json` file containing the two keys that define a solc Standard JSON input
(`"language"`, `"sources"`). If so, and the user hasn't already passed
`--compile-force-framework`, it's set to `solc-json` automatically. Detection
is safe on missing files, non-JSON files, and malformed JSON — it just
returns `False` and falls through to the original, clear error message.

Docs updated in `docs/src/tools/ReadStorage.md` to document the new
`contract_source` behavior and add a usage example.

## Testing

Added to `tests/tools/read-storage/test_read_storage.py`:

- `test_is_solc_standard_json` — unit tests of the detection helper (valid
  Standard JSON, non-standard JSON, non-JSON file, missing file, malformed
  JSON syntax).
- `test_read_storage_from_standard_json` — end-to-end test that runs the real
  `slither-read-storage` CLI once against a `.sol` file and once against an
  equivalent Standard JSON file with **no extra flags**, and asserts the
  resulting storage layouts are identical.

```
$ pytest tests/tools/read-storage/test_read_storage.py -k "standard_json" -v

tests/tools/read-storage/test_read_storage.py::test_is_solc_standard_json[StorageLayout.sol-False] PASSED
tests/tools/read-storage/test_read_storage.py::test_is_solc_standard_json[not_standard.json-False] PASSED
tests/tools/read-storage/test_read_storage.py::test_is_solc_standard_json[standard_json_input.json-True] PASSED
tests/tools/read-storage/test_read_storage.py::test_read_storage_from_standard_json PASSED

4 passed, 2 deselected in 1.31s
```

Manual verification, reproducing the exact scenario from the issue:

```
$ uv run slither-read-storage 0424.json --contract-name TestVariables --json out.json

INFO:Slither-read-storage:
Contract 'TestVariables'
TestVariables.x with type uint256 is located at slot: 0

INFO:Slither-read-storage:
Name: x
Type: uint256
Slot: 0

INFO:Slither-read-storage:
Contract 'TestVariables'
TestVariables.owner with type address is located at slot: 1

INFO:Slither-read-storage:
Name: owner
Type: address
Slot: 1

INFO:Slither-read-storage:
Contract 'TestVariables'
TestVariables.paused with type bool is located at slot: 1

INFO:Slither-read-storage:
Name: paused
Type: bool
Slot: 1

$ cat out.json

{
    "x": {
        "name": "x",
        "type_string": "uint256",
        "slot": 0,
        "size": 256,
        "offset": 0,
        "value": null,
        "elems": {}
    },
    "owner": {
        "name": "owner",
        "type_string": "address",
        "slot": 1,
        "size": 160,
        "offset": 0,
        "value": null,
        "elems": {}
    },
    "paused": {
        "name": "paused",
        "type_string": "bool",
        "slot": 1,
        "size": 8,
        "offset": 160,
        "value": null,
        "elems": {}
    }
}
```

No extra flags required — matches the exact command from the issue report.

## Scope note for maintainers

This fix is scoped to `slither-read-storage` only. A more general fix — giving
`SolcStandardJson.is_supported()` real content-based detection in
`crytic-compile` — would let every Slither tool accept Standard JSON targets
directly, not just `read_storage`. Happy to open a follow-up issue/PR there
if that's of interest.

author: garmstro
body:
Introduces per-user and per-IP rate limiting across all API and redirect endpoints using [slowapi](https://github.com/laurentS/slowapi) backed by in-memory storage.

## What changed

**New module `linkvault/rate_limit.py`** defines two `Limiter` instances:
- `limiter` — used on authenticated/management endpoints (links, analytics, users). Keys by a short SHA-256 hash of the Bearer token when present, falling back to client IP for unauthenticated paths like `/users/register`.
- `redirect_limiter` — used on the public `GET /{slug}` hot path, keyed by IP only with a higher default quota to avoid impacting normal traffic.

A shared `rate_limit_exceeded_handler` returns a consistent `{"error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "..."}` JSON body with a `Retry-After: 60` header on every 429.

**`linkvault/main.py`** wires up `SlowAPIMiddleware`, attaches the limiter to `app.state`, and registers the 429 handler.

**`linkvault/config.py`** adds two new settings:
- `RATE_LIMIT_API` (default `"200/minute"`) — applied to all API endpoints.
- `RATE_LIMIT_REDIRECT` (default `"300/minute"`) — applied to the redirect endpoint.

Both accept any `limits`-library format string and can be overridden via environment variables.

**All API routers** receive `@limiter.limit(...)` / `@redirect_limiter.limit(...)` decorators and a `request: Request` parameter (required by slowapi).

## Notable decisions

- **In-memory storage only** — no Redis/Memcached dependency. This means counters are not shared across multiple processes/replicas. Acceptable for the current single-process deployment; can be swapped to `redis://` by changing `storage_uri`.
- **Token hash as bucket key** — the key function hashes the raw Bearer token rather than looking up the user in the database, keeping the hot path free of DB round-trips. The 16-character hex prefix is collision-resistant enough for bucketing.
- **No default limits on the middleware** — every limit is applied via an explicit decorator so each endpoint's quota and key function are unambiguous and auditable.
- **`links.py` uses lambda wrappers** (`lambda: settings.RATE_LIMIT_API`) on some decorators to ensure the setting is read at call time rather than at import time, making test monkeypatching reliable. `delete_link` and the analytics/users routes use the value directly since slowapi also evaluates string limits at call time.
- **Test isolation** resets `_storage` between tests via `monkeypatch` and uses unique IP/token values per test to prevent counter bleed.

author: pher217
body:
## Goal

Give an agent a way to ask a **human** a question and get an answer **later**, without blocking
the agent's process — the gap between `consultum consult` (synchronous, model-to-model) and
`contrib/pair` (asynchronous, but assumes both sides are live sessions watching each other).
Neither fits an unattended agent escalating a judgment call to a human who might not look for
hours.

Design doc: `docs/human-inbox.md`. Operating manual: `contrib/inbox/SKILL.md`.

## Changes

- **`contrib/inbox/inbox.sh`** (new) — the channel itself. Verbs: `ask`, `list`, `show`, `check`,
  `wait`, `answer`, `root`, `close`, `prune`, `watch`. Mirrors `contrib/pair/pair.sh`'s idioms
  (`newid`, atomic `mv` publish, `chmod 700`, stdin/`--file`-only bodies, `die`/usage shape) as a
  sibling contrib tool, not a shared library.
- **`contrib/inbox/SKILL.md`** (new) — the `/inbox` skill operating manual.
- **`docs/human-inbox.md`** (new) — layout, root rationale, redaction, atomicity/concurrency,
  exit codes, the `set -e` trap on `check`'s exit 20, non-goals.
- **`test/inbox-channel.test.mjs`** (new) — 15 tests, `node --test`, matching
  `test/pair-channel.test.mjs`'s style.
- **`docs/threat-model.md`** — new adversary section **A8** (channel-specific risks: redaction-
  bypass-by-outage, a forged `answered` flag, the colliding-root data-loss scenario, a drifting
  hardcoded root, argv/traversal). No existing text altered.

## Approach

- **Root is `~/.claude/inbox` by default — a sibling of, not nested under, pair's
  `~/.claude/consult`.** `pair.sh close <topic>` (no `--force`) decides a channel is safe to
  delete by counting `request-*.md` files directly under the topic dir — a filename this tool
  never produces. Nesting the inbox there would make `pair.sh close inbox` see zero
  `request-*.md` files and `rm -rf` a populated inbox. **Reproduced live** (see Test Summary).
- **`inbox.sh root` is the single source of truth for the default path** — added mid-task after a
  real defect surfaced in a parallel worker (vigil) that had hardcoded its own guess at the
  default and silently drifted from it. `root` is a pure, side-effect-free query; external
  callers in other repos are documented (`SKILL.md`) to call it instead of hardcoding a copy.
- **Redaction is resolved, not vendored.** `ask` walks from the `consultum` binary on `PATH`
  (`command -v` → `readlink -f`, with a `python3 os.path.realpath` fallback for a `readlink`
  without `-f` → package root → `src/redact.js`) rather than importing `consultum` as a package
  (which doesn't resolve outside this repo) or copying the regexes. Any resolution failure
  hard-fails `ask` before any directory is created — a redaction control that silently no-ops is
  worse than no control.
- **Atomicity via same-filesystem `mv`, not `$TMPDIR`.** The working directory for a new question
  is built inside `open/` itself (`open/.tmp.$$-$RANDOM`), not under `$TMPDIR`, because a
  cross-filesystem `mv` is not atomic. `answer` uses `mkdir answer.claim` as an atomic
  exclusive-create lock before writing, so two concurrent `answer` calls can't both pass a
  check-then-write race.
- **`meta.json`'s `answered` field is a mirror, never the source of truth.** Every read path
  checks `[ -f answer.md ]` directly; a forged `meta.json` cannot fake an answer.

## Test Summary

- `bash -n contrib/inbox/inbox.sh` — clean.
- `node --test test/inbox-channel.test.mjs` — **15/15 pass**, covering: atomic ask + id-only
  stdout + 0700 mode; pending `check` exits exactly 20 with empty stdout; answer→check round
  trip; double-answer refusal with byte-for-byte original preserved; `wait` without `--timeout`
  exits 10 without polling (<1s); `wait --timeout 2` exits 21 in ~2s; secret redaction
  (`GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...` never reaches disk); missing-redactor hard-fail with zero files
  written; a forged `meta.json.answered` still reports pending; path-traversal `--slug` rejected;
  default root not nested under pair's; `close` moves the whole dir; `prune` only ever touches
  `closed/`; `root`'s two contracts (default path, no side effects; exact env override).
- `npm test` (full suite, typecheck + all tests) — **247 pass, 0 fail, 17 skipped** (pre-existing
  Windows-only skips), inbox tests included in the same run.
- **Mutation testing** on 4 guards — each confirmed to break its corresponding test when removed,
  then restored to green:
  - T2 (`check` always exits 0) → `not ok 2` ("check on an unanswered question exits 20...")
  - T4 (remove the overwrite guard in `answer`) → `not ok 4` ("answering twice refuses...")
  - T7 (skip `redact_stdin`, plain `cat`) → `not ok 7` ("ask redacts secrets before anything...")
  - T8 (missing-redactor made non-fatal, falls back to writing unredacted content) → `not ok 8`
    ("ask hard-fails and writes nothing when redaction cannot be resolved")
- **Live pair.sh safety assertion**, populated inbox at the *default* root under a throwaway
  `$HOME`:
  ```
  $ HOME=$DEMO_HOME bash contrib/inbox/inbox.sh ask --slug demo <<< "important question"
  # writes $DEMO_HOME/.claude/inbox/open/<id>/{question.md,meta.json}
  $ HOME=$DEMO_HOME bash contrib/pair/pair.sh close inbox
  pair: no channel 'inbox' — run: pair.sh init inbox
  exit=1
  # the inbox question is still on disk, untouched
  ```

## Files Changed

- `contrib/inbox/inbox.sh` — the channel CLI (new)
- `contrib/inbox/SKILL.md` — `/inbox` skill manual (new)
- `docs/human-inbox.md` — design doc (new)
- `test/inbox-channel.test.mjs` — test suite (new)
- `docs/threat-model.md` — new A8 adversary section (append-only)

author: s0up4200
body:
Trackers do not put the word boundaries of a show name where the scene name puts them, and the title check compared the two spellings literally. `Kiss.X.Sis` parses to the title `Kiss X Sis`, while Aither lists the same release as `KissXSis`. `Re.ZERO.Starting.Life.in.Another.World` parses to `Re ZERO Starting Life in Another World`, while Aither lists `Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-`, and `NormalizeForMatching` deletes the colon instead of turning it into a space, so the candidate normalizes to `rezero starting life in another world`. Both candidates were byte-identical in size and from the same release group, and both were rejected as `title mismatch`. Reported on Discord by Asinine

The title check compares sets of normalized titles and accepts any overlap, so the fix stores the space-free spelling of each title next to the normal one. The set only grows, so this cannot turn a match into a rejection. Distinct shows still stay apart once the spaces are gone, which the tests pin: `ef a tale of melodies` does not equal `ef a tale of memories and melodies`, and `fbi` does not equal `fbimostwanted`.
