author: qinqon
body:
Follow-up to #82940, which did the same for `main`. Moves the conformance jobs on `release-4.18` … `release-4.22` from the baremetalds workflow to the Azure conformance workflow, and narrows them to the tests relevant to this component.

## Current state

Every stable branch is red on every recent run:

| branch | recent runs | ODF step | total conformance failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| release-4.18 | 7/7 FAILURE | SUCCESS | 82 |
| release-4.19 | 9/9 FAILURE | SUCCESS | many |
| release-4.20 | 11/11 FAILURE | SUCCESS | 3 |
| release-4.21 | 3/3 FAILURE | SUCCESS | 3 |
| release-4.22 | 2/2 FAILURE | SUCCESS | 3 |

**Note the difference from #82940:** ODF is *not* broken here. `hypershift-kubevirt-baremetalds-odf` succeeds on every stable branch — the ODF-to-OCP skew that breaks `main` is specific to the `5.0` platform version, and ODF 4.20 works fine on 4.21/4.22.

What fails is the conformance step, on things unrelated to KCCM. release-4.22 is representative:

```
[sig-kubevirt] migration ... should maintain node readiness
[sig-node] Managed cluster should verify that nodes have no unexpected reboots [Late]
```

and 4.20/4.21 are `[sig-builds]` flakes plus the same migration test.

## What this changes

Each branch gets the same block as `main`:

```yaml
- as: hypershift-kubevirt-conformance-azure
  optional: true
  steps:
    cluster_profile: openshift-org-azure
    env:
      TEST_ARGS: --run \[sig-kubevirt\].services|LoadBalancer|terminating.endpoints
    workflow: hypershift-kubevirt-azure-conformance
```

The baremetalds-specific pins (`ODF_OPERATOR_SUB_CHANNEL`, `REDHAT_OPERATORS_INDEX_TAG`, `LVM_*`, `METALLB_*`, `LOCAL_STORAGE_*`) are dropped — the Azure workflow's `hypershift-kubevirt-install-odf` resolves the ODF catalog dynamically, which is what stops this rotting on each OCP bump.

## Test selection

The regex selects **13 tests**, covering all four scenarios that drive the cloud provider's `EnsureLoadBalancer`:

| # | test |
|---|---|
| 1-7 | `[sig-kubevirt] services` (2x LoadBalancer, 3x NodePort, 2x direct pod-to-pod) |
| 8-12 | `[sig-network] Services ... terminating endpoints` x5 |
| 13 | `[sig-network] Services ... on Type LoadBalancer` (multiprotocol) |

KCCM's node controller is covered structurally: without it, nodes keep the `node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized` taint and never go Ready, so `hypershift-kubevirt-health-check` fails before the tests start.

`[sig-kubevirt] migration` is deliberately excluded. The migration itself succeeds and `kubevirt-cloud-controller-manager` is not involved — but every in-guest client loses its API-server connection ~45s after its own migration completes with `http2: client connection lost` (matching client-go's HTTP/2 health check window), so the kubelet lease lapses and the node briefly flaps `NotReady`. Same symptom as OCPBUGS-57594 / OCPBUGS-57642 on other CNIs. The hypershift Azure periodics continue to run that test daily, so the signal is not lost.

## Expected outcome

I checked the 13 selected tests against the latest baremetalds run of each branch:

| branch | result for the 13 selected tests |
|---|---|
| release-4.19 | **13/13 pass** |
| release-4.20 | **13/13 pass** |
| release-4.21 | **13/13 pass** |
| release-4.22 | **13/13 pass** |
| release-4.18 | 8 pass / **5 fail** |

So 4.19-4.22 are expected to go green.

**release-4.18 is a known exception.** The five failures there are precisely the `[sig-kubevirt] services` tests that cross *guest* nodes, while both *infra-cluster* ones pass — a guest-to-guest networking problem, not test noise. This PR does not address it and the job is expected to stay red on 4.18 until that is investigated separately. I've kept 4.18 in scope so all branches share one configuration; happy to drop it if reviewers would rather not carry a known-red job.

## Notes for reviewers

- `hypershift-kubevirt-azure-conformance` is already exercised across this whole version range by the `openshift/hypershift` periodics, including a **SUCCESS** on release-4.18, so the workflow itself is proven on these payloads.
- On baremetalds the workflow set `TEST_SKIPS`, which makes the conformance chain append `--file /tmp/tests`. The Azure workflow sets no `TEST_SKIPS`, so `TEST_ARGS` passes straight through. Either way `--run` and `--file` AND together, so the selection is the same 13 tests.
- Jobs are `optional: true` while they establish a track record; they can be made blocking in a follow-up.
- `release-4.23` is left alone here — it still carries the stale `ODF 4.20` / `v4.20` pins and has no job history at all, so it needs its own look.
- The `openshift-priv` mirrors will be regenerated by automation.

/cc @openshift/openshift-team-hypershift


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- Moves KubeVirt conformance jobs for releases 4.18–4.22 from the bare-metal workflow to the Azure workflow.
- Uses the `openshift-org-azure` cluster profile and targets 13 KCCM load-balancer scenarios.
- Removes bare-metal-specific ODF, LVM, MetalLB, and local-storage settings.
- Keeps the jobs optional while gathering reliability data. Release 4.18 remains expected to fail because of guest-to-guest networking issues.

author: allens
body:
CLAUDE.md asserted:

> The pre-commit gate is format + lint + typecheck + test, mirroring CI.

**There was no gate.** No `.husky`, no hook anywhere — it was a convention followed by hand, phrased as a guarantee. This makes it true, and rewrites the sentence to describe what actually runs.

## No husky

Git has had `core.hooksPath` since 2.9, and `package.json`'s `prepare` points it at `.githooks` on `npm install` — which is the only thing husky was adding. Taking a dependency for that would sit badly with [ADR-0005](../blob/main/docs/adr/0005-builtins-over-dependencies.md).

`|| true` guards the case where git is absent or the tree isn't a repo, so a failing `prepare` can never break an install.

## Three checks, not four

`npm test` is ~12s, and **a gate slow enough to be routinely skipped with `--no-verify` is worse than no gate** — it makes the claim false again while still reading as true. CI runs all four and `ci-gate` is the required check; this only shortens the loop.

## The argument is tokens, not speed

Running the three by hand is three commands and three outputs to read before every commit. The hook collapses that into the commit itself, quiet on success. It also stops a bad commit reaching CI, which is the expensive round-trip.

And it can't be fooled the way manual verification can. **This session reported a green typecheck that had actually failed**, because `&& echo "TYPECHECK OK"` was chained off a pipe and `tail` always exits 0. A hook's exit code is git's.

That exact bug recurred while testing this PR — I wrote `git commit … | tail -6; echo "exit=$?"` and got `exit=0` from `tail` while the commit was correctly *blocked*. Verified properly instead: HEAD didn't move and the file stayed staged.

## Guards the fresh-worktree trap

Without `node_modules`, `typecheck` resolves up into the main checkout and fails on the builtin shims `jsconfig.json` maps away — which reads as a broken hook rather than a missing install. The hook says so explicitly.

## Verified

- **Blocks**: committing deliberately unformatted code was rejected; HEAD unmoved, file still staged.
- **Passes**: this PR's own commit went through the hook clean.
- Mode is `100755` in the index (set explicitly — a Windows checkout won't infer it).

author: pilote-design
body:
Le client a fourni son relevé financier Crisalid S31 (semaine du 27 juillet au 2 août 2026). Il a invalidé **trois hypothèses** du lot 103 et corrigé **une erreur de conception**. Le corpus de test n'est plus supposé : c'est ce document.

## D'abord, une fausse alerte que je corrige publiquement

J'ai signalé dans la PR #271 que `parseFinancier` lisait peut-être le nombre de tickets dix fois trop grand. **C'était faux, et le rapport hebdomadaire est juste.** Le format réel est `Nb Tickets 409 Nb Tickets 1` : la seconde colonne répète son LIBELLÉ, donc la capture s'arrête d'elle-même sur le « N ». J'avais raisonné sur un format supposé au lieu d'attendre le document. Rien à corriger, et une assertion verrouille désormais le cas.

## L'erreur de conception : les règlements ne retombent PAS sur le CA

Le lot 103 exigeait que la somme des modes de règlement égale le CA net, sinon quarantaine. **C'est faux par construction.** Le relevé donne :

| | |
|---|---|
| CA net | **18 347,75 €** |
| Encaissé | **17 456,55 €** |
| Écart | **891,20 €** |

Les 891,20 € sont les **comptes clients** : la marchandise est vendue, l'argent n'est pas rentré. Une boucherie qui livre des restaurants en aura toujours.

Et c'est une bonne nouvelle, parce que **pour la trésorerie c'est l'encaissé qui compte, pas le CA**. Le lot ajoute donc `encaisse_ttc` (migration `lot105_financier_encaisse`), et `app/api/tresorerie` compte l'encaissé quand il est confirmé, le CA seulement à défaut — en **comptant les journées** ainsi retombées au CA (`journees_au_ca`), puisque leur montant est alors surestimé de l'encours client. L'écart CA − encaissé est conservé : c'est l'encours, une donnée utile en soi.

## Les trois défauts du parseur, tous invisibles sans le document

Sur ce relevé, le lot 103 sortait **74 976 942,99 €**. La quarantaine a tenu — rien n'a été publié — mais rien n'était lu non plus.

1. **Un compteur précède le montant.** `CARTE 372 13980.83 €` : 372 est le nombre d'encaissements. Collés, ça donnait 37 213 980,83 €.
2. **Le bloc est imprimé deux fois** (deux colonnes de la mise en page). Additionner sans dédoublonner **double exactement** les encaissements — et un doublement exact ne se voit pas à l'œil sur un total. 6 lignes dédoublonnées sur 13.
3. **Les libellés sont ceux de la caisse** : `CARTE`, `CARTE_TR`, `TRESTAU`, `BON.ACHAT`, `ESPECES`, `CHEQUE`, `VIREMENT`. Pas « Carte bancaire », pas « Titres restaurant ». `CARTE_TR` et `TRESTAU` sont **tous les deux** des titres restaurant (75 + 181 = 256 €) — et `CARTE_TR` ne doit surtout pas tomber en carte bancaire.

## Le nouveau garde-fou : l'arithmétique du document

Le bloc porte son propre total, **avec un compteur** : `Total 463 17456.55 €`. On ne le cherche ni par sa position ni par un titre de section — les colonnes s'entremêlent. On le reconnaît à l'arithmétique : le bon total est celui dont le **compteur ET le montant** retombent sur les lignes dédoublonnées. Deux vérifications indépendantes. Sans total confirmé, rien n'est publié.

**Le compteur/montant a deux lectures légitimes et aucun indice local ne les départage** : « 1 984.70 » vaut 1 984,70 € ou 1 fois 984,70 €. Le parseur essaie les deux et laisse le total du document arbitrer. Une version intermédiaire recollait toujours les milliers et transformait `TRESTAU 20 181.00 €` en 20 181 € — vingt fois trop.

**Et le piège que ça a ouvert :** la lecture qui ne recolle pas les milliers lit `12 000.00` comme `000.00` = 0 €… et lit la ligne de total de la même façon. Zéro égale zéro, le compteur tombe juste, **une lecture entièrement fausse se confirmait elle-même**. Deux bornes : le total doit être strictement positif des deux côtés, et un mode encaissé N fois ne peut pas totaliser 0 € — cet invariant disqualifie la lecture avant toute comparaison.

## Preuves

- **81 assertions**, dont le corpus réel entier, rejouées **depuis le contenu extrait de la branche**.
- Lecture du vrai PDF de bout en bout (même chemin qu'en production, `pagerender` par coordonnées) : CA 18 347,75 € · encaissé 17 456,55 € · 463 encaissements · 409 tickets · panier 44,86 € · période 27/07 → 02/08 · CB 13 980,83 · espèces 1 338,11 · TR 256 · chèque 984,70 · virement 836,91 · bon d'achat 60.
- Typecheck **3, la baseline**. `next build` **exit 0** depuis la branche. Diff octet-à-octet **vide sur les 3 fichiers**.

## Ce qui reste ouvert

- **Le relevé fourni est HEBDOMADAIRE.** Le suivi quotidien attend un relevé d'une journée : à confirmer côté Crisalid que la période d'édition peut être réglée sur la journée, et à intégrer dans la règle de transfert automatique.
- **Les bons d'achat** (60 €) entrent dans le total encaissé de la caisse, mais ce n'est pas un flux bancaire — c'est un avoir consommé. La lecture les isole (`bon_achat`) ; à l'écran de décider s'ils comptent dans le solde.
- **Un seul document, une seule boutique.** Une autre caisse écrira d'autres libellés — la table des modes est faite pour s'étendre d'une ligne.

author: evgenii-bond
body:
## Why

Sui is removing JSON-RPC from the node binary in mid-October 2026, and the official fullnodes already answer every JSON-RPC method with `-32601 Method not found`; gRPC-Web is what they kept serving. The third-party JSON-RPC nodes the 1.3.0 failover leaned on are on the same clock.

## What

`@lombard.finance/sdk-sui` 1.3.0 -> **2.0.0** (breaking). Full CHANGELOG entry included.

### Breaking changes

- Every exported function that took a `client: SuiClient` (`claimLBTC`, `unstakeLBTC`, `getBalance`, `isBasculeCheckEnabled`, `getBasculeDepositStatus`) now takes a `client: SuiGrpcClient` from `@mysten/sui/grpc`; build one with `createSuiGrpcClient(network, options)`
- `createSuiClient`, `getDefaultSuiRpcUrls`, `resolveSuiRpcOptions`, `ISuiRpcOptions`, `ISuiNetworkRpcOptions` removed; replaced by the `*Grpc*` equivalents. Endpoint override key is `grpcUrls` (old `rpcUrls` values would not work: JSON-RPC nodes do not serve gRPC-Web, so reusing the key would break silently)
- `suiModule({ rpcUrls })` -> `suiModule({ grpcUrls })`
- `claimLBTC`/`unstakeLBTC` return the executed transaction in the gRPC core shape (`ISuiExecutedTransaction`); the `digest` field survives unchanged
- Endpoints with credentials or query strings are rejected at construction (WHATWG fetch refuses userinfo urls; the transport appends `/package.Service/Method` so a query string cannot survive)
- `@mysten/sui` dependency floor moved to `^1.45.2`, the first 1.x with the gRPC client

### Added

- `createSuiGrpcClient(network, { grpcUrls, timeoutMs })`: the 1.3.0 failover policy translated to gRPC-Web. Reads walk the endpoint list on transport errors, retryable statuses (403, 404, 405, 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504), a 200 that is not a gRPC-Web answer, and trailers-only UNIMPLEMENTED/INTERNAL/UNAVAILABLE/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. A submit is re-sent only on UNIMPLEMENTED, which proves nothing was executed. The last-good endpoint is remembered
- Default endpoints per network: official fullnodes first, then suiscan (the one public third-party node that answered a gRPC-Web probe; publicnode and blockvision do not speak it)
- `executeSignedTransaction` + `ISuiExecutedTransaction`, exported for consumers submitting wallet-signed bytes

### Changed

- Dynamic-field reads (treasury `bascule_check` flag, Bascule deposit table) derive the field object id locally, exactly as the chain does, and read the node-rendered JSON (`suix_getDynamicFieldObject` has no gRPC counterpart). Rendering differences are absorbed inside: flattened Move structs, u64 as string, enums as `{"@variant":"Name"}`
- Coin decimals come from `StateService.GetCoinInfo` instead of `suix_getCoinMetadata`; unpublished metadata still falls back to LBTC decimals, a node failure still throws

## Verification

- 67 unit tests pass (transport failover suite ported to gRPC semantics, bascule fixtures rebuilt on the wire shapes)
- 6 live tests pass against real nodes: `bascule_check` flag reads booleans off all three deployed treasuries (prod/testnet/stage) through the new code path; deposit-table field-id derivation matches the chain's own ids for real prod entries; both networks reachable over gRPC-Web
- `turbo build` + `turbo lint` + `tsc --noEmit` clean
- Independent review: no blockers, 5 minors, all fixed in this diff

## Consumer impact

The main app reads only `.digest` off claim/unstake results, which is unchanged. On the app-side bump, TS will point at every call site that must switch from the JSON-RPC client to `createSuiGrpcClient`.

author: kolaczek
body:
Adds a thin **progress bar along the bottom edge** of the streamed dash map (rider request, 8/2026).

## What it shows
- **Left (solid cyan-white):** how far along the whole trip the rider is.
- **Red tick:** current position (the split point).
- **Right (tinted):** the road ahead, coloured by a coarse traffic-delay level — green (clear) / amber (moderate) / red (heavy) / grey (unknown).

## How the traffic tint works — honest scope
The tint compares the **live Apple ETA** against the trip's own **baseline pace** (planned distance ÷ planned time, captured at start):

```
ratio = liveEta / (remainingDistance / baselineSpeed)
ratio >= 1.40 -> heavy (red)
ratio >= 1.15 -> moderate (amber)
else          -> clear (green)
```

⚠️ This is a **single overall level for the whole road ahead, NOT per-segment flow.** Apple `MKDirections` returns only a scalar `expectedTravelTime` — no geometry-resolved traffic. A true per-section yellow/red "jam at km 12" colouring is impossible on Apple and waits on a **BYOK live-traffic provider** (TomTom Traffic Flow — see `routing-engines.md`). Degenerate inputs (no baseline, ~arrived, non-finite ETA) render neutral grey so the bar never makes a false claim.

## Changes
- `DashNavSettings.progressBarEnabled` (default **ON**), store key `v9`→`v11`.
- `ActiveNavigator`: whole-trip distance+time baseline captured at start (single + multi-stop); `rideProgressFraction`; pure `trafficDelayLevel(...)` core + `TrafficDelayLevel` enum.
- `MapViewSource`: `RideProgress` state + `setRideProgress` + `drawProgressBar` (CPU CGContext, flat outer ctx, bottom edge).
- `ActiveNavLoop`: push progress each tick when enabled; clear when off / not navigating / stop.
- `StreamingView`: "Route progress" section with the toggle + honest caption.

## Tests
`tools/fake_dash/tests/test_route_progress.py` — 23 cases mirroring both pure cores (fraction clamps + delay thresholds/boundaries + degenerate inputs) with a Swift drift-guard. Full fake_dash suite green.

## Not verified
Swift not compiled — Linux host has no Xcode/MapKit toolchain. Logic verified via the Python mirror + diff review. **Run a local Xcode build before merge.**

Independent of #64 (live-traffic reroute); branched from `main`.

author: daimpad
body:
Nachlauf zu #93. Dort ist die SHACL-Validierung gelandet — ein rundum guter Beitrag von @jstet, der zwei echte Konformitätslücken geschlossen und die Prüfung dauerhaft in die CI geholt hat. Was fehlt, ist nur noch das Drumherum, damit die Arbeit auch bei den Nutzenden ankommt.

## Warum das nötig ist

#93 wurde ohne Versionserhöhung gemergt. Der Release-Workflow liest die Version aus dem Plugin-Header und überspringt den Bau, wenn dafür schon ein Release existiert — auf `main` stand weiterhin `2.35.3`. Die Änderung liegt also im Repository, erreicht aber keine einzige Installation, weil kein Release-ZIP entsteht.

- Version `2.35.4` in Plugin-Header, `ODW_VERSION`, README-Badge und CLAUDE.md
- CHANGELOG-Eintrag zur SHACL-Validierung, mit Nennung des Beitragenden

## Drei Kleinigkeiten aus dem Review von #93

Die waren dort als nicht blockierend eingestuft und sind offen geblieben:

- **`generate-fixtures.php`** legt sein Ausgabeverzeichnis jetzt mit `is_dir()`-Guard an, sodass wiederholte Läufe keine `mkdir(): File exists`-Warnung mehr erzeugen — und bricht mit Exit-Code 1 ab, wenn Verzeichnis oder Datei nicht schreibbar sind. Bisher wurde für jede Datei ein „✓" ausgegeben, auch für solche, die nie entstanden sind.
- Die Schreiblogik steckt in `write_fixture()`, statt an zwei Stellen dupliziert zu sein.
- **`validate.mjs`** nennt bei fehlendem Fixture den Grund und den nötigen Befehl, statt „(skipping)" zu melden und dann doch abzubrechen.

Das Falsch-Grün war mit #93 bereits geschlossen — der Validator bricht bei fehlendem Fixture ab. Hier geht es nur noch darum, dass auch der Generator selbst ehrlich meldet, was er getan hat.

## Verifiziert

- Generator zweimal hintereinander: warnungsfrei
- Abbruch mit Exit-Code 1 sowohl bei nicht anlegbarem Verzeichnis als auch bei fehlgeschlagenem Schreibvorgang
- `npm run test:shacl`: alle drei Fixtures `conforms`, 0 Violations (7 informative Deprecation-Warnungen wie erwartet)
- Fehlendes Fixture → Exit-Code 1
- PHPUnit 199 Tests grün, PHPCS 0 Verstöße, PHPStan Level 6 sauber

## What

- The consent banner is now a **blocking modal**: full-viewport backdrop (blur + dim), page scroll locked, no way to continue without choosing. Desktop shows a centered card, mobile a bottom sheet.
- **Generic copy** in both locales, matching what most sites show: "Wir verwenden Cookies / We use cookies" + the usual one-liner, with buttons "Alle akzeptieren / Accept all" and "Nur essenzielle Cookies / Essential only" (equal visual weight, no dark pattern).
- **Legal pages are exempt** (`/legal`, `/de/legal`): the modal links to the privacy policy, so that page must stay readable without a prior consent decision.
- Consent mechanics unchanged: same `vornac_consent_v1` key, default-deny stays, "Accept all" fires the `gtag('consent','update')` for all four signals.

## Why

The GA4 tag diagnosis reported a ~0% consent rate — the subtle corner banner was simply ignored, so Google almost never received granted signals. A mandatory choice should raise the accept rate substantially.

## Verified (local build, browser)

- DE + EN copy renders, backdrop blocks and locks scroll.
- Decline → stores `denied`, no consent update, modal closes and unlocks.
- Accept → stores `granted`, `consent update` (all four signals) lands in the dataLayer, modal closes and unlocks.
- `/de/legal` shows no modal, no scroll lock.
- Mobile (375px): bottom-sheet layout, stacked buttons.

author: davidrobert
body:
## Sumário

**PR1 de 2 da [[A40.l18]] — vocabulário inerte. Nada escreve `degraded` ainda**; o writer é o PR2.

Fecha o handoff reader-first que a A40.l21 (#1232) abriu: o cliente TS ganhou `degraded` naquele PR e o Python só agora.

### 1. O membro do enum

`PipelineStageStatus.degraded` (ADR-357 §3) — terminal e não retomável, ao contrário de `needs_review`, que existe justamente para o resume re-entrar.

### 2. Gate de paridade no lugar de um tripwire one-shot

O `test_degraded_stage_status_ainda_nao_existe` que a l21 deixou era negativo por construção: cobrava a conferência dos 3 read sites **uma vez**, no PR que criasse o membro, e mandava se deletar — deixando as duas cópias do enum sem nada ligando de novo. Os 3 read sites que ele nomeava foram conferidos e já casam `degraded` (`degradedStage.ts`, `pipelinePhases.ts`, `format.ts`).

No lugar dele, `backend/tests/test_pipeline_status_enum_parity.py` trava a paridade permanente entre o enum Python e a união TS de `frontend/src/lib/api/pipeline.ts` — que é **escrita à mão**, não sai de codegen. O comentário em `pipelinePhases.ts:142` já nomeava o risco por escrito (*"com duas cópias, o próximo status novo entra pela metade"*) e não havia gate. Foi exatamente o que aconteceu entre l21 e l18.

O gate cobre **os dois enums** — `PipelineRunStatus` também não tinha nada ligando as cópias.

### 3. Correção por medição do critério de aceite

A lane e a ADR-357 §Consequências previam **"`make update-openapi-snapshot` ⇒ diff vazio; diff ⇒ §3 violada"**. Isso reprovaria o PR que **cumpre** a §3.

`backend/app/schemas/pipeline.py:44` declara `status: PipelineStageStatus` em `PipelineStageLogResponse`, então o enum de stage é superfície pública de API: criar `degraded` muda `openapi.json` e `DB_SCHEMA_REFERENCE.md` em 1 linha cada. A previsão original raciocinou só sobre o status de **run**.

A asserção certa preserva a intenção: `PipelineRunStatus` **inalterado** (o que a §3 protege — `partial_failure` é reuso, não status novo), `PipelineStageStatus` ganha **exatamente `degraded`**. ADR editada in-place por ainda estar `Proposto`.

### 4. Lane desbloqueada

`status: blocked` era medição de 2026-08-03, quando a l21 ainda não tinha mergeado. Ninguém flipa o campo no merge da dependência, então a lane P0 sumiu do `SPRINT_CURRENT` justamente ao ficar pegável — modo de falha simétrico ao que o §Predicado nasceu para matar (antes `open` mentia para cima; agora `blocked` mentiu para baixo). Registrado como delta datado, sem reescrever a tabela ancorada em `33bb0710`.

## Como testar

1. `pytest backend/tests/test_pipeline_status_enum_parity.py -q` → 3 passed.
2. Prova de mutação (o gate morde nos dois sentidos):
   - remova `degraded` do enum Python (o estado de ontem) → vermelho;
   - adicione um membro à união TS que o Python não tem → vermelho, no `PipelineRunStatus`.
3. `make update-openapi-snapshot && make update-db-schema-reference && git diff` → 1 linha em cada, só no enum de stage.
4. `pytest backend/tests -q -m "not migration"` → 3072 passed.

## Ordem de merge

Idealmente **atrás de #1241 (A40.l19)**, que declara `degraded` no tipo do DB. As duas ordens funcionam (o gate da l19 é subconjunto `python ⊆ declarado`, e esta PR não tem o gate), mas l19-primeiro deixa o invariante satisfeito em todo instante.

author: israeltraigent
body:
> "3 models × 4 binary knobs = 48 configurations." — exact numbers, no "roughly", no "about".

**What this branch lands, after two owner follow-ups: baseline 12, enhanced 48.** Both are asserted
in `sdk-execution.md`'s fence, and every assistant-facing document now states them. The two sections
immediately below record the *first* proposal, whose baseline was 6; they are kept as the argument
that produced the shape, and are superseded by the follow-up sections at the end. Where any of them
disagree, the later section wins.

## What existed, measured before changing anything

| space | ordinary branch | reasoning-strong-tier branch | pinned by |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 3 models × 2 temperatures = **6** | 3 models × 2 prompt styles = **6** | `assert configuration_count(BASELINE_SPACE) == 6` |
| enhanced | 3 × 3 temps × 3 styles × 2 self-check = **54** | 3 × 1 × 3 × 2 = **18** | **nothing** |

The reasoning branch is real and was documented nowhere. `sdk-execution.md` said only "drop
temperature as a swept knob for the whole walkthrough"; the number 18 appeared in exactly one place
in the repository — `test_reasoning_branch_document_still_clears_the_cap`, which pinned that
branch's *score* (76) and never its size. A customer on a reasoning strong tier got a third of the
advertised space and no document said so.

## What it becomes (first proposal — the baseline here is superseded at 12 below)

| space | both branches | pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 3 models × 2 prompt styles = **6** | `assert configuration_count(BASELINE_SPACE) == 6` |
| enhanced | 3 models × 4 binary behaviour knobs = **48** | `assert configuration_count(ENHANCED_SPACE) == 48` |

Plus three more asserts that keep them from drifting: temperature is length 1 in both, every
behaviour knob is length 2, and the baseline is a subset of the enhanced space knob by knob.

**The two branches are now identical, and that is the whole reason to pin temperature.** The
reasoning-branch test no longer pins a second number — it asserts the two documents are equal.

## The baseline proposal, argued (superseded: the second axis below takes it to 12)

**6, as 3 models × 2 prompt styles.** Not a new shape: it is exactly what the existing guidance
already prescribed for the reasoning branch ("the baseline instead uses two prompt styles"). Making
it universal *removes* a branch rather than adding one.

Four things it has to satisfy, and does:

1. **Small and cheap** — same 6 rows, same 18 tuning rows, same cost as today.
2. **Keeps its assert** — `== 6` is untouched, and it is the precedent this PR copies for `== 48`.
3. **Trials still equal the space** — `BASELINE_TRIALS` defaults to 6, so `grid` enumerates all six
   points deterministically and `1 <= BASELINE_TRIALS <= configuration_count(BASELINE_SPACE)` holds.
4. **It must rank a lever the enhanced run will actually use.** This is the load-bearing one, and it
   is why the second axis is `prompt_style` and not something else. The baseline exists to produce
   evidence for the enhanced space. Under the old shape its second axis was temperature — which,
   once temperature is pinned, the enhanced run does not carry at all. The baseline would have been
   ranking a knob that no longer exists downstream. `prompt_style` is in both spaces, so the
   evidence transfers.

`prompt_style` is also the only knob in the `general` high-impact catalog besides `model` and
`temperature`, so the baseline ranks a knob the scorer already considers high-impact.

## The knobs: new vocabulary, and what it costs

`thinking_shape` and `reflect` are **new names**. Checked against the scorer:

| knob | in `CANONICAL_RANGES`? | in `OPEN_CATEGORICAL_KNOBS`? | in `HIGH_IMPACT_KNOBS["general"]`? | scored as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | no | **yes** | yes | breadth, 3 values → 1.0 |
| `temperature` | yes | no | yes | pinned, 1 value → 0.0 |
| `prompt_style` | no | no | yes | breadth, 2 values → 0.5 |
| `thinking_shape` | no | no | no | breadth, 2 values → 0.5 |
| `reflect` | no | no | no | breadth, 2 values → 0.5 |
| `self_check` | no | no | no | breadth, 2 values → 0.5 |

Neither new knob needs a catalog entry: they are categorical, so `knob_variation` scores them on
breadth, which is the honest signal for a name the scorer has never seen. Coverage is unaffected —
it measures the catalog's knobs, and all three are present.

**What it costs, stated rather than smoothed over.** A categorical knob scores `(distinct - 1) / 2`
capped at 1, so a **binary** knob can never exceed 50%. The worked example's agent pillar moves:

| | knob-count | variation | coverage | agent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (3 styles, 3 temps, 54 configs) | 35/35 | 30.4/40 | 25/25 | **90** |
| after (4 binary knobs, 48 configs) | 35/35 | **20/40** | 25/25 | **80** |

Ten points, entirely in the sub-score that measures *breadth of values* rather than *usefulness of
knobs*. That is the price of an exactly predictable space made of two-valued behaviour switches,
and it is recorded in the test rather than worked around by giving a binary knob a third value it
does not have.

Knob-count stays at full marks: 5 varying knobs is inside the 4–6 plateau, and 48 is well under
`20 × 12` so the oversize clause does not bind. 12 trials cover **25%** of 48, against 22% of 54.

## Values, not only knobs (owner addition)

The baseline informed *which knobs* the enhanced space carries. It now also informs *which two
values each*, read off the **lowest**-scoring combination:

- **gap to the winner within 0.05** → the knob evidently did not decide the run; **replace it**.
- **gap beyond 0.05** → it clearly mattered; **keep it, narrow its values toward the winner**.

`0.05` is `calibrate_evaluator.SEPARATION_MARGIN`, read from that module in the test rather than
retyped, and the guidance says the sharing is deliberate so nobody later reads it as a coincidence.

Neither move resizes anything — 48 is which knobs and which values, never how many. The evidence is
described as what it is (six trials, three observations a side): `the baseline's best combination
used X`, never `X is better`. The customer's own knob still wins ties, and every knob replaced and
value narrowed is named on the approval card.

## The framing

> The knobs are reduced to demonstrate the principle cheaply — a first run has to finish, cost
> little, and be readable — and Traigent knows tens of knobs it can recommend once the principle is
> shown. This is a demonstration, not the ceiling of what Traigent can do [...] Never present the
> smaller space as though the improvement were bought by shrinking the search.

author: globalpocket
body:
## Summary
- Extends existing `task.run` with `verification_recovery_context_read` for current verification recovery tasks.
- Adds Rust-owned provenance, permission, path, UTF-8, symlink, and byte-budget validation before reading one diagnostic-guided excerpt.
- Carries the excerpt only into in-memory prompt context while ledger/RPC/VSIX expose bounded metadata and hashes.

## Capability gain
A headless recovery task can move from bounded verifier diagnostic handles to one safe runtime-owned workspace context read without an external raw file read.

## Why existing behavior was insufficient
M30.1 and R3.3 identify safe diagnostic locations, but recovery prompts previously had no runtime-owned way to materialize a focused source excerpt from current recovery provenance. `selected_index_context` requires a separate caller-provided index-selected read and cannot substitute for recovery provenance revalidation.

## Architecture
- Protocol: request-only context read target and bounded task-run summary.
- Runtime: validates current recovery provenance, ReadWorkspace, safe diagnostic path, file kind, UTF-8, budget, and replay summary.
- Context: adds prompt-only `VerificationRecoveryContextPromptContext`.
- Ledger: records `VerificationRecoveryContextReadMaterialized` metadata only.
- VSIX: mirrors validation and rejects raw content/path fields.

## Safety boundary
No new RPC, no generic workspace read, no shell/git/network/service execution, no workspace mutation, and no raw excerpt, prompt, provider response, stdout/stderr, command, environment, absolute path, canonical path, or secret in ledger/RPC evidence. Prompt previews and LLM response previews are redacted when privileged context is present.

## Tests
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --workspace`
- `cargo test --workspace`
- `pnpm guard:diagnostics`
- `pnpm guard:phase-value`
- `pnpm --filter brownie-vsix check`
- `pnpm --filter brownie-vsix test`
- `pnpm --filter brownie-vsix build`
- `git diff --check`

## Non-goals
No recovery proposal apply, retry execution, generic file browser, codebase-index query, multiple-file read, directory read, or report/history/readiness wrapper.

## Value gate
- Target capability: `headless_autonomous_development`
- Concrete gain: admitted verification recovery `task.run` can authorize one diagnostic-guided bounded workspace context read.
- Non-duplicative: distinct from M30.1 diagnostics, M29.1 cargo-test execution, and M28.1 recovery apply continuation.
- Runtime behavior changed: yes, Rust runtime reads and materializes prompt-only recovery context under provenance and permission gates.

body:
## Auth: 회원가입/로그인 기본 구현 (더미 로직)

### What (변경 사항)
- `auth/schemas.py`: UserCreate, UserResponse, Token, TokenData 스키마 정의
  - UserCreate에 username/password 검증(field_validator) 적용
- `auth/validators.py`: username/password 검증 규칙을 독립 함수로 분리 (source of truth)
- `auth/security.py`: 비밀번호 해싱(bcrypt), JWT 액세스 토큰 생성/검증, get_current_user 의존성 구현
- `auth/service.py`: 회원가입/로그인 비즈니스 로직 구현 (DB 연동 전 더미 로직)
- `auth/router.py`: /register, /login, /validation-rules 엔드포인트 추가
- `auth/dependencies.py`: get_db 임시 mock 함수 추가 (core.database 완성 전까지 사용)
- `main.py`: auth 라우터 연결
- `requirements.txt`: bcrypt, python-jose, sqlalchemy, pydantic, python-multipart 추가

### Why (변경 이유)
- 팀 분담 구조상 auth 파트를 우선 구현하되, DB(core) 연동이 완료되기 전까지 병행 개발이 가능하도록 서비스 계층을 더미 로직으로 구성했습니다.
- 회원가입 검증 규칙(username/password)을 auth/validators.py에 분리하여, 추후 GET /api/auth/validation-rules로 프론트엔드와 규칙을 동기화할 수 있게 했습니다.

### How (검증 방법)
​```
pip install -r requirements.txt && uvicorn main:app --reload
​```
- `POST /api/auth/register`
  - `admin` 외 아이디 → `201` + UserResponse 반환
  - `admin` → `409 Conflict`
- `POST /api/auth/login` (form-data)
  - `testuser` / `secret123` → `200` + JWT 토큰 반환
  - 그 외 → `401 Unauthorized`
- `GET /api/auth/validation-rules` → username/password 검증 규칙 JSON 반환
- `/docs`(Swagger UI)에서 각 엔드포인트 요청/응답 스키마 확인 가능

(아래 "현재 가능한 api 더미 응답"에서 자세한 내용 첨부)

---

### 팀원께 전달 사항

**@core 담당자님**
1. `main.py`의 CORS 미들웨어(`CORSMiddleware`) 관련 — 저희 프로젝트는 프론트엔드 서버가 별도로 존재하지 않아 CORS 설정이 불필요할 수 있습니다. 필요 없다면 삭제 부탁드립니다.
2. 편의상 `core/config.py`에 `Settings`(pydantic-settings 기반 환경설정)를 미리 작성해 두었습니다. `database_url` 등 필드가 이미 있으니 DB 연동 시 참고해 주시고, 필요 시 자유롭게 수정해 주세요.

**@프론트엔드 담당자님**
- 회원가입 시 username/password 검증 규칙은 `auth/validators.py`에 정의되어 있고, `GET /api/auth/validation-rules`로 그대로 조회 가능합니다. 폼 검증 시 하드코딩하지 마시고 이 엔드포인트 값을 참고해 주세요.
- `/login`은 JSON이 아니라 `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (form-data) 형식으로 요청해야 합니다 (`OAuth2PasswordRequestForm` 사용 중).
- 아직 DB 연동 전, 어떤 테스트 가능한지 아래 기입 해 두었습니다. 참고 바랍니다.

### 현재 가능한 api 더미 응답
#### 회원가입 (POST /api/auth/register)
- username이 "admin"인 경우에만 409 Conflict (중복 에러) 응답
- 그 외 모든 아이디는 검증 규칙만 통과하면 201 Created로 성공 처리됩니다
- 다만 실제로 DB에 저장되지 않습니다. 즉, 방금 가입한 계정으로 로그인 테스트는 불가능합니다.
- 응답 바디의 id는 항상 1, created_at은 요청 시각으로 고정됩니다 (실제 DB 값 아님)

#### 로그인 (POST /api/auth/login)
- 오직 username: testuser, password: secret123 조합만 성공 (200 + JWT 토큰)
- 그 외 모든 조합은 아이디 존재 여부와 무관하게 401 Unauthorized로 응답 (보안상 아이디 존재 여부를 구분하지 않도록 의도적으로 통일한 처리입니다)
#### 검증 실패 케이스 (422 Unprocessable Entity)
- 아이디: 3~50자, 영문/숫자/_/-만 허용
- 비밀번호: 8~72자, 영문+숫자 혼합 필수, 앞뒤 공백 불가
- 정확한 규칙은 GET /api/auth/validation-rules로 언제든 최신값 조회 가능합니다

author: schroedk
body:
Closes #109.

`sample_suffix` documented a `[0, 1)` draw and computed one that could return exactly `1.0`. Replaced with the canonical 53-bit mapping.

- The draw is `((next_u64() >> 11) as f64) * (1.0 / (1u64 << 53) as f64)`; every value is exactly representable, so nothing rounds to `1.0`.
- `index_for_draw` splits the CDF search out of `sample_suffix`, so a draw can be injected instead of reached through the RNG.
- The `min(end - 1)` clamp stays. See below.

## The clamp is kept, and the reason is not the one on the issue

The issue left open whether the clamp is still needed. It is, but only at `f32`, and for a reason the issue did not name: `index_for_draw` narrows the `f64` draw to `T`, and `f32` rounds every draw above `1 - 2^-25` to exactly `1.0`. So the `[0, 1)` guarantee does not survive narrowing.

Searching 2M random distributions for a start whose `remaining` rounds up, counting those with any overrunning start:

| draw | overruns |
| --- | --- |
| `u = 1.0` (what the old mapping could produce) | 253293 / 2M |
| `u = 1 - 2^-53` at `f64` (the new mapping's maximum) | **0** / 2M |
| `u = 1 - 2^-53` narrowed to `1.0f32` | 246571 / 2M |

At `f64` the new draw's own bound rules the overrun out. At `f32` it stays reachable, and without the clamp `sample_after` indexes `neighbors[end]` and panics.

`the_top_draw_narrowed_to_f32_still_needs_the_clamp` pins this with a 5-weight reproducer found by that search. Removing the clamp fails it with `start 2: index 5 is past the CDF`. The earlier version of this test used uniform weights and was vacuous — the scan's `<` is strict, so `r == total` already stops correctly, and only `r > total` overruns.

## No re-baselining was needed

The issue predicted this would touch the wire-format fixtures, `deterministic_with_fixed_seed`, and the residual bounds. None of that happened, and the prediction was wrong for a structural reason: the two mappings agree to within one ulp of `u`, so the sampled index only moves when a draw lands within `2^-53` of a CDF bucket boundary.

Factorization output is bit-identical between the two mappings across 35 cases — grids 6x6 to 30x30, complete graphs of 8/40/120 nodes, seeds `0`, `1`, `42`, `7919`, `u64::MAX` — hashing every bit of the solution. (`deterministic_with_fixed_seed` also compares two runs of one build, so it could not have been sensitive to the mapping either way.)

## Mutation gate

The two survivors that produced this issue are resolved:

- `84:67` — the `+ 1.0` expression is gone. Every mutant on the replacement line is caught (`>>`/`<<`, both `*` mutants, both `/` mutants).
- `103:24` — the clamp is now killed under all five of `Some(k)`, `min(end + 1)`, `min(end / 1)`, `min(end - 0)`, `max(end - 1)`.

Every mutant in `index_for_draw` is caught. The only remaining `sampling.rs` survivor is the pre-existing `seed()` accessor, unrelated to this change.

## Verification

`cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` green, clippy and fmt clean.

author: alvaad4
body:
## Problem
Sometimes SpeakEazy keeps recording after the Fn/Globe key is released — the app "thinks you're still pressing."

## Investigation
The v1 fix (00272c4) had three remaining holes:
1. **Watchdog rode the UI timer** — `rumps.Timer` runs on the main AppKit thread, which pauses during menu tracking / modal windows: exactly when a wedge is likeliest to go unnoticed.
2. **Listener state desync** — when macOS disables the event tap (slow callback / GIL stall) the Fn *release* event is dropped; `FnListener._down` stayed `True`, inverting every subsequent press/release.
3. **No backstop** — if the OS itself reports a stale "key down" modifier state (sleep/wake, secure input), the watchdog agreed with the wrong answer and recorded forever.

## Fix — three independent layers (`watchdog.py`)
- **Dedicated watchdog thread** (0.25s poll, 0.6s grace) — survives main-thread stalls; replaces the UI-timer watchdog
- **Listener resync from hardware** after any tap-disable, and before every forced stop — a lost release can no longer invert the state machine
- **120s hold-mode hard cap** (`MAX_RECORDING_SECONDS`) — fires even if macOS claims the key is still down; toggle mode exempt
- Engine `start`/`stop` now lock-guarded (release event + watchdog can race) and `recording_started` is tracked
- Timestamped `[hotkey]`/`[engine]`/`[watchdog]` logging so the next occurrence is diagnosable from `/tmp/speakeazy.log`

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run python scripts/verify.py` — 28/28 (7 new checks: grace period, sustained key-up stop, toggle-mode exemption, hard cap with stuck key, resync heals missed release, resync no-op when in sync)
- [x] App restarted live with the new code — status item present at window layer 25, process healthy
- [ ] Adam: dictate normally for a day; if a stuck press recurs, the log now names the layer that caught it

author: dpage
body:
## Summary

- Current models including the whole Claude 5 family reject `temperature`
  outright, and the server attached one to every request, so the web client
  failed with `anthropic (400): temperature is deprecated for this model`.
  The model comes from the client's selector rather than `llm.model`, and that
  selector defaults to `claude-opus-5`, so a fresh session hit this with
  nothing misconfigured.

- There was no way to opt out: `llm.temperature` defaulted to `0.7` and
  `mergeConfig` treats `0` as unset, so `cfg.LLM.Temperature` was always a
  real value that `main.go` wrapped in `llm.Float()` for all four providers
  unconditionally. That also silently defeated the fix already released in
  `pgedge-go-llm-lib` v0.2.0, which stopped `WithDefaults` filling a nil
  temperature with 0.7 so callers could defer to the provider: this server
  never passed nil for it to preserve. The library floor therefore moves to
  v0.2.0, which the fix needs to have any effect.

- Neither the server nor the CLI client sends a temperature now, so each
  provider applies its own default. The `llm.temperature` option and the
  `PGEDGE_LLM_TEMPERATURE` environment variable are retired, and the two demo
  compose files stop passing the latter.

- Callers of the LLM proxy API may still send a per-request `temperature`,
  which the library forwards only when present. That field is deliberately
  left in the API and the OpenAPI schema; this change is about the server no
  longer imposing a value of its own.

## Compatibility

Config is parsed with a lenient `yaml.Unmarshal`, so existing files that still
set `llm.temperature` keep loading and the value is simply ignored.
`TestLoadConfigWithRetiredTemperature` pins that, and the CLI config fixture
deliberately retains `temperature: 0.5` for the same reason.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt`, `make lint`: all clean.
- [x] `make test`: 905 tests pass, 0 failures, including the new
      retired-option test.
- [x] Verified live against the real Anthropic API in a local environment with
      sixteen PostgreSQL instances configured. Before the change, a question
      asked with `claude-opus-5` selected fails with the 400 above; with this
      build the same question succeeds, the agent calling
      `read_resource (pg://system_info)` and `count_rows` and answering
      correctly (PostgreSQL 14.20, 5 rows in `public.region`).

Reported from a live test environment where this reproduced on first use.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Changed**
  - Removed automatic temperature/sampling configuration from server and CLI LLM requests.
  - Retired `llm.temperature` and its environment-variable setting; existing configurations continue to load, but the setting has no effect.
  - Per-request proxy calls may still provide a temperature value, which is forwarded when supplied.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated configuration guides, examples, quickstarts, and deployment samples to remove the retired setting.
  - Added changelog details describing the updated LLM request behavior.

Wire size (cl100k per-tool `{name, description, input_schema}` JSON, CoderAgent/CLI config): **eval 876 → 691, exec_command 706 → 529, lsp 729 → 641** — about **450 tokens / ~8% of the whole tool payload** (total 6,480 → 6,030; compact full-list JSON 5,840 → 5,390).

author: justrach
body:
Integrates twelve branches. Every one is individually green on CI, but four of them break each other when combined, in ways no single branch could see. That is what this branch is for.

## What it bundles

| PR | |
|---|---|
| [#455](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/455) | #416 lazy MCP schemas — **measured 64.8% catalog cut**, ~1,700 tokens off every request |
| [#451](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/451) | #440 tool-result handles by default |
| [#454](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/454) | #445 transcript line deferred to first compaction |
| [#457](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/457) | #441 append-only transcript (+ a real Windows defect) |
| [#459](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/459) | #411 post-compaction durable-state note |
| [#460](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/460) | #391 pre-compaction notes-to-self |
| [#461](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/461) / [#458](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/458) | #429 output inversion, batches 2 and 3 |
| [#456](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/456) | #444 — the anyOf "flake" was a display artifact |
| [#448](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/448) / [#449](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/449) / [#450](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/pull/450) | GUI agent overview, live A/B eval harness, subagent-steering design |

## Four cross-branch breaks, found and fixed here

**1. A compile error neither branch could produce alone.** #411 dropped the `prompts` alias from `agent_compact.zig` as unused, having moved the last `compact_instruction` reference into its own module. #445 added `noteSessionCompacted` call sites that reach through exactly that alias. Both are correct in isolation; merged, `agent_compact.zig` does not compile.

**2. Two leaf modules for one constant.** Batch 2 split `settings_path` into `harness_settings.zig`; batch 3 split the same constant (plus `confinedPath`, `noSymlinkEscape`, `readOnlyAllowed`) into `harness_policy.zig`. Both to solve the same problem — letting a module read the settings file without importing the terminal-cluster `approvals.zig`. Consolidated onto `harness_policy`, which is already a pure-std leaf; `harness_settings.zig` is removed and its two importers repointed.

**3. A silently dropped feature.** #440 added the `GRAFF_TOOL_HANDLE_BYTES` knob to `setupSkillsAndTheme`. Batch 2 moved that whole function into `session_settings.zig`. Git merged both happily and the knob simply ceased to exist — no conflict, no error, just a feature that stopped being parsed. Re-homed with its import.

**4. A process-global that segfaults across tests.** #391's `g_note_session` is a process-wide global; when armed, `setSystemPrompts` reads the filesystem through `agent.io`. #391's tests never armed it, so the hazard was invisible on its branch. #445's tests do arm it, via stub `Agent`s with `io = undefined` — and once *any* test leaves it armed, every later composition in the same binary segfaults inside `compact_note.pathFor`. Fixed three ways: the global now **owns** its name instead of borrowing a caller's buffer (names too long disarm rather than truncate, since a truncated name would read a *different* session's notes), the stub agents get a real `io`, and the tests disarm on exit so suite order stops mattering.

Also carried: `resetSessionCompacted` now re-arms #391's note store when the session identity moves, since `/new` and `/resume` repoint the name and would otherwise inject the previous conversation's notes into the new one — the same stale-identity bug #445 exists to prevent for the transcript line, one store over.

## Verification on the merged tree

- `zig build test` → **1113/1113, exit 0**
- `scripts/eval-tier1.sh` → **green** (fmt, 600-line ceiling, reachability at 1074 declared, build, tests, invariants, SDK)
- E2E, all pass against a freshly built ReleaseSafe binary: `test-pty-codex-ws.py` (the one that caught #391's mid-turn request-count change), `test-pty-overflow.py`, `test-spill-artifact.py`, `test-tty-release-on-exit.py` (the #396 raw-mode guard that batch 2's `run_finished` re-plumbs)
- `test_count_baseline` bumped 994 → 1113. It was already 49 behind before this batch and is a hand-bumped release-cut chore.

## Not included, deliberately

#429 batch 4 (`agent.zig`, 20 offending imports) should be cut **from this integrated result**, since it depends on the event vocabulary both batches extend in conflicting directions. #430 and #431 follow it.

Open issues surfaced by this batch: [#452](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/issues/452) (no GC sweeper for `.graff/tool-results/`), [#453](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/issues/453) (a session rename leaves the transcript line naming a deleted file), [#462](https://github.com/justrach/codegraff/issues/462) (the write-only-handle Windows defect still live in `playbook.zig` and `serve_events.zig` — the latter corrupts the durable EventLog, which #431's attach-replay acceptance depends on).

No CHANGELOG entry yet: that wants a version number, which is the release cut's call.

author: reppl
body:
Round 6 of the autonomous security-hardening loop (state issue #9). Seven confirmed defects fixed, each surviving an independent adversarial refuter and covered by a reproduction test observed failing before and passing after. Baseline was fully green before any change; the suite is 942 passing (+19 new).

## Fixed

1. **Collection `forced` settings permanently overwrote the user's global settings** (`src/stores/settingsStore.ts`, `src/context/CollectionDataContext.tsx`). A remote `settings.json`'s `forced` block was written into the user's persisted global settings with no backup, and the only teardown action had zero callers. Viewing one hostile allowlisted-CDN source once — reachable via a single unconfirmed `/gh/<user>/` link that auto-adds and activates the source — rewrote the visitor's display config across reloads and source switches, several keys unrecoverable without a full reset. Now snapshots the user's own value per forced key (source-scoped, so a refetch cannot clobber it), restores on source change via a dedicated effect (a source with no `settings.json` never reaches the apply path), and rolls back on rehydration for crash recovery — mirroring `_mechanicOverridesBackup`. The dead `clearCollectionForcedSettings` is repurposed into `restoreCollectionForcedSettings`.

2. **Object-typed entity fields crashed the whole collection view** (`src/hooks/useCollection.ts`). `summary` and the resolved platform `title`/`shortTitle`/`summary`/`year` were cast, not coerced. The `.loose()` schema lets an object through, which is truthy and reaches JSX as a child, so React throws "Objects are not valid as a React child" — the device-badge sink fires on first paint in the default grid. Coerced with a shared helper, matching the existing `title`/`year`/`videos` guards.

3. **`collectionStats` min/max spread crashed on large collections** (`src/utils/collectionStats.ts`). `Math.min(...values)`/`Math.max(...values)` over a per-card array throws `RangeError` past the engine argument limit (~125k), and `CollectionToast` renders outside the collection error boundary, so the app blanks. Replaced with a single-pass loop.

4. **Uncapped entity-type fan-out** (`src/loaders/collectionLoader.ts`). `loadCollection` mapped the untrusted `entityTypes` record into a `Promise.all`, each type fanning out into several probe fetches — a collection with tens of thousands of empty types amplified one load into ~80k CDN requests plus GitHub-quota exhaustion. Capped and pooled, always retaining the primary type. (The round-5 caps only covered the per-directory id path.)

5. **Uncapped discovery fan-out** (`src/hooks/useMyPlausibleMeDiscovery.ts`). Discovery ran a `Promise.all` over every `collection.json` in the GitHub tree; the username is attacker-controlled and discovery auto-runs on the startup picker with no click, so a `/gh/<user>/` link to a repo listing thousands of collections turned one page load into a CDN flood. Capped the count and pooled the metadata fetches.

6. **Unbounded media per card** (`src/hooks/useCollection.ts`). `card.imageUrls` (images + videos) was uncapped and feeds the gallery dot buttons and the load-time preloader, so a hostile entity could mount tens of thousands of nodes / requests. Capped the combined list at the data layer.

7. **Hard reset silently left data behind or hung** (`src/lib/clearPersistedData.ts`, `src/db/index.ts`). The three IndexedDB cleanups ran sequentially and only the first (`deleteDB`) was failure-intolerant, and `deleteDB` had no `onblocked` handler. A blocked or failed app-DB delete either hung the reset dialog or aborted the remaining steps, leaving cached collections and the plugin DB on disk while the UI reported "delete everything" complete. Added an `onblocked` handler and ran the cleanups independently via `Promise.allSettled`.

## Considered and rejected (refuted)

- **`applyMechanicOverrides` second-activation backup clobber** — unreachable: the Start Game overlay is gated on `!activeMechanic`, so overrides only apply when no mechanic is active, and every deactivation restores the backup first.
- **Write-only `collectionForcedSettings` mid-session revert** — the claimed spontaneous-revert mechanism is false: TanStack Query's structural sharing keeps `data.settings` identity stable across refetches, so the apply effect does not re-fire. Folded into fix 1 (wire up / remove the dead state).

## Deferred (nitpick / out of scope)

TruffleHog pre-commit `--since-commit HEAD` empty-range scan; gitleaks checksum not provenance-anchored; `build:analyse` writing `stats.html` into the deploy root; forced `cardBackStyle`/`titleDisplayMode` enum mismatch vs the store types; `getDB()` in-flight dedup (the root cause that makes the delete-blocked path reachable). No dependency changes (0 npm-audit findings on production deps).

## Verification

`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors), and `npm test` (942 passing, +19 new) all green.

author: youssofal
body:
Release 2.5.3. Small release focused on the agent lane and the API surface.

## What's in it

- **Cross-session postcommit yield**: background session-bank commits abort
  the moment any request is admitted, whichever session they belong to.
  Kills the occasional dead or sluggish agent turn (worst measured case:
  a follow-up turn 44% slower with ~0.75s extra first-token latency).
  Same-session grace preserved so streaming tool turns keep their prefix.
- **Chat-encode memoization**: repeat requests skip template render +
  tokenize (77-92ms per request at agent transcript sizes; sub-millisecond
  on hit). Warm follow-up latency in gate runs: 194-961ms band down to a
  steady 65-74ms.
- **Stats footer scoped to MTPLX-owned surfaces**: API responses no longer
  end with the TPS footer external tools counted as model output (~430ms
  timing pollution, usage mismatch, temp-0 inequality). App/browser keep it.
- **usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens**: thinking separated
  from visible output for API clients.
- **Endpoint hygiene**: clean JSON 400/404s, no Python internals on the wire.
- **Anonymous request controls honored by default**: OpenAI semantics for
  explicit body params (temperature, top_p, top_k, thinking, penalties,
  generation mode). Managed MTPLX clients stay server-owned. Closes #241.
  Rollback: MTPLX_CLIENT_CONTROLS_DEFAULT=hints.
- **Greedy draft coupling**: temp-0 requests run the draft sampler greedy;
  depth-2 acceptance .526 -> .590.
- Opt-in post-restore eager-round knob (off by default) and its tests.

## Gates

- Full pytest suite green; server suites green.
- ABBA A/B vs stock 2.5.2 (die-temp banded, matched pairs): decode flat at
  512/8k both pairs; honor probe verified (anonymous temp=0 applied,
  owner=client); zero regressions.
- Full release notes: docs/releases/v2.5.3.md; changelog updated.

Two candidate optimizations were benchmarked and deliberately NOT shipped
after inversion in matched-state A/B (dense prefill chunk 4096, post-restore
eager default) — receipts in the release QA record.

## Why

GitHub emailed on 1 Aug that the **"Update Life in the UK test info"** scheduled workflow will be **auto-disabled soon** — GitHub kills scheduled workflows after 60 days without repository activity, and the last push to this repo was 9 June. Quiet periods are normal here by design: the fee-sync job only commits when the GOV.UK fee actually changes (it's been £50 throughout), so the repo can legitimately go months without a commit.

## What

- Adds a **keepalive step** at the end of every run that re-enables the workflow via the Actions API (`PUT …/workflows/update-test-info.yml/enable`), which resets the 60-day auto-disable clock indefinitely. Runs with `if: always()` and is non-fatal on failure.
- Adds the `actions: write` permission the keepalive call needs.

This push itself already reset the inactivity timer, so the immediate disable threat is gone; merging makes the fix permanent (scheduled runs execute the workflow from `main`).

## Notes

- The repo-audit brief's concern that this workflow "fires 2× per day" is **by design, not a bug**: two UTC crons (20:00 + 21:00) cover BST/GMT, and the London-time gate lets exactly one of them do the work each day. No cron change needed.

## Summary

- map every LLM state mutex lock failure to a typed `AppError::Llm`
- cover all current LLM lock sites across model, chat, and LLM commands
- add a regression test for poisoned mutex handling

## Root cause and impact

LLM state locks used `.unwrap()`, so a panic while holding the mutex poisoned it and caused every later LLM command to panic until the application restarted. Commands now return `LLM state mutex poisoned` through the normal application error path instead.

The embed mutex was also audited; its direct lock sites already map poisoning to `AppError` and did not use the panic-prone pattern.

author: justadreamer
body:
Implements #363. Draft: the shape of the API is the thing to agree before it is worth polishing.

## Why

An element that finds something wrong with the request cannot tell the caller without failing it. `Errors` is not usable for a non-fatal problem - `Pipeline.Process` throws whenever the collection is non-empty and the host has not set `SuppressProcessExceptions`, whatever `shouldThrow` says on the individual error - so a consumer that wants to explain a bad evidence value has to build its own channel. The only construction available is an `ElementDataBase` subclass stashed on the flow data, which `JsonBuilderElement.GetAllProperties` then serialises into the response, and which has no stated threading contract. Both are framework properties, so both are fixed here rather than once per consumer.

## What changed

- `IFlowWarning` / `FlowWarning`, and `Warnings` / `AddWarning` on `FlowData`.
- `AddWarning` / `GetWarnings` extension methods on `IFlowData` in `FlowDataExtensions`.
- `JsonBuilderElement.AddWarnings` writes the messages to a top level `warnings` array, called from `BuildJson` right after `AddErrors`.

Two things worth a reviewer's attention rather than being buried in the diff.

**`IFlowData` is unchanged.** The members are on the concrete `FlowData`, reached through extension methods that cast, which is the approach the stop token took for the same reason - no major version bump. The cost is that a mocked `IFlowData` carries no warnings, so a test that mocks the interface and expects an element's warning to reach the JSON will see nothing. Putting the members on the interface, as #363 sketched, is cleaner and breaking; say which you would rather have.

**Synchronisation is the requirement, not a detail.** The lock is assigned in the field initialiser rather than on first use, so two elements in a `ParallelElements` group cannot each install a lock and then add to the same list while holding different ones. Reading returns a snapshot taken under that lock. This is deliberately not how `AddError` does it - the lazy initialisation there is the race described in #362, which this does not touch.

`AddWarnings` merges rather than overwrites, so a subclass that already writes a `warnings` entry of its own keeps it. Without that, a subclass gets either an `ArgumentException` on the duplicate key or silent loss depending on which of `Add` or the indexer is used.

## Testing

`FiftyOne.Pipeline.Core.Tests` 283/283 and `FiftyOne.Pipeline.JsonBuilderElementTests` 273/273 pass locally.

New coverage: warnings recorded and read back with the element that recorded them, the snapshot semantics, the null message guard, and that a warning does not reach `Errors`. `FlowData_Warnings_AddedConcurrently` has eight threads recording while a ninth reads throughout, asserting no warning is lost and no read fails. It was checked against a deliberately unsynchronised implementation of `AddWarning` first, where it fails - a concurrency test that has never been seen to fail is not evidence of anything.

On the builder side: the message reaching the `warnings` array with the rest of the data still present, no `warnings` entry when nothing warned, and the merge with a subclass entry.

## Not included

- The `AddError` initialisation race and the wider threading audit (#362).
- Other language ports and the response specification. If `warnings` is accepted as part of the JSON response shape, they should follow.

author: goedderz
body:
### Scope & Purpose

Queueing callbacks on the scheduler now captures the current ExecContext, and restores it during the execution. This callbacks from inadvertently using an arbitrary ExecContext, leaked from a previous callback on the same worker thread.

This in particular fixes the AQL async paths (async prefetch and AsyncExecutor), which run entire execution subtrees on scheduler workers: mid-execution lazy collection adds (DOCUMENT(), single-server traversal vertex lookups) previously skipped the collection permission check there because the worker fell back to implicit superuser; commit-time cancellation/read-only checks and audit logging degraded the same way.

Part of COR-811.

author: valerielinc-ops
body:
Il guard di ordinamento #2569 passava per fortuna, scadeva in silenzio, e la
diagnosi di partenza sulla coda era sbagliata. Tre cose separate, misurate una
per una prima di toccarle.

## Implementato

**1. L'invariante #2569, come è davvero.** Letto dalla issue e dal codice, non
dedotto: il follow-up chiedeva «CDN push IT success prima dei push shard
non-IT». Nel workflow è implementato come *nessuno shard di locale non-IT
pubblica prima che `cdn-build-id.txt` valga il `DEPLOY_BUILD_ID` di questa
build*. I push delle 25 sezioni IT **non hanno alcun rapporto con quella
condizione**: `push-section-shard.sh` legge `dist/<sub>` in sola lettura, copia
in `$RUNNER_TEMP` e ci fa girare l'offload con `cwd` dentro la copia — e
`offload-generated-images-cdn.mjs` risolve il proprio dist come
`path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'dist')`, quindi non può toccare `dist/og`,
`dist/data`, `dist/assets`, `dist/job-canon`. `strip-section-subtree.sh` fa solo
`rm -rf dist/<sub>`. **Il payload CDN è byte-identico ai due punti di chiamata**,
quindi la push si può anticipare.

Anticipata: nuovo step `Push generated assets to CDN (early — ahead of the shard
pushes)` subito dopo `Validate locale shard output`, che esegue **solo** la
sezione 2 di `deploy-it-pages-prep.sh` (`DEPLOY_CDN_PUSH_ONLY=1`). Il resto del
prep resta dov'era, nello stesso ordine — in particolare l'offload IT gira
ancora *dopo* i push di sezione, che è l'ordine da cui dipende il commento sulle
section shard. Handshake via `CDN_BASE`: se la push early riesce esporta
`CDN_BASE` in `$GITHUB_ENV` e `Deploy prep` salta la propria push; se fallisce,
`CDN_BASE` resta vuoto e `Deploy prep` pusha esattamente dove pushava prima — il
path di fallimento è identico al comportamento pre-modifica, più un retry
gratuito.

**Perché #2569 regge ancora.** Il predicato del gate non cambia di un carattere
(`cdn-build-id.txt == DEPLOY_BUILD_ID`, marker scritto per ultimo nella stessa
pubblicazione atomica del payload): viene solo soddisfatto ~40 min prima. E
l'invariante si **estende**, non si allenta: le 25 section shard IT — che
girano lo stesso offload verso la CDN sulla propria copia (`CDN_BASE_FIXED` in
`push-section-shard.sh`) ma non sono mai state gated — prima andavano live
*prima* che il payload di questa build esistesse; ora pubblicano dopo.

**2. Il margine, in secondi.** Misurato sul run 31076991699 (concluso
**success**), marker live alle 08:38:12:

| leg | gate | attesa | margine su 2700s |
|---|---|---|---|
| de | 07:52:58 → 08:38:12 | 2714s wall (elapsed 2700s) | **0s** — match al 181° e ultimo poll consentito |
| en | 08:00:20 → 08:38:20 | 2280s | 420s |
| fr | 08:07:45 → 08:38:18 | 1833s | 867s |

Con la push anticipata, sulle stesse durate: `Validate locale shard output`
chiude alle 07:51:18 e la fase CDN misura 214s (`Deploy prep` parte 08:34:38, il
marker è live alle 08:38:12) → marker live ~07:54:52. de attende ~114s
(**margine 2586s**), en e fr trovano il marker già pubblicato e passano al primo
poll (**margine 2700s**). Il margine più stretto passa da **0s a 2586s**.
Wall-clock del deploy invariato (IT resta il percorso critico, 122,7 min), ma si
liberano **~112 minuti-runner** per run (2600 + 2280 + 1833 = 6713s di attesa
che non viene più pagata).

Aggiornato anche il commento di `CDN_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S`, che era ormai falso:
attribuiva l'attesa alla latenza di pubblicazione di GitHub Pages sul repo CDN,
ma `vars.CDN_TARGET` è `r2` e sullo stesso run il marker era live **prima che
`Deploy prep` finisse**. Il collo di bottiglia era la posizione della push
nell'ordine degli step, non la CDN.

**3. Il timeout diventa rumoroso — e distinguibile — senza abortire nulla.**
La tolleranza resta: `continue-on-error` invariato su gate, push e surfacing, e
`Push locale shard` resta gated su `steps.cdn-gate.outcome == 'success'`. Uno
shard indietro non abbatte gli altri 26. Quello che cambia:

- **Near miss.** `wait-cdn-build-id.sh` aveva due soli stati, distanti un poll, e
  dall'esterno identici (`continue-on-error` riporta `conclusion: success` in
  entrambi i casi). Un match che arriva entro `CDN_WAIT_MARGIN_WARN_S` (600s)
  dal budget continua a pubblicare lo shard, ma emette `::warning::` + una riga
  di job summary. È il rilevatore che avrebbe segnalato lo 0s di margine del run
  31076991699 **un deploy prima** che 31062047677 mandasse in timeout tutti e
  tre i leg.
- **Due cause, due issue.** Timeout del gate e fallimento della push erano
  segnalati da **un solo step**, con **un solo titolo**, il cui corpo dava la
  colpa alla deploy key dello shard. Il 2026-08-06 il Build del leg IT del run
  31062047677 è fallito, il marker non è mai stato scritto, i tre gate non-IT
  hanno bruciato 2700s ciascuno — e sono state aperte le issue #5224 (fr), #5225
  (en), #5227 (de) contro deploy key che erano perfettamente valide. Ora sono
  due step con `if:` mutuamente esclusivi, due titoli, e il corpo del timeout
  porta i fatti misurati (secondi attesi, budget, id atteso, ultimo id visto) e
  manda a leggere il **leg IT**, non il repo dello shard. Lo step di resolve
  chiude entrambi i titoli.
- **Annotazione error, non warning.** Uno shard non pubblicato è un fatto di
  grado error: entrambi gli step emettono `::error title=…` e una riga di
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, che è la superficie visibile su un run verde.
- Il marker letto dalla rete viene ridotto a `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,64}` prima di
  finire in `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` e da lì nel corpo di una issue, e passa agli step
  via `env:` — mai interpolato nel testo di un `run:`.

**4. Starvation: la premessa era sbagliata, e la cura proposta non curava.**
Misurato via REST sulle 48h 2026-08-04T12:00Z→2026-08-06T12:00Z (#5251):

- **141 run** di `deploy.yml`: 121 cancellati, 10 success, 8 failure, 2 attivi.
- **121 su 121** i run cancellati avevano **zero job avviati** — verificati uno
  per uno (`/actions/runs/<id>/jobs` → `total_count == 0`), compresi quelli
  rimasti pending 4286s. **Zero minuti-runner.** La cancellazione è il gruppo di
  concorrenza che funziona (newest-wins), non una perdita.
- **`paths-ignore` non si applica a `workflow_dispatch`**, e **40 dei 141 run
  (28%)** arrivano proprio da lì: 15 workflow di dati chiamano
  `scripts/lib/trigger-deploy.sh` dopo aver committato, perché i push fatti con
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` non innescano workflow. Publisher jobs sync, Auto-translate,
  prezzi carburante, newsletter QA, ALTEN, 404 sweep sono **tutti** di quella
  famiglia. Allargare la denylist ne intercetta **zero**.
- Dei 101 run da `push`, solo **2** hanno un commit di dati automatico come head:
  su quel canale `paths-ignore` sta già facendo il suo lavoro. Gli altri 99 sono
  merge di codice, che devono deployare.
- **Ritardo introdotto dalle cancellazioni: zero.** Newest-wins garantisce che il
  run che parte contenga ogni commit superato. Il limite vero è la durata del
  build: mediana **130,5 min**, mediana del divario fra due build che **partono**
  **128,3 min** — il lock è saturo al ~100%, non affamato. L'attesa in coda
  mediana per un run che poi builda è 9,8 min; la coda lunga (104,5 e 121,6 min)
  è notturna, cioè idle, non contesa.

Quindi **`paths-ignore` non è stato toccato**. La misura è scritta accanto alla
denylist e pinnata da un test, perché la prossima diagnosi non rifaccia la
stessa strada.

**5. Casi negativi dimostrati.** 19 test nuovi in
`tests/deploy-cdn-ordering-gate.test.ts`, ognuno appaiato al caso che deve
prendere. Ogni guardia è stata mutata e vista diventare rossa:

| mutazione | test che diventa rosso |
|---|---|
| push CDN early spostata dietro il fan-out delle sezioni | `early CDN push must precede the IT section-shard pushes` |
| `Push locale shard` non più gated sul marker | `the #2569 invariant itself is unchanged` |
| i due surfacing step ricollassati in un solo `\|\|` | `each cause has its OWN step` |
| titolo della issue rinominato solo nello step di resolve | `a green push resolves BOTH canonical issue titles` |
| avviso near-miss rimo
