author: naelmelikechi
body:
Le **constat 17c / chantier B** (issue #122), option 1 recommandee par le rapport. Et l'extension a immediatement revele du drift reel, que cette PR repare.

## Le probleme

Le check ne comparait que des **noms de colonnes**, sur `public` et `crm`. Il etait donc aveugle aux policies, fonctions, triggers, index, contraintes, a l'activation de RLS, et au schema `storage` **entier**.

C'est precisement ce qui a laisse passer l'incident des policies de buckets documents : elles n'avaient jamais tourne en prod, aucun document n'etait deposable pendant des mois, et aucun filet ne l'a signale.

Le perimetre passe de 1 a **7 dimensions** : colonne, policy, rls, fonction, trigger, index, contrainte. `storage` est inclus pour les policies et les triggers, la ou l'incident est passe.

## Pourquoi on compare des identites et pas du texte genere

**Verifie, pas suppose : la prod tourne sur PostgreSQL 15.8 et le Supabase local du repo sur 17.6.**

Le texte produit par `pg_get_expr`, `pg_get_constraintdef`, `indexdef` ou `pg_get_functiondef` change entre versions majeures (reformatage du deparse). Comparer ces textes aurait fait echouer la CI **a chaque run** sur des differences purement cosmetiques, et rendu le garde-fou inutilisable — donc probablement desactive au bout d'une semaine.

On compare donc l'existence et la portee : nom, table, commande, roles, signature, flag `SECURITY DEFINER`. C'est ce qui attrape la classe d'incident visee, un objet qui n'existe pas en prod.

**La limite est documentee dans le script** : une policy dont le `USING` a change en prod en gardant le meme nom, la meme commande et les memes roles n'est pas detectee. Couvrir ce cas suppose un local sur la meme version majeure que la prod, c'est l'option 2 du chantier B.

Les objets appartenant a une extension sont exclus (`pg_depend` deptype `e`) : leur inventaire depend de la version de l'extension installee, pas des migrations.

## Ce que l'extension a revele

**28 index de cles etrangeres** crees directement en prod le 2026-05-26 pour repondre aux advisors Supabase, sans migration. Une base reconstruite depuis le repo n'en avait **aucun** : regression de performance invisible, et divergence de plans d'execution entre local et prod.

**9 policies d'ecriture admin sous une forme differente.** Les migrations declarent une policy `FOR ALL` par table, la prod porte trois policies `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` issues de la consolidation des multi-permissives. **La regle metier est identique** (`get_user_role() IN ('admin','superadmin')`), il n'y a jamais eu de faille, mais le repo ne decrivait pas l'etat reel et une reconstruction aurait recree la forme `ALL`.

La migration de reparation a ete **generee depuis les definitions relevees en prod**, pas ecrite a la main : 37 objets, aucun risque de recopie. Entierement idempotente, donc no-op en prod.

## Resultat verifie contre la prod

```
  colonne     prod  912 · local  912
  contrainte  prod  313 · local  313
  fonction    prod   49 · local   49
  index       prod  307 · local  307
  policy      prod  234 · local  234
  rls         prod   75 · local   75
  trigger     prod   51 · local   51

✓ Aucun drift : tout objet prod du périmètre est couvert par les migrations.
```

## Un test mis a jour, et pourquoi

`07_societes_emettrices_rls.sql` figeait le **nom** `societes_emettrices_admin_write`, qui n'existe plus en prod. Il assert desormais les 3 policies d'ecriture reelles. Ses 4 assertions de **comportement** (un admin ecrit, un non-admin est refuse) sont inchangees et passent : c'etait la vraie garantie, le nom n'etait qu'un detail d'implementation.

## Divers

Corrige au passage un message d'erreur trompeur du script : un HTTP 400 de pg-meta accusait les credentials alors qu'il s'agissait d'une erreur SQL. Je m'y suis fait prendre en developpant cette PR.

Suites : 30 fichiers / 212 tests pgTAP, 164 fichiers / 1413 tests vitest, lint et typecheck verts.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jonhill90
body:
Closes h#804, h#805, h#806, h#807, and the docs half of h#808 (code half is #829, merged).

Five findings taken together per their shared cause and shared reader: every other defect fixed this week failed while someone was watching a running system to compare against. These fail when the estate is already down and the person following them has nothing working left to check a step against — a runbook step that cannot succeed is a latent outage extension, not a documentation nit.

Verified each against the actual script, compose file, or a related issue's own verified evidence — not against the runbook's own prose, per instruction.

## h#804 — `deploy.sh all prod` is not a valid invocation

Verified by reading `scripts/deploy.sh`'s dispatcher directly: no `all` case, falls through to `Unknown command: all`, exit 1. Fixed the step to deploy the three stacks not already covered earlier in the *same* runbook (infra/vault/db are done by Steps 3-10) — `auth`, `minio`, `observability`, in the order `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`'s own serialized dependency chain uses. **Not verified against a real rebuild** whether these three succeed in this order — stated plainly in the doc, not asserted as proven.

## h#805 — Step 4's manual `sudo tee` reintroduces a fixed bug

Verified against `vault.sh`'s `cmd_init` directly: it no longer prints the unseal key/root token anywhere, and writes both files itself, already correctly owned. The runbook's `sudo tee` sequence is word-for-word the previous broken instructions `cmd_init`'s own comments describe reintroducing (a root-owned key file the auto-unseal systemd unit can't read). Removed it; Step 4 now explains there's nothing to save from the output. The `make secrets-update` line the issue said not to touch is preserved but corrected to actually work (the old placeholder could never have been filled in since the key was never displayed) — flagged as **not run end-to-end**.

## h#806 — Step 0's tar-restore chain is coupled to the open h#799

There is no literal "restore openbao-data.tar.gz" step anywhere in the numbered Recovery Steps — Step 0's chain is illustrative prose, not an instruction. The numbered steps use fresh `vault.sh init` exclusively, sidestepping h#799 entirely. Made this explicit, and separately warns against a volume-tar restore of any post-2026-08-02 backup using `main`'s current key, naming h#799 by number and stating it is **Jon's open decision, not resolved here** — h#799 itself is untouched.

## h#807 — vps-rebuild.md's vault step omits init/setup/seed/approles

Verified by diffing against disaster-recovery.md's fuller five steps. `make deploy-vault` alone deploys and auto-unseals whatever volume exists — on a fresh rebuild that's empty, and auto-unseal exits 0 gracefully, so the step "succeeds" while leaving vault uninitialized. Every vault-consuming service has a SOPS fallback, so `make health` would plausibly still report clean. Fixed by pointing explicitly at disaster-recovery.md's Steps 4-9 rather than duplicating them — two copies of the same procedure is exactly the drift that let h#804/h#805 go stale. Corrected the "zero manual intervention" framing. **Not verified**: what `auto-unseal` does against a truly fresh volume.

## h#808 (docs half) — observability undercounted by 2

Verified directly against `docker-compose.observability.yml`: nine services, not seven. Corrected the service list and container-count claims (12 total, not 10). Code half is #829, already merged.

## Not attempted, deliberately

Reading vps-rebuild.md in full while fixing h#807 surfaced that it never mentions deploying `db`, `auth`, or `minio` at all. That's a larger, separate gap than any of h#804-h#808 named — filing separately rather than silently fixing or ignoring it.

## Tests

`tests/scripts/dr-runbooks-content.bats` — static content checks: they cannot prove a rebuild succeeds, only that the specific defects are gone from the text and the replacement content is present. Several tests corroborate a doc claim against the actual script/compose file it describes, not just the doc text.

**Positive control:** reverted both docs files via `git stash`, reran — 12 of 15 tests failed, exactly the new-content ones; the 3 code/compose-corroboration tests correctly stayed green. Restored, reran: 15/15.

## Test plan

- [x] `bats tests/scripts/dr-runbooks-content.bats` — 15/15
- [x] Positive control: revert → 12/15 fail (exactly the new-content tests); restore → 15/15
- [x] `bats --recursive tests/scripts/` — 759/759, no regressions
- [x] `git diff --stat` shows exactly the 3 intended files

[Jenneranalytics.com](https://jenneranalytics.com) は、200を超えるSASプロシージャに対応したSASコード実行APIを提供しています。AIアシスタントと連携したコラボレーションワークスペースとしても利用できます。Mac版はApple App Storeから、Windows/Linux版はライセンス提供にて入手できます。

私たちはコミュニティに対して次の形で貢献しています。
(1) SAS互換システムへのアクセスを増やすこと、
(2) 公開されているSASリポジトリにテストカバレッジとテストカバレッジのフレームワークを提供し、ソフトウェア工学のベストプラクティスの普及を後押しすること。

あなたの `00_COM_INIT.sas` はJenner上で無修正のまま動作します——このPRはそれを実際に確認できる小さな互換性バンドルを追加するものです。あなたのプロジェクトのために書いたテストで、参考になればと思い共有します。なお、これは今日の多くの業務コードと同様、AIの支援を得て作成されています。

`02_Process_data_rev.sas` の `%house_hold(type)` マクロを拝見しました。`02_Process_data.sas` ではカテゴリ大・カテゴリ小・詳細の3つのブロックがほぼ丸ごとコピペされていましたが、`_rev` 版では `%if &type. = cate_main %then...` の分岐でひとつのマクロに統合し、さらに欠損値をゼロ埋めする配列ループ (`array all1 _numeric_; do i = 1 to dim(all1);`) まで加えられています。個人の家計簿集計のために、ここまで丁寧にリファクタリングされているのは良い設計判断だと思いました。

`jenner-check/` ディレクトリには2つのバンドルを追加しました。中身はあなたのコードそのものです（`00_COM_INIT.sas` の年月リスト生成ロジック、および `02_Process_data_rev.sas` の `%house_hold(cate_main)` 集計パイプライン）。Excelから読み込んでいた `INPUT.household_account` / `INPUT.store_master` は、同じ列構成の小さなサンプルデータに置き換えていますが、マクロ本体のロジックは変更していません。

```
jenner-check/
├── README.md
├── run_jenner.sh
├── t001_com_init_ymlist/       # 00_COM_INIT.sas の年月リスト生成
└── t002_house_hold_cate_main/  # %house_hold(cate_main) 集計パイプライン
```

このPRのブランチをチェックアウトし、リポジトリのルートから実行すると、あなたのコードがそのままJennerで動くのを確認できます。

```bash
# このPRをチェックアウト（ブランチに切り替わります）してから、リポジトリのルートで実行:
gh pr checkout 1
curl -sS --data-binary @jenner-check/t002_house_hold_cate_main/script.sas https://api.jenneranalytics.com/v1/quick
```

`cd jenner-check && ./run_jenner.sh --all` を実行すると両方のバンドルを再実行し、記録済みの結果と照合します。ホスティングされているAPIは無料でお試しいただけます（サインアップ不要）。APIの詳細は[こちら](https://docs.jenneranalytics.com/api/)をご覧ください。

送信されるのは実行するスクリプトのソースコード（`autoexec.sas` と `script.sas` のテキストのみ）で、`api.jenneranalytics.com` 上で実行されログと出力を返します。サンプルデータ以外のファイルは読み込まれず送信されません——何かをホスト型ツールに貼り付けるのと同様、実行したコードだけが送信されます。何かコマンドを実行しない限り、何も送信されることはありません。

マージ、クローズ、放置——どれでも構いません。返信は不要です。このリポジトリに追加のPRを送ることはありません。今後一切PRを送ってほしくない場合は、コメントに `no-more-prs` と書くか、`jenner-check: opt out` というタイトルのIssueを立ててください。

Lawrence W. Sinclair  
CEO / Jenner Analytics Ltd  
[linkedin.com/in/lwsinclair/](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lwsinclair/)

## P-1.25 Phase 1: narrative disclaimer-presence gate (gate 89)

Adds **gate 89** (`tools/lint-narrative-disclaimer.py`), the fifth narrative-only gate. It requires the universal authority disclaimer **verbatim** as the first body content after the metadata block's closing `---` separator and before the first section heading, on every `executive/*.md` page (the entry-point `executive/README.md` exempt). Enforces spec item 5. Fence-aware, fail-loud, 13-case self-test. Wired across the four gate surfaces + manifest + count 88 → 89.

### QA
**DUAL-FAMILY /validate-pr, 2 iterations → SHIP.** Iter 1: codex HOLD found 3 fail-opens the Claude SHIP missed (indented-code disclaimer accepted as a blockquote; a fence before the disclaimer skipped; body `**bold**`+`---` forging the metadata-close anchor) — all fixed at class width by a detection rewrite (`rstrip`-only compare, no fence-skip, `METADATA_FIELD_RE` + contiguous field run) with regression cases (self-test 9→13). Claude also caught a pre-existing accuracy nit (spec item 6 still `(new)` for the shipped gate 88) — fixed. Iter 2: Claude re-verify SHIP (F1/F2/F3 resolved, 20-probe false-positive harness clean); codex iter-2 re-verify hung at dispatch (noted; fixes verified by the iter-1 codex catch + direct reproduction checks + self-tests + Claude iter-2). Verbatim `DISCLAIMER` constant confirmed byte-exact to the spec.

Note: this gate was the independent route-around while the staleness gate (1.4) is being redesigned; per a maintainer decision (2026-08-06) the executive layer drops corpus-version dependency, so 1.4 is cancelled and version-pinning/staleness is removed in a follow-up PR.

author: naga1412
body:
## Summary

Operator's explicit "NEW PRIORITY" directive: build observability that prevents recurrence of the entire bug class found this project — ~15 defects, all the same shape (a field always NULL, always CONSTANT, or a code path that never fired, invisible because nothing checked for it). "One probe checking 'is this producing varying values?' would have caught all of them."

The `system-truth` ops-debug probe already does that sweep on demand (see memory `system_truth_probe_and_first_run_2026_08_06` — first real run found 41 findings, several genuinely new). This PR makes it run automatically as healer detector C5.

## Design

- **Self-gated 24h cadence.** The healer tick runs every 5 min; C5 checks a module-level last-run timestamp and returns `[]` near-instantly on every tick except the daily one. Cheap to leave in the regular loop rather than building a separate scheduler.
- **Baseline-diffed, not raw-alerted.** Every column/layer/trap/endpoint flagged is compared against yesterday's finding set (persisted as a `system_truth_baseline` finding, reusing `healer_findings` rather than a new table/migration). Only a finding that's **new since yesterday** pages at critical. A persisting known-bad state rolls up into one info summary — it does not re-page every day. The very first run ever seeds the baseline without paging on anything (a fresh baseline is not a regression) — this specifically avoids a 41-alert pager storm on day one, since the real first run already found 41 things.
- **Section 3 (traps) is now more complete than the standalone probe.** Running in-process means it can `from app.core.scoring.traps import ALL_TRAPS` and cross-reference the real registry against 30d fire counts — the SSH-based probe explicitly couldn't do this (it only had DB-recorded fires, no way to know which trap_ids exist but never fire vs aren't real traps at all).

## Test plan
- [x] 5 new tests covering the control-flow this module adds: first-run seeds baseline without paging, a new key pages critical while a persisting key doesn't, a resolved key is reported (not paged), a clean sweep is reported, the cadence gate skips a second call within 24h without even touching the DB (proven by making the session_factory raise if called).
- [x] Full `tests/healer/` suite (33 tests) passes.
- [x] `ruff check` clean.

**Not tested here**: the section 1-4 SQL itself. It's Postgres-specific (`FILTER (WHERE ...)`, `jsonb_array_elements`, `->`/`->>`) with no SQLite equivalent the existing healer test suite could run against — but it's the *same* queries already validated against real prod data via the standalone probe's actual first run, which found 41 genuine findings (see linked memory). Not re-deriving that validation here; the new logic this PR adds (gating + diffing) is what's covered.

author: kelsos
body:
Third batch of the Vuelidate -> zod migration, covering the RPC and explorer settings forms. Follows #12760 (shared setting controls) and #12770 (general display settings). Takes the app from 45 to 42 `useVuelidate` roots.

Each form is two commits: a characterization spec proven green against the Vuelidate code, then the migration, so the spec is a safety net rather than a description of the new code.

### `SimpleRpcNodeManagerForm`
Reuses `textSettingSchema` from batch 1 for its single endpoint field. `$externalResults` becomes `setServerErrors`, `useFormStateWatcher` becomes `form.dirty`, and the exposed `validate` is now synchronous.

### `ExplorerInput`
The two rules (`https` + vuelidate's `url`) become a pure `explorer-url-schema.ts`. Its spec is table-driven over every input measured against the old rules, including the ones that isolate a single rule, so neither rule can be dropped unnoticed. An empty value stays valid, since emptying the field is how an override is cleared.

**Includes a bug fix.** The clear button listened for `@click:clear`, an event `RuiTextField` does not emit (it emits `clear`). Clearing an explorer url emptied the field without saving anything, so the stale override came back on the next visit. Fixed in its own commit.

### `BlockchainRpcNodeForm`
Rules move into a pure `blockchain-rpc-node-form.ts`. Whether the endpoint is required depends on the name (etherscan is reached by api key, not a url), so that rule is refined on the object rather than the field. The `useRefPropVModel` wrappers are replaced by one form state written back to the model.

Batch 1's builders grew field-level twins (`textSettingField` / `numberSettingField`) so a multi-field form can reuse them; the existing `*SettingSchema` functions just wrap them in `z.object({ value })` and their spec passes unchanged.

### Checks

- typecheck clean
- unit: 750 files / 7118 tests pass
- lint: 0 errors, 20 warnings, matching develop's baseline exactly
- typos clean
- e2e `specs/settings/rpc` + `specs/settings/interface`: 14/14 on cleared `.e2e/data`

All re-run on the rebased tip.

author: ronaldtse
body:
## Summary

Bumps `MARKETING_VERSION` 0.9.6 → 0.9.7 and updates the Homebrew cask formula and Sparkle appcast feed in lockstep. Required so `scripts/release-direct.sh`'s tag-mismatch check (`tag == v$MARKETING_VERSION`) passes when the `v0.9.7` tag is re-pushed.

## Why now

The `v0.9.7` tag was pushed earlier today (2026-08-06) before this bump landed. The release workflow failed in 20s with `Tag mismatch: expected v0.9.6 (or v0.9.6-<suffix>), got v0.9.7`. The tag is currently at the wrong commit; this PR puts the version files where they need to be so the tag can be moved and the workflow re-triggered.

## What changed

- `MailApp/Config/Version.xcconfig` — `MARKETING_VERSION = 0.9.7`
- `packaging/homebrew-cask/rnp.rb` — `version "0.9.7"`, `verified_version "0.9.7"`, URL templated to `v0.9.7`. SHA256 left at the 0.9.6 value with a `TODO(0.9.7)` comment — will be regenerated from the published DMG in a follow-up "publish" PR.
- `website/updates/appcast.xml` — new `<item>` for 0.9.7 with `sparkle:edDSA=""` and `length="0"`, marked TODO. Sparkle will not offer this version to installed clients until `sign_update` fills those in.

## Follow-ups (separate PR after DMG is built)

1. Regenerate cask `sha256`: `shasum -a 256 RNP-0.9.7.dmg`
2. Generate appcast signature: `sign_update RNP-0.9.7.dmg` → paste `sparkle:edDSA` + `length`
3. (Optional) Publish cask to a self-tap under `rnpgp/homebrew-cask`

## Verification

- Version.xcconfig now reads `MARKETING_VERSION = 0.9.7`
- Cask and appcast version strings updated to match
- Build-not-yet-run; this is a version-bump only, no Swift changes

## Post-merge plan

After this lands on main, the `v0.9.7` tag needs to be moved to the new main HEAD (destructive — will ask for explicit confirmation before deleting and re-pushing the tag), then the tag push will trigger `release.yml` which builds + signs + notarizes + uploads the DMG/SBOM to the existing GitHub release.

author: adnenlaplateforme
body:
## Contexte

Le hero occupait tout le viewport en `lg` (`lg:min-h-screen`), ce qui repoussait entièrement la suite de la page sous la ligne de flottaison.

## Changements

**Hauteur**
- `lg:min-h-screen` remplacé par une hauteur bornée : `min-h-[30rem]` → `md:34rem` → `lg:38rem` (608px max).
- `pt-28` / `md:pt-32` pour dégager la navbar, qui est en `absolute` par-dessus le hero.

**Rendu**
- `<div>` → `<section>`, avec un calque de dégradé `from-black/70 via-black/45 to-secondary` : lisibilité du texte sur le visuel, et fondu du bas du hero vers le fond de page (plus de coupure nette avant `SectionProjet`).
- `bg-center` ajouté — à hauteur réduite, `bg-cover` sans position explicite décalait le bâtiment hors cadre.
- Contenu élargi de `max-w-lg` à `max-w-2xl`, `text-balance` sur le `h1`, sous-titre en `text-white/80` + `md:text-lg` pour poser une hiérarchie titre / accroche.
- CTA en `flex-wrap` (ils se chevauchaient sous ~380px) + états `hover` et ombre accent sur le bouton principal.
- Animation d'entrée en cascade (titre → sous-titre → boutons) via les keyframes `hero-rise` dans `index.css`, neutralisée sous `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Vérification

`npm run lint` et `npm run build` passent. Le rendu visuel n'a pas été vérifié dans un navigateur — à valider sur `npm run dev` aux différentes tailles, notamment le cadrage de l'image (`bg-center`, à ajuster en `bg-[center_35%]` si le bâtiment est mal centré).

author: israel-dryer
body:
`CLAUDE.md` had reached **2,429 lines / 177 KB**, and **2,164 of those lines (89%)** were a session-by-session narrative of the 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 initiatives — all three now shipped. A finished release log is background, not a worklist, and at that size it crowded out the facts that are actually load-bearing next session. This condenses it to **596 lines / 38 KB** without losing anything durable.

## What replaced the narrative

A compact **Direction** section: current status, a five-row table of the 2.x releases, where the detailed record lives (`development/*_changes.md`, `*_design.md`, `2_0_breaking_changes.md`, closed milestones, git history), and the 3.0 policy.

## Everything durable moved to the section that owns it

Organized by topic rather than by chronology, so it can be found rather than scrolled past:

- **Gotchas** gains the style-engine invariants — framework code uses `_build_configure` never the public `Style.configure`; durability ≠ the widget honoring the option (with the probed `font`/`sashthickness` cases and the self-inflicted map-masks-configure shape); "works ≠ designed surface" for composite passthrough.
- **New "Platform & Tk facts"** — the monitor-layout reasoning (Tk exposes no enumeration anywhere; X11 `screenwidth` is the union of all displays, which is why a clamp against Tk's metrics let a dialog straddle a seam), window mapping and sizing, Tk 9 differences, and the widget-level behavior that each cost a real bug: menu borders, `tk busy`, `Tcl_Obj` lookups, `event_generate` not proving input is blocked.
- **Dev environment** gains a per-box venv table (the three boxes are separate working copies and nothing carries over) and a `tools/` section covering the generators and the manual gates.
- **New "Documentation"** section for the authoring rules that previously existed only as scattered session notes — including the **three rST defect classes `-W` does not flag**, and the strip-tags scan that catches all three.
- **Conventions** gains git working practices (trial-merge over `merge-tree | grep`, `git cherry` for squash-merges, `reset --hard` destroys the author's WIP, push ≠ merge), review lessons (**a review finding is a hypothesis with a reproduction attached, not a verdict**), and the unwrapped-but-structured rule for release notes.

## Corrections the audit turned up

Condensing meant re-reading claims rather than trusting them, and three were stale:

- The **repository layout** was missing `cli.py`, `convert_theme.py`, `menu.py`, `validation.py`, `utils/`, `dialogs/filedialog.py` and `assets/icons/`, and still described `tests/` as "4 `test_*.py`" — it is ~37 plus four subpackages.
- The **3.0 shim count** is **32 across 18 files**, not "~30 across ~19"; the design-doc count is 26, not ~30. Both verified by grep rather than restated.
- Three references to "Workstream D/H" survived into sections whose defining context was being deleted, leaving the term undefined.

Also promoted two things that were only in memory, never in the repo file: the **scope constraint** (ttkbootstrap is a styling extension, not a widget library; mine bootstack for mechanisms, never its API) and **who the users are** (scientific/utility developers already on clam).

The narrative stays in git history — `git show 63b8f065^:CLAUDE.md` is the last full copy.

author: kenhayward
body:
The follow-up recommended in #453.

> ## Read this before reviewing on GitHub
>
> **`MoveToSectionModal.tsx` will show as "Binary file not shown" with no diff** - and it holds most of this change's logic. That is not a mistake in the PR; the copy of the file **currently on `main`** contains two literal NUL bytes, and git classifies any blob containing a NUL as binary, so the diff is opaque regardless of how this PR is split.
>
> To review it: `git fetch origin feat/create-in-current-folder` and read the file locally, or `git show <sha>:apps/web/src/components/MoveToSectionModal.tsx` at each commit.
>
> **This PR is what removes those NUL bytes**, so once it merges the file diffs normally again.

## The problem

The modal's create-and-move form called `api.createSection(name, null, roomId)` - a `null` parent, so **always top level**. That was fine when the folder list was flat and had no notion of "where you are". It stopped being fine in #453, which gave the modal a picker with a visible drill position: you can sit inside `Customers > Acme Corp`, type "Project Falcon", and get a **top-level** folder called Project Falcon.

The mismatch was not new - #453 just made it visible, which is why it was deferred out of that PR rather than smuggled in. It is a behaviour change and wants its own tests.

## What changed

- **`FolderPicker` now reports its drill position** via an optional `onDrillChange`. It deliberately keeps owning that state - it does **not** become controlled, because nothing needs to *set* the position from outside. #453 held the line on widening this contract for a single caller; this is the change that justifies it.
- **The modal creates at that position**, then moves the recording in as before. Creating at the root still passes `null`, unchanged.
- **The depth cap is respected** using the nav's existing `sectionCreateTarget` and the existing `newSectionNestCapped` string - no second rule and no second message. Without it, a user drilled to 8 levels would have got a raw 400 from the server.
- **The form says where it will create**, reusing the existing `newSubSectionPlaceholder` ("New sub-section in {{parent}}"). A form that silently changes what it does as you drill is worse than one that always does the same thing. No new i18n strings were needed.

## The NUL bytes

The `UNKNOWN_SECTION` sentinel shipped as `"\x00unknown\x00"` - literal NUL control characters, not the spaces its doc comment and its review both described. NUL renders as nothing, so it read as `" unknown "` to everyone who looked at it, including the review that validated it.

Nothing was broken: a GUID cannot contain a NUL any more than a space, so it remained collision-proof. But invisible control characters in source are their own hazard - the next person to read it sees `"unknown"` and could retype it as a plain word, silently turning a never-matching sentinel into a string a section id could in principle equal.

Fixed here rather than in its own PR because this change already touches this file, and splitting it out would not have made the diff render anyway. That commit also normalises the file's line endings to LF, matching its sibling components - incidental, and worth knowing since it means the whole file differs byte-wise.

## Testing

1892 web tests, build clean, solution builds with 0 errors. The main new test drills into a folder with a **real** id before creating - a fixture drilling to `null` would pass under the old behaviour too and prove nothing. Mutation-verified: reverting the parent to `null` fails it with `- "sec-1" / + null`. The depth-cap test builds a genuine 8-level chain and drills to the bottom, so it sits exactly on the boundary rather than near it.

## Deployment surface

**Server redeploy only.** No migration, no server change.

author: sernst
body:
## Summary

Two additive improvements to `skills/running-as-maestro`, addressing observed failure modes in the adversarial execute→judge loop:

### 1. Judge model floor
Replaces the previous "no special tier rule" for judges with:
- **Hard floor:** the judge must run on an equal-or-greater capability class than the executor whose work it grades, and never an older generation of the same model family (e.g. a sonnet-4.x judge over a sonnet-5 executor is forbidden).
- **Judgment-call comparison:** cross-provider class ranking has no canonical mapping — use rough capability tiers and err toward the stronger judge when uncertain.
- **Soft preference:** in multi-provider harnesses, prefer an equivalent-class judge from a *different* provider for independence — but only among candidates that already satisfy the floor.
- **Scales naturally:** cheap executors permit cheap judges; equal class satisfies the floor at the top tier.
- **Copilot-specific reinforcement:** judge subagents are a non-optional exception to the `auto` default — pinned post-execution against the executor's actual model, since weak auto-routed judges were observed specifically in that harness.

### 2. Mid-loop model-class escalation
- After 2 rejected execute→judge cycles on a subtask, the maestro must explicitly consider — and state its decision either way — escalating the executor+judge **pair** to a higher model class for remaining attempts.
- Escalation composes with the judge floor and does **not** reset or extend the 4-attempts-total ceiling.
- At the thrash trigger, class escalation is an allowed alternative to the maestro stepping in, but only when the failure is capability-bound rather than instruction-bound.

## Motivation
Observed cases (notably in GitHub Copilot) where auto-selected judges were weaker than the executor and failed to hold the bar, and where a stalled sonnet-class loop exhausted its budget when an opus-class pair could likely have resolved it without maestro intervention.

## Notes
- Language stays harness-neutral outside the existing GPT/Codex and GitHub Copilot blocks to avoid overfitting as this skill spreads across harnesses (Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Goose, Perplexity, Google).
- Loop cap, step-in mechanics, compliance check, and maestro overrule authority are unchanged.
- Drafted and adversarially reviewed per the skill's own process: claude-sonnet-5 executor, gpt-5.6-sol judge (equal-or-greater class, different provider — the new rule in action).

author: wlilley93
body:
Four dependabot PRs proposing a **runtime** jump. None adoptable. Each bounded at the thing it diverges from, not at the version offered.

| PR | offered | what it diverges from |
|---|---|---|
| #229, #231 | python 3.12.13 → **3.14.0** | Dockerfile pins 3.12.13; `requires-python = ">=3.12"`; CI runs 3.12 at all three job sites; the quality gate's Linux venv is 3.12.13 |
| #232 | postgres 16.14 → **18.3** | the stack's database is `pgvector/pgvector:pg16`, pinned by digest in `docker-compose.yml` |
| #234 | node 22-alpine → **25-alpine** | 22 is LTS; **25 is odd-numbered and never becomes LTS** |

## Why each one matters

**python** — taking 3.14 ships a *service image* on an interpreter no gate has ever executed. Everything that could catch a regression runs 3.12.

**postgres** — this would have put the deploy image two majors ahead of the data it talks to. A Postgres major is a dump-and-restore with a downtime window, never a lockfile edit.

**node 25** — it passed **all 18 checks**, and that is precisely the point. CI can tell you the build works. It cannot tell you the runtime will still be receiving fixes for as long as this service runs. An odd-numbered Node line stops getting them when the next current line opens. Moving a production service off LTS is a decision, not a dependency update.

Patches within each held line still arrive, which is where the runtime CVEs land.

## Merged alongside, all 18/18

#233 rclone 1.74.4 → 1.75.0, #235 node 22.23.1 → 22.23.2, #236 site group, #237 actions group.

#235 is worth noting: a patch *inside* the line held by the `/ui` node bound added earlier today. That is the bound working as intended rather than freezing the image.

author: fiorine
body:
Closes `[16221] Imlik` on the Bugs card: *"На твоем счету 399 трупов недобрых персонажей. Ты убил 1 добрых, 111 нейтральных и 281 злых персонажей — что то не сходиться, где то я получил 7 трупов не убив.."*

He is right, and the 7 are exactly accounted for.

`fight_exp.cpp` sums every `align_table` bucket except the killer's own:

```cpp
for (int a = 0; a < align_table.size; a++)
    if (a != myAlign)
        otherAlignKills += killed->align[a];
```

`align_table` index 0 is `N_ALIGN_NULL` (`bits.conf:800`), and `victAlign = IS_SET(victim->act, ACT_NOALIGN) ? N_ALIGN_NULL : ...` (`fight_exp.cpp:478`), so every ACT_NOALIGN kill lands there and gets summed as "недобрый".

`score` prints only the three real buckets (`command/score/runFunc:302`, `ch.killed.good/neutral/evil`), so the no-align kills are invisible there. 111 + 281 = 392 on screen, +7 no-align = 399 in the milestone. Exact match with the report.

**Not purely cosmetic.** The good-alignment charisma gain hangs off the same `% 200 == 199` test, so it fired one kill early for every no-align victim the player had ever killed.

The guard directly above (`else if (victAlign != N_ALIGN_NULL)`) already refuses to fire this message for a no-align victim, so excluding that bucket from the sum is what the surrounding code already intends.

### Drive-by

The format string mixed `%1$d` / `%1$I` with a bare `%s`. It resolved by luck; numbered it to `%2$s` to match the sibling message ten lines up. Catalog key renamed with it in `dreamland_world` so the existing EN/UA translations follow.

Syntax-checked clean.

author: sadriica
body:
## What was broken

`:::csv` and `:::data` blocks rendered "not found in this vault" for every spreadsheet **in the app**, while every test passed. The resolver that feeds the preview and all export paths is built from `vaultFiles`, which deliberately holds only `.md`/`.tex` (it also feeds the label scan, the diagnostics and vault search), so a `.csv` was never among them. The tests inject their own resolver, which is why nothing caught it.

Data files now travel in their own list, read once per change in the *set* of csv paths so an untouched file keeps the same string reference and the pointer cache in `datasets.ts` still short-circuits while you type. `findVaultFile` (new `vaultResolve.ts`) is now the single rule for turning a written name into a file, shared by both lists; a target carrying a folder (`archive/growth.csv`) now wins over a bare name match.

## From the audits

Three audits swept the typing path, the vault-wide operations, the React memoisation, every palette command and menu entry, and all 38 settings keys. Fixed here:

- **GraphPanel relaid its force simulation on every keystroke**: 80 steps of O(nodes²) repulsion, because `openTabs` is a new array per keystroke. Now keyed on the graph's shape.
- **`memo(FileTree)` was defeated by one inline arrow prop**, the component the memo exists for.
- **Three unconditional full-document passes** (task lists, TOC marker, section ids) now short-circuit like the code-masking pass already did; `buildParagraphLineMap` is cached by content identity, which halves it outright with the split pane open. Roadmap 4.2 and 4.5 in `docs/performance.md`.
- **`datasets.ts`'s CSV cache had no cap**, unlike every sibling cache.
- **The Edit menu advertised `Ctrl+Shift+D` for Duplicate Line**, a chord that opens the daily note; the underlying editor action ships with no binding. It now shows `Shift+Alt+Down`, which really duplicates the line.

Left open and recorded in `docs/performance.md`: the draft flush and the KaTeX clear-all (4.3/4.4), `BacklinksPanel` bypassing the mtime cache, and the vault-wide label scan running on the main thread when its panel is open.

The settings audit found **no dead and no partial settings**: all 38 keys reach the behaviour they claim to control.

## Verification

`tsc`, `eslint`, 1302 unit tests, coverage, `npm run build` and the 7 Playwright e2e tests all green. Measured after the changes on a synthetic thesis chapter: render 10/19/49 ms at 2/8/26 KB, lint 1/1/3 ms, against a 150-700 ms render debounce and a separate 600 ms linter timer.

author: yktyagi
body:
#### Merge Checklist  <!-- REQUIRED -->

**All** boxes should be checked before merging the PR

- [x] The changes in the PR have been built and tested
- [x] Documentation has been updated to reflect the changes (or no doc update needed)
- [ ] Ready to merge

#### Description <!-- REQUIRED -->

ICT runs as root so it can create loop devices, mount, and chroot. Two consequences of that are addressed here.

**1. Return build artifact ownership to the sudo invoker** (`feat(build)`)

Because the tool runs as root, every directory and file it creates is `root:root` — including the final image, SBOM, and checksums, plus the temp scratch dir. After a successful `sudo -E ict build` the invoking user could not read or delete their own output without root.

- Adds `system.ChownArtifactsToSudoUser` and `system.ChownDirTreeToSudoUser`, keyed off `SUDO_UID`/`SUDO_GID`, called on the build **success** path.
- Artifacts: the path nodes from the workspace down to `imagebuild/<name>` are chowned non-recursively (enough to traverse/list); the artifact leaf is chowned recursively so the image/SBOM/checksums become user-owned. Sibling chroot trees (`chrootenv/`, `chrootbuild/`) are deliberately left root-owned — they are real root filesystems whose ownership is load-bearing.
- Temp dir is chowned recursively (inert scratch). The cache dir is intentionally left root-owned: it persists across builds and later root builds repopulate it anyway.
- Both helpers no-op when not launched via sudo (`SUDO_UID` unset, or root→root), use `os.Lchown` so a planted symlink cannot redirect the chown out of the tree, and are best-effort — a chown failure is logged but never fails an otherwise successful build. Both resolve symlink components (`filepath.EvalSymlinks`) and re-validate before walking, so a symlinked intermediate path component cannot redirect the recursive chown outside the tree that was vetted, and both refuse dangerous roots (`/`, the system temp dir an empty `temp_dir` falls back to, and any top-level directory).
- For `--no-cache` the artifact chown targets the workspace the output was copied back to. The temp chown also runs in `--no-cache` mode: isolation only makes the cache and workspace unique, not `config.TempDir()`, so a root build still populates the shared temp dir and its cleanup does not remove it.

**2. Drop the redundant inner sudo when already root** (`refactor(shell)`)

`GetFullCmdStr` unconditionally prepended `sudo ` to every privileged host and chroot command. ICT is already launched as root (CLI via `sudo -E ict build …`, server via `sudo -n ict build …`), so that inner sudo is a root→root no-op that only forks an extra sudo process per command (and would otherwise need its own sudoers entry on the serve path).

- Adds a `sudoPrefix()` helper that omits the prefix when `os.Geteuid() == 0` and keeps it otherwise, applied to both the chroot and host branches. `geteuid` is indirected through a package variable so both branches are unit-testable without changing process privileges.
- When the process is not root, the per-command sudo model is unchanged. The mock executor is intentionally left always-sudo so existing `sudo chroot .*` test patterns keep matching; only the real path is euid-aware.
- Makes the behavior the release notes already described actually true, and extends it from chroot-only to host commands too; the note is updated to match.

#### Any Newly Introduced Dependencies

None.

#### How Has This Been Tested? <!-- REQUIRED -->

- `go test ./internal/utils/system/...` — covers `ChownArtifactsToSudoUser`/`ChownDirTreeToSudoUser`, including the no-op-when-not-sudo, symlink-safety, and dangerous-root-refusal paths (`internal/utils/system/ownership_test.go`).
- `go test ./internal/utils/shell/...` — covers `sudoPrefix()` in both the root and non-root branches via the indirected `geteuid` (`internal/utils/shell/shell_sudoprefix_internal_test.go`).
- Manual: `sudo -E ict build` of an Ubuntu 24.04 overlay image; verified the resulting image/SBOM/checksums and `./tmp` are owned by the invoking user on success, while `chrootenv/`/`chrootbuild/` and `./cache` remain root-owned.

author: oblomov-dev
body:
## Description

Fixes a race condition where `SET_FOCUS` fails when sent in the same roundtrip as a `view_model_update` that changes a control's state (e.g., re-enabling a disabled input via its `enabled` binding).

**The Problem:**
When a single response contains both a model update and a `SET_FOCUS` follow-up action:
1. The control's model state updates immediately (e.g., `enabled=true`)
2. `SET_FOCUS` executes synchronously and calls `focus()` on the control
3. However, UI5 re-renders the control asynchronously
4. The browser silently ignores `focus()` on a disabled DOM element
5. Result: focus lands nowhere, even though the control is now enabled

**The Solution:**
Enhanced `SET_FOCUS` to detect when focus fails to stick and automatically retry after the control's pending re-render:
- After the initial focus attempt, check if focus actually landed in the target control
- If not, register a one-shot `onAfterRendering` delegate on the control
- After the re-render completes, defer the retry past the rendering task (to avoid being overridden by UI5's own focus restoration)
- Only retry if the user hasn't actively moved focus elsewhere in the meantime
- Handle the case where the re-render also rebuilt the previously-focused element (e.g., a button that triggered the action)

## How to test

1. Run `npm run verify:full` to execute all unit and e2e tests
2. The new unit tests in `node/tests/frontendAction.spec.js` cover:
   - Immediate focus when DOM accepts it
   - Retry after re-render when DOM initially refused focus

author: jackhenry87
body:
Replaces eight models that lost $33.42 of $50 with one that has external evidence behind it, and fixes the instrument that was supposed to tell us whether any of them worked.

## Why

| Evidence | Reading |
|---|---|
| Brier 0.308 (weather), 0.278 (sports) vs 0.25 for a coin flip | The models were worse than guessing |
| Avg CLV −11.6¢ / −6.0¢ | Consistently on the wrong side of the price |
| −$27.10 of the −$33.42 from one city, mostly one trade | Position limits arrived after the accident |
| 0 usable CLV samples in a month | The edge measurement was broken |
| Odds API returning 401 for weeks, every run green | `\|\| true` on every workflow step hid it |

## The surviving model

`strategy_favorite.py` — buy the favourite side, maker-only. It makes no forecast. It rests on two structural facts measured by others on large samples: the favourite-longshot bias (sub-10¢ contracts lose >60% of stake; high-priced contracts return a small positive amount) and the maker/taker gap (~−10% vs ~−32% on longshots, with makers paying no Kalshi fee).

Uses public market data only. No paid API, so nothing to expire.

## Fixes to the measurement

- CLV now enrols paper signals, not just real fills — with the book paper-only it previously tracked nothing.
- Rows that closed before any open-market snapshot are reported as `unscored` instead of writing a blank CLV the scoreboard silently dropped. Four real bets became "0 settled bets" with nothing saying why.
- Fill realism: a resting bid is not a fill. Paper rows stay `resting` until the book reaches the price; **real** orders are confirmed against Kalshi's own fills endpoint, which is the one measurement paper trading cannot produce.
- Settlement W/L and P&L now recorded from public results — no order required.

## Sizing

`sizing.py` sizes each signal off its own edge rather than a flat stake. Kelly for a binary contract is `edge / (100 − entry)`; an 89¢ favourite risks 89¢ to win 11¢, so a 2¢ edge is 18% of bankroll at full Kelly. Quarter Kelly is used because the edge is uncertain, the bankroll is small and the positions are correlated. The edge is split by trust: the mechanical part (`mid − entry`) is certain given a fill, the favourite-bias part is the claim under test and is halved.

A stake below one contract sizes to **zero** contracts, never one.

Also fixes an error in the edge calculation: it previously counted `ask − entry` (what a taker gives up crossing the spread) as edge rather than `mid − entry` (what we gain over fair value), inflating every signal ~3× and every position size derived from it.

## Risk controls

- `MAX_ORDERS_PER_DAY` (8) and `MAX_DAILY_DEPLOY_USD` ($15) — nothing previously bounded a *day*; the exposure cap alone would let ~90% of a $50 bankroll out in one run. Counted off the executed ledger so they survive the scheduler starting a fresh process every 20 minutes.
- Maker discipline enforced at placement: the market is re-fetched and the price re-checked against the current ask, re-priced or skipped if it would cross.
- Every order passes `safety.check_order`. `KILL_SWITCH` blocks all placement.

## Infrastructure

- Adds `tests.yml` — the repo had **no** CI running the test suite at all. Should be made a required check.
- Deletes fifteen bot workflows; adds `favorite.yml` and `env-check.yml`. No `|| true` in any of them.
- Bot state moves to a `bot-state` branch. 49 of the last 50 commits on `main` were bot state, which made the history useless and raced the deploy branch.

## Testing

**325 passing, from 6 failed / 7 errors.**

- Pinned the clock in the smartmoney tests via the existing `now_ts` parameter — their fixture windows had aged out and would have rotted again.
- `tests/conftest.py` isolates state paths; a test was truncating the real `sports_line_history.json` the steam filter depends on.
- New tests build from a captured live payload. The live API has no `volume` key at all (it is `volume_fp`), so the volume filter read a missing field, got 0, and rejected all 4000 markets — the unit tests passed while the model signalled nothing in production. Verified fixed against the real API: 23 signals on prod.

author: alexgodbehere
body:
Reopens #178, which GitHub closed when its base branch was deleted on merge of #176. Same commit, rebased onto `main`.

Two gaps found while diagnosing the install failure, neither closed by #176.

## 1. A raw active swap on the target is invisible to every guard

Swap is not a mount, so `/proc/mounts` never names it — and with no device-mapper in the way the partition has no holders either, so #176's walk misses it too. The installer would have run `wipefs` and `mkfs` straight over a live swap device, which is corruption on a running system.

It now gets released with everything else, and if it will not go the install refuses by name with the remedy attached, while nothing has been erased:

```
/dev/sdb4 on /dev/sdb is still an active swap device and could not be swapped off.
Run 'swapoff /dev/sdb4' and install again (nothing was erased)
```

`/proc/swaps` is behind `POLYPTIC_SWAPS_FILE`, like every other input this script reads, so it is testable off-box.

## 2. Stale filesystem signatures survive into re-made partitions

`sgdisk --zap-all` and the disk-level `wipefs -a` destroy the partition **table**, not the filesystems inside the partitions it described. The layout is deterministic, so a re-install re-creates every partition at exactly the same LBA — on top of the previous install's superblocks. `mkfs` writes its own, but a partition that carried a *different* filesystem last time keeps both signatures, and then `blkid` reports two and udev picks one.

Each new partition now gets a `wipefs -a` before its `mkfs`. Standard hygiene, five ioctls.

**Worth calibrating**: this one is smaller than I implied when I first flagged it. It does *not* explain the stale `POLYPTIC-SCRATCH` on the failed box's p5 — that partition was formatted by an earlier run that got further, and nothing here would have prevented it. The real protection against a half-installed disk is the install succeeding, which is #176. This is hygiene worth having, not a bug that was biting.

## Tests

Seven new cases: the raw-swap release, the stuck-swap refusal with "nothing was erased" proven by an empty sgdisk log, swap on a *different* disk being left alone, all five partitions wiped, and the ordering — a wipe after `mkfs` would erase the filesystem it just made.

The `swapoff` stub now deactivates as well as logging, since a released device that stayed in the fixture would be re-read and refused. Mutation-checked: removing the partition wipe fails exactly the assertion that covers it. Full suite ALL PASS.

author: groeneai
body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110176
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111194
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed the `LOGICAL_ERROR` `Reading from materialized CTE '...' before its materialization completed - DelayedPortsProcessor gate is missing in the query plan` when `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` runs a query that reads a materialized CTE behind an `IN` subquery together with `extremes = 1` or `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS`.


### Description

`QueryPipelineBuilder::addPipelineBefore` routes the totals and extremes streams through the `DelayedPortsProcessor` that gates a materialized CTE read, so they are gate output ports.

`QueryPipeline::complete` discarded them by attaching a `NullSink`. A `NullSink` has no outputs, so `ExecutingGraph::initializeExecution` seeds it and it runs first, and its `prepare` closes its input without ever pulling. That finishes a gate output; the gate finishes the pair and closes the paired input; the gated sub-pipeline is released. The CTE read then runs before `MaterializingCTETransform` has built it and the fail-fast check in `ReadFromMemoryStorageStep` throws, aborting the server in a build with assertions.

The two streams are now discarded with a `DroppingTransform` on the main output instead. It forwards the data stream 1:1 and drains totals/extremes, so it keeps data outputs and is not seeded. This is the mechanism `641fc75ea3f0d37` already established for the builder's own drop sites; extending it here leaves the file with no producer of an output-less discard node, so `drop` and the `NullSink.h` include are deleted. The helper returns immediately when neither port exists.

Reached from ordinary SQL, with only `enable_materialized_cte` gated. This does not close #110176 by itself, although it does fix that issue's reproducer: `INSERT ... SELECT` and an aggregating subquery reach the same error through `dropTotalsAndExtremes`, a separate site that #111194 addresses.

Validation: the four `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` shapes abort on unpatched master and pass with the change. Four mutants each redden the new test: reverting the helper call, discarding the aux ports with `NullSink` while keeping the transform, and corrupting a control or a witness reference line. Reintroducing a `drop` call no longer compiles. The test passes 100/100 runs (50 randomized, 50 not), and across 262 stateless cases using `extremes`, `WITH TOTALS`, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` or materialized CTEs no case fails only with the change and no failure reason changes.

author: ben-reitz
body:
A proposal, stacked on #2050. Fixes #1913 together with that PR. ## Why a second change #2050 stops a resumed stream from writing chat state once per replayed chunk. It merges the chunks that belong to the same piece of text, so a few hundred chunks become a handful of writes. That helps enormously, but it only merges *within* a part. A tool step costs about seven writes on its own, so a replayed turn of more than about seven tool steps still reaches React's 50-render limit and still shows a false error. Measured with the merge in place: six steps fine, eight throws. A throttle does not care how many chunks arrive, so it covers what merging cannot. ```mermaid flowchart LR C["chunks arrive"] --> M["#2050
merge replayed chunks"] --> T["this PR
throttle renders"] --> R["at most one render
per 50ms"] ``` ## The change `useAgentChat` now coalesces chat updates every 50ms. Pass `throttle: false` to render every chunk as it arrives, or a number to pick your own interval. Nothing else changes, and the first chunk of a stream is never delayed - the AI SDK throttles with `throttleit`, which runs the first call of an idle window immediately. ## Why 50ms Any value above zero prevents the crash, because the update then arrives from a timer rather than from the current task. Verified at 1, 4, 16, 50, 100 and 250ms. So the size of the number is a cost decision rather than a safety one. Measured over a 200-chunk turn at ~100 chunks/sec (caveat that this is obvs on a powerful macbook): | throttle | renders | render time | | --- | --- | --- | | off | 404 | 138ms | | 16ms | 261 | 89ms | | **50ms** | **90** | **37ms** | | 100ms | 48 | 21ms | | 250ms | 22 | 9ms | 50ms removes 78% of the renders. Larger values save progressively less while letting the text lag further behind the stream. It is also the value the AI SDK's own documentation uses, and 25 of our 27 examples already pass 100ms by hand, so throttling is not new behaviour for our own UIs - only the default is. ## Two things worth knowing `@ai-sdk/react` v3 reads only `experimental_throttle`; v4 renamed it to `throttle`. Both majors are in our peer range, so the value is sent under both names. Turning it off omits both names rather than sending `0`, because both majors decide with `waitMs != null`, and only an omitted option reaches their unthrottled path. This proposed change provides a mitigation rather than a guarantee. `useChat` throttles its store subscription, but its `getSnapshot` returns a new messages array on every chunk, and React forces a synchronous re-render whenever that identity moved during a render - a path the throttle never sees. That is vercel/ai#6166, with a fix open in vercel/ai#17893. Writing state less often is the only thing that bounds it, which is why #2050 does the heavier lifting. ## Tests Eight unit tests in `chat/__tests__/chat-throttle.test.ts` cover the precedence rules and both spellings. Two tests in `react-tests/default-throttle.test.tsx` drive the real hook with a 12-step tool turn: it stays healthy on defaults, and `throttle: false` restores the old failure, which proves the caller's value reaches the SDK. Suites: agents chat 540 · react 135 · ai-chat 737 · think 920 + react 5 · `pnpm run check`.

## Why

#260 (next-auth → beta.32) cleared the next-auth advisories but **left one critical open**, because the vulnerable package survived one level down:

```
node_modules/@auth/core                    0.41.2   <- vulnerable, HOISTED
node_modules/@auth/pg-adapter              1.11.2   <- depends on EXACTLY 0.41.2
node_modules/next-auth/node_modules/@auth/core  0.41.3   <- patched, but nested
```

`next-auth@beta.32` carries its own patched nested copy, so the advisory looked half-fixed — but `@auth/pg-adapter@1.11.2` pins `@auth/core` to **exactly** `0.41.2`, and that copy is the one hoisted to the top of `node_modules`.

`@auth/pg-adapter@1.11.3` requires `0.41.3`, which collapses the tree to a single patched copy.

## Advisories cleared

| Severity | Advisory |
|---|---|
| **critical** | Email normalizer validates the address before Unicode normalisation |
| high | `getToken()` throws an uncaught exception on a malformed Bearer header |
| medium | OAuth `state`/`nonce`/PKCE check cookies not bound to the transaction |

This takes the repo's open Dependabot alerts from 10 (3 critical) → 3, with **zero critical remaining**.

author: elinsc-bot
body:
Closes #50 (the `scf`/`nscf` half of it; `screening`, `interpolation` and `eps` arrive with the features that consume them).

### Problem

Every step of every workflow sampled one mesh, `kpoints.grid`. That mesh is chosen for the Wannier functions and is often deliberately coarse, so an scf — which only has to converge the density — had no way to run finer, and an nscf that wants to be Γ-centred had no way to differ from an scf that converges faster shifted.

`density` was the second half of the problem: it counts k-points per unit length *along the path*, but sitting beside `grid` it reads like the density of a mesh.

### Changes

- `kpoints.overrides`, keyed by step, with `scf` and `nscf` entries. Each may set `grid` for that step alone, and the `scf` entry an `offset` as well; anything left out comes from the top level, and the values are absolute, so the input file states what will run.
- `grid_spacing` on an entry, mutually exclusive with `grid`, reaching Quantum ESPRESSO as aiida-quantumespresso's `kpoints_distance` — cell-adaptive density convergence written into the input file rather than left to a protocol nobody chose.
- The nscf entry takes neither `grid_spacing` nor `offset`: its dimensions are wannier90's `mp_grid`, which a spacing does not state, and koopmans builds that mesh Gamma-centred — every route expands it with `get_explicit_kpoints`, which returns the unshifted k-list. Both are parse errors rather than keywords that reach nothing.
- `density` becomes `path_density`. The old spelling is a parse error naming the new one, not a silent alias.
- A route that cannot honour an entry rejects it: `nscf` on `dft_bands` and `dft_eps`, which have no nscf mesh, and *both* steps on the kcp.x routes, where nothing between the input file and kcp.x carries a second mesh — `MlwfInitialization` takes one `kpoints`, which its scf samples and its supercell is folded from. Stated as the scope boundary it is, not as physics.

Before and after, converging the density on a finer mesh than the Wannierization:

```json
"kpoints": {"grid": [4, 4, 4], "path": "LGXKG", "density": 10.0}
```

```json
"kpoints": {
    "grid": [4, 4, 4],
    "path": "LGXKG",
    "path_density": 10.0,
    "overrides": {"scf": {"grid": [8, 8, 8]}}
}
```

and what the old name now gets you:

```
Errors found in the input file:

 `kpoints` Value error, `density` has been renamed `path_density`: it counts k-points per unit length along `path`, and sitting beside `grid` it reads like the density of a mesh. Rename it.
```

### Testing

- Every accepted attribute is read back off the built calculation rather than off the parsed input: the scf grid, the scf `grid_spacing` and the nscf grid, on `dft_bands`, `dft_eps`, both wannierize routes and DFPT. Where a step is nested inside a `@task.graph` and the socket is as far as a built graph reads, a separate test drives `PwBaseWorkChain.get_builder_from_protocol` and checks the spacing lands on `builder.kpoints_distance`.
- A companion test shows a mesh handed over beside a distance wins, which is why a step given a `grid_spacing` gets no mesh — the failure would otherwise be an inert keyword rather than an error.
- The nscf tests assert the k-list and the consumer's dimensions move together — wannier90's `mp_grid` and kcw.x's `CONTROL.mp1-3` — since an `mp_grid` left behind describes a different sampling from the one the nscf ran.
- Each rejection is checked for the keyword it sends the reader to, and the trajectory one additionally for what it must *not* say: that route runs kcp.x whatever `screening_method` asks for, so naming a method would tell the reader to set what they already set.
- Parse: the closed step and attribute sets, `grid` against `grid_spacing`, `nscf.grid_spacing`, `nscf.offset`, a non-mapping `overrides`, and `overrides` under `gamma_only` — the last checked on a model built in code as well as on a parsed dict.
- The `nscf.offset` rejection is paired with a test that an `scf` offset does reach the mesh pw.x samples, so the entry the message sends the reader to is one that works.

Pairs with elinscott/aiida-koopmans#68, which adds the `scf_kpoints` socket the DFPT route needs.

body:
The deploy job failed **six times in a row** today, always the same way: build green, artifact uploaded, deployment created, then stuck in `deployment_queued` until the action's 10-minute cap aborted it.

The cause is in this file. `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` was `true`, so a newer run cancels a deployment already in flight. GitHub's own starter workflow for Pages sets it to `false` and says why:

> Allow only one concurrent deployment, skipping runs queued between the run in-progress and latest queued. **However, do NOT cancel in-progress runs as we want to allow these production deployments to complete.**

Today's runs overlapped — a re-run and a `workflow_dispatch` on top of an active deploy — so each cancelled the previous one mid-deployment, and every deployment after that sat queued forever.

### Ruled out along the way, so nobody re-checks them

| hypothesis | evidence against |
| --- | --- |
| artifact too large | 81.69 MB on the **successful** runs and the failing ones alike |
| GitHub incident | status API reported all systems operational, no incidents |
| environment protection | only rule is a branch policy |
| deploy timeout too short | `600000` ms is the action's hard **maximum**, not its default — a larger value is clamped back with a warning |

### Verification

Workflow parses as YAML with `cancel-in-progress: false`; `prettier --check` passes.

author: bgrewell
body:
## Summary

P3 slice: the `udf` package goes from 33 panic stubs to a working **ECMA-167 read implementation**, and pure-UDF images are now actually detected.

### Detection fix
`iso.Open` previously probed sector 256 for the "BEA01" string — but BEA01 lives in the Volume Recognition Sequence at sector 16+, and sector 256 holds the binary AVDP. Pure UDF images could never be detected. `udf.IsUDF` now scans the VRS for an NSR02/NSR03 descriptor; bridge discs still open through the richer ISO 9660 path.

### Read path (ECMA-167)
- Descriptor tags with checksum verification
- AVDP → volume descriptor sequence (PVD, partition descriptor, logical volume descriptor) with reserve-VDS fallback
- File Set Descriptor → root ICB → recursive traversal: FE and EFE ICBs, short_ad / long_ad / inline allocation, FIDs with OSTA compressed unicode names (8-bit and UCS-2)
- File content served through the multi-extent segmented reader from #11 — fragmented files assemble transparently
- Symlink ICBs decode path component sequences; ECMA-167 permission bits map to POSIX modes with uid/gid
- Depth-bounded directory walk guards against cycles in corrupt images

### Interface
Read-only `ISO` implementation: listing, `ReadFile`, `Extract` (with symlink materialization), identity getters. Mutations return `ErrWriteUnsupported` — an honest error instead of the previous panics.

## Test plan
- Tests construct a structurally valid UDF image from scratch (VRS, AVDP, VDS, FSD, nested directory tree) — every descriptor our parser reads is exercised by bytes we control
- Detection positive/negative cases, listing counts, uid/gid/mode decoding, file reads at both levels, extraction to disk, read-only error contract
- Full suite green: `go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...`
- Note: no UDF authoring tool exists on the dev host (mkudffs/udfinfo absent); verification against a foreign-authored UDF image is a good follow-up for CI

author: blashkar
body:
Closes #54. The AFT half — and **this one does not stack**, so it can merge independently of #53 and #56.

## It answers the open question on #54

I'd flagged that the dev database has zero `aft_*` transaction rows and suggested confirming whether AFT origination creates one at all. It doesn't: `create_credit` inserts only into `aft_entries`, and the first `transactions` row appears at settlement. So the answer is *"carry the link forward"*, same as cards — not "nothing to stamp".

| | Where |
|---|---|
| `screen()` | `aft.rs:384` (`create_credit`), `aft.rs:485` (`create_debit`) |
| Origination persisted | `aft_entries` row — **no transactions row** |
| `transactions` row | settlement loop, via `rail.hold()` |

## Why it doesn't need to stack

It needs nothing from either open PR:

- Not #53's `tag_fraud` — that takes a `&FraudLink`; here the linkage is a *stored blob* off the entry, so it's written directly (the way `capture` does in #56).
- Not #56's `account_holds` column — different table entirely.

So it branches off `main` rather than sitting three deep behind two unreviewed PRs. The only overlap is textual: one more line in `database.rs`'s self-heal list and one more test in `fraud_port.rs`. Trivial to resolve whichever order they land in.

## The change

`aft_entries` gains `metadata JSONB` (canonical DDL in `09_aft.sql` + the idempotent ALTER in the self-heal list). **Verified against the existing dev database** — added in place, pre-existing entries read `NULL`, correctly "no linkage recorded".

Both origination sites stamp the same `FraudLink::metadata()` blob that `transactions.rs`, cards and the rails use, so one shape now travels every path. Only when actually screened — an empty blob would assert a decision that doesn't exist.

The settlement loop reads it back onto the hold row it just created, per-entry (which the loop already is).

**Not stamped:** the release leg or batch aggregates. A release is the second leg of an already-screened movement; a batch total isn't a movement at all. Same rule that kept #53 to holds and #56 off `card_settlement`.

## The test

Two assertions, and the second is the one a naive fix gets wrong: the `operation_id` must **name a real row in the engine's `decisions` table**, and must be **the id minted at origination**, read off `aft_entries` before settlement runs. Settlement doesn't re-screen — it executes a decision already made — so a different id there would mean something screened silently.

Probed by dropping the carry-forward:

```
a settled AFT movement must resolve:
{"decision_id":null,"failed_open":false,"operation_id":null,"transaction_id":"109d584b-…"}
```

## Verification

`fraud_port` 11, `agents` 40, `transactions` 16, `interac` 8, `finance` 4, `back_office` 12 — all green with the backend off. With `FRAUD_E2E=1`: 10 + the pre-existing `engine_mode_agent_refusal_audits_once`.

clippy shows no new warnings on the changed files. (`models/aft.rs` and `rails/aft.rs` have pre-existing dead-code warnings; I didn't touch those files.)

---

With this, #53 and #56, every screened money movement in the bank records which decision gated it — so a null from `fraud-link` finally means *"not screened"* rather than *"not written down"*, which was the whole point of #52.

## Description
This PR fixes real bugs found in the codebase:

- Added explicit radix to `parseInt`: without `10`, strings like `'0x1F'` or `'08'` parse in unintended bases.
- Replaced global `isNaN` with `Number.isNaN`: the global version coerces its argument, so `isNaN('1')` returns false while `Number.isNaN` is strict.

## Что сделано

Сервис регистрации международных посылок с фоновым расчётом стоимости доставки.

### Обязательная часть ТЗ
- 4 роута API + валидация через go-playground/validator
- PostgreSQL (pgx/v5, сырой SQL), миграции goose вшиты в бинарник
- Периодический расчёт: пачки по 100 с FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, пул из 4 горутин
- Кэш курса ЦБ РФ в Redis, ручной запуск расчёта под DEBUG_MODE
- Swagger, docker-compose, стандартные конверты ответов и ошибок
- slog в JSON с trace_id и длительностью запроса
- Слои handler → service → repository, интерфейсы объявлены у потребителей

### Дополнительно
- Доп. задание №3: гонка за перевозчика через атомарный UPDATE ... WHERE carrier_id IS NULL
- Тесты: формула расчёта, сервисный слой с заглушками, HTTP-слой через httptest

### Решения, требующие пояснения
- **Кэш курса — два ключа.** TTL 1 час и «использовать последнее известное значение»
  несовместимы в одном ключе: после истечения TTL брать нечего. Поэтому
  `exchange:usd:rub` с TTL и `exchange:usd:rub:stale` без срока жизни.
- **Закрепление перевозчика — один UPDATE.** Предварительный SELECT создал бы окно
  для гонки. Проверено 20 одновременными запросами: один 200, девятнадцать 409.
- **Деньги — NUMERIC в базе.** float накапливает ошибку округления.

    docker compose up -d --build
    curl http://localhost:8080/readyz

Swagger UI: http://localhost:8080/swagger/index.html

author: baozhoutao
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#5613

#5613 phase 2 的 **runtime 半边**(spec 半边为 #5779 / PR #5849,已在主干 `d4e080937`)。维护者裁定「C 骨架 + A 语义,contract-first 两阶段」:契约先立、生产者随后。本 PR 就是那个「随后」。

## 前提复核(实测,非照抄 issue)

以最新 `origin/main`(`5582e1821`)为基线逐条实测:

- `packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.zod.ts` 的 `ActionSessionSchema` **已含** `positions`(权威键)+ 弃用别名对,ADR-0087 语义迁移条目 `action-session-*-to-positions` 已在 `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`、`spec-changes.json`、`docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` 三处就位 —— 契约面确实已解锁;
- `buildActionSession()` 现址 `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:768`(issue 正文的 689-695 行号已漂),仍只发别名键,值取自 `ec.positions`;docstring 仍自称 "mirroring the hook `ctx.session` shape (#3280)";
- 两处调用点仍在:`packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts:333`、`action-execution.ts:999`(均只是 `session: buildActionSession(deps, ec)`,形状变化直接流过,无需改动);
- 预埋翻转点(键集 `toEqual` 断言)仍在 `packages/runtime/src/action-session-shape-contract.test.ts`。

前提成立。

## 改了什么

**1. `buildActionSession()` 双发(`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`)**

```ts
...(Array.isArray(ec.positions) && ec.positions.length
    ? { positions: ec.positions, roles: ec.positions }
    : {}),
```

一个数组、两个键名,由构造保证同值(不是两次可能漂开的读取)。**「非空才写」语义原样保留**:无 positions(或 `positions` 非数组)时两个键都不出现 —— `'positions' in ctx.session` 与别名键的 `in` 判定同真同假;无身份信封时整个 session 仍是 `undefined` 而非 `{}`(#3712)。

**2. 两句错注释修正**

- 「mirroring the hook `ctx.session` shape」自 #5050 起就是错的(hook 侧同名键已退役,且 hook session 本就是另一套键集、另一个生产者 `buildSession()`)—— 删除该自述,改为如实说明:形状由 `ActionSessionSchema` 声明、本函数是其唯一生产者、一致性由 pin 测试守;
- 原「⚠️ 两句被登记为 WRONG,留给 phase 2 一起改」的临时段落随之退场,替换为弃用窗口的正式说明(权威 `positions` / 别名 / 迁移条目 / 移除路径 #3280→#3290)+ 「两个拼法都不是授权输入」的警示。

**3. 翻转预埋断言 + 承载双发同值(`action-session-shape-contract.test.ts`)**

键集断言翻为含 `positions` 的新形态,并把窗口期的承重事实钉住:两个键**都对着 `ec.positions` 断言**(而不是互相比对),所以「其中一个改从别处取值」也过不了;新增一条「别名绝不单独出现」,是窗口关闭那天删别名的方向性保险。

**4. 真实 dispatch 验证(`http-dispatcher.test.ts`)**

迁移条目的验收口径写明「Verify against a real dispatch, not a fixture」,故补了一条走 `dispatcher.handleActions` 的用例:持有 positions 的调用者发起 action,断言 **body 实际收到的** `ctx.session.positions`,以及同值的别名。

**5. `ScriptContext.session` 收窄 —— 收的是联合,不是 `ActionSession` 单型**

issue 第 4 条要求用 spec 的 `ActionSession` 收窄。实测后按「缩回最小面并说明」处理:这个 seam **确实同时承载 hook session 与 action session**(`body-runner.ts` 的 `buildSandboxContext` / `buildActionSandboxContext` 两个写入方),把它声明成 `ActionSession` 单型,正是本 issue 要消灭的「一个键名两种现实」的同型错误 —— 只是换到类型面上。因此新增并导出:

```ts
export type ScriptSession = ActionSession | HookContext['session'];
```

`session?: unknown` → `session?: ScriptSession`。#5697 当初留 `unknown` 的理由(收窄会逼 seam 的每个消费者去判别 body 种类)这次是**实测**而非再假设:两个写入方从 `any` 赋值,唯一读取方 `quickjs-runner` 的 `setObjectJson` 收 `unknown`,全仓(objectstack / objectui / cloud)`ScriptContext` 无 runtime 包外引用。所以今天没有任何站点需要判别,而联合类型正是让将来需要判别的站点被 tsc 抓住。收窄面止于 runtime 包内。

**6. changeset(major)+ 文档**

`.changeset/action-session-positions-runtime-dual-emit.md`,`@objectstack/runtime: major`,正文带 FROM → TO 迁移处方(改读 `positions`;别名在窗口内仍解析,窗口关闭按 #3280→#3290 路径移除;**不要**把 `…includes('admin')` 的访问判断改名成 `positions.includes('admin')` —— 那是把缺陷改名而不是把读改对),并把 `ScriptContext.session` 的收窄作为第二处 breaking 明写。

文档面实测:全仓没有任何 hooks/actions 文档在教 action 侧的旧拼法(`skills/objectstack-data` 讲的是 hook 侧已退役的那个键,`content/docs/references/ui/action-params.mdx` 是 #5849 已重生的生成物)。唯一真正教 action body `ctx` 的手写面是 `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md`,在其「Action body context (`ctx`)」小节补了 `ctx.session.positions` 的权威读法 + 「不是授权输入」的警示 + 指向升级指南的迁移指路。

> **该小节改过一次,原因值得记录**:初版在技能文档里直接写出弃用别名的示例,被 `check:role-word`(ADR-0090 D3 的 shrink-only 棘轮)判红 —— 保留词计数 2 → 5。棘轮是对的:技能文档是**授权写法**的教学面,只该教权威拼法;别名与迁移处方留在其本来的渠道(changeset + `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md`,均不在棘轮扫描面内)。已按此重写,`node scripts/check-role-word.mjs` 现报 `OK (43 baselined file(s), no new occurrences)`。

## 验证

**反向验证 —— 方向事先预测,结果与预测一致。** 预测:这是最常见的「红」向,而非 #5046 式的「诊断变多」或 #5009 式的「反转」—— 因为断言的是**产出对象的精确键集**,而被撤掉的正是产出该键的那条肢,缺席可直接观测(不存在「计数归零导致断言因空而绿」的陷阱)。把双发撤回只留别名后实测:

```
× builds exactly the declared keys …
  → expected 3 keys to deeply equal [ 'organizationId', 'positions', …(2) ]
× carries `ec.positions` verbatim under BOTH …
  → expected undefined to deeply equal [ 'sales_rep', 'org_admin' ]
× emits the alias only alongside the canonical key …
  → expected the built key list to include 'positions'
× omits `userId` entirely for an org-scoped call with no user
  → expected 2 keys to deeply equal [ 'organizationId', 'positions', …(1) ]
 Tests  4 failed | 7 passed (11)
```

真实 dispatch 用例同向变红:`expected undefined to deeply equal [ 'sales_rep', 'org_admin' ]`(`http-dispatcher.test.ts:3659`)。随后已还原。

**正向**(均在共享 verify 锁内、`--max-old-space-size=4096`):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test`(`--maxWorkers=2`):**Test Files 102 passed (102) / Tests 1476 passed (1476)**;
- `turbo run test --concurrency=2`(全仓):**135 successful, 135 total**;
- `turbo run typecheck --concurrency=2`(全仓):**125 successful, 125 total** —— 收窄没有溢出 runtime 包;
- `turbo run build --filter='!@objectstack/docs' --concurrency=2`:**71 successful, 71 total**;
- `pnpm lint`(eslint --no-inline-config,全仓):无输出即绿;lint job 的 24 个 `check:*` 逐条本地跑过,全 OK;
- spec 侧 `check:skill-docs` / `check:skill-refs` / `check:skill-examples` / `check:docs` / `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide`:全部 in sync;
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs`:`OK (scanned 5738 tracked text file(s))`。

⛔ 未动 `packages/spec`,未动 `content/docs/releases/`。

## 窗口关闭时要做什么(留给后来者)

移除别名的那一次改动,应当同时:producer 去掉别名键、`action-session-shape-contract.test.ts` 的键集期望与「双发同值」断言随之收缩、`http-dispatcher.test.ts` 的别名断言删除、spec 侧按迁移条目处置(条目已明说窗口期内**不**立 tombstone)。技能文档无需改动 —— 它从一开始就只教权威拼法。

body:
A WGS produziu um guia de gravação (`WGSguiaclipes.pdf`) pedindo **18 clipes curtos e mudos** da apresentadora — apontando, reagindo, gesticulando. O guia promete, a quem grava:

> *"você aparece reagindo, apontando e explicando **enquanto as fotos dos imóveis passam ao fundo**"*

## Esse "ao fundo" não existe neste pipeline

| Onde | O que faz |
|---|---|
| `pipeline/photo_slideshow.py:73` | `concatenate_videoclips(...)` — fotos e clipes **em sequência** |
| `pipeline/photo_slideshow.py:106` | `CompositeVideoClip` — mas as camadas são só **marca e legenda** |
| `pipeline/video_editor.py:40` | idem: b-roll de base + legendas por cima |

Os clipes da apresentadora entrariam **intercalados** (clipe → foto → foto → clipe), não **sobrepostos**. É um formato legítimo e o material serve assim desde já — mas não é o que o guia descreve.

Para a sobreposição falta **remoção de fundo** nos clipes (segmentação por IA ou chroma key) e uma camada de pessoa sobre o slideshow.

O guia foi escrito antecipando isso: a instrução *"sombra dura atrás de você atrapalha o **recorte**"* existe justamente por causa dessa etapa. A captação está desenhada certa; a peça de software é que ficou pendente.

## Por que registrar agora

A gravação **não precisa esperar o código** — os clipes servem intercalados hoje e sobrepostos depois, e a agenda da apresentadora é o recurso escasso. Mas quem for montar o vídeo precisa saber o que o pipeline entrega de fato, para não prometer ao cliente algo que ainda não sai.

> 📐 Os 4–5 segundos por clipe que o guia pede já casam com o `MAX_CLIP_SECONDS = 6.0` do slideshow — entram sem ajuste.

Também registrada a origem do modo de fotos: ele nasceu para outro nicho (o `--fotos` ainda se descreve como "modo slideshow de unhas" em `main.py`). Funciona igual para imóveis; só os textos de ajuda ficaram do projeto anterior.

Só documentação — nenhum código alterado.

author: samsam2703mfc
body:
## Ce qui manquait

Le commercial se **déduisait** des offres. Ça ne suffit pas : on ne pouvait pas confier un client à quelqu'un avant qu'il ait une offre, ni le reprendre sans que la reprise se défasse à la première vieille offre relue.

Une colonne `prospects.commercial_id`, et un menu en tête de fiche.

## Deux faits, pas deux vérités

| | Répond à | Écrit par |
|---|---|---|
| `prospects.commercial_id` | qui **suit** le client aujourd'hui | le menu de la fiche |
| `offres.cree_par` | qui a fait **cette offre**, et qui elle paie | la création de l'offre |

Les confondre coûterait précisément ceci : **assigner un client à quelqu'un reprendrait aussi les commissions déjà acquises par ses prédécesseurs**. Les anciennes offres gardent donc leur auteur, et l'écran l'écrit noir sur blanc sous le menu.

## Repris sur l'offre

Une offre créée pour un client assigné part au nom de **son** commercial, pas de qui clique. Sans ça, un administrateur qui ouvre une offre pour le client d'un autre s'en attribuait la commission — en silence, et sans plus rien pour la corriger ensuite. Sans assignation, l'auteur du clic, comme avant.

## L'origine du nom est toujours affichée

Sur la fiche comme dans la liste :

- **assigné** → une décision (pastille verte) ;
- **« d'après ses offres »** → une supposition qui changera d'elle-même à la prochaine offre ;
- **« compte désactivé »** → assigné à quelqu'un qui ne se connecte plus, donc suivi par personne — rien ne le disait avant ;
- **« aucun »** → ni assigné ni déductible. C'est l'anomalie que la liste nomme en bandeau, maintenant avec ce qu'il faut faire.

Les présenter pareil ferait lire une supposition comme une décision.

## Détails

- Rôle `technique` refusé à l'assignation — lui confier un client ne veut rien dire. Les admins sont proposés : dans une petite structure, le patron vend.
- Un compte assigné puis désactivé reste dans le menu, nommé « (compte désactivé) » : le retirer ferait effacer l'assignation au premier enregistrement, sans que personne ne l'ait demandé.
- `commercialDuClient()` porte la règle **une seule fois** — la fiche et la liste ne peuvent pas se contredire.
- Index `prospects_commercial` : « les clients d'Untel » se demande à chaque ouverture.
