author: tanglefast23
body:
Phase 4: **Portuguese (BR), French, Indonesian and German.** With this, all seven languages are enabled — `en`, `es`, `pt-BR`, `fr`, `id`, `de`, `vi` — 349 keys each, each with its own locked-terminology glossary.

Stacks on #97 (Spanish) and #98 (Vietnamese).

## German last, and it paid off

The plan put German last because it is the longest language and would surface any remaining layout ceiling. It surfaced none — and it produced the **fewest** budget overruns of the four (6, versus French's 15). Knowing it was the ceiling test meant writing terse German from the start rather than translating loosely and trimming after.

31 strings busted their character budgets across the four languages and were rewritten shorter. The budget is a copy rule; relaxing it was never on the table.

## The gate caught me cheating

Shortening French `Versement Ferveur` → `Versement` saved characters by **deleting the game's own noun**. Gate 9 failed it immediately. It reads `Ferveur versée` now — a label has to keep naming the thing it names, and "shorter" is not a licence to drop the term the player is learning.

That is the whole reason terminology is locked in CI rather than in a style doc.

## Column short forms

Each locale declares its own, measured against the real font by gate 8 rather than counted in characters:

| | EN | ES | PT-BR | FR | ID | DE | VI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Played | P | PJ | J | J | MN | SP | ST |
| Won / Drawn / Lost | W D L | G E P | V E D | G N P | M S K | S U N | T H B |
| Goal difference | GD | DG | SG | DB | SG | TD | HS |
| Points | PTS | PTS | PTS | PTS | PTS | PKT | Đ |

## A test that had to change meaning

`use-copy.test.ts` proved English fallback by asking an untranslated locale for a string. There is no untranslated locale left — so that assertion would have been testing nothing. It now asserts the opposite for all six: every shipped locale returns its **own** copy. Fallback stays covered by the resolver's own tests, where it belongs.

## Verification

- `npx jest src/i18n` — **85 gates** green with all seven locales enabled
- `npx jest src/ui` — 846 green
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean

## What's left

**Phase 5**, the long tail: `content/*.json` prose — events, tips, Bert, the glossary — roughly 1,270 strings. Reachable by key since #96, translated for nobody yet.

**Device QA is still owed for every language.** Nothing in this chain has run on hardware. German on the league table and Vietnamese in Handjet are the two checks that most want a real screen.

author: seanmcilroy29
body:
## Summary

The nightly regeneration commit message included `[skip ci]`, which GitHub interprets as an instruction to skip all CI — including the GitHub Pages build and deployment. This meant the dashboard data was being updated on `main` every night, but the live site was never re-deployed to serve the new version.

## Why [skip ci] was there

It was added to prevent an infinite loop: if a `push` trigger caused the generate workflow to run, its own commit would re-trigger it. However, the generate workflow is only triggered by `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` — **not** by `push` — so there is no loop risk and `[skip ci]` was never needed.

## The fix

Removed `[skip ci]` from the commit message. After merging, each nightly regeneration commit will correctly trigger a GitHub Pages rebuild and the live site will stay up to date.

author: brianegge
body:
Two dependency-update bots were configured here, but only one was ever used. Renovate has not opened a single pull request against this repository — 0 of the last 200 — while Dependabot has been keeping the action pins current. A second configuration that never runs is a second thing to keep correct, so this removes `renovate.json` and puts the effort into Dependabot instead.

## What changes

**Removed** `renovate.json`.

**`.github/dependabot.yml`** gains:

- a third entry watching `/docker/build`, so the images the CI build containers derive from — `rockylinux:9` in `rhel9.Dockerfile` and `ubuntu:noble` in `xenial.Dockerfile` — are tracked like everything else. These were the only container images in the repo nothing was watching.
- grouping for minor and patch action bumps, plus `open-pull-requests-limit: 5`. Every workflow pins its actions to a commit SHA, so Dependabot is the only thing that moves those pins; without grouping that becomes a stream of one-line PRs. The existing `codeql-actions` group is listed first and so still wins for those.

## Coverage after this change

| Surface | Watched by |
|---|---|
| Workflow actions (all 5 workflows) | `github-actions` at `/` |
| `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` | `docker` at `/.devcontainer` |
| `docker/build/{rhel9,xenial}.Dockerfile` | `docker` at `/docker/build` — **new** |
| `flake.nix` / `flake.lock` | nothing — see below |

Both `devcontainer.json` files build from `../Dockerfile` rather than naming an image directly, so the existing `/.devcontainer` entry already covers them; no `devcontainers` ecosystem entry is needed.

## Two things worth knowing

**Nix is not covered.** Dependabot has no Nix support, so `flake.lock` stays a manual update. Renovate does support Nix in principle, but never ran here, so nothing regresses — the gap predates this PR. If we want it automated, a scheduled `nix flake update` workflow is the usual answer and can be a separate change.

**The `/docker/build` entry wants a post-merge check.** Dependabot matches Dockerfiles by name, and these use the `<name>.Dockerfile` form rather than a plain `Dockerfile`. That form is expected to match, but it is worth confirming on the repository's Dependabot "last checked" page once this lands rather than assuming it silently works.

OpenSSF Scorecard's Dependency-Update-Tool check is satisfied by either tool, so removing Renovate while keeping Dependabot leaves that check at 10/10.

The layout was previously sized entirely in vw units and chained together with negative margins, with no media queries at all. Body copy rendered at roughly 4.5px on a phone and each section's position depended on every section above it.

Layout

Word art

- Bound the vertical sweep so the artwork's canvas-clipped end copies stay out of the hero

- Paint the art via CSS mask so its colour is a token, not baked into the PNG

Content and styling

JavaScript

author: andyzhangx
body:
## Summary
This PR is being closed instead of merged.

## Why
After looking at the Windows unmount behavior again, the more likely issue is that application pods still have active access to the mounted Azure Files share when `NodeUnstageVolume` tries to remove the SMB global mapping.

In that situation, adding a driver-side timeout is not the right fix. A timeout would only make the unstage path fail faster, while the underlying problem would still be that the workload has not released the file share cleanly.

## Current recommendation
If Windows unmount gets stuck, the user should first resolve the application-side issue, for example by:
- identifying pods/processes that still access the mounted file share
- stopping or draining the affected workload/node so file handles are released
- retrying after the SMB mapping can be removed cleanly

Given that, this PR will be closed.

**A display face.** Fraunces, variable, self-hosted: the Caddyfile sets `font-src 'self'`, so a CDN would work in development and be blocked in production, which is the worst way to find out. Only the `latin` subset ships — 67 kB, covering English, Italian and the prime in *L′*. It goes on headings and card titles and nowhere it would merely label: `.panel__title` is an `h2` and takes the text face back, because small uppercase letterforms are where a display serif stops being characterful. A measured number is still monospaced and tabular.

**Warm paper, and a second colour that means something.** `--spark` joins `--accent` under a rule: blue is the instrument, violet is the voice that explains. A measured quantity is never violet and a chapter control is never blue, so the handover from the story to the bench is visible before it is read.

**A homepage that asks before it states.** Every card led with a target — *"η < 1 on ≤ 2400 kg"* before saying what a truss is. Now it leads with the question the exercise answers, names the discipline underneath, and folds target, constraint and verification into *"the numbers behind it"* — the treatment ADR-017 already gave the prose on an experiment page. Four cards go two-up instead of three. The product's claim keeps its exact wording (ADR-016) and moves above the heading, read from `brand.tagline` so it cannot drift from the footer's copy.

## 2. A door — `shared/guide.js`, ADR-021

Four chapters above the mission: how the air holds a wing up (including that the equal-transit-time story is false), why what you are looking at is a slice and everything is per metre of span, what the four digits of a NACA number actually name, and then six angles of attack to press. *Go to the simulator* sits in the same position on every chapter, and taking it is remembered.

No modal, no overlay, no focus trap — the instrument is in the document the whole time. A browser that refuses storage loses the memory and nothing else.

- **Chapters are prose**, so they live in `content.json` / `content.it.json` beside the nine sections, and `check-i18n.mjs` now compares them across languages — with two rules of its own, since a chapter's `figure` names a drawing function and its `presets` carry the incidences the buttons run, both behaviour rather than prose.
- **Diagrams are generated** from `naca.js`, the four-digit formulae extracted out of `app.js` and proved point-for-point identical to what they replace. The reason is the one that makes the homepage thumbnails real solves, and it paid immediately: the first flow diagram ran its streamlines straight *through* the section.
- **A preset is a click, so it may solve.** It writes to the `<input>` and lets that control's own handler carry the value into the parameter object, never writing to the object directly — the second leaves the field showing one angle while the solver receives another. While a solve is in flight the ladder is disabled *with its reason in the tooltip* rather than removed.

**Three defaults moved with it.** Streamlines are on from the first result, asked for per page rather than globally, because a solver that publishes no vector field cannot draw one. Panels 240 → 320 and the sampling grid 192 → 256, chosen by measuring: panels are nearly free at +0.19 s and no payload, resolution is paid in **bytes** at about 1.1 MB per step, and 320 × 320 would have been 1.6 s and 3.9 MB for a page whose invitation is to press six buttons. Every measured residual in `docs/exercises/airfoil.md` was re-measured rather than re-worded.

## 3. The diagrams shipped hardcoded in English

They drew their own labels as literals inside `figures.js`, so the Italian page showed English captions under an Italian heading. Nothing caught it: `check-i18n.mjs` reads `t('key')` calls and `data-i18n` attributes, and a bare string inside an SVG is neither. They now come from the catalogue, which both fixes the page and puts them where the checker can see them — and they were shortened, because the Italian ran out of the `viewBox` on a phone.

## 4. One idea written down instead of half-built

The panel method is exactly linear in α, so two solves determine the flow at *every* angle and a slider could redraw at 60 fps with no further jobs. It is a proposal (`docs/proposals/instant-incidence.md`) rather than a commit because of §8 of the contract, not the arithmetic: the page would be showing numbers it computed itself from a basis the solver published, and in a lab that prints a residual on every run that is a different claim needing its own verification, its own answer to what a kept run records, and a rule for when the basis goes stale.

## Also fixed on the way past

`scripts/check-i18n.mjs` had no `heatsink` in its exercise list, from the release that built it — two content files nobody was comparing.

## Checks

`pytest` 344 passed · Playwright 75 passed · `ruff`, `mypy`, `check-pins`, `prettier`, `check:i18n` and the workflow's documentation check all run locally and pass. Verified in a real browser at 1280, 1100 and 375 px, in both languages and both colour schemes.

Two assertions changed rather than followed, and both were saying the wrong thing:

- the streamlines test *clicked* the tool and then looked for curves, which now turns them off;
- the four `.card__facts` assertions would have kept passing against a closed `<details>` without proving anything, since `toContainText` reads `textContent` — they now open the fold and require the quantity to be visible.

## Not in scope

The other three exercises open the way they always did. `guide.js` is shared so they can have chapters, but their chapters are physics prose to be written, not scaffolding to be reused.

author: haydenrear
body:
Implements **FI-02**, the epic's thesis ticket. `Refs #152`. Base `epic/falsifiable-instruments` (`51fe73d`, FI-01 merged).

## The enumeration — this ticket's product

```
python3 examples/validation/instruments/demonstrate.py
```

**37 rows enumerated.** Five were checked and classified **not** instruments — `fitness_functions`, `budgets`, `skill_feedback`, `case_modules coverage`, `score_tools index`, each of which refuses nothing by its own docstring — recorded so the denominator can be audited rather than trusted.

Of the **32 instruments**:

| | count |
|---|---|
| demonstrated **failing** input | **23** |
| demonstrated **passing** input | 27 |
| **CANNOT be shown to fail** | **9** |
| demonstrated **blind spot** | 9 |

Baseline was "roughly 0 of ~9". No target is set on the ratio and none should be.

Every demonstration stages its own tree in a tmpdir, breaks the **subject** rather than the instrument, and declares the verdict the instrument must return. The runner exits non-zero for exactly one reason: a declared demonstration stopped reproducing.

### The nine that cannot be shown to fail

| instrument | why |
|---|---|
| `code_complexity.py` | by construction and on purpose — a thermometer, one exit constant and it is zero |
| `check_catalogue.py --verify-suite` | a wrong prediction is printed and never added to `problems` — **FI-02-DF-01** |
| `run_port_swap.py` | `main()` ends in an unconditional `return 0` — **FI-02-DF-02** |
| `test_source_citations.py` | inline predicate over a `__file__`-derived list — **FI-02-DF-03** |
| `test_spec_yaml_valid.py` | same shape — **FI-02-DF-03** |
| `test_spec_manifest_records.py` | same shape — **FI-02-DF-03** |
| `test_port_declarations.py` | same shape — **FI-02-DF-03** |
| Test Graph nodes | needs gradle + JBang, not provisioned here; note `spec_workflow_force_failure.py` **is** a shipped demonstrated failing input |
| ticket-state agreement | **the instrument does not exist** — PA-02-DF-02, and an enumeration that omitted what should exist and does not would be flattering itself |

## What surprised me — the blind-spot column

S2 asks whether a criterion can fail. The question that actually paid was **what true thing can it not say.** Three of four findings came from that; none from the first.

- **The blinding sanitiser goes RED on `ports-as-adapters` and stays CLEAN on `"This is ARM B, the hexagonal treatment arm ... given the HEXAGONAL prompt by HP-02"`** — PA-06-DF-11's exact sentence, now run end to end on a three-file fixture this repo owns rather than against sealed evidence. Both halves are re-runnable.
- **`run_port_swap.py` prints a red control and exits 0 — and already has.** `swap-reference_ports.json` carries PA-M14 in `control_red` and that run exited 0, while `run_controls.py` exits 1 for the same condition. PA-04-DF-02's two-driver hazard, third occurrence.
- **Every `predicted_*` annotation in `seeded_faults.toml` is unchecked prose.** `--verify-suite` prints `*** DISAGREES ***` and does not append it. Three of that script's four modes can and do go red, which is why the fourth was not noticed.
- **Four repo tripwires share one shape** that makes them undemonstrable. The thermometer tripwire was the fifth member of that family, and it was wrong in both directions for a whole epic.

## The tripwire (PA-06-DF-05), fixed — **not** by renaming the string

- `executable_references()` — an **import under any alias**, or a string whose **whole value** is a path/module token. A prose sentence naming the script is not a reference, which is exactly the input that had it red.
- `test_no_reader_of_this_instrument_gates_on_its_output` — **the invariant the docstring always stated.** Taints from a reference onto if-tests, comparisons, asserts and exits, and it **does** reach `specs/`, which the reference scan no longer does because the plan declares that tree out of model.
- Red, green **and blind spot** are demonstrated in `tests/test_instrument_demonstrations.py`. The blind spot is real, is not closed, and is counted: a consumer that reads the JSON without naming the instrument is invisible — the route the one real reader takes.
- Its cost is named: **two** exempt files, both files whose subject is the scanner, pinned by a test asserting they would otherwise be flagged.

## What I rejected

- **Repairing `run_controls.py`** (FI-01-DF-01). Demonstrated instead, in-process and fast. Repairing the driver that decides kill tables, inside the ticket enumerating it, is an instrument change during the measurement — FI-01 declined it for the same reason.
- **Giving `run_port_swap.py` an exit code.** Same reason, plus it is the driver FI-03..FI-06 must measure with, and the change would alter every recorded invocation in `RESULTS.md`.
- **Repairing PA-06-DF-01 / FI-01-DF-02** (the catalogue harness refusing per-arm catalogues). FI-02 measures *with* that harness; FI-01-DF-02 records that a blanket fix would silently drop a real check on five sealed files.
- **Making `--verify-suite` refuse a wrong prediction.** No new gates. A wrong prediction is a finding about the predictor; the suggested fix is a reported count.
- **Refactoring the four undemonstrable tripwires.** That would have quietly reduced the count, which is the product.
- **Renaming the grepped string**, and **splitting a token to evade my own scanner** in the demonstration file. Both are the six-lines-of-YAML move; the second was live temptation when my own file tripped the new check, and the honest answer was a named exemption with a test proving it is load-bearing.
- **Counting argparse usage errors as failing inputs.** "You typed the command wrong" is not a verdict about a subject.

## Goal contribution

**GOAL-instruments-can-fail (direct).** Baseline "roughly 0 of ~9" → **23 of 32 enumerated instruments** with a demonstrated failing input, 9 without and each says why, plus 9 demonstrated blind spots. The goal targets only that nothing is silently omitted; `test_every_row_is_classified_and_every_gap_carries_a_reason` and `test_the_named_instruments_are_all_enumerated` make that a test rather than a claim. Re-runnable at FI-06 on the integrated tip.

**GOAL-scorecard-carries-a-delta (enabling).** `score_tools check`, `audit` and `seal` are enumerated with demonstrated failing and passing inputs; `audit`'s blind spot (OPEN/UNVERIFIED are printed and not counted) is recorded.

**GOAL-fixture-can-diverge (guard).** No gate added. Nothing here refuses anything about the repository's design.

## Evidence

```
uv run --with pytest --with pyyaml python -m pytest tests -q
    at the implementation commit  ->  1235 passed
    after close ticket FI-02      ->  1231 passed
python3 examples/validation/instruments/demonstrate.py --tier all  ->  exit 0,
    "Every declared demonstration reproduced."   (all 37 rows, fast and slow)
```

Zero failures either side. The four-test difference is `close ticket` moving `specs/tickets/FI-02/` into `specs/.history/`, which retires that ticket's four parametrised workflow tests; no test changed verdict.

The predecessor epic's carried red (`test_nothing_executable_reads_this_instrument`) is green.

**Parent commit (`git archive 51fe73d`):**

- its own tripwire → `1 failed, 34 passed` — the known red
- **+ the new tripwire alone** → `36 passed`, proving the parent *tree* never gated and the old test's red was a false positive
- **+ the new demonstrations without the harness** → `3 failed, 5 errors`

## Scope note, stated rather than left to a reader

The plan's `implementation_scope` is `[tests/, scripts/, references/]`. The harness landed in a **new** directory, `examples/validation/instruments/`, beside FI-01's `probe_demonstrations.toml`. Under `tests/` it would be a test; FI-06 needs a command. No file in FI-01's conflict key (`examples/validation/ab/`) was touched. `references/architecture_advice.md` (this ticket's declared workflow key) gained an "S2 applied to ourselves" section carrying the counts.

author: tgvashworth
body:
## What this changes

`gyrinx/tasks/registry.py` is platform code, but its `_get_tasks()` imported
eight task functions from `n23.core.tasks` by name. The platform therefore had
to know what the edition calls its work — one of the concrete blockers to
standing up a second edition (#2093).

This inverts it. Each app declares its own routes in a module-level
`task_routes` list in its own `<app>/tasks.py`:

```python
# n23/core/tasks.py
@task
def backfill_pins(...): ...

task_routes = [
    TaskRoute(backfill_pins, ack_deadline=600),
]
```

A new `gyrinx/tasks/discovery.py` walks the installed apps and collects those
lists, modelled on `django.contrib.admin.autodiscover()`. This is the first
autodiscovery in the codebase, so it also sets the pattern. Registering a task
in a new app now needs no platform edit at all.

## Topic names are unchanged

**This is the important one, and it is verified rather than asserted.**
`TaskRoute.path` is derived from `func.__module__`, so a task's Pub/Sub topic
follows the module its function lives in. **No task function moved module** —
only the route declarations did.

Every route's `path`, `topic_name`, `ack_deadline`, retry delays and schedule
were dumped before and after the change and compared. The two are byte-identical:

```
$ diff before.canon after.canon
$ echo $?
0
```

All eight, unchanged:

| task | topic |
|---|---|
| `trigger_discord_issue_action` | `{env}--gyrinx.tasks--gyrinx.api.tasks.trigger_discord_issue_action` |
| `backfill_pins` | `{env}--gyrinx.tasks--n23.core.tasks.backfill_pins` |
| `complete_campaign_list_clone` | `{env}--gyrinx.tasks--n23.core.tasks.complete_campaign_list_clone` |
| `hello_world` | `{env}--gyrinx.tasks--n23.core.tasks.hello_world` |
| `propagate_content_cost_change` | `{env}--gyrinx.tasks--n23.core.tasks.propagate_content_cost_change` |
| `propagate_default_child_fighter_assignment` | `{env}--gyrinx.tasks--n23.core.tasks.propagate_default_child_fighter_assignment` |
| `reconcile_all_lists` | `{env}--gyrinx.tasks--n23.core.tasks.reconcile_all_lists` |
| `refresh_list_facts` | `{env}--gyrinx.tasks--n23.core.tasks.refresh_list_facts` |

No topic is renamed, so nothing is orphaned and provisioning has nothing new to
create on deploy. `test_topic_names_derive_from_the_declaring_module` pins this
going forward.

## Design notes

- **Declarations are discovered, not tasks.** We deliberately don't scan for
  `@task` functions and register whatever turns up. A route carries per-task
  config and provisions a Pub/Sub topic — infrastructure with a cost and an IAM
  footprint — so it stays an explicit statement of intent. That's the option-D
  rejection recorded in `.claude/notes/task-registry-footgun.md`; this change is
  that note's option B, landed as a declarative list rather than the
  `@gyrinx_task` decorator it sketched. The decorator is still open as a later
  refinement (it's the only version that makes omission *structurally*
  impossible), which is why the #1947 system check stays the tripwire.
- **Per-task config survives.** The three `ack_deadline=600` routes keep their
  deadline and their explanatory comments, now sitting beside the functions they
  describe. Asserted by `test_discovery_preserves_per_task_config`.
- **Discovery stays lazy**, for two independent reasons now written on
  `_get_tasks()`: (1) importing an app's tasks module runs Django's `@task`,
  which loads the configured backend, which does
  `from gyrinx.tasks.registry import get_task` at module scope — doing discovery
  at registry-import time would re-enter the module half-built; (2) discovery
  walks `django.apps`, which isn't populated until every app has loaded, later
  than the registry is first imported. Deferring to first call sidesteps both.
- **Ordering is deterministic**: INSTALLED_APPS order, then declaration order,
  with no set iteration anywhere (`first_party_task_modules()` returns a list,
  and `checks._task_module_paths` now dedupes in first-seen order instead of
  building a set). Confirmed stable across three runs. The only change is that
  `trigger_discord_issue_action` now groups with its own app instead of sitting
  mid-list; topic provisioning is order-insensitive.
- **`FIRST_PARTY_PREFIXES` is still needed**, but now has a single home in
  `discovery.py`, shared with `checks.py`. It's what stops a third-party app's
  `tasks.py` being imported on our behalf. Sharing it matters: the check's job is
  "every declared `@task` is registered", so if it scanned a different module set
  than discovery collected from, the difference would be an unpoliced hole.
  `checks.py` no longer repeats the app scan.
- **Error messages now point at the right file.** The `gyrinx.tasks.E001` hint
  and `PubSubBackend.enqueue`'s "not registered" error used to send authors to
  `gyrinx/tasks/registry.py`; they now name the app's own `task_routes`.

## Testing

- Full suite: **4160 passed, 13 skipped**. Net +9 tests: 10 new in
  `test_discovery.py`, and `test_app_discovery_covers_edition_namespaces` moved
  out of `test_checks.py` into it (the prefix filter it exercises now lives in
  `discovery.py`). That implies a pre-change baseline of 4151 on this tree — one
  more than the 4150 I was given; `HEAD` is exactly `origin/main` (9b1d67c5) and
  nothing failed, so the difference is in the baseline figure, not a regression.
- The chaos/redelivery coverage still exercises real routes through the registry:
  `test_task_chaos_concurrency.py` and `test_maintenance_pin_ops.py` — 26 passed.
  They import the real `n23.core.tasks` functions and resolve them via
  `get_task()` in manual-queue mode, so they'd fail if discovery missed a route.
- `manage check` — clean, 0 issues (this is what runs the #1947 check).
- `./scripts/dev.sh` starts and serves `HTTP 200`; provisioning correctly skipped
  outside Cloud Run.
- `./scripts/fmt.sh` clean; `ruff check` clean; all pre-commit hooks pass.

## Docs

Updated the how-to, technical reference, `gyrinx/tasks/CLAUDE.md`, the package
docstring and `n23/__init__.py` (background tasks are no longer on its list of
reverse-dependency blockers). The design note records what actually shipped.

author: mlacayoemery
body:
The cluster workflow from #182 **failed on its first dispatch** — which is exactly why I dispatched it instead of assuming it worked.

```
>> pointing containerd at the local registry
Error response from daemon: No such container: esgame-registry
```

`kind.sh` wired containerd at the local registry unconditionally. That registry is only needed by `overlays/local-registry` — for images built here and never pushed. `overlays/published` pulls both from ghcr and needs none of it, which is what `deploy/k8s/README.md` already claims and what the workflow relies on.

**Worse than a plain failure:** the cluster had already been created by that point, so a retry took the `cluster already exists` branch and went straight back to the same line. It could not self-heal.

The wiring is now conditional on the container existing, and when it's absent it says what to do rather than dying:

```
>> no esgame-registry container, so containerd is not being redirected
   overlays/published works as is; for overlays/local-registry, run
   deploy/registry/registry.sh up && deploy/registry/registry.sh push, then this again
```

Both branches exercised — `docker inspect` returns 0 for the running registry and non-zero for a name that doesn't exist. I can't create a kind cluster on this host to test the whole path (`kind` isn't installed and the inotify limits are back at 128), so the real proof is re-dispatching the workflow once this merges. I'll report what it does.

## My error, and worth naming

I grepped `kind.sh` for a registry dependency, found nothing in its `need` guards, and concluded there wasn't one. The dependency was thirty lines further down, outside anything a grep for `need` or `registry.sh` would surface. Reading the block would have found it.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## What

Extends the `captureDelete` registry to **four of the six** clinical kinds the issue names — `allergy`, `condition`, `immunization`, `skin-lesion` — and gives the undo-buffer purge the photo half of the file-reclaim rule it already had for clips.

Deleting a weigh-in has been reversible since #30. Deleting a penicillin allergy was not. That inversion is what this closes for the passport's highest-traffic rows.

## Why these four, and what remains

`encounters` and `medical_documents` are deliberately **not** in this PR. They are not "more of the same":

- **Visits** — `encounters` has ~12 inbound `encounter_id` back-links (records, meds, conditions, procedures, imaging, immunizations, episodes, appointments — the last a CAS since #2201). The current delete NULLs every one of them. A faithful restore has to decide, per link family, whether undo RE-POINTS live rows at the restored visit — which the entity registry has no vocabulary for (it re-inserts rows, it does not re-point surviving ones) and which the codebase has three documented precedents for *not* doing. That is a design decision, not a registry entry.
- **Uploaded documents** — the file on disk plus extracted rows across ~13 tables, and it must stay in step with the imported-row cleanup, document-reassignment and extracted-count accounting lists (`lib/import-footprint.ts`). Restoring a document without re-deriving those three registries would leave the "every table written by import stays represented" rule silently broken.

Both deserve their own PR with their own argument. A well-argued partial beats a rushed whole.

## What each capture carries

| Kind | Children | Reconciled links | Side effects deliberately NOT inverted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allergy` | `allergy_reactions` (ON DELETE CASCADE) | document / visit / provider | — |
| `condition` | — | document / visit | `intake_items.indication_condition_id` null-out |
| `immunization` | — | visit / provider | `sweepImmunizationDismissals` (#376) |
| `skin-lesion` | `lesion_photos` (explicit — `lesion_id` has no cascade) | document / visit / provider | `care_plan_items` follow-up links (#700) |

Three points worth calling out:

- **`conditions.edited` rides in the snapshot** (migration 161). A hand-corrected episode-promoted condition restores still edit-LOCKED, so `syncPromotedCondition` holds out of it instead of reverting the correction on the next episode transition. And a re-promotion inside the window cannot clobber the restore, because `syncPromotedCondition` only ever UPDATEs an existing row — it never re-creates one.
- **The lesion's photo FILES are deliberately left on disk** by the delete (the `activity_videos` posture, #1224) so a restore re-points at them. `deleteLesionPhotosForLesion` — which unlinks — is no longer on this path.
- **Inbound null-outs stay uninverted on purpose**, matching the three documented siblings (`protocols.intake_item_id`, the medical-record follow-up links, `intake_items.source_record_id`): the clinical row comes back, the other row's link stays honestly cleared. The confirm copy now says so rather than promising "This can't be undone".

Two mechanisms were added rather than hand-rolled per kind:

- **`EntitySpec.uniqueKey`** — the clinical roots sit under a partial `UNIQUE(profile_id, external_id)` and their importer re-inserts with `OR IGNORE`, so a document reprocess inside the (30-day) window can re-take a deleted imported row's key and a verbatim re-insert would abort the whole undo on the index. Declared, restore ADOPTS the live row — the registry-declared twin of the `liveRowIdForCapturedRoot` (#509) treatment for sync-tombstoned roots.
- **`captureDelete` owns the clinical inbound null-outs**, exactly like the `intake_items` ones above them, so both delete paths inherit them. This fixes a latent bug: `intake_items.indication_condition_id` was NULLed only in `deleteCondition`, so the Data → Manage bulk delete of a condition a medication treats tripped the FK.

## Purge-time unlink, from day one

`capturedPhotoFiles` is the pure twin of `capturedVideoFiles`; `capturedFilesOf` → `unlinkPurgedFiles` fans out to both halves, so **all three** purge paths (expiry sweep, Delete permanently, Empty trash) reclaim photos as well as clips.

The photo half needs a rule the clip half does not: **the thumbnail is a derived sibling.** Since #1844 phase 3, `lesion_photos` carries no `thumb_path` column — the thumbnail lives beside the stored file under `thumbSiblingPath`. A purge that reclaimed `stored_path` alone would leave the thumbnail of a deleted dermatology close-up on disk indefinitely, so the unlink derives it, behind the same "skip anything a live row still references" guard (content-hash naming means a re-upload can share the file).

## `DATASET_UNDO_KIND`

`allergies`, `conditions` and `immunizations` are deletable datasets AND undoable roots, so the compiler-guarded map forces a decision: all three are mapped, and the bulk delete now captures each selected row. `skin_lesions` is not a deletable dataset, so it needs no entry (asserted). One consequence had to be handled: the undo branch of `deleteDatasetRows` returns before the plain path's pre-image read, so the immunization dismissal sweep now takes its removed-vaccines pre-image on that branch too.

## No schema changes

None. No migration slot used.

## How tested

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm test` — 777 files / 11430 tests pass (pure registry + `capturedPhotoFiles` + `DATASET_UNDO_KIND` assertions added)
- `npm run test:db` — all three shards pass (585 files / 4569 tests)
  - new `lib/__db_tests__/clinical-undo.test.ts`: per-kind capture/restore fidelity (children, clinical qualifiers, the `edited` lock, the photo series re-parented onto the new id), dangling document/visit/provider links NULLed on restore, `external_id` adoption, and the photo unlink across the sweep / Delete permanently / Empty trash — plus the two negative cases (an UNDONE delete keeps its files; a file a live row still references survives).
  - new `lib/__action_tests__/clinical-undo.actions.test.ts`: the typed `{ undoId, error? }` outcomes and the profile-scoped refusals.
  - the FK reflection guard in `lib/__db_tests__/undo-delete.test.ts` (the #598 class) passes for every newly captured table, which is what pins that no outward link was left undeclared.
- Targeted e2e at CI parity: `E2E_PORT=6600 npx playwright test e2e/clinical-undo.spec.ts --repeat-each=3 --retries=0` — 6/6
- Regression e2e: `skin`, `trash`, `undo-delete`, `allergy-dedup`, `immunization-delete-confirm`, `condition-suggestion`, `multi-view`, `records-page`, `records-hub.mobile`, `immunizations`, `entry-vocabularies` — all pass
- `npx vitest run lib/__tests__/e2e-hygiene.test.ts` — clean after the final spec edit

author: jean-ely-pro
body:
## Origine

Question posée à la lecture du guide : « chaque bloc doit-il être copié dans
`templates-client/` ? »

Non — et si la question se pose après lecture, c'est que le guide laissait le doute. Il
indiquait « créer un type → `templates-client/` » sans dire que les sections livrées
fonctionnent telles quelles.

## Ce qui est ajouté

Les trois cas, distingués :

| Vous voulez | Vous faites |
|---|---|
| Utiliser une section livrée | **rien** |
| Créer une section propre au site | un nouveau fichier dans `templates-client/blocs/` |
| Changer le rendu d'une section livrée | copier son fichier, même nom |

Seul le troisième implique une copie, et il doit rester rare : un fichier recopié ne reçoit
plus les corrections du socle.

## Le CSS d'abord

Ajouté aussi : une maquette différente se traite presque toujours dans `client.css`, sans
toucher au moindre gabarit. On ne copie une section que si la **structure HTML** doit changer —
jamais pour une couleur, un espacement ou une disposition.

Pour rendre ce conseil applicable, le guide liste maintenant les classes des sections livrées
et de la structure du site.

## Vérifications

L'état actuel du dépôt le démontre : `templates-client/blocs/` ne contient aucun bloc, et les
cinq types livrés sont disponibles et rendus.

Toutes les classes citées ont été relevées dans les gabarits, pas écrites de mémoire —
y compris les variantes `bloc-texte-image--gauche` et `--droite`.

Documentation seule ; aucun code touché. 156 tests inchangés.

author: twitzelbos
body:
A reusable **`ratatui-serial`** crate: a `no_std` ratatui `Backend` that renders to an arbitrary byte sink via **ANSI/VT100 escape sequences** — so an embedded device (a Daisy Seed) can *host* a full terminal UI over its **USB-CDC / serial** link, with a host terminal emulator (`picocom`, `screen`, PuTTY) as the display.

## Why
The Daisy already brings up USB-CDC serial; a TUI over that link is just ANSI bytes out + keys in. ratatui gained `no_std` support in v0.30 but its built-in backends (crossterm/termion) are host-OS/std, so driving a terminal over serial needs a custom `Backend`. This is that backend — and it's not Daisy-specific: anyone with a serial link can use it.

## What it does
- Implements `ratatui_core::backend::Backend`: `draw`, cursor show/hide/get/set, `clear`/`clear_region`, `size`/`window_size`/`flush`.
- Diffs **cursor position** and **SGR style** across cells so a redraw emits minimal escape traffic.
- Colors: 16 named + **RGB** (`38;2;…`) + **indexed** (`38;5;…`); modifiers: bold/dim/italic/underline/blink/reverse/hidden/crossed-out.
- Caller supplies the terminal size (no `SIGWINCH` over serial); `resize()` if you query it out of band.
- `no_std`, allocates nothing itself (needs a global allocator only because `ratatui-core` does).

## API
Generic over a tiny `Writer` trait (implement it for your serial port in ~3 lines), plus an optional **`embedded-io`** feature that blanket-impls `Writer` for any `embedded_io::Write`. A `Vec<u8>` impl is provided for host buffering/tests.

```rust
let backend = SerialBackend::new(port, 80, 24);
let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
terminal.draw(|frame| { /* ratatui widgets */ })?;
```

## Testing
3 host tests assert the exact ANSI for positioned styled text (cursor move + combined SGR + style/cursor diffing), cursor/clear/size, and RGB/indexed color. Builds `no_std` for `thumbv7em-none-eabihf` (default and with `embedded-io`); clippy + fmt clean under `-D warnings`; host tests wired into CI.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
Wiring it into `daisy-usb-audio` — a global allocator + a `Writer` adapter over the CDC `SerialPort` + a demo TUI (a natural fit: a **serial mixer control surface** with meters/faders, tying into the deferred multi-input-mixing idea).

body:
My Cariboo Now's RSS feed 403s on every direct fetch (see FEED_ERRORS.md),
so its articles always come in through the Brave/Kagi/Google News search
fallbacks instead. Those fallbacks build Article objects straight from
search snippets, bypassing the count/channel-based boilerplate detector
in fetch_feed_articles entirely — so whichever articles happened to get a
real search snippet looked fine, and whichever got the site's shared meta
tagline ("Stay connected with My Cariboo Now...") showed it raw. Same gap
existed for topic-news search results.

Add a direct tagline regex (_is_tagline_boilerplate) applied once at
Article construction so it's stripped regardless of fetch path or batch
size, and extract the local-domain body-fetch enrichment into a shared
_enrich_thin_local_articles() helper so every path — not just direct RSS
— recovers real article text after stripping.

author: mhrezaei
body:
The interactive setup wizard was stuck pre-M4, so **installing via the UI produced an SSH-only tunnel** (no TLS/mail arsenal) — the reason a UI-provisioned node showed `Endpoints: 0` and every pipe was `mimic=ssh`, while the non-interactive CLI (used in testing) worked. This also undercut anti-filtering for UI installs.

## Fix
- **Mimic selection at setup** via a checkbox (`survey.MultiSelect`); first option **`all`** = the whole arsenal, default `ssh+tls`.
  - Foreign builds `cfg.Mimics` on conventional ports (ssh=listen-port, tls=443, smtp=587, imap=143, smtps=465, imaps=993).
  - Iran builds `node.Endpoints` toward those ports.
  - SSH-only prompts (port / decoy / move-ssh) appear only when SSH is selected.
- **Observability:** each sub-pool's scale logs are labeled `pool=tcp|udp`, so the (already auto-warmed) **UDP sub-pool is visible** in journalctl. (It was there all along — the `max=6` lines — just unlabeled.)

## Tests
mimicPort / containsStr / allMimics-completeness. Full `-race` suite green; amd64+arm64 build clean. Version → **v0.7.2**.

author: geoffkoh
body:
## PP-94 — theme icons in headless SVG

Cloud-provider views rendered with the right colours and shapes but no service logos: theme icons are remote URLs, and PP-93 required output with no external references, so they were dropped.

They are now fetched once each and embedded as `data:` URIs. The fetch happens in **Python** (`icons.py`), next to the theme fetching it mirrors — which keeps the Node renderer entirely off the network and makes the whole path testable over `file://` URLs.

### Failing soft

An icon that 404s, times out, is not an image, or exceeds 256 KB is logged and dropped, and its element renders without one. Rendering never fails because a CDN is down, and works offline. Results are cached per process **including failures**, so twenty instances of one service fetch once and an unreachable host is not retried per node.

The non-image guard matters more than it sounds: an error page served with `200 text/html` would otherwise be base64'd into the diagram and rendered as junk.

### Two things only the rendered output revealed

1. **`svg.ts` never drew the icon** — PP-93 carried the field through but ignored it.
2. **A 30px icon inside a fixed 110px box squeezed the description out.** Descriptions were being clipped mid-word on exactly the nodes that had logos. Icon-bearing nodes now get a 36px allowance in `nodeSize`, matching the web app, where the box grows with its content.

The allowance is gated on the icon being present, and I re-ran the layout comparison harness to prove the gate: **the eight views without icons are byte-identical, and only the two AWS deployment views move — by exactly 36px.**

### Verification

- `uv run pytest` 485 passed (17 new), `ruff` clean, `mypy --strict` clean.
- `tests/test_icons.py` covers embedding, pass-through of existing data URIs, unreachable/non-image/oversized rejection, one-fetch-per-URL, and one bad icon not stopping the others — all offline over `file://`.
- `tests/test_render.py` gains an end-to-end render through a themed workspace asserting `href="data:image/png;base64,`, and its no-external-references test now allows `<image>` but still forbids `href="http`.
- **Checked against the real AWS theme over the network**, not just fixtures: `ProductionDeployment` embeds two PNGs, keeps no `http(s)` reference, and the logos render — confirmed by rasterising the SVG and looking at it.

Documentation claiming the output contains no images was corrected rather than left to rot: it contains images, and that is the point — they travel inside the file.

### Noticed, not fixed

The AWS theme sets element `color` (AWS purple) without a `background`, so themed nodes render purple text on the default slate fill — poor contrast, visible in the rendered output. This is faithful to the web app, which resolves colours identically, so it is a defect in *both* renderers rather than something this PR introduced. Worth its own ticket.

body:
## Summary

- `ResourceListView` can now render a leading checkbox column for bulk operations. Selection is **controlled by the caller** — the table renders what it is given and reports intent back, holding no state of its own.
- The column appears only when both `selection` (the selected ids) and `onToggleSelection` are passed. Omit either and the rendered table is byte-for-byte what it was, so no existing list changes.
- `onToggleAllSelection` is what adds the header checkbox, and is called with the state the box is moving to. The box reports checked when every row on the page is selected, indeterminate when only some are, and unchecked when the page is empty.
- Keeping selection with the caller is what lets it survive paging and searching — the caller decides whether "select all" means this page or everything it knows about. The README shows the page-scoped version.
- The checkbox cell stops click propagation, so a list can keep `onRowClick` navigation *and* offer selection. This mirrors how the existing actions cell behaves.
- Styling hooks: selected rows get `.row--selected`, the header and body cells get `.field--selection`. Both use the existing `--prince-*` custom properties, with new `--prince-color-selected` / `--prince-color-selected-hover` falling back to a light blue.

Driven by a Vesper Admin need — bulk-assigning an app to selected users from a company's Users tab — but there is nothing app-specific here, so it is worth raising upstream to `tcds-io` as well.

## Notes for review

author: alistair3149
body:
PHPCS is failing on every branch, and not at the PHPCS step: it fails at `composer install`, and
the "Run PHPCS" step is skipped. Composer refuses to resolve the dependency tree at all.

`squizlabs/php_codesniffer` picked up CVE-2026-67434 (OS command injection, Packagist advisory
PKSA-rdkp-vv9z-mjkg), published 2026-08-05 23:53 UTC and affecting `< 3.13.6`. Composer blocks
advisory-affected packages by default, and `mediawiki/mediawiki-codesniffer 44.0.0` requires
exactly `php_codesniffer 3.9.0`, so resolution has no candidate:

    - mediawiki/mediawiki-codesniffer v44.0.0 requires squizlabs/php_codesniffer 3.9.0 -> found
      squizlabs/php_codesniffer[3.9.0] but these were not loaded, because they are affected by
      security advisories ("PKSA-rdkp-vv9z-mjkg")

`composer.lock` is gitignored, so CI resolves from scratch on every run and broke as soon as the
advisory reached Composer's data. A local checkout with an existing lock only warns, which is why
this does not reproduce until the lock is deleted.

`mediawiki-codesniffer 52.0.0`, released today, is the first release requiring `php_codesniffer
3.13.6` — the patched version. 51.0.0 and 50.0.0 are still on 3.13.5. So the bump is 44 -> 52
rather than a smaller step; there is no closer version that resolves.

Eight majors of sniff rules turned out to cost almost nothing: the run is clean apart from one
warning, `@phan-template` on `Neo4jValueBuilderRegistry::buildParsedValues()`. Phan is not used
here — no `.phan` directory, absent from composer.json and CI — and that was the only `@phan-`
annotation in the tree, so it was inert. `@template` is what PHPStan and Psalm actually read, so
this fixes a docblock that had no effect rather than appeasing a linter.

`Generic.Formatting.NoSpaceAfterCast`, which phpcs.xml enables directly, is deprecated as of
php_codesniffer 3.4 and is removed in 4.0; it printed a deprecation notice on every run. Replaced
with the documented equivalent, `Generic.Formatting.SpaceAfterCast` with `spacing` 0. Verified it
still enforces: adding a space after a cast fails with
`Generic.Formatting.SpaceAfterCast.TooMuchSpace`.

Verified with `vendor/bin/phpcs -p -s --standard=phpcs.xml` exactly as CI invokes it (exit 0, no
deprecation notice), PHPStan, and the Domain suite.



<sub>AI-authored — Claude Opus 5 (1M context); investigation and fix; verified with `vendor/bin/phpcs -p -s --standard=phpcs.xml` as CI invokes it, a negative control on the replacement sniff, PHPStan, and the Domain suite.</sub>

author: dev-mohsinm
body:
Follow-up to merging #7 and #17, closing the hazard that was sitting in the main checkout's index.

## What was staged

```
AM .claude/worktrees/tx-scheduled-section
A  .claude/worktrees/ynab-load
M  .gitignore
```

A git worktree is a full checkout containing a `.git` **file**, so `git add .` stages it as a **gitlink** — a submodule-style reference pointing at a path that exists on no other machine. Committing those breaks `clone` for everyone. I unstaged them; this stops them coming back.

`settings.local.json` is per-machine by its own name. **`.claude/skills/` is deliberately left un-ignored** so it can still be committed if you want it in the repo.

## On the staged `.gitignore`

The staged edit added a single line, `key`. PR #7 landed a superset of it — `key`, `*.jwt`, `*.pem`, `.ynab-token`, `.raqam-dump/` — with a comment explaining that `key` holds the service-role JWT that bypasses RLS. Verified `git show origin/main:.gitignore | grep -qx key` before discarding the redundant local edit, and `git check-ignore -v key` confirms it on merged main.

Same class of problem as that block: local state `git add .` sweeps up by accident.

author: ashleeradka
body: ## TL;DR The skill detail page showed a **History** tab for any skill, including ones with no recorded revisions, where clicking it produced "No changes recorded yet." The tab now appears only when there is at least one revision behind it. ## Why A tab is a promise that there is something there. For a freshly created skill, or any skill the workspace has not committed a change to yet, that promise was empty. Hiding the strip costs nothing: the page then renders exactly as it did before history existed, which was already what happened for an assistant too old to report history at all. That second case is the useful precedent. `useSkillHistory` already distinguished `null` (this assistant cannot report history) from `[]` (it can, and there is nothing recorded), and hid the strip for `null`. From a reader's point of view those are the same situation, so both now take the same path. ## Before / after | Skill state | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Has revisions | Files / History tabs | Unchanged | | No revisions recorded | Files / History tabs, History opens onto an empty state | No tab strip; the files card sits directly under the header | | Assistant predates the route | No tab strip | Unchanged | | History still loading | Tabs render immediately | No tab strip until the read resolves | ## Why it's safe - **Purely presentational.** No API, route, or query change. The read, its 404-to-null mapping, and the gateless-degrade contract from #40228 are all untouched. - **No flicker.** The gate is `!isLoading && revisions.length > 0`, not the count alone, so the strip cannot appear and then vanish mid-read. It stays hidden while in flight and appears once, if warranted. - **No stranded panel.** The active tab pins to Files whenever the strip is hidden, so a tab selected before the query answered cannot leave the page on a panel that is no longer rendered. - **The editor still survives.** The files panel keeps its `forceMount` and inline `display`, so an in-progress skill edit is not lost when the strip appears or the tab changes. ## Removed `isUnsupported` on `useSkillHistory` has no callers left, since `hasHistory` subsumes it, so it is gone rather than left as speculative API. The docstring that claimed the two cases "must stay distinct" now says what is actually true: they stay distinct in the fetch, because the 404 mapping is what makes a missing route quiet, and callers are free to collapse them. ## Verified `SkillRevisionList`'s "No changes recorded yet" state is kept and still story-covered. It is no longer reachable from the tab, but a refetch that returns an empty list while the panel is already open still lands there, so it is defensive rather than dead. Storybook, all four states on the real `SkillDetail` page: | Story | Tabs rendered | |---|---| | `Default` | Files, History | | `HistoryTruncated` | Files, History | | `NoHistoryYet` | none | | `HistoryUnsupported` | none | `NoHistoryYet` replaces the old `HistoryEmpty` story, since what it demonstrates is now the absence of the strip rather than the empty state inside it. Follow-ups from #40228 are tracked in LUM-3084, JARVIS-1467, and JARVIS-1468; none are affected by this change. ---

author: lodgvideon
body:
The receive half of #345, split from #386 as promised there because it changes a structure the loss detector depends on.

## 5 Whys

1. **Why does receiving a packet allocate?** — `ackTracker.receive` calls `sort.Slice`.
2. **Why does that allocate?** — `sort.Slice` takes a reflect-based swapper, which escapes.
3. **Why sort at all?** — the new packet number is appended to the end, so the slice is momentarily out of order.
4. **Why append to the end?** — it was the simplest way to reuse one merge pass over the whole set.
5. **Root cause: a full re-sort was paying for a disorder of exactly one element** — and the invariant (sorted, disjoint, **non-adjacent**) already guarantees that one element can touch at most two ranges.

## Change

Position search plus four cases: join two ranges, extend the upper one down, extend the lower one up, or splice in a new one-element range.

| steady state | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| permanently gapped (worst case) | 860 ns, **88 B, 3 allocs** | 21.6 ns, **0, 0** |
| contiguous (ordinary case) | 71.7 ns, **88 B, 3 allocs** | 4.8 ns, **0, 0** |

Benchmarks measure from a **warmed** tracker — from empty they would report one-off slice growth instead of the per-packet cost.

## The underflow trap, avoided by construction

Adjacency is tested as `hi+1 == pn` and `lo == pn+1`, **never** `hi == pn-1`. Packet numbers start at zero, and `pn-1` underflows to `MaxUint64` there — which would read as adjacent to a range at the top of the number space.

## Differential oracle

A passing suite does not prove a rewrite of a structure the loss detector reads. The **old implementation is kept verbatim in the test file** as an oracle; the new tracker must agree on the range set, the truncation floor **and** the `truncated` flag — checked **after every packet**, so a transient divergence cannot cancel itself out.

- 13 hand-picked shapes: holes filled from both sides, two ranges joined, duplicates, reordering, packet number **zero arriving last**, zero after high ranges.
- Truncation driven to 4× `maxAckRanges`, then fed arrivals **below the floor** so ranges merge while truncation is already in effect.
- 160 random sequences across four window widths (dense merging → sparse truncation).
- A separate test asserts the structural invariant directly, including that **no two retained ranges are left adjacent** — the subtle one, since two touching ranges would make a later insert merge the wrong pair.

## Mutation results, including two honest non-catches

**Caught:** dropping the two-range join · off-by-one in the upward merge · appending instead of inserting in order.

**Not caught — equivalent mutants, not gaps:**
- `hi == pn-1` instead of `hi+1 == pn`: with `pn == 0` the position search always yields `i == len(ranges)` (no range sits below zero), so the `pn-1` form is never evaluated. The underflow is unreachable either way; the safe form is kept because it stays safe if that precondition ever moves.
- `>` instead of `>=` in the position search: `hi == pn` cannot occur for a packet number the caller has already established is new — it would be contained.

I checked both rather than reporting them as coverage holes.

## Verification

`go test -race ./quic/ ./http3/` green · `go vet ./...` · `golangci-lint run` 0 issues · **bench-gate OK**.

body:
## Summary

Sprint 5B: the intelligent matching stage between Smart Import's parsed preview (Sprint 5A) and the database, built in the requested priority order. No parser files were touched — no defects were found in Sprint 5A during this work.

1. **Venue matching** (`venueMatching.js`) — two tiers: *exact* (normalised name + city, mirroring `auto_create_venue()`'s own normalisation) then *fuzzy* (the existing `search_entities` RPC). For the `msm-gig-guide` profile, where `venueName`/`city` are deliberately left unresolved, the venue name is derived from `venueBlock` (text before the first comma).
2. **Artist matching** (`artistMatching.js`) — same two-tier approach against `profiles` (`band` + `solo_artist`, merged since Smart Import can't tell them apart upfront). Rows that never attempt a per-row artist (`generic-dash-list`) get a `not_applicable` tier rather than being wrongly flagged "New Artist".
3. **Duplicate detection** (`duplicateDetection.js`) — exact and near (e.g. "Day Fever" vs "Day Fever - Bournemouth") clusters within the pasted batch, plus matches against existing `gigs`, preferring a resolved venue id over raw text when available.
4. **Review interface** — a new stage below the parser preview (`SmartImportReview` in App.jsx) with filter tabs for exactly the five buckets: Ready, Needs Review, Duplicate, New Venue, New Artist (`reviewBatch.js` derives one per row via documented precedence — duplicate > parser issues > new venue > new artist > fuzzy match > ready).
5. **Import Batch architecture** — `runMatching.js` is an async orchestrator that assembles the batch as a plain in-memory array (React state), no new Supabase tables, no writes anywhere in this stage.

A shared `textNormalize.js` also strips Sprint 5A's verbatim status wording (`"The Mafia (CANCELLED)"` → `"The Mafia"`) before using a name as a matching query, so flagged rows still find their real match.

Still no import button — the "Do not implement the final import" constraint holds; that's Sprint 5C.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Why We Are Making This Change
In clinical research software, ensuring both statistical correctness and strict adherence to clinical requirements is paramount. Previously, our testing pipeline lacked hard blocks against code coverage regressions or unmapped clinical requirements. This created a risk where untested execution paths or unvalidated regulatory requirements could silently slip into production, threatening the clinical validation status of our releases.

To eliminate this vulnerability, this PR introduces a robust, dual-layer quality and compliance gateway that programmatically blocks any pull request containing untested code paths or missing clinical requirement verifications.

---

### Key Decisions and Rationale

1. **Hard-Failing Code-Density Check:**
   * **What:** Integrated `@vitest/coverage-v8` in `vitest.config.ts` with strict minimum coverage thresholds. Added a local `npm run test:coverage` script.
   * **Why:** This ensures that no developer can merge code that lowers the overall test coverage. The build will fail immediately if untested execution paths are introduced.

2. **Automated Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM):**
   * **What:** Created a compliance-validation script (`scripts/generate-rtm.mjs`) that maps documented clinical requirements to automated test suites. 
   * **Why:** We must guarantee that 100% of defined clinical requirements are backed by active, passing tests. The script generates an interactive Markdown matrix featuring direct, active links (`[file.spec.ts#Lline](./file.spec.ts#Lline)`) to the test locations, facilitating frictionless external audits.

3. **Strict Validation Fail-Safes in CI/CD:**
   * **What:** Updated `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to run coverage and requirement verification sequentially. Added local-only validation flags (`--lenient` / `--local`) to avoid blocking offline local environments while preserving strict enforcement in the CI environment.
   * **Why:** Any failure in unit tests, coverage thresholds, or requirement mapping will physically halt the pipeline and block branch merges. The validated RTM report is archived as an immutable artifact on every run to serve as a verifiable audit trail.

---

### Detailed Changes

#### 1. Code Quality & Test Coverage
* Configured `vitest.config.ts` to utilize `@vitest/coverage-v8` for comprehensive coverage reporting.
* Defined strict line, branch, statement, and function coverage thresholds.
* Added `"test:coverage"` and `"verify:compliance"` to `package.json` to empower developers to run compliance checks locally before pushing.

#### 2. Compliance Mapping & Validation Engine (`scripts/generate-rtm.mjs`)
* Implemented parsing logic to extract clinical requirements and associate them with existing test suites.
* Configured the validation engine to exit with a non-zero status (`process.exit(1)`) if any requirement is unmapped, untested, or failing.
* Configured an interactive Markdown exporter to output human-readable verification reports.

#### 3. CI/CD Pipeline Adjustments (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
* Set up a workflow block that runs unit tests, runs coverage audits, and executes the compliance check on every pull request.
* Enforced that pipeline failures cannot be bypassed or ignored.
* Configured `actions/upload-artifact` to capture and store the final Requirements Traceability Matrix (`RTM.md`) for every pipeline run.

## Summary

- align vendored `gatewaybridge` ingress/egress schemas with the current Building OS contract
- preserve numeric, string, and boolean telemetry end to end through connectors, Normalizer, SQLite store-and-forward, Admin API, and Admin UI
- report the applied Point List revision through the additive Egress `GatewayStatus` heartbeat

## Why

Building OS moved `TelemetryFrame` from numeric-only field 3 to a wire-compatible `oneof` (`value_num = 3`, `value_str = 6`, `value_bool = 7`). The gateway still generated and persisted only `double value = 3`, converted booleans to 0/1, and placed strings in attributes. This remained interoperable for numeric readings but could not comply behaviorally for first-class string and boolean telemetry. The vendored Egress schema also lacked the additive Point List revision status message.

- numeric field 3 retains its wire number and type
- explicit `0.0`, empty string, and `false` retain oneof presence
- existing SQLite numeric rows are migrated in place and replay as `value_num`
- new SQLite rows store the complete protobuf frame while retaining legacy numeric columns
- peers that do not understand `GatewayStatus` can ignore the additive oneof case

author: spacebear21
body:
Bumps the Dart bindings to `0.2.1+payjoin-1.0.0-rc.8` and pins the `payjoin-ffi` wrapper dependency to `e4f5a0b3`, the `payjoin-1.0.0-rc.8` tag commit.

The FFI surface is unchanged since rc.7 — `git diff payjoin-1.0.0-rc.7..payjoin-1.0.0-rc.8 -- payjoin-ffi/src` is empty, only the `payjoin` dependency line in `payjoin-ffi/Cargo.toml` moved — so a patch bump covers it. What reaches consumers is rc.8's tightened sender validation: an input must declare a sighash type that commits to all inputs and outputs, so only ECDSA `SIGHASH_ALL`, taproot `SIGHASHDEFAULT`/`SIGHASH_ALL`, and an unset type are accepted.

### Versioning convention

Adopts the pub.dev build-metadata convention that [`bark_bitcoin`](https://pub.dev/packages/bark_bitcoin/versions) uses: `<package version>+payjoin-<crate version>`. The semantic version before the `+` stays what consumers write constraints against, while the metadata after it names the wrapped `payjoin` release directly on the pub.dev listing instead of requiring a changelog lookup. `dart pub publish --dry-run` accepts the string.

### Release documentation

The Dart package carried no publishing instructions, though `payjoin-ffi/README.md` claims each language directory has them, so `CONTRIBUTING.md` gains a `Releasing` section covering the versioning convention and the publish steps.

It documents two archive-content traps, both stemming from `.pubignore` *replacing* `.gitignore` at publish time rather than adding to it:

- `lib/payjoin.dart` is gitignored but must be present and current, since it is the binding surface consumers import.
- `native/Cargo.lock` is gitignored but absent from `.pubignore`, so a local build leaves one behind that would ship a lockfile resolved against the `.cargo/config.toml` path overlay. 0.2.0 happened not to ship one; a dry run from a built tree does include it.

### Known limitation, not addressed here

`scripts/generate_bindings.sh` always builds with `_test-utils`, so the bindings it emits declare test-only APIs such as `TestServices` and `BitcoindEnv` while consumers build the native library without that feature, leaving those declarations backed by symbols absent at runtime. Unpacking the published 0.2.0 archive confirms it already ships them; `@Native` resolves lazily, so this is latent rather than breaking. Recorded as a known limitation in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Giving the script a production mode, as `payjoin-ffi/csharp` does with `PAYJOIN_FFI_FEATURES`, is left for a follow-up, along with adding `native/Cargo.lock` to `.pubignore`.

Disclosure: co-authored by Claude Code

body:
## Promote v0.35.0

Frozen at `f4deead3bf63163e17726cf63da2bfecbd5caddf` — the commit where `0.35.0` was versioned. Commits merged to `develop` afterward require an explicit candidate refresh or ship in the next release.

- Merge this PR with a **merge commit** (do not squash or rebase).
- If multiple promote PRs are open, merge them in version order (oldest first).
- Merging publishes a GitHub Release for `v0.35.0` and triggers the existing GHCR `v*` image publish (`latest` channel).
- The `release/v0.35.0` branch can be deleted after this PR merges.

### Changelog

## 0.35.0 (2026-08-06)

This release expands source-control setup and review workflows, adds a direct homepage feedback path, and improves reliability across automations, Slack routing, and self-hosted sandboxes.

### Highlights

- Review pull requests with line-anchored comments across GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps.
- Configure and safely disconnect every supported source-control provider from Settings.
- Share feedback directly from the homepage without interrupting normal task workflows.
- Scan and run custom automations more easily with clearer schedules, destinations, and independent controls.

### Minor changes

- Add a dismissible homepage feedback prompt that lets users book time with the founders or send feedback by email without interrupting their normal workflow.
- Post line-anchored inline pull-request review comments across GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps, with provider-aware suggestions and safe fallback when an anchor is rejected.
- Let administrators configure non-GitHub source-control providers with complete callback guidance and safely remove persisted GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps connections from Settings.

### Patch changes

- Make custom automations easier to scan with human-readable schedules and clearer destinations, and keep creation and other run controls available while an automation is being queued.
- Keep sandbox HTTP and WebSocket traffic reachable on LAN-hosted deployments and fall back to the task API when a live sandbox connection cannot stop an active task.
- Keep OpenCode task sessions consistently identified as Roomote while preserving the current workflow and implementation guidance.
- Explain when automatic Slack routing is temporarily unavailable instead of silently showing the workspace picker, while keeping sensitive provider errors out of user-facing messages.
- Stop task closeouts from promising a follow-up self-review when every selected GitHub repository is excluded from automated processing.
- Let administrators disconnect GitLab, Gitea, and Bitbucket OAuth connections when provider client credentials come from runtime configuration.
- Preserve deleted-line review thread anchors on Bitbucket and Azure DevOps so later reviews can match and reply to existing inline comments.
- Let sync reviews resolve Roomote-authored inline threads after verifying the flagged code was fixed, including when GitHub marks the original anchor outdated.

### Jarvis answer-first
- entrega uma resposta concreta antes de perguntar
- restringe seletores a alternativas materiais solicitadas explicitamente
- bloqueia loops de perguntas e exige uma entrega depois de qualquer escolha

### Jarvis operacional
- adiciona `OperationalPolicy` com classificação por domínio, risco e reversibilidade
- executa criações e atualizações locais de baixo risco com recibo e ação de desfazer
- exige confirmação explícita para exclusões e operações financeiras
- mantém operações pendentes sem alterar dados e evita confirmações duplicadas
- cobre tarefas, agenda, projetos, hábitos, metas, ideias, CRM, documentos, notas, inbox, planejamento diário e financeiro

- aplica fundo preto azulado e grade azul discreta

- migra visualmente nós antigos brancos e ajusta textos, bordas, seleção e sombras

## Por que

O Jarvis devolvia decisões ao usuário em forma de opções genéricas e executava ferramentas mutáveis sem uma camada central de risco e reversão. O Canvas também misturava uma área escura com cartões brancos, quebrando a consistência visual do Motion Hub.

## Impacto

O Jarvis agora pensa e entrega antes de perguntar, opera o Hub com resultados verificáveis e permite desfazer alterações locais. Ações destrutivas ou financeiras só acontecem após confirmação. O Canvas passa a usar um tema escuro consistente em toda a experiência.

### Diagnóstico Groq

body:
## Summary

Adds keyless cosign signing of every pushed image digest in `docker.yml` — prerequisite for configuring `argocd-image-updater` on `redact-extproc` with the same provenance verification every other auto-updated image on this platform uses.

## Related Issues

Source of truth: requested in ADORSYS-GIS/ai-helm-values (redact-extproc image-updater discussion, 2026-08-06), following the same pattern as ADORSYS-GIS/lightbridge-code-intelligence's `image-pipeline.yml`.

## Type of Change

- [x] CI/CD or tooling

## Changes Made

- Added `id-token: write` to the build job's permissions (needed to mint an OIDC token for keyless signing).
- Tagged the build step (`id: build`) so its `digest` output is available.
- Added `sigstore/cosign-installer@v3` + a `cosign sign --yes` step, gated the same as the push itself (push runs only).
- Applies to all three images this workflow builds (not special-cased to `redact-extproc`), so the same image-updater pattern is available to all three going forward.

## Checklist

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] Tests added/updated for changes (CI-only change, no application code touched)
- [x] All tests pass (`just all-checks` not applicable — no Rust/chart code changed)
- [x] Documentation updated if needed (inline comments explain the why)

## Security Considerations

- [x] Security impact reviewed (describe below)

Strictly additive: signs images that were previously pushed unsigned. No change to what gets built or pushed, no new secrets, uses the existing `GITHUB_TOKEN`/OIDC identity already available to the job. Keyless signing publishes a Rekor transparency-log entry per digest — public, expected, same as `lightbridge-code-intelligence`'s.

## Testing

- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] Integration tests
- [x] Manual testing
- [x] Other: verified the workflow YAML parses; the actual sign step can only be verified live (push event, no push happens on a PR build) — will confirm cosign verification works once this merges to main and a real push-triggered run executes, before wiring the image-updater annotations on the ai-helm side.

## Security Considerations (again, testing note)

N/A — see above.

---

## Intent / Source of Truth

Requested: configure `argocd-image-updater` for `redact-extproc` in `ai-helm-values` so its tag isn't a manual bump every time (as it has been through today's incident chain). Every other auto-updated image on this platform (`lightbridge-code-intelligence`) verifies cosign signatures before promoting a tag; this repo's images were unsigned, so configuring image-updater the same way would silently never find anything to promote. This PR is the prerequisite; the image-updater annotations land in `ai-helm` once this is confirmed working.

Source of truth: ADORSYS-GIS/lightbridge-code-intelligence's `.github/workflows/image-pipeline.yml` (the `cosign sign --yes` pattern this mirrors, adapted from buildah/podman to `docker/build-push-action`).

## Verification

```
python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/docker.yml'))"   # OK
```
Structural only — the actual signing behavior needs a real push-triggered run (this workflow doesn't push on PR builds, so there's no digest to sign in CI for this PR itself). Will verify `cosign verify` against the resulting signed image once merged, before wiring image-updater in ai-helm.

- [x] Verified locally (YAML parses; matches the established sibling-repo pattern)

## AI Usage Declaration

body:
## Summary
Pins the file-metadata surface so a host-state leak fails visibly: st_ino,
st_dev, st_atime/st_mtime/st_ctime, statx's btime, st_nlink and st_blocks,
across stat / fstat / lstat / statx over regular files, directories, symlinks,
pipes and /proc entries.

Complements the DetInode newtype rather than duplicating it. That change makes a
host-inode leak a COMPILE error at one boundary; this fixture proves no OTHER
path leaks one at RUNTIME. A type cannot catch a leak arriving through a syscall
return value it never wraps, so both are needed and neither subsumes the other.

Includes a BRANCH on an inode comparison: lstat sees the symlink, stat follows
to the target, and the guest takes a different path (with an extra syscall)
depending on whether those inodes differ. A printed inode could be normalised
away; a taken branch could not, because the divergence has already changed what
the program did next.

Determinism: the fixture only observes -- no syscall handler, no scheduling
policy and no metadata virtualisation is changed, so it cannot itself alter how
deterministic a run is. Its value is as a ratchet. It makes TWO assertions about
time, and the second is the point: (1) values identical across a double-run, and

## Determinism
 the fixture only observes -- no syscall handler, no scheduling
policy and no metadata virtualisation is changed, so it cannot itself alter how
deterministic a run is. Its value is as a ratchet. It makes TWO assertions about
time, and the second is the point: (1) values identical across a double-run, and
(2) mtime STILL ADVANCING within a single run. Equality alone is satisfied by a
frozen clock -- a determinism bug dressed as a pass -- so freezing or rounding
time to force (1) is caught by (2). The advance check keys on st_mtim.tv_nsec,
not st_mtime: at 1-second granularity the second-level delta is 0 on any fast
host and the assertion would be inert.

## Linux Semantics
 ordinary Linux APIs with unmodified semantics -- stat/fstat/
lstat, statx invoked through the raw syscall with STATX_ALL (glibc may predate
it), symlink/mkdir/pipe for the object types. lstat-vs-stat distinguishing link
from target is standard Linux behaviour and is asserted as such. No particular
inode or device VALUE is asserted, only that values are stable, internally
consistent (fstat agrees with stat; statx agrees with stat) and free of host
identity.

## Validation
 builds -Wall -Wextra -Werror. Native: 3 runs, 3 DISTINCT outputs
(raw host inodes ~224475026 on dev 46) -- so the fixture is non-vacuous and any
stability under hermit is earned. hermit ptrace --strict: 3/3 identical,
metadata fully virtualised (file ino=4 dev=1, pipe ino=8 dev=3), statx ino
agrees with stat, mtime_nsec_advanced=1, branch A taken. e9patch preprocessing
with the ptrace runtime --strict: 3/3 identical and byte-identical to ptrace.
Assurance: L1 (backend ptrace, relaxations none). Not L2 -- no --verify-strict
bitwise_parity witness was taken for this fixture.

DO NOT MERGE - landing is serial and owned by hermit-det2.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Context & Motivation

Previously, the product's core values were hardcoded in two separate locations: the About page cards and the FAQ accordion in the content registry. This duplication created a high risk of text drift and required dual-maintenance whenever copy, visual themes, or icons needed updating. 

This Pull Request establishes a single source of truth for the product's core values by centralizing them into a structured registry, ensuring consistent messaging across both the high-level marketing cards and the detailed FAQ sections.

---

### Key Decisions & Rationale

1. **Type-Safe Central Registry (`src/data/coreValues.ts`)**:
   - Created a dedicated `CoreValue` TypeScript schema specifying a unique key, title, description, vector icon key, visual theme configurations (Tailwind classes for backgrounds and text colors), and corresponding FAQ questions.
   - This ensures any metadata changes (such as styling or icon choice) are strictly typed and centralized.

2. **Programmatic FAQ Generation (`src/data/contentRegistry.ts`)**:
   - Instead of manually maintaining duplicate strings for the FAQ section, the content registry now programmatically maps the `coreValues` dataset to construct the `about` category FAQs. This enforces automatic synchronization whenever a copywriter or developer updates a value's details.

3. **Dynamic Presentation Layer (`src/pages/about/+Page.tsx`)**:
   - Refactored the About page value grid to dynamically iterate over the core values array.
   - Implemented an icon mapping utility to safely resolve registered string keys (e.g., `"Zap"`, `"Shield"`) to their respective React components from `lucide-react`.

---

### Detailed Changes

- **Added `src/data/coreValues.ts`**: Holds the newly defined `CoreValue` schema and the primary data configuration for the four core values (Zap, Shield, Database, Code).
- **Modified `src/data/contentRegistry.ts`**: Cleaned up hardcoded duplication; updated the `'about'` FAQ items to map dynamically from the new core values registry.
- **Modified `src/pages/about/+Page.tsx`**: Replaced the static, hardcoded card structures with a dynamic `.map()` routine that utilizes the registry's theme parameters and icon mappings.
- **Modified `src/pages/about/Page.test.tsx`**: Updated testing suites to ensure that both the dynamic card grids and the synced FAQ content render correctly and correspond to the single-source registry dataset.
